7851e78b35628447.title: India's forex reserves decline $5 billion to $721 billion: RBI data
7851e78b35628447.summary: India's forex reserves dropped by USD 5.011 billion to USD 721.016 billion during the week ended October 16, the Reserve Bank of India said on Friday. In the previous reporting week, the kitty declined by USD 8.578 billion to USD 726.027 billion. The reserves touched an all-time high of USD 785.706 billion for the week ended September 4, driven by heavy greenback inflow as part of a special concessional swap for deposits from the diaspora through which banks raised a record nearly USD 133 billion but have been on a declining trend ever since. Experts attribute the sharp decline in the kitty to deployment of FCNR(B) resources and currency defence put up by the RBI through dollar sales. For the week ended October 16, foreign currency assets, a major component of reserves, decreased by USD 5.758 billion to USD 591.847 billion, according to the data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). c0a49ba673521b52.summary: iPhone maker Apple's India revenue grew by over 32 per cent to Rs 1,04,607 crore in FY26, according to the document shared by market intelligence firm Tofler. "Apple India Private Limited provides and markets Apple brand products and software, and reported its revenues for the financial year 2025-26 at Rs 1,04,607 crore, a 32 per cent jump since the last financial year," Tofler said. Apple India net profit grew by 66 per cent to Rs 5,311 crore in the same fiscal. The company's total expenses for the fiscal were reported at Rs 96,224 crore, Tofler said.

f3e4879ac88cc5d1.title: Coforge Q2 results: Net profit surges 56.5% to ₹588 cr, revenue up 53.6%
f3e4879ac88cc5d1.summary: Coforge posted a 56.5 per cent increase in consolidated profit to Rs 588 crore in the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, driven by AI-led execution of deals, the company said on Friday. The IT firm had posted a net profit of Rs 375.8 crore in the same period a year ago. "Right now the margin uptake that we are seeing is in the existing fixed price projects where AI is getting infused," Coforge Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director, Sudhir Singh, said during the company's earnings call. Coforge signed 8 large deals the highest number signed in a single quarter across North America, Europe and Australia, which led to a total contract value of the new orders of USD 1.04 billion during the reported quarter. The company increased the operational profit margin guidance to 17 per cent for the next year from the range of 15.5 per cent to 16 per cent. Revenue from operations during the reported quarter increased by 53.6 per cent to Rs 6,171 crore from Rs 4,016 crore a year

7b5a154b830be4c5.summary: Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Jordan on Friday, killing seven people and wounding 40 others, authorities said. The shooting took place at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, about 180 kilometres (110 miles) south of the capital, Amman. Footage broadcast on Jordanian state television showed two gunmen who appear to be holding pistols approaching the church and firing shots. A third man who appears to be holding a semiautomatic rifle then approaches and opens fire, and all three then run toward the church. Video footage taken by witnesses shows broken glass and pools of blood on the floor of the church. Dorgham Halasa, who was among the mourners inside the church, said intense gunfire erupted 15 minutes after the funeral had started, and then people started running. "It was a weird situation, and heavy gunfire," Halasa said. He did not see the gunmen, but said other people reported seeing four of them. The Associated Press could not independently verify the number

a30320a748957285.title: HYDRAA operation unearths illegal extraction of water from Sunnam Cheruvu
a30320a748957285.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Updated - October 24, 2026 08:20 pm IST - HYDERABAD Pipelines dropped into Sunnam Cheruvu. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement The Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA) has unearthed several establishments drawing water illegally from Sunnam Cheruvu, Madhapur. In a major operation on Saturday (October 24, 2026), HYDRAA forces removed dozens of pipelines discreetly laid into the lake from several buildings at Borabanda Phase-3 and Navbharat Nagar areas. The large hoses were attached to pump sets in the residential buildings on the other end, and buried under the earth outside to avoid detection. The houses raided revealed massive bore-wells drilled in bedrooms and kitchen areas, a statement from HYDRAA said. Photos and videos shared by the agency showed water sumps and bore-wells dug up beneath cots. Using heavy machinery, HYDRAA forces excavated the pipelines and traced them back to their source points. The operation which began at 6.30 a.m. continued up to evening, with officials removing 15 bore-wells, and unearthing a large number of pipes laid into the lakes. The statement said HYDRAA acted upon complaints from local residents about depleting ground water reserves due to unlawful extraction of water from the lake for supplying to hotels and hostels in Madhapur. b8b8014b8ecf7b27.title: Aung San Suu Kyi speaks to son after five years in detention in Myanmar
b8b8014b8ecf7b27.summary: The son of Myanmar's former leader Aung San Suu Kyi said Friday that when he finally got to speak with his mother, who has spent more than five years in detention in the Southeast Asian country, it seemed in some ways like not much time had passed at all. "She sounds like herself, and still sounds strong," said Kim Aris, adding that her voice was a bit croaky, like she had a cold. Myanmar's military government on Thursday allowed Aris a 20-minute phone call with his 81-year-old mother, one of the world's most famous political prisoners. He spoke from Myanmar's embassy in London to Suu Kyi in her country's capital, Naypyitaw, where she's serving an 18-year sentence under house arrest. Suu Kyi has been detained since February 2021, when Myanmar's army ousted her elected government. Held mostly incommunicado, she's serving an 18-year prison term on charges that supporters and rights groups say are bogus and politically inspired. It's not the first time she has been kept as a prisoner -

2759c8ffd56e2f7a.title: Rescuers search for survivors after Tibet earthquake kills 16, injures 76
2759c8ffd56e2f7a.summary: Rescuers combed through a remote area in the Chinese region of Tibet on Friday after a magnitude 7 earthquake killed at least 16 people, injured 76 and collapsed hundreds of homes, according to Chinese state media. The disaster struck Nagqu, a city north of Tibet's capital Lhasa that is some 4,800 metres (15,748 feet) above sea level, on Thursday. At least 339 homes collapsed, and officials told journalists they were concerned about further building collapses from aftershocks, as well as casualties from rockslides. China's national broadcaster CCTV aired footage on Friday showing collapsed houses and shattered stone walls in Nagqu. More than 12,000 residents in the region were evacuated, with additional shelters under construction, China's official news agency Xinhua reported. No one was reported missing in Baqen County in Nagqu, where the earthquake struck. Search and rescue efforts are complicated by the geography and low temperatures, officials said. While they were crossing the road, a white compact sedan car allegedly approached at high speed. When Ranjit and his friends signalled the driver to slow down, the occupants of the car reportedly became angry, took a U-turn and returned to confront them, the complaint stated. Following an altercation, Mr. Nitish alerted other friends, who arrived at the spot. A heated exchange reportedly broke out between the two groups. The occupants of the car then allegedly attempted to run the vehicle into the group. While the others managed to move aside, Ranjit was hit by the car. The car allegedly ran over his legs and dragged him for nearly 100 metres before the occupants abandoned him in the middle of the Hosur service road and fled the scene, according to the complaint. 1df76ae7afa31607.title: CG Power and Industrial Solutions Q2 profit jumps 44% to ₹409 crore
1df76ae7afa31607.summary: CG Power and Industrial Solutions on Friday posted 44 per cent jump in consolidated net profit at Rs 409.09 crore for September quarter FY27, supported by higher revenues. The Mumbai-headquartered entity had clocked a profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 284.44 crore in the year-ago period, it said in an exchange filing. During the quarter, the company's total income increased to Rs 3,883.25 crore from Rs 2,988.89 crore in Q2 FY26. From power systems segment, the revenue was Rs 1,766.76 crore as against Rs 1,254.49 crore in the year-ago quarter. The industrial systems business contributed a revenue of Rs 1,868.61 crore in the quarter as against Rs 1,533.33 crore in July-September FY26. The company's board approved enhancing capex investment for the GIS brownfield project at Vilholi, Nashik, from Rs 35.17 crore to Rs 44.62 crore. It also gave nod to invest Rs 15.31 crore to enhance EHV (extra high voltage) circuit breaker manufacturing capacity by 3,600 units (annually) at S3 Unit-II ...

0404e1873c16f985.title: Petronet LNG, Gruner Renewable float JV to develop compressed biogas plants
0404e1873c16f985.summary: Petronet LNG and Gruner Renewable Energy have formed a 50:50 joint venture to develop a portfolio of compressed biogas (CBG) plants across India, which entails an initial investment of about Rs 1,200 crore. This model is first of its kind in India, where the JV partner is undertaking sourcing of feedstock, EPC, operations and maintenance and offtake of organic manure, thus integrating the CBG value chain, a statement said. The proposed partnership envisages the development of 10 CBG plants, each with a designed capacity of 18 metric tonnes per day, taking the planned aggregate capacity to approximately 180 metric tonnes per day. The combined investment for the proposed portfolio is estimated at around Rs 1,200 crore, it informed. The partnership brings together Petronet LNG's established position in India's LNG and natural-gas infrastructure ecosystem with Gruner Renewable Energy's experience in CBG project development, engineering, feedstock mobilisation and plant operations. The development assumes significance in the wake of the country's push to build 100 million tonne of coal gasification capacity by 2030 under the National Coal Gasification Mission, aimed at converting coal into chemicals and bringing down the import dependence on products such as LNG, urea, ammonia and methanol. "We are going ahead with the joint venture of BHEL and Coal India, which is BCGCL....I am happy to share that we have started ground construction activities... d7d7f7c06453556f.title: J&K Bank Q2 result: Profit climbs 10.6% to ₹546 cr, asset quality improves
d7d7f7c06453556f.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Bank on Thursday reported a 10.6 per cent rise in net profit to Rs 546.36 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, driven by earnings growth and improvement in asset quality. The bank earned Rs 494.11 crore net profit in the year-ago period. Sequentially, its profits surged 28.8 per cent from Rs 424.18 crore in the first quarter of the current fiscal year, a bank spokesperson said. The bank announced the financial results after its Board of Directors reviewed and approved the quarterly and half-yearly figures at a meeting held at its corporate headquarters here on Thursday. Its net interest income rose 5 per cent during the quarter to Rs 1,502 crore. The lender's other income more than doubled to Rs 314.90 crore from Rs 153.76 cr a year ago. For the first half of the current fiscal year, the bank's operating expenditure grew 1.5 per cent, and its operating profit rose over 15 per cent to Rs 1,492 crore. 23929620c4ef6107.title: India must make growth employment-intensive, not just fast: Ex-RBI chief
23929620c4ef6107.summary: Sustaining economic growth of 7 per cent or more will require stronger private investment, labour-intensive manufacturing, better human capital and deeper integration into global value chains, former RBI Governor D Subbarao has said. Subbarao also said that the challenge is not merely to grow fast, but to make growth productive, employment-intensive and resilient. "India's 7.8 per cent growth in the first quarter suggests that the economy is more resilient than many expected...I am optimistic about India's medium-term prospects, but not complacent," he told PTI. Recently, the World Bank raised India's GDP growth forecast for the current fiscal year to 7.1 per cent, up 0.5 percentage points from its April projections, supported by robust domestic demand and strong exports, despite global headwinds. "Sustaining growth of 7 per cent or more will require stronger private investment, labour-intensive manufacturing, better human capital and deeper integration into global value chains..

b603c52963c725a4.title: Essar Ports wins ₹2,276 crore Tuna Tekra terminal project at Kandla
b603c52963c725a4.summary: Essar Ports has secured a letter of award from Deendayal Port Authority to develop an 18.33-million-tonne-a-year multipurpose cargo terminal at Tuna Tekra in Gujarat's Kandla port, marking a renewed push by the group to expand its ports business. The project carries an estimated cost of Rs 2,276.06 crore, including an investment of Rs 1,552.57 crore by Essar Ports and Rs 723.49 crore by the port authority, the company said in a statement. The terminal will be developed under a 30-year build-operate-transfer concession through the public-private partnership route, with Essar emerging as the highest bidder in a global competitive bidding process. The project will add capacity for handling dry and other multipurpose cargo on India's western coast, as the country seeks to expand port infrastructure to accommodate growing trade and improve logistics efficiency, it said. The proposed facility will have four berths, each measuring 300 metres, providing a total berth length of 1,200 metres

8e00001f3b35f80a.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Adani Group chairman Gautam Adani and Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran in Mumbai on Wednesday morning before heading to Jamnagar in Gujarat to visit Reliance Industries' giant oil-refining complex, the world's largest single-site refinery, along with Vantara and giga factories being developed by the conglomerate. Rubio, who arrived in Mumbai on Tuesday afternoon, first met Adani, followed by a meeting with Chandrasekaran, sources said. Neither side released details of the meetings. Adani heads one of India's largest conglomerates, with interests spanning ports, airports, energy, logistics and infrastructure. The group has also been expanding its renewable-energy and manufacturing businesses, sectors that are central to India's ambitions to strengthen domestic supply chains and attract global investment. Chandrasekaran, who leads Tata Sons, the Tata Group's holding company, oversees a sprawling business empire with interests in automobiles, .

c059d79704334d01.title: Rajnath Singh to unveil Land Warfare Doctrine at Army Commanders meet
c059d79704334d01.summary: The three-day Army Commanders' Conference began here on Wednesday, during which Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will release the 'Land Warfare Doctrine' -- a vision document providing an overarching framework to prepare the force for challenges posed by the evolving character of warfare and future conflicts. It brings together the senior leadership of the Indian Army to deliberate on the evolving security environment, operational preparedness, capability development and future-ready transformation initiatives, officials said. Chaired by the Chief of the Army Staff, Gen Dhiraj Seth, the apex-level biannual forum is being held from October 21-23, the defence ministry said. "With its comprehensive agenda, the conference will provide an important forum for the senior leadership of the Army to review ongoing initiatives, identify future thrust areas and formulate appropriate policy directions towards building a progressive, adaptive, technologically enabled and future-ready Indian Army,"

fa3078e71023d329.title: Pakistan cuts GDP growth estimate to 3.65 per cent in fiscal year 2026
fa3078e71023d329.summary: The Pakistan government has slightly revised the gross domestic product (GDP) growth down to 3.65 per cent for the outgoing fiscal year (FY26), attributing the adjustment to a mild slowdown in the industrial and services sectors, according to a media report on Tuesday. The country's GDP registered modest growth alongside an increase in per capita income in dollar terms, reflecting a sluggish pace of recovery in the country's overall output compared with the previous year, the government said. In May 2026, the government had projected the economy to grow by 3.70 pc in FY26, revising its earlier estimate of 4 pc. The revised growth rates in agriculture, industry and services in FY26 are 3.50pc, 3.34pc and 3.81pc, respectively, compared with earlier growth rates of 2.89pc, 3.51pc and 4.09 pc. The 23-year-old from Telangana, who also holds the Asian record, is a two-time Para World Championships medallist, having won the gold in 2024. She is also a Paralympic bronze winner in the same event. On Tuesday, Japan's Niina Kanno (58.92sec) won the silver and her compatriot Akane Kato (1:00.26sec) took bronze. The T20 classification covers athletes with intellectual impairments. Athletes in this category experience challenges with processing information, concentration, and executing race plans or tactical strategies. 7482ead028b895f1.title: Indian table tennis players bag five bronze medals at Asian Para Games 2026
7482ead028b895f1.summary: Ravi Baby Sahana and Prachi Pandey scripted history by becoming India's first para table tennis players to make the podium in the standing category at the Asian Para Games, as the country secured five bronze medals here on Tuesday. Paralympics medallist Bhavina Patel, Sonalben Patel, Prachi and Sahana all went down to accomplished Paralympic medallists in their respective women's singles semifinals, while Jehan Madan bagged a bronze medal in the men's singles class 1 event by virtue of finishing fourth in a five-paddler field. The haul also took India past its medal tally from the previous edition, where it had won two bronze medals in para table tennis. Sahana and Prachi's bronze were particularly significant as they became the first Indians to win medals in the standing category at the Asian Para Games. Tamil Nadu's Sahana went down 8-11, 2-11, 4-11 to five-time Paralympic gold medallist Mao Jingdian of China in the Class 9 semifinal. Class 9 in para table tennis is a standing .

5d3d056af94e4cda.title: India to host SCO Civilisation Dialogue Forum by year-end: Rajnath Singh
5d3d056af94e4cda.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday announced that India will host the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum by the end of this year and invited all member countries to participate in it. Singh made these remarks while addressing the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe, Tajikistan. "India, at the end of this year, will host the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum. We invite all SCO member countries to participate in it," Singh said. During the SCO summit of the Council of Heads of State in Tianjin in 2025, Prime Minister Narendra Modi proposed to create a Civilisational Dialogue Forum to strengthen people-to-people ties and allow sharing of the richness of ancient civilisations, art, literature, and traditions on a global stage. 129317366508a5c6.title: Shafali Verma reprimanded for breaching ICC Code of Conduct in 2nd T20I
129317366508a5c6.summary: India vice-captain Shafali Verma was on Tuesday handed an official reprimand for throwing the ball to the ground in frustration after dropping a catch during the second T20I against Zimbabwe. The 22-year-old was found to have breached Level 1 of the ICC Code of Conduct during India's nine-wicket victory in Raipur on Sunday. Verma was found to have breached Article 2.2 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which relates to "abuse of cricket equipment or clothing, ground equipment or fixtures and fittings during an International Match," an ICC media release said. In addition to this, one demerit point has been added to Verma's disciplinary record, for whom it was the first offence in a 24-month period. The incident occurred in the 12th over of Zimbabwe's innings when Verma, after dropping Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano at mid-off off Shree Charani's bowling, threw the ball to the ground in frustration. c5b45e39515cebce.summary: Cognizant and Google Cloud on Tuesday announced an expansion of their partnership to accelerate the adoption of agentic AI, including a new 'Gemini Frontier Capability Group'. The group brings together a dedicated global workforce that pairs Google's full-stack, enterprise-ready AI platform with Cognizant's domain, industry and engineering expertise as an AI-builder, according to a release. Supported by more than 18,000 dedicated Cognizant associates, the new group represents a substantial joint investment and builds on the momentum created by Cognizant's dedicated Gemini practice launched in April 2026. The new group is designed to bridge the path from pilot to production, equipping enterprises with the ability to safely deploy resilient, enterprise-grade agents that can help drive measurable business value, the release said. "Establishing our dedicated Gemini Frontier Capability Group lets our best frontier engineering talent focus entirely on getting frontier AI into production

bd7479f5fd8b87f5.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday said all institutions and political parties of the country should unite for national interest and fight together against the enemies of the country. Participating in Dussehra celebrations here, Modi also said that no matter how big or difficult a crisis may be, no one should sit back relying on others and recognise their own strength. "May our thoughts be aligned, and may... all the institutions of the nation, all political parties, stand together for national interest. We must proceed with this very spirit and we must fight together against the enemies of the country," the PM said. Underlining that his government's goal is to make India self-reliant, the prime minister said, "We must have faith in our resources. We must turn our resolve into power and find solutions through our own hard work. Because Lord Shri Ram taught us that the difficulties cannot stop our journey." He said in 'Ram Rajya', there is no discrimination against anyone and .

8fb74366d3fdbad4.summary: Vice President J D Vance declined to endorse Israeli President Benjamin Netanyahu for reelection a day after President Donald Trump endorsed the embattled Israeli leader. 6dc6053bbb569952.title: Just Dial Q2 profit declines 9.73% to ₹107.8 cr despite 13% revenue growth
6dc6053bbb569952.summary: Just Dial Ltd, a leading local search engine, has reported a decline of 9.73 per cent in its consolidated net profit to Rs 107.8 crore in the September quarter of FY27, on a year-on-year basis. It had posted a net profit of Rs 119.44 crore in the July-September quarter a year ago, according to a regulatory filing. However, Just Dial's revenue from operations was up 13.11 per cent in the September quarter at Rs 342.82 crore, compared to Rs 303.07 crore in the corresponding quarter a year ago. Just Dial's total expenses stood at Rs 262.81 crore, up 14.6 per cent YoY in the September quarter. The company, owned by Reliance Retail Ventures, the retail arm of billionaire Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance Industries Ltd, reported a 5.6 per cent rise in total income to Rs 397.38 crore in the second quarter of FY27. Share of Just Dial Ltd on Monday settled 2.82 per cent higher at Rs 732.55 apiece on the BSE.

20bf7e85d649d76c.title: PM Modi greets people on Vijayadashami, wishes happiness and prosperity
20bf7e85d649d76c.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday greeted people on the occasion of Vijayadashami and prayed that the festival would enrich everyone's life with happiness, prosperity, and success. "Heartiest greetings of Vijayadashami to everyone. May this festival of victory, filled with joy and faith, empower everyone's resolve with renewed strength," Modi said in a post on X in Hindi. "May every life be enriched with happiness, prosperity, and success-this is my sincere wish," he added. The festival celebrates Lord Rama's vanquishing the 10-headed demon king Ravana, and symbolises the triumph of good over evil. It is celebrated across the country with revellers coming out in large numbers to witness the burning of Ravana effigies, marking a culmination of 10 days of festivities filled with rituals, songs, dance and processions.

7219997d9a65701c.title: Bhagwat warns protests may serve political interests, fuel social divisions
7219997d9a65701c.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Tuesday cautioned that regime-change agitations do not resolve fundamental problems, warning that protests could become instruments of political interests and fuel divisions in society rather than delivering solutions. Addressing the annual Vijayadashami gathering here, Bhagwat cited recent upheavals in Bangladesh, Nepal, France, and Albania, asserting that forces pursuing their own interests use regime change as a means to alter political circumstances, rarely achieving intended results. "They claim that changing a regime will change the situation, but that has never really happened," he said. Bhagwat claimed that a stronger India would constrain such forces, making the country a target of attempts to weaken and divide it. While some global powers want India to develop, they do not want it to become too powerful, as it could challenge their dominance, he added. The Paraguay international's shot revived memories of a strike from a similar range from David Beckham when playing for Manchester United against Wimbledon on the opening day of the 1996-97 Premier League season. It remains one of English soccer's most famous goals and thrusted Beckham into the global spotlight. 0e7efd4b08cd369c.title: IDBI Bank sale to Fairfax: FinMin cites 2003 law, Delhi HC judgment
0e7efd4b08cd369c.summary: The finance ministry on Saturday said the legislative history of the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003, a Delhi High Court judgement and successive Union Budget speeches reflect the evolution of its policy towards the strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank. The Cabinet earlier this week approved strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank by selling 60.72 per cent stake to Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings for about Rs 53,000 crore (USD 5.5 billion). The deal is the largest foreign investment in India's financial sector so far and a major milestone in the country's banking privatisation drive. In a clarification on the legislative developments regarding reduction in government holding in IDBI Bank, the ministry said the Delhi High Court on December 17, 2018, held that the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003, contained no prohibition against reducing the government's stake in IDBI Bank Ltd. 0d0f27ff46cd7b20.title: Soybean output may dip to 2%; MP, Rajasthan to cushion Maharashtra losses
0d0f27ff46cd7b20.summary: India's soybean production is expected to decline marginally by 2.11 per cent to 107.93 lakh tonnes in the ongoing Kharif season despite drought-like conditions in several regions, the Soybean Processors Association of India (SOPA) has said. Higher output in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan will likely largely offset crop losses in Maharashtra, according to the association's first crop estimate report. The data was shared during the concluding session of SOPA's international soybean conference in Indore on Saturday. Soybean is a key oilseed crop that provides domestic cooking oil and a protein base for the livestock and poultry industries. Overall production is estimated to decline by 2.11 per cent from the previous season, the association said. It attributed the losses in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana to prolonged dry spells and moisture deficiency during critical stages of crop growth. Scientists hope the mission, which is expected to take five years, will provide clues to how Phobos and its smaller sibling Deimos formed, and hopefully even shed light on the origins of life in the solar system. The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency's launch of the spacecraft Tuesday on a new Japanese mainstay H-3 rocket comes as the United States, China and others consider sending astronauts to Mars. Samples from Phobos will provide useful data for scientists to consider using a Martian moon as a base for a future manned mission to the planet, said MMX project manager Yasuhiro Kawakatsu. "Despite their potential importance, Martian moons have never been fully investigated," Kawakatsu said. "They are known as the most important unclimbed mountains in the solar system." a722e6aae76e6979.title: Hybrids, CNG may contribute 50% of sales in 2-3 years: Renault India CEO
a722e6aae76e6979.summary: As French carmaker Renault pushes multifuel powertrain strategy in India, Renault India CEO Stephane Deblaise said hybrid and CNG technology can possibly account for almost half of the automaker's powertrain mix in its sales over the next 2-3 years. His comments came as the company bets big on hybrid and CNG technology in its India strategy. The automaker on Saturday launched its first strong hybrid offering on the Duster SUV, and plans to launch factory-fitted CNG models in the future. When asked how Renault India's powertrain mix could look over the next 2-3 years, Deblaise told PTI: "It is possible, 50 per cent is possible from hybrid and CNG, but we do not have a target." India's car market is increasingly seeing multiple powertrain technologies develop alongside each other, including hybrids, CNG and electric vehicles, rather than one single technology replacing another immediately. Automakers see hybrid technology as a practical bridge as the electric vehicle ecosystem evolve

ed44f33125f40768.title: India to keep Russian oil imports near current levels after Trump waiver
ed44f33125f40768.summary: India is expected to keep importing Russian crude at close to current levels after US President Donald Trump waived sanctions and tariffs mandated by a new law on major buyers of Russian oil, analysts said. Trump issued an executive order late on Friday waiving the "sanctions, restrictions, and duties" under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, a day before a 30-day deadline for enforcement expired. He signed the law on September 18. The law authorised tariffs of up to 100 per cent on goods from the five largest importers of Russian crude and gas, and sanctions on Russia's shadow fleet of tankers. The waiver is not specific to India and could also benefit China. The order lets the administration reconsider it later. India is the largest importer of Russian seaborne crude, averaging 1.8 million barrels per day this year, ahead of China at 1.2 million, ship tracking data showed. Italy, Turkey and the Netherlands completed the top five. India took about 1.82 million

244a544fe652c0b2.title: Puja pandal stampede: PM announces ₹2 lakh ex gratia, Shah to visit injured
244a544fe652c0b2.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday said the stampede in Kolkata is extremely distressing and announced an ex gratia of Rs 2 lakh to the next of kin of each deceased and Rs 50,000 for the injured. At least 10 people are feared dead in a stampede following a crowd surge at a community Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Saturday evening. "The stampede in Kolkata is extremely distressing. My thoughts are with those who have lost their loved ones. May the injured recover at the earliest," Modi said in a post on X. The prime minister said the local administration is providing all possible assistance to those affected. Modi announced that an ex gratia of Rs 2 lakh will be given from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund to the next of kin of each of those who lost their lives and Rs 50,000 to each injured person.

7df0f8c7e7e0d7b1.title: Centre revises Ladakh hill council rules, allows 7-24 elected members
7df0f8c7e7e0d7b1.summary: The Centre has amended the legal terminology, administrative structure and electoral provisions governing the Autonomous Hill Development Councils in Ladakh to align them with the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, which led to the creation of the Union territory of Ladakh. Under the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (Amendment) Regulation, the number of elected seats in each Council will be determined by the Ladakh administration, with a minimum of seven and a maximum of 24 seats. The administration can nominate up to four members from among women and "unrepresented communities", subject to the one-sixth limit of the population, the regulation states. The sitting Lok Sabha MP representing Ladakh will be an ex-officio member of the Councils constituted for each district. Each Council will have a term of five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless dissolved earlier. The term can be extended if holding elections is considered impracticable. Th

Published - October 24, 2026 04:41 pm IST - MUMBAI A man walks past the Kotak Mahindra Bank branch in New Delhi | Photo Credit: Reuters Kotak Mahindra Bank reported a 26% year-on-year (YoY) increase in net profit to ₹5,645.38 crore for the quarter ended September, beating analysts’ estimates based on LSEG data but falling short of domestic brokerages’ projections of 27-32% growth. The lender’s total income rose 18% YoY to ₹29,426.88 crore. Other income increased nearly 25% to ₹9,571.01 crore. However, sequentially, total income and other income declined 2.1% and 18.3%, respectively. Net interest income (NII) grew 16% YoY to ₹8,459 crore. Net interest margin (NIM), however, contracted to 4.31% from 4.54% in the preceding quarter. The bank attributed the decline to deposits mobilised under the Reserve Bank of India’s special window for foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) accounts, through which it raised ₹55,344 crore. Asset quality improved, with gross non-performing assets (GNPA) declining to 1.04% from 1.39% a year earlier. Net NPA fell to 0.24% from 0.32%. Provisions declined 15% YoY to ₹803 crore. Operating expenses rose 14% YoY to ₹5,271 crore, partly offsetting the gains from higher income and lower provisions. For the first half of FY27, net profit stood at ₹11,125.84 crore. As of September 30, net advances grew 25% YoY to ₹5,77,295 crore, while deposits increased 23% to ₹6,51,491 crore. bcfc461a8cec3809.summary: Amritsar, Bathinda and Faridkot in Punjab were among the five most polluted cities in India, according to real-time Air Quality Index (AQI) rankings. Amritsar recorded an AQI of 392, followed by Bathinda at 368 and Faridkot at 360. Meerut in Uttar Pradesh and Fatehpur rounded out the top five, with AQI readings of 355 and 354, respectively. Meanwhile, Delhi continued to record ‘poor’ air quality on Friday, with an AQI of 230. beb21fd12844965c.title: Kumaran Nagar bus terminus in Kolathur needs sprucing up
beb21fd12844965c.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription Additional Subscription Benefits Need help with your subscription? Updated - October 24, 2026 05:20 pm IST Kumaran Nagar bus terminus on October 20, 2026. This has turned the terminus slippery and flyblown, and it smells bad. Kumaran Nagar bus terminus in Kolathur is unhygienic with cow dung all over the place. Commuters say that the bus services operated from the terminus are very poor, and hence the terminus remains vacant for most of the day; also, commuters hardly wait here for the buses. So, all these have provided a conducive environment for cows to occupy the terminus. Alcohol bottles found at the terminus point to misuse of the terminus for consumption. It may be noted this terminus was redeveloped and inaugurated early this year but the facility fell into a state of neglect within a few weeks. The toilets are also unhygienic due to the erratic water supply. The room meant for lactating mothers is kept under lock-and-key. Further, there is no timekeeper here. Commuters are clueless when the next bus would arrive. Though there is a room dedicated for the timekeeper, it also remains locked. Services operated from the terminus need to be improved. There are buses only to Guindy and Anna Square. Further, the frequency is also very poor and not reliable. So commuters rely on share autorickshaws to access Paper Mills Road. From there, they go to the Retteri junction or the Perambur bus terminus or the Thiru Vi Ka Nagar terminus to access buses to other places. This is quite inconvenient. Where is the need to redevelop a bus terminus which receives poor patronage? N. 7ab5c6c7938a4e2b.title: Tree falls near school in Ashok Nagar; a lucky escape for students
7ab5c6c7938a4e2b.summary: Updated - October 25, 2026 02:25 am IST Sixth Avenue in Ashok Nagar following the rains in October 2026. Photo: special arrangement A tree near Sixth Avenue (near the entrance of GRT school) in Ashok Nagar fell on October 21. As luck would have it, it was a holiday for the school on account of the rains. This road comes under the purview of Ward 135 in Zone 10 (Kodambakkam). Earlier, on October 18, another tree had fallen, and this was on 86th Street in Ashok Nagar. In this incident, a bike was damaged. From time to time, a road is dug up several times for various works including stormwater drain construction, laying water pipes, sewage pipes and telecommunication cables. This could damage the roots of trees, and as a result, they get uprooted. Hence, the Parks Department of the Greater Chennai Corporation should take necessary measures without any delay and prevent the occurrence of untoward incidents. 1b57d91edcfdc6bd.title: BPCL Q2 profit falls 22.5% to ₹4,993 cr as fuel price freeze hits earnings
1b57d91edcfdc6bd.summary: State-owned Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) reported a 22.5 per cent fall in September quarter net profit as earnings from operations weakened due to a retail price freeze despite rising costs. BPCL's standalone net profit declined to Rs 4,993 crore in July-September, the second quarter of fiscal 2027, from Rs 6,443 crore a year earlier, according to a company statement. Revenue from operations rose to Rs 1.58 lakh crore from Rs 1.22 lakh crore, while Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) fell nearly 14 per cent to Rs 9,437 crore from Rs 10,968 crore. India's second largest fuel retailer earned USD 32.53 on turning every barrel of crude oil into fuels like petrol and diesel in July-September, as compared to USD 10.78 a barrel gross refining margin in the same period a year back. 1ca9ef8d9f92f32d.title: Ashoke Sen becomes first Indian physicist to win 2026 Oskar Klein Medal
1ca9ef8d9f92f32d.summary: Indian physicist Ashoke Sen has been awarded the 2026 Oskar Klein Medal, becoming the first Indian physicist to receive the honour. Sen, an ICTS-Infosys Madhava Chair professor at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences (ICTS)-Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), Bengaluru, is widely regarded as an architect of modern string theory. The theory postulates that the elementary constituents of matter are tiny one-dimensional, string-like objects instead of point particles. It thus tries to put forth a unifying description for matter and forces between them. Established in 1988 and named after the Swedish theoretical physicist Oskar Klein, the medal is awarded annually by Stockholm University and the Nobel Committee for Physics of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. Honouring the memory of Klein, the organising committee of the Oskar Klein Memorial Lectures every year invites a distinguished researcher to give a memorial lecture and to receive the Klein medal. 6c6127476d7dc231.title: JK Cement Q2FY27 result: Profit rises 6.3% to ₹169 cr; revenue jumps 23.7%
6c6127476d7dc231.summary: JK Cement Ltd on Saturday reported a 6.31 per cent increase in its consolidated net profit to Rs 169.3 crore for the September quarter of FY2026-27, helped by volume gains. The company had posted a net profit of Rs 159.25 crore in the July-September period a year ago, according to a regulatory filing from JK Cement Ltd (JKCL), the flagship company of JK Organisation Group. Its revenue from operations was up 23.65 per cent to Rs 3,733.42 crore in the September quarter of FY27 compared to Rs 3,019.20 crore in the year-ago period. The company reported "robust volume growth and higher profitability despite cost pressures," JKCL said in its Investor Presentation. Its grey cement sales volume rose 21 per cent to 5.37 million tonnes (MT) in the second quarter of FY27. Similarly, white cement volume was up 13 per cent to 0.49 MT. The lender had earned a net profit of Rs 561 crore in the year-ago period. Total income rose to Rs 6,382 crore in the quarter under review from Rs 5,224 crore in the same period a year ago, AU Small Finance Bank said in a regulatory filing. Interest income increased to Rs 5,612 crore as against Rs 4,511 crore in the corresponding second quarter of the previous year. Net interest income of the bank improved to Rs 2,820 crore in the July-September quarter, from Rs 2,144 crore in the September quarter of 2025, registering a growth of 32 per cent. Net interest margin increased to 5.8 per cent from 5.5 per cent at the end of September 2025. Asset quality of the bank also improved with gross non-performing assets (NPAs) rising to 1.99 per cent of gross advances at the end of the September quarter 2026

Updated - October 24, 2026 07:29 pm IST - HYDERABAD Senior BJP leader Gudur Narayana Reddy on Saturday proposed a three-point action plan to help Telangana address water, agricultural and power challenges arising from El Niño conditions, stressing the need for coordination among the government, experts, farmers and local communities. Mr. Reddy said the government’s focus on safeguarding drinking water supplies and preparing for difficult conditions in the coming months was appropriate. He said the emphasis should now be on translating policy directions into localised, measurable and publicly accessible action. He proposed setting up a small, time-bound technical cell comprising officials from the Irrigation, Groundwater and Agriculture departments, along with independent hydrologists and agronomists from agricultural universities, research institutions and ICAR institutes to coordinate measures and address emerging challenges. His second suggestion was to expedite community-level groundwater recharge and water conservation works in the most water-stressed mandals. Desilting tanks and check dams, developing farm ponds and creating percolation pits should be prioritised before peak summer, he said. As a third measure, Mr. Reddy proposed a public monitoring dashboard that tracks three key indicators: reservoir releases, the movement of drinking water tankers, and the number of hours of electricity supply to agricultural feeders. Updated - October 24, 2026 07:10 pm IST - MYSURU A new book titled ‘Who are the Kodavas (Coorgs)?’ written by journalist and author P.T. Bopanna has been launched. A statement by the author said the book, which decodes the mystery of the origin of the Kodavas, is based on the first genetic study of the community. The credit for providing these early scientific leads to the puzzle should go to Coorg-born Professor Buttiyanda Kuttapa Thelma, widely known as B.K. Thelma, whose team comprised scientists from the University of Delhi South Campus and the Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology, Hyderabad, the statement said. “The genetic study of Kodavas has not only attempted to resolve the question around the origin of Kodavas, but has also thrown insight into Indian population genetics, demonstrating that even small, tight-knit communities may harbour vast genetic complexities, shaped by centuries of migration, isolation and social customs,” the statement added. fcce9943226f9bd1.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:37 pm IST - PARVATIPURAM TDP leader and wife of TDP MLA Bonela Vijaya Chandra taking up door to door campaign in Parvatipuram. | Photo Credit: ARRANGEMENT Telugu Desam Party MLA Bonela Vijaya Chandra on Saturday (October 24, 2026) said that Parvatipuram municipality has been witnessing rapid growth as the State government has sanctioned around ₹162 crore for the development of the civic body, which was established in 1959 and is one of the oldest in the State. Along with TDP leader and his wife, Bonela Anusha, he campaigned for TDP’s candidate for the chairperson post, Belagam Karuna, and for councillors in 36 wards. Speaking to the media, he said that voters are keen to vote for the TDP, JSP, and BJP in the ensuing elections, as the government has taken steps to lay new pipelines from the Thotapalli reservoir to the city, since the old pipes were damaged long ago. He stated that the government has been spending around ₹89 crore on new pipelines and has ensured dedicated water supply to every household in Parvatipuram. Ms. Anusha said there was an overwhelming response from voters to the quick developmental activities in nook and corner of the town. She alleged that the YSRCP government had neglected the town’s development during its tenure. She added that the TDP women’s wing formed special teams to intensify a door-to-door campaign in the next few days. Rajagopal Birdwatching enthusiasts in and around Tiruchi have reported a steady inflow of migratory birds from late September to the region, with their flight schedules possibly affected by the absence of summer rain and the ongoing northeast monsoon in Tamil Nadu this year. “Due to the prolonged hot weather this year, fewer migratory birds were spotted near Tiruchi’s water bodies in late September compared to 2025. RAGU Hockey Karnataka fought back from a two-goal deficit to hold Punjab National Bank (PNB) to a 2-2 draw in a Pool-A match of the 97th All-India MCC-Murugappa Gold Cup hockey tournament at the SDAT Mayor Radhakrishnan Stadium here on Saturday. PNB dominated with its raids in the first half, but Karnataka showed greater purpose after the break to claw its way back into the contest. Neeraj put PNB ahead in the 14th minute with an impressive individual effort. Winning the ball from an opponent near the left sideline, he beat and dribbled past two Karnataka players and closed in on goal before slotting the ball past goalkeeper K.K. Tharun Ganapathy. Gursimran Singh doubled PNB’s lead in the 16th minute, converting a penalty corner with a drag-flick. Though Tharun intercepted the effort, he could not keep it out. Karnataka began its recovery in the 32nd minute through a well-coordinated move. Maji Ganesh found Bhrath Mahalingappa Kurtakot, who directed the ball for C.J. Rahul to finish. G. Vishwas completed Karnataka’s comeback in the 52nd minute. The side had chances to snatch victory, winning two penalty corners in the final three minutes, but failed to convert either. The results: Pool-A: Punjab National Bank 2 (Neeraj 14, Gursimran Singh 16-pc) drew with Hockey Karnataka 2 (C.J. Rahul 32, G. Vishwas 52). Pool-B: Indian Navy 5 (Rajat Sharma 15, Ashis Topno 35-pc, Nitesh 38, Sundra Pandi 58, K. Selvaraj 60) bt SAI-NCOE Bhopal 2 (Mohammed Zaid Khan 26, Bhrat Kaushik 59). Updated - October 24, 2026 07:40 pm IST - TIRUCHI The National Platform for Domestic Workers (NPDW) has urged the government to regulate the domestic service sector and provide better working conditions for its employees. At a press meet held here on Saturday, P. Clarammal, State coordinator, Tamil Nadu Domestic Workers Association, said that women formed a large section of the household service sector and they often had to work in unsafe conditions. “We urge the government to formulate laws that will ensure the personal safety of domestic workers and prevent exploitation by employers,” she said. The body focused on the enactment of comprehensive central legislation for domestic workers, and the ratification of the International Labour Organisation’s C.189 (Decent Work for Domestic Workers) convention by the Union government. The inclusion of domestic workers in the draft labour legislation proposed by the Union government in 2020 was also mooted. The body also urged the constitution of a trilateral labour board in every State to settle issues faced by the sector. Domestic workers should also be able to enrol in schemes such as the Employees’ State Insurance (ESI) and Provident Fund, and a minimum salary of ₹5,000 should be made mandatory for them, it said and suggested paid leave of three months for those availing maternity and ESI leave. Meeshapulimala, one of the Munnar region’s highest peaks, is witnessing the blooming of Neelakurinji and will open to tourists starting Monday (October 26). The peak falls under the jurisdiction of the Kerala Forest Development Corporation (KFDC) in Munnar. KFDC Munnar Manager Akhil Das said visitors will have the opportunity to view the blooms at higher elevations. “The KFDC has arranged multi-utility vehicles (MUVs) for the 30-kilometre journey from Munnar to Meeshapulimala at a fare of ₹1,250 per person. Tourists will be picked up from the Munnar KFDC office and transported in these specially arranged vehicles. The package includes a snack box and drinking water,” he said. KFDC District Manager Sujith P.K. stated that the corporation, in association with the Wildlife Trust of India (WTI), has launched the ‘Kurinji’ mobile application for online bookings. Visitors can reserve slots and make payments directly through the app. “The key attraction at Meeshapulimala is the Neelakurinji bloom alongside sightings of the endangered Nilgiri tahr. KFDC plans to provide a unique ecotourism experience here,” Mr. Sujith said. Officials added that the Kurinji mobile app lets users easily find locations and other travel details. Updated - October 24, 2026 07:41 pm IST - KOCHI Image for representational purpose After grappling with a rise in influenza cases for months, Ernakulam has reported relatively fewer cases in October. According to the health authorities, influenza activity may be declining even as the district braces for monsoon-related diseases such as dengue and leptospirosis. A health official said the dip in influenza cases was expected. “Influenza is a seasonal outbreak, and the disease is in the declining phase now. But with intermittent rains, we are expecting an increase in dengue cases. We have to intensify precautionary measures against dengue and other monsoon-related communicable diseases. This can be done by focussing on source-reduction activities, which need to be strengthened,” the official said. A total of 335 influenza cases were reported until October 23, according to the Health department. The district registered a total of 588 dengue cases during the month, including 168 confirmed and 420 suspected cases. It also reported 31 cases of leptospirosis, including 24 confirmed and seven suspected cases, and two deaths due to the disease. Updated - October 24, 2026 07:10 pm IST - TIRUCHI The condition of several roads in Tiruchi has turned from bad to worse after the recent spell of rain. | Photo Credit: M. MOORTHY The current spell of rain over the past few days has battered many key roads in the city, causing hardship to commuters and motorists. Since the onset of the northeast monsoon on October 15, Tiruchi has been getting rainfall. The rainfall was not heavy in the city up to Thursday and it received only light showers. However, it received heavy rain in different parts on Friday.The continuous rainfall has damaged many arterial roads and interior roads. Uneven road surfaces and potholes have become common sights on major stretches, with the top layer eroded in many places. The damaged patches have led to frequent skidding incidents, particularly affecting two-wheeler riders. Anna Nagar roads, Karur bypass, old Madurai road, West Boulevard Road, Major Saravanan Road and important stretches around the Central Bus Stand, such as Rockins Road, McDonalds Road, VOC Road, and Williams Road, have suffered significant deterioration. Similarly, stretches around the Chathiram Bus Stand were also damaged. Similar issues have cropped up around the Gandhi Market, Palakarai, Varaganeri and others. With heavy vehicle movement continuing through these roads, the loose surface material has begun to dislodge, worsening driving conditions. Recently patched up roads too have also suffered the damage. Motorists say the situation has grown increasingly unsafe, especially during nighttime travel. “We encounter many deep potholes and eroded stretches on the city roads. A total of 212 Domestic Breeding Checkers (DBC) have been engaged in door-to-door inspections across 60 wards of the corporation to identify mosquito larvae in water storage tanks, drums, flower pots, coconut shells, discarded tyres and other potential breeding sites. Larvicides are being applied and mosquito control activities are being carried out to prevent mosquito breeding. Fogging operations are also being carried out across all wards using four vehicle mounted fogging machines and 20 handheld pulse fogging machines to control mosquito population. a7a625e6948fe0cc.title: TN coach Murray wants the players to develop a cohesive style of play
a7a625e6948fe0cc.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription Additional Subscription Benefits Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 07:18 pm IST - CHENNAI William Murray. | Photo Credit: R. RAGU William Murray, Hockey Unit of Tamil Nadu’s (HUTN) high-performance coach, wants the State team to be more than just a winning unit. The Englishman, who joined the Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu (SDAT) in May on a two-year contract, wants his players to develop an exciting, cohesive style of hockey that draws crowds. An FIH coach educator, Murray first came to India this year to conduct Level 3 coaching courses for Hockey India (HI) in Rourkela and Hyderabad before taking up the role of coaching the Tamil Nadu men’s team. He has worked in Hong Kong and Belgium, and coached England’s u-18 and Scotland’s u-21 teams. Murray believes the lack of early exposure to artificial turf has influenced Indian players’ technical and tactical development. “Too often, it’s very individualised here. Even things like pushing (push pass), since it’s not done in the same way on gravel, grass, or dirt pitches, there’s a desire to get the ball off the floor as much as possible. Whereas on astro, you want the ball on the floor, where it moves quickly but smoothly. That allows the whole team to stay connected up the pitch and work together. “I’m trying to implement some quite rigorous tactical concepts, which will take time. I want us to be exciting - to play fast, with style and swagger, but also in a connected way,” he said. The coach is also keen to strengthen the State’s hockey pipeline. “More than just focusing on one team, for me it’s about making sure the whole ecosystem is rich, so that any young player, whatever their background, if they’re good enough, gets the opportunity and understanding to be nurtured and grow to their potential,” he said. Updated - October 24, 2026 07:08 pm IST - Hyderabad Researchers found traces of West Eurasian and Steppe-linked maternal lineages among some Konkani-speaking communities, offering fresh insights into the region’s complex population history. | Photo Credit: Jaison Sequeira Ancient migrations into South Asia may have involved women as well as men, according to a new genetic study of Konkani-speaking communities along India’s west coast. Comparisons with ancient DNA suggested that prehistoric migrations into South Asia were more complex than previously understood. Researchers from the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB), Hyderabad, and Mangalore University found traces of West Eurasian and Steppe-linked maternal lineages among some groups, offering fresh insights into the region’s complex population history. The findings of the study led by CCMB’s K. Thangaraj and Mangalore University's M.S. Mustak challenge the notion that Bronze Age migrations into the subcontinent were driven predominantly by males. The Konkan region, stretching from Daman in the north to the Gangavalli River and Karwar in the south, is known for its rich cultural, linguistic and social diversity. Although Konkani is spoken across the region, its speakers belong to several communities with distinct histories and traditions. The population was broadly classified into Sarasvata and non-Sarasvata groups, based on oral traditions regarding ancestry linked to the ancient Sarasvati region. Published - October 24, 2026 07:29 pm IST - SIVAGANAGA In view of upcoming memorial observances, District Collector P. Akash has announced holidays for schools and colleges across seven unions in the Sivaganga district on October 27 and 30, alongside temporary closures for the district’s prominent archaeological site. The closure on October 27 marks the memorial day of Marudu Pandiyar brothers, which is observed in Kalaiyarkovil. Following this, schools and colleges will shut down again on October 30 for the birth anniversary and memorial day of freedom fighter and leader Muthuramalinga Thevar, a major annual event held at Pasumpon in the neighbouring Ramanathapuram district. The holiday directives apply to all schools and colleges situated within seven designated unions: Sivaganga, Devakottai, Tirupattur, Thiruppuvanam, Manamadurai, Kalaiyarkovil, and Ilayangudi. Additionally, as part of the safety and crowd management measures surrounding the Pasumpon Thevar Jayanthi celebrations, the district administration has announced a two-day closure for the Keeladi Site Museum in Sivaganga district, which will stay shut for visitors on October 29 and 30. Updated - October 24, 2026 07:15 pm IST - COIMBATORE During the National Management Week 2026, around 250 students of PSG Institute of Management (PSGIM), Coimbatore, will take management learning beyond the classroom and into the community through initiatives focusing on waste management, rabies awareness, and preventing pollution caused by indiscriminate poster pasting, under the overarching theme of ‘Clean and Safe City’. Observed from October 26 to 31 under the aegis of the Association of Indian Management Schools (AIMS-New Delhi), the initiatives reflect a simple yet meaningful belief: building a better city is a shared responsibility. During the week, students will engage with communities at more than 30 identified waste hotspots across Coimbatore. By promoting waste segregation at source and responsible disposal, they will encourage everyday practices that protect the environment and improve neighbourhoods for everyone. The initiative will also highlight the connection between unmanaged waste and street dogs. Discarded food and other waste can attract dogs to public spaces, increase the risk of conflict and create unhealthy conditions for people and animals. Students will also conduct rabies awareness activities across 30 identified locations in the city in association with the Humane Animal Society (HAS), to promote rabies prevention, safe interactions with street dogs and humane animal care. These activities will reinforce the importance of keeping public spaces free of food waste and other refuse that can attract dogs. The epicentre, at a depth of 10 kilometres, was monitored at 32.54 degrees north latitude and 93.97 degrees east longitude, the centre said. There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage from Saturday's earthquake. The fragile Tibetan Plateau is prone to powerful earthquakes as it lies in a region where the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates collide, generating significant seismic activity. c552bb9e3da8e7a4.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 07:56 pm IST Union Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh. File | Photo Credit: PTI The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) has extended the tenure of Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh by one year, until October 31, 2027. Also read | Defence Secretary holds key meetings at Shangri-La Dialogue 2026, pushes for Indo-Pacific security cooperation His current tenure was scheduled to end on October 31, 2026. Mr. Singh will now serve in the role until October 31, 2027, or until further orders, whichever comes first, in relaxation of FR 65(d) and Rule 16 (1A) of the All India Service (Death-Cum-Retirement Benefits) Rules, 1958, the Centre said on Saturday (October 24, 2026). Mr. Singh took over as Defence Secretary at South Block on November 1, 2024 . He took over from Giridhar Aramane, a 1988-batch IAS officer of Andhra Pradesh cadre, who had retired from service October 31, 2024 after a two year stint. He is a 1989-batch IAS officer from the Kerala cadre and assumed the charge of the Officer on Special Duty (Defence Secretary-designate) on August 20, 2024. Updated - October 24, 2026 08:07 pm IST - MYSURU The Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary | Photo Credit: File Photo A network of human rights organisations will conduct a fact-finding mission into the fatal shooting of three persons in the Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary in Hanur taluk of Chamarajanagar district that took place in the early hours of August 20. The two-day high-level fact-finding mission, scheduled for Monday and Tuesday, October 26 and 27, will be jointly led by former Solapur Commissioner Harish Mangalal Baijal, IPS, and retired Karnataka Forest Service officer Raju, a former IFS officer. Representatives of several human rights organisations will be part of the mission. In a press statement, People’s Watch executive director Henri Tiphagne said three farmers were killed, and another person was injured in the shooting involving Karnataka Forest Department personnel. Identifying the deceased as Anthony Sami, John Rose Peter and Kumar, alias Savariyappan, the statement said the fourth person, Mahimai Das, was reportedly injured and subsequently taken to a hospital. The Forest Department has reportedly maintained that the four men had illegally entered the forest to hunt wildlife and were carrying weapons. According to the department’s account, the men had attempted to fire at forest personnel, who returned fire in self-defence. However, family members of the deceased and others associated with them have disputed this account. They maintained that the men were farmers who entered the forest in connection with their livestock, not to hunt wildlife, the statement said. The incident, therefore, should not be viewed merely as a confrontation between forest personnel and alleged hunters, the statement said. Published - October 24, 2026 08:09 pm IST - Hyderabad Women lighting a lamp during the fourth Bathukamma & Dasara celebrations at Studio Center in Detroit, United States. The spirit of Telangana didn’t just travel to Michigan, it bloomed there. The Global Telangana Association (GTA) Detroit Chapter hosted its fourth Bathukamma & Dasara celebrations at the Studio Center with around 1,800 members of the Telugu diaspora gathering for a vibrant display of culture, devotion, and belonging. The venue transformed into a riot of colours as women and young girls arrived adorned in beautiful silk sarees and traditional langa vonis . But the true centerpiece was hundreds of intricately arranged Bathukamma flower mounds, brought by attendees as offerings to Goddess Gowri and mother nature. The air resonated with devotional songs as participants danced in circles around the floral stacks, their synchronized claps and movements creating a mesmerizing spectacle. The festivities opened on a spiritual note with a traditional Shami pooja conducted by the local temple priest. The GTA Detroit executive committee left no stone unturned in crafting a holistic community experience. A , specially prepared by local Indian restaurant Aha Biryani, was served to all the attendees. Prominent leaders from various Indian communities, including the Michigan Republican Party Treasurer, Sunny Reddy, graced the occasion. 8cd49f4ce03e2111.title: Malabar Devaswom Board orders eviction of convention centre from temple land
8cd49f4ce03e2111.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 07:59 pm IST - PALAKKAD Malabar Devaswom Board has ordered steps to evict Club-6, a partnership firm that operates a convention centre on 77.90 ares of temple land at Puthur, Palakkad, after declaring its 30-year lease invalid. In an order dated September 8, Devaswom Commissioner T.C. Biju rejected a request to retrospectively approve the lease, which was executed in 2017 without the prior sanction required under Section 29 of the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Act, 1951. The Commissioner directed the deputy commissioner to appoint a person to oversee the temple’s administration and expedite eviction proceedings. The order said the president of Ramanathapuram Grama Devaswom Society, which executed the lease, had failed to establish his legal authority to lease the property belonging to Ramanathapuram Devaswom. The society’s registration under the Societies Registration Act in 2022 did not confer the powers of a trustee under the HR&CE Act. The lease was granted to Club-6 for 30 years. The society’s president later sought retrospective approval, arguing that the arrangement was intended to generate income for the temple. The Commissioner rejected the plea, holding that the required sanction had to be obtained before the lease was executed and that the law did not permit the retrospective approval sought. The order also questioned the handling of rent payments. Records showed payments only from 2022, despite the lease having begun in 2017. The rent was deposited into accounts held in the society’s name, and the evidence did not establish that the proceeds had been properly accounted for by the legally authorised temple administration. Updated - October 24, 2026 07:56 pm IST Students and teachers accord a reception to the Chief Minister’s Gold Cup, to be presented to the winners of the State School Sports Meet, at Government Model Girls Higher Secondary School in Thrissur on Saturday. | Photo Credit: K. K. NAJEEB The Chief Minister’s Gold Cup, the coveted trophy for the 68th State School Sports Meet, received an enthusiastic welcome at Government Model Girls Higher Secondary School in Thrissur on Saturday, ahead of the sporting extravaganza scheduled to begin in Kozhikode district on October 25. Weighing 117.5 sovereigns of gold, the trophy was received at the school entrance by elected representatives, education officials, teachers and student groups amid the accompaniment of a band troupe. The reception was organised under the leadership of the Thrissur Education District. MLAs, K. Rajan and Rajan J. Pallan, Thrissur Mayor Dr. Niji Justin, District Panchayat president Mary Thomas, Deputy Director of Education T. Shyla and District Educational Officer Ajith John were among those who welcomed the trophy. The public representatives expressed hope that Thrissur would bring the prestigious cup back to the district through outstanding performances by its young athletes at the State School Sports Meet. The reception was followed by a procession that began at Government Model Girls Higher Secondary School, with students, public representatives, officials and representatives of various organisations joining the celebrations. The procession showcased the enthusiasm and team spirit of the school community, with around 300 students participating in the event. The band troupe of Holy Family School led the musical accompaniment, while student contingents from several educational institutions added colour and energy to the march. Updated - October 24, 2026 08:11 pm IST - Paris, France Protesters march along the Avenue Jean Zay during a demonstration "against racism, fascism and imperialism" on October 24, 2026 | Photo Credit: AFP French police fired tear gas on Saturday (October 24, 2026) to prevent protesters in several cities from advancing to the centres, in fresh nationwide demonstrations held a week after riots broke out, AFP journalists saw. Riot squads fired tear gas at protesters in Lyon, Lille, Toulouse and Nantes, hours after Interior Minister Laurent Nunez warned: “We will not tolerate any violence or any disturbance of public order.” “The police are really mobile... They come and disperse marches before they even form,” said a 21-year-old student who had turned up to protest, speaking on condition of anonymity. Elsewhere, authorities and rattled shopkeepers geared up for potential new street violence. Near Paris’s Bastille neighbourhood, a clothing store had removed all its merchandise from shelves ahead of the demonstrations, while a nearby restaurant was boarded up with signs insisting it was “still open”. Many other retailers in the capital also had wooden boards covering their windows. The Louvre and the Musee d’Orsay museums were closed. The capital’s police said at midday officers had confiscated “various forbidden items” but described the situation as “calm”. They distributed sweets during the farmers grievance redress meeting held at the Dindigul Collectorate on Friday. At the meeting presided over by Dindigul Collector Durgamoorthi, the farmers said residents of Kalanjipatti and Veriyappur were affected by the stone quarry operations. They demanded that the licence should be cancelled. A section of farmers complained that sewage had accumulated in a pond at Avilipatti. They also complained that the inlet channel leading to the Thattankulam tank and the supply channel leading to the Nagayakottai tank had been encroached upon. The Collector said steps would be taken to provide proper drainage facilities in Avilipatti and the encroachments would be removed. Collector Durgamoorthi presiding over the farmers redressal meeting held at Dindigul Collectorate on Friday. | Photo Credit: KARTHIKEYAN G Farmers said coconut trees in Guziliamparai area had withered and dried up. They urged the authorities to conduct a survey and provide adequate compensation to the farmers. A section of farmers demanded that a survey be conducted across the district and adequate compensation be paid to affected farmers. The Collector assured the farmers that steps would be taken to conduct a survey in this regard. Farmers complained that the road from Natham to the foothills of Sirumalai was severely damaged. Though several petitions were submitted in this regard, no action taken by the authorities. Farmers who surrendered their lands for the bypass road project should be compensated properly, they said. The Collector said steps would be taken to ensure that the road repair work was carried out expeditiously and proper compensation would be provided to the farmers. Pu

Ravi Singh, Railways’ hard-hitting willow-wielder, is quite new to the rigours of First Class cricket. The 25-year-old — who has a penchant for striking big in the shorter formats — hasn’t taken long to adjust to the longest discipline, averaging a creditable 58.2 after seven Ranji Trophy innings. Ravi, who works as a ticket collector in Howrah, had to bide his time before finding his place in the Railways team. He shifted from Varanasi to Lucknow to hone his skills under coach Saurabh Dubey, though he couldn’t quite break into the senior Uttar Pradesh set-up. But once he landed a Railways job, Ravi’s career finally stoked some steam. “After playing well for the under-23 side, I was called to the National Cricket Academy [now Centre of Excellence]. The Syed Mushtaq Ali and Vijay Hazare tournaments went quite well for me. Some of those matches were broadcast and the selectors at a higher level watched them. I was called for IPL trials, and, after seven or eight years of not playing anything [significant], things suddenly started falling my way,” Ravi said at the MAC Stadium on Saturday, two days ahead of the Ranji game against Tamil Nadu. Ravi was picked up by Rajasthan Royals for ₹95 lakh in the IPL 2026 auction. Eminent musicians from across the country will perform in the week-long festival, said secretary P.N. Subharaman. Dinesh The scary scenes during the Dasara celebrations in Shivamogga on Thursday, October 22, were allegedly triggered by a last-minute change in the order of the elephants in the procession. Forest officials and mahouts had resolved that Sagar, the tusker that carried the howdah in previous years, would lead the group of three elephants. Somanna, the elephant chosen to carry the howdah this time, was participating in the procession for the first time and had hardly been exposed to crowds. However, after the procession had covered about 500 metres, the order was changed. Somanna was brought to the front, suddenly exposing it to the crowd, while the other two elephants were left behind. Within a short distance, it lost its composure and turned back. Deputy Conservator of Forests Prasanna Krishna Patagar, speaking to a news portal over the phone, said the order of the elephants was changed on the instructions of an MLA. A video clip of the procession also shows the MLA speaking to the DCF, after which the order was altered within minutes. However, at a press meet, Minister Madhu Bangarappa maintained that in previous years too, the elephant carrying the howdah had led the group, and the same practice was followed this year. He said he was not aware whether the order was changed at the MLA’s instructions. Chief Conservator of Forests of the Shivamogga Circle K.T. Hanumanthappa, who submitted a preliminary report on the incidents to the PCCF (Wildlife), has recorded the sequence of events. a89ead5d48e84b19.title: Food production unit raided at Kadri, unhygienic products seized
a89ead5d48e84b19.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Published - October 24, 2026 07:47 pm IST - MANGALURU Officials raided Kudpi's Foods located near Kadri Manjunatha Temple in the city on Saturday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Food safety officials raided ‘Kudpi’s Foods’ located near the Kadri Manjunatha Temple in the city on Saturday and seized and sealed food products found in an unhygienic condition. A notice was issued to the unit due to lack of hygiene, an official release said. Halwa and date-based products were seized, sealed, and sent for laboratory testing, it said. The establishment was instructed to implement all measures when preparing food products, especially those intended for the festive season. It was directed to take appropriate steps to prevent risk of food poisoning, repair the drainage system, and ensure that pests, cockroaches, and rats cannot enter the production unit. The unit was instructed to undergo thorough cleaning before resuming the preparation of any food products. The raid was carried out by a team led by C. H. Praveen Kumar, district designated officer for food safety, acting under the instructions of Health and Familay Welfare Minister U. T. Khader, the release added. Published - October 24, 2026 08:31 pm IST - HUBBALLI The special drive against use of manja launched by the Hubballi Dharwad Police Commissionerate continued on Saturday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT The special drive against use of manja launched by the Hubballi Dharwad Police Commissionerate continued on Saturday with more cases being booked taking the total number of cases booked to 16. A day after a 38-year old woman was killed after manja (abrasive kite string) slit her throat in Hubballi, the Police Commissionerate had launched the special drive on Friday. According to the Hubballi Dharwad Police Commissioner, during the special drive, 124 places were inspected and 69 locations where manja was being used were checked. The police had so far removed dangerously hanging manja strings at 63 locations and checked 67 shops where manja was being reportedly sold. While 11 cases including those against sellers, users, and also a parent for allowing a kid to use the abrasive string to fly kite were booked on Friday, five more cases were booked in Bendigeri, Old Hubballi, APMC Navanagar, and Kasabapet police stations on Saturday. On Thursday, lab technician Vidya Manjunath Goudar was killed after the abrasive kite string got entangled around her neck, slitting her throat, while she was riding a two-wheeler. The incident led to backlash and various leaders, including Pralhad Joshi, Basavaraj Horatti, Prasad Abbayya and others, calling for strict action against the sale and use of manja. e2e6617ead524a35.title: Puducherry CEO holds meeting with representatives of political parties on Special Summary Revision
e2e6617ead524a35.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 08:33 pm IST - PUDUCHERRY Chief Electoral Officer A.S.P.S. Ravi Prakash held a meeting with representatives of six recognised political parties in Puducherry on Saturday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Chief Electoral Officer A.S.P.S. Ravi Prakash held a meeting with representatives of six recognised political parties in Puducherry to brief them on the Special Summary Revision (SSR) exercise being undertaken in the Union Territory. The Election Commission of India has directed the Election Department to undertake the SSR of the photo electoral roll in the Union Territory. The representatives of political parties were informed about the procedural aspects involved in the conduct of the SSR. The instructions given by the ECI were passed on to the representatives of political parties at the meeting held on Friday. The CEO sought the cooperation of all parties in ensuring the smooth conduct of the revision process, a release here said. “During the meeting, the CEO explained the important legal provisions and procedural aspects of the SSR, with particular emphasis on the instructions given by the Election Commission. The CEO also clarified and addressed the concerns raised by the representatives of political parties,” the release said. Deputy Chief Electoral officers B. Thillaivel and M. Kandasamy were present.
