555d80f878d4d30a.title: Anniversary of Mysore Chalo observed in city
555d80f878d4d30a.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Updated - October 24, 2026 08:28 pm IST - MYSURU The Mysore Chalo movement, which began on September 1, 1947, played a significant role in the freedom of the Princely State of Mysuru. | Photo Credit: M.A. Sriram The Mysuru District and City Freedom Fighters’ Association commemorated the 80th anniversary of the Mysore Chalo movement at the Freedom Fighters’ Park in Subbarayana Kere on Saturday. Members of the Freedom Fighters’ Association garlanded the statue of Mahatma Gandhi at 10.30 a.m. They later took out a march to Ramaswamy Circle and paid a floral tribute at the memorial of Ramaswamy, who sacrificed his life on September 13, 1947, for the freedom of Mysuru. The Mysore Chalo movement, which began on September 1, 1947, played a significant role in the freedom of the Princely State of Mysuru. While India attained Independence on August 15, 1947, Mysuru hoisted the national flag for the first time on October 24, 1947, marking the beginning of the Independence era. While speaking on the occasion, Yogananda, Working president of the Freedom Fighters’ Association, said, “On October 24, 1947, Jayachamarajendra Wadiyar, the then ruler of the Mysuru State, announced the merger of the Princely State into the Indian Union and declared Independence.” Association Secretary Ravi, Pandith Aradya and others were present on the occasion. 6856c2e295feacf9.title: Maruthu brothers remembered on memorial day
6856c2e295feacf9.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 08:24 pm IST - SIVAGANGA RAMANATHAPURAM: TAMIL NADU: 24 October 2026: Tamil Nadu Ministers paying floral tributes at Maruthu Pandiyar brothers memorial in Tirupattur in Sivaganga district on Saturday. Photo: handout_e_mail / The Hindu. | Photo Credit: HANDOUT_E_MAIL Marking the 225th death anniversary of Maruthu Pandiyar brothers, leaders from various political parties garlanded the statues at the manimandapam in Tirupattur in Sivaganga district on Saturday. The memorial day of the Maruthu Pandiyar brothers was observed as a government event at the manimandapam in Tirupattur, Sivaganga district. District Collector P. Akash hoisted the national flag and garlanded the statues of the Maruthu brothers. District Superintendent of Police Abhishek Gupta, District Revenue Officer Sailendran, and others participated. Minister for Energy Resources and Law C. T. R. Nirmal Kumar, Minister for Natural Resources T. K. Prabhu, Minister for Labour Welfare and Skill Development J. Mohamed Farvas and Minister for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises P. Mathan Raja, paid their respects at the venue. On behalf of DMK, former ministers K. R. Periyakaruppan, R. S. Rajakannappan, T. R. B. Rajaa, MLA Muthuraja, former MLA Tamilarasi, and Town Panchayat President Sengaimaran paid their respects. On behalf of AIADMK, former ministers Dindigul C. Srinivasan, Sellur K. Raju, Gokula Indira, Kamaraj, Manikandan, and former MLAs Rajan Chellappa and Senthilnathan paid their respects. MDMK General Secretary Vaiko, AMMK General Secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran, BJP District Secretary Pandithurai, Congress National Secretary Mayura Jayakumar, former MLAs Mangudi, among others paid their respects. CPI(M) District Secretary Mohan, Communist Party of India former MLA Gunasekaran, also paid their respects. Published - October 24, 2026 08:24 pm IST

Swaroopa on Friday instructed officials concerned to expedite the process, including land acquisition, of establishing four industrial areas in Udupi district. She was speaking while presiding over the District-Level Single Window Committee meeting and the ‘Kaigarika Spandana Samiti’ (Industrial Response Committee) meeting at her office. Chandeesh and other officials at the Muthuramalinga Thevar memorial ahead of Thevar Jayanthi in Ramanathapuram on Saturday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement A total of 480 high-definition cameras, mobile CCTV cameras and specialised drones would be deployed for real-time monitoring in and around Pasumpon in Ramanathapuram district through a Centralised Control Room. The Director General of Police (Head of Police Force) Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal, who visited the Pasumpon village on Saturday, took stock of the preparedness of the police force for the Thevar Jayanthi scheduled to be held on October 30. According to a press release, the camera systems are equipped with facial recognition and number plate recognition capabilities to strengthen surveillance and facilitate the timely identification of persons and vehicles, wherever required. Over 460 police patrol vehicles and quick reaction teams ( QRTs ) would be deployed for bandobust duties during the Jayanthi. The DGP inspected the commemoration venue, reviewed the preparations and interacted with the organisers to assess the arrangements and discussed operational requirements. Later, a review meeting was held at Kamuthi in which ADGP (Law and Order) T. S. Anbu Tamil Nadu, Inspector General of Police, (South Zone) Vijayendra Bidari, Commissioner of Police, Madurai City, S. Rajendiran, DIGs of Police, Abhinav Kumar (Madurai Range) and Manivannan (Ramanathapuram Range) and Superintendents of Police G. Chandeesh (Ramanathapuram), Abishek Gupta (Sivaganga), Gautam Goyal (Virudhunagar), R. Shivaprasad (Thoothukudi) and Devanathan (Madurai) attended. The security would comprise seven DIGs of Police, 40 SPs and over 18,000 police

f5ed28e5f787aba0.title: APEPDCL puts 12 coastal districts on high alert for Cyclone Arnab
f5ed28e5f787aba0.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 08:15 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited (APEPDCL) Chairman and Managing Director Immadi Prudhvitej on Saturday (October 24, 2026) instructed field officials across 12 coastal districts to maintain maximum operational readiness following IMD warnings of ‘Cyclone Arnab’ expected between October 26 and 28. Chairing a teleconference with Superintending Engineers and Executive Engineers, the CMD ordered division-wise control rooms to be set up in Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Kakinada, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari, Eluru, and Polavaram. To ensure uninterrupted power supply to critical services, field teams have been mobilised with emergency vehicles, replacement transformers, electric poles, and clearing equipment for immediate damage restoration. The distribution utility’s corporate headquarters will monitor grid stability around the clock. Consumers have been cautioned to avoid fallen electrical wires, damaged poles, and uprooted trees, and to report power disruptions through the toll-free helpline 1912 or district control rooms. 5748a86141fe1bbf.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 08:27 pm IST - TIRUNELVELI Tirunelveli district monitoring officer Sandeep Nanduri inspects the drainage desilting work in Tirunelveli Town on Saturday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Tirunelveli district monitoring officer Sandeep Nanduri reviewed the precautionary measures taken in the district to tackle the Northeast monsoon in the presence of Collector Anand Mohan on Saturday. During the the review meeting, Mr. Nanduri said that with the onset of monsoon and widespread rainfall in the district, the district administration has taken immediate precautionary measures to tackle the situation of heavy rain and flooding. He added that areas vulnerable to heavy rains had been identified and were being closely monitored, with necessary precautionary measures in place. More than 5,466 volunteers are ready to assist in rescue operations, he noted. Mr. Nanduri further said that seven relief centres had been kept ready to provide safe shelter to people in the event of heavy rain. Similarly, buildings such as schools and marriage halls had also been identified and kept ready to set up as relief centres, depending on the situation. He stressed that essential facilities including drinking water, medical facilities, food and generators are available to the public in these centres without any hindrance. He also emphasised the need to create awareness among farmers about precautionary measures to protect crops from damage caused by heavy rains. In case of crop damage due to disaster situations, the concerned officials should be prepared to immediately assess the damage and take appropriate measures to provide relief to affected farmers, Mr. Nanduri said. Subsequently Mr. Nanduri inspected Kallanai Street, Nedungulam, Kandiyaperi and other locations to review the precautionary measures in place to combat the mons

a7b5a5be05d9f25f.title: TDB to set up food safety laboratory at Pampa for evaluation of FSSAI parameters in production of prasadam
a7b5a5be05d9f25f.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 08:22 pm IST - KOCHI The Travancore Devaswom Board recently informed the Kerala High Court that a laboratory would be set up at Pampa for evaluation of prasadam as per Food Safety and Standards Authority of India parameters, including testing for pesticides and toxin levels, before the start of Sabarimala pilgrimage season. The Division Bench of Justices Raja Vijayaraghavan and K.V. Jayakumar was informed that the Food Safety department would identify requirements and prepare a time-bound implementation plan. A decision was also taken to obtain National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories accreditation simultaneously, the Board stated. Currently, the samples are sent to a laboratory in Thiruvananthapuram for evaluation. The Food Safety department had apprised the Board that the equipment for the laboratory would cost around ₹2 crore to ₹3 crore and the laboratory would require an air-conditioned space of about 1000 sq. ft.; these requirements were affirmed by the Board. The department also agreed to arrange qualified personnel to operate the equipment and conduct the tests. It would examine the possibility of deploying two existing, duly appointed food safety officers for statutory inspection and sampling at Sabarimala. Published - October 24, 2026 08:33 pm IST - KOTTAYAM Aroma Chundan, rowed by the Aroma Boat Club, crosses the finish line in the final of the Thazhathangady Boat Race, part of the Champions Boat League, in Kottayam on Saturday. | Photo Credit: VISHNU PRATHAP Aroma Chundan, rowed by the Aroma Boat Club of Paravur in Kollam, raced to victory in the Thazhathangady Boat Race, the Kottayam leg of the Champions Boat League (CBL). Aroma Chundan crossed the finish line in 3 minutes and 21.227 seconds to win the title. Melpadam Chundan, rowed by Pallathuruthy Boat Club, finished second in 3 minutes and 21.802 seconds, followed by Niranam Chundan of Niranam Boat Club in 3 minutes and 21.925 seconds. Veeyapuram, Cheruthana, Arppookara, Punyalan Niranam, Nadubhagam and Thalavady finished fourth to ninth, respectively. In the smaller boat categories, Puthenparambil won in the Iruttukuthi B-grade event, Champion clinched the Veppu B-grade title, Moozhi won in the Churulan category and Munnuthaikkal emerged victorious in the Iruttukuthi A-grade event. Aroma Boat Club will receive ₹5 lakh in prize money for the victory, while Pallathuruthy Boat Club and Niranam Boat Club will receive ₹3 lakh and ₹1 lakh, respectively, for finishing second and third. District Police Chief K.M. Sabu Mathew distributed the prizes at the valedictory function. Earlier in the day, Assembly Speaker Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan inaugurated the race at a function presided over by Water Resources and Housing Minister Mons Joseph. .Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Joseph said the Speaker had submitted a proposal for constructing a permanent pavilion for the Thazhathangady boat race. The government would examine the proposal and take a favourable decision, he said. Kottayam Municipal Chairperson M.P. Santhosh Kumar hoisted the flag to mark the beginning of the ceremony. The Speak

Published - October 24, 2026 08:16 pm IST - HYDERABAD The Cyberabad police have invoked the Preventive Detention (PD) Act against a 29-year-old alleged property offender who has been involved in 14 criminal cases since 2017, including cases of cheating, kidnapping, robbery and extortion. Cyberabad Commissioner of Police M. Ramesh ordered the detention of Nagaraju Raghu Varma alias Nagaraju Karthikeya Raghu Varma alias Vamshi alias Alluri Vijaya Ram. He was lodged in Central Prison, Cherlapalli, Medchal district. According to the Cyberabad police, Varma is a native of Poduru mandal in West Godavari district of Andhra Pradesh who migrated to Hyderabad and initially worked as a driver. Police said he later turned to criminal activities in pursuit of easy money. “Varma impersonated a police officer and approached people claiming that criminal cases had been registered against them at various police stations. He allegedly threatened them with legal consequences and extorted money by promising to help them,” said the police, adding that he was also accused of kidnapping targeted persons and robbing them after threatening them with firearms. Between 2017 and 2026, he was involved in 14 cases relating to cheating, kidnapping, robbery, extortion, criminal intimidation and offences under the Arms Act, 1959, according to the police. This is the third time that the Cyberabad police have detained Varma under the PD Act. He was previously detained in 2021 and 2024. Police said he resumed criminal activities after both releases and was subsequently involved in four more cases involving kidnapping, extortion and robbery while allegedly impersonating a police officer. Published - October 24, 2026 08:29 pm IST - Hyderabad Information and Public Relations Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy made it clear that the government would soon give details of the house sites to be allotted to journalists, as promised earlier. In a statement here, he said the modalities were discussed with Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy during his New Delhi visit and the job of identifying the land and giving a blue print was entrusted to a senior officer, who is on the job. Mr. Reddy said that the government was committed to fulfilling the long-pending demand of journalists for house sites and is working towards a permanent solution that will ensure allotments are free from legal complications. Mr. Reddy said that the government was taking steps to provide house sites in habitable locations where journalists could live with their families with dignity. He urged journalists who had been waiting for nearly two decades to remain patient, and a decision would come soon. Recalling the history of the issue, Mr. Ponguleti said land was allotted during the tenure of Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy in undivided Andhra Pradesh. However, the process remained stalled for a prolonged period because of a case pending in the Supreme Court. The Minister said that the Congress government, led by Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy, had taken the initiative to address the long-pending demand within months of assuming office. On September 8, 2024, a programme was organised at Ravindra Bharathi in Hyderabad, during which land was handed over to the journalists’ housing society, he recalled. 64bedd84a350a66a.title: Four-year-old boy from Tiruppur district dies of dengue
64bedd84a350a66a.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 08:27 pm IST - COIMBATORE The Health Department has confirmed the death of a four-year-old boy from Tiruppur district due to dengue. The child, identified as Tamil from Kungumapalayam village in Palladam Block, was diagnosed with Dengue Shock Syndrome combined with sepsis and Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC), at the Coimbatore Medical College Hospital, where he was referred to by a private clinic. In a press release, Hospital Dean M. Geethanjali said that since the child was admitted with after-effects of two epileptic attacks and low blood-pressure, normal saline bolus, and noradrenaline adrenaline were administered. There was respiratory failure and the child was kept in life-support. Though attempts were made to normalise blood pressure, the child suffered circulatory failure, and despite administering blood products and resuscitative efforts, the child died of cardiac arrest on Friday night, the press release said. Updated - October 24, 2026 08:41 pm IST - TIRUVARUR: Compensation under the the Prime Minister’s crop insurance scheme has been released to farmers who were not able to take up sowing during the kuruvai season in 2026-27 in Tiruvarur district. According to an official release, the Centre has announced that a sum of ₹77.70 crore would be distributed as compensation to farmers in 159 hamlets in Tiruvarur district under the ‘prevented sowing’ clause of the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY). While a sum of ₹12.05 crore would be disbursed to 4,868 farmers in the first phase on October 24, it would be distributed to others in subsequent phases. The amount would be credited directly into the accounts of the beneficiaries. Kuruvai coverage in Tiruvarur district stood at 77,573 hectares last year and dropped by 31,235 hectares this year, the release added. Murali, former Principal of The Madura College, who spoke on ‘Changing directions of Higher Education in Tamil Nadu,’ warned that Tamil Nadu’s higher education sector was facing several crises, and the government appeared to be facilitating the expansion of private and foreign universities instead of strengthening public universities and government colleges. Asserting that education is not merely a means of obtaining employment, he described it as a vital public resource that fosters independent thinking, scientific temper, social justice, human rights awareness, and democratic values. He cautioned that the growing tendency to transform education into a commercial service directly threatens the educational rights of students from poor and middle-class backgrounds. Periasamy A TNSTC bus driver was killed when the vehicle he was driving came in the path of a landslide at Burliyar, near the Coimbatore-Nilgiris district border, on the intervening night of Friday (October 23, 2026) and Saturday (October 24). There were no other passengers in the bus; the conductor, who sustained injuries, has been admitted to a hospital. According to the rainfall report issued by the Nilgiris district administration, Burliyar recorded 250 mm of rainfall in the 24 hours ending at 7 a.m. on Saturday, which was categorised as extremely heavy rainfall. More than 300 people were stranded along the ghat section following multiple landslips. A TNSTC bus plying on the Coimbatore-Nilgiris route was struck by a landslip at Burliyar in the early hours of Saturday, with soil and debris falling onto the vehicle. Photo & video: M. Periasamy (@peri_periasamy) https://t.co/3LKRVvMAtf The deceased driver was identified as Janagaraj, 55, of Katteri in the Nilgiris district. He was driving the bus from Coonoor to Coimbatore when the incident occurred. The conductor, Keshavan, was rescued and admitted to the Mettupalayam Government Hospital for treatment. A mini goods carrier also fell into a gorge at the landslip site. Its driver, Moushin, 38, managed to climb out of the vehicle and reach safety. Updated - October 24, 2026 08:40 pm IST Preetham R is one of the youngest to be exhibiting his collection. Three years ago, Preetham R stumbled upon a small box stacked with coins in the almirah and fell in love with it. “Although my father had shown me his collection when I was much younger, it was in college that I took a liking to coins,” says the 22-year-old who completed his B.Com. He is one of the youngest who is participating in the three-day coin exhibition conducted by Chennai Coin Club that concludes on October 25. More than 50 numismatics from different states are taking part in this event, and Preetham’s short journey with coins shows that it is never too late to start a hobby. “I started segregating the coins in the box into different types and researching them to develop more interest,” says the resident of Ayanavaram. A one-rupee copper coin was one of his first that he brought home on his own. Today, the youngster has a collection of 1,000 coins, with those minted from 1950 onwards being his specialisation. At the ongoing exhibition, besides selling some of his coins, he hopes to buy some rare ones to add to his collection. For those keen on starting coin collection as a hobby now, he says, it is not just a knowledgeable and a learning experience but a good investment option. Organisers of the Chennai Coin Club exhibition say the three-day event is aimed at raising awareness about counterfeit currency and fake coins that are increasingly doing the rounds. All the participants at the exhibition are experienced numismatics who are showcasing their best collection and share their knowledge. Published - October 24, 2026 08:55 pm IST - MYSURU Pramoda Devi Wadiyar of the erstwhile Mysuru royal family speaking to reporters in Mysuru on Saturday. | Photo Credit: M.A. Sriram Pramoda Devi Wadiyar of the erstwhile royal family of Mysuru has said she will issue a statement shortly on the circumstances that led to the cancellation of the traditional Vajra Mushti Kalaga during the Vijayadashami celebrations at the Mysuru palace on Wednesday. Responding to reporters’ queries in Mysuru, Ms. Wadiyar said she was yet to gather complete information about the developments that led to the cancellation of the historic martial tradition. Vajra Mushti Kalaga, an ancient form of martial combat in which wrestlers strike each other on their shaved heads with knuckle-dusters, has traditionally been held ahead of the erstwhile royal family’s private procession on Vijayadashami. The event was, however, cancelled this year after wrestlers alleged that the police had prevented some of them from entering the Mysuru palace premises in time to participate. Meanwhile, Ms. Wadiyar, however, expressed satisfaction over elephant Prashanta successfully carrying the golden howdah and ensuring the smooth completion of the Jamboo Savari. She admitted that she had been anxious about Prashanta carrying the golden howdah. It may be mentioned that it was 54-year-old male elephant Prashanta’s first time performing the task following the retirement of his predecessor, Abhimanyu, upon attaining the age of 60. 8b12a85b6581e384.title: Rain batters main roads in Tiruchi city
8b12a85b6581e384.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Updated - October 24, 2026 08:52 pm IST - TIRUCHI The condition of several roads in Tiruchi has turned from bad to worse after the recent spell of rain. | Photo Credit: M. MOORTHY The wet spell over the past few days has battered many key roads in the city, causing hardship to commuters and motorists. Since the onset of the Northeast monsoon on October 15, Tiruchi has been receiving rainfall. The showers were light until Thursday. However, heavy rain lashed different parts of the city on Friday, and the incessant rainfall has left arterial roads and interior lanes damaged. Uneven road surface and potholes have become a common sight on major stretches, with the top layer eroded at many places. The damaged patches have led to frequent skidding incidents, particularly affecting two-wheeler riders. The roads in Anna Nagar, Karur bypass, Old Madurai Road, West Boulevard Road, Major Saravanan Road and important stretches around Central Bus Stand such as Rockins Road, McDonalds Road, VOC Road, and Williams Road have suffered significant deterioration. Similarly, stretches around Chathiram Bus Stand have also been damaged. Similar issues have cropped up around Gandhi Market, Palakarai, Varaganeri and other areas. Published - October 24, 2026 08:39 pm IST - Thiruvananthapuram Vaisakh Chandran. | Photo Credit: File Photo The last two seasons were forgettable for off-spinner Vaisakh Chandran. A finger injury, followed by a shoulder injury, sidelined him. In between, he lost his bowling action and, consequently, his wicket-taking ability. The Ranji Trophy match against Karnataka at the KCA Stadium in Mangalapuram last season was particularly chastening; he was savaged by Karun Nair and R. Smaran, conceding over 100 runs at nearly five runs an over. His shoulder injury then flared up, forcing him to spend the rest of the season in rehabilitation. “I knew something was wrong but I was helpless. I was just going through the motions in the match against Karnataka. The shoulder was hurting as well. I felt a sharp pain on my right shoulder whenever I threw the ball while fielding. I think I over-bowled in the nets. I was told to bowl 30 overs daily during practice by our former coach and I followed it. The pain worsened, forcing me to consult a doctor who advised rest,” During his rehabilitation, he watched the video of the Karnataka match and compared them with old footage and realised his bowling action had changed drastically. “I went back to the drawing board, worked on my action. I also sought the help of Biju George, who pointed out the flaws and helped me to correct them,” he said. “It is a common problem for all bowlers to lose their original action when they play a lot. Every bowler has a specific arm slot from which he delivers the ball comfortably. In Vaisakh’s case his release point and arm path were different from his earlier action. I made slight adjustments to his loading and recoil and things fell into place,” Biju.explained. Published - October 24, 2026 08:55 pm IST - HYDERABAD The Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) detected violations at 125 medical shops across Hyderabad, its surrounding areas and other districts of Telangana during a special enforcement drive against the illegal sale and diversion of habit-forming drugs | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement The Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) detected violations at 125 medical shops across the State during a special enforcement drive against the illegal sale and diversion of habit-forming drugs. Show-cause notices have been issued to all 125 medical shops as discrepancies were detected. The Drugs Wing of TG SAFE, along with Enforcement Wing police personnel and Excise Enforcement personnel, conducted raids on Saturday (October 24), in areas covering Gajularamaram, Quthbullapur, Malkajgiri, Kapra, Habsiguda, Uppal, Jeedimetla, Balanagar, Medipally and Shamirpet. Similar enforcement operations were carried out in other districts of the State. The inspections focused on the indiscriminate sale of habit-forming medicines, including Tramadol, Alprazolam, Nitrazepam, Tapentadol, Zolpidem and Pregabalin-containing formulations, as well as codeine-containing cough syrups. TG SAFE officials conducted decoy operations and test purchases to check whether medical shops were dispensing prescription medicines, particularly those classified under Schedule H1 and Schedule X of the Drugs Rules, without complying with regulatory requirements. The violations detected included the sale of prescription medicines without valid prescriptions issued by registered medical practitioners, failure to maintain prescription and Schedule H1 drug registers, and dispensing medicines in the absence of a registered pharmacist. ccac7c2927062ae1.title: KTR urges youth against ignoring AI
ccac7c2927062ae1.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:05 pm IST - HYDERABAD BRS working president K.T. Rama Rao at the inauguration RandomTrees office in Hyderabad. | Photo Credit: Arrangement BRS working president K.T. Rama Rao has urged youth to embrace Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an opportunity for innovation and employment, instead of living in fear of the technology, particularly its impact on jobs. The former IT and Industries Minister, who was inaugurating the India headquarters of data, AI and innovation firm RandomTrees here, said this underscoring the significance of continuous learning, skill development and harnessing emerging technologies. Every technological revolution initially creates apprehensions but eventually opens new avenues for growth, he said, recalling the resistance to introduction of computers in the banking sector. Adapting to change was essential for progress and portraying AI as a ‘monster’ would only create unnecessary fear among people, Mr. Rao said. Highlighting the importance of strengthening Telangana’s technology ecosystem, attracting investments and preparing youth for future employment opportunities, he said the BRS government had taken several initiatives to position Hyderabad as a leading global IT destination and attract global capability centres of multinational companies. He expressed confidence that the city could emerge as a major hub for AI research, data science and technological innovation, a release from his office on Saturday said. With private sector playing a major role in employment generation, the governments should focus on creating a business-friendly environment rather than attempting to provide jobs directly to everyone. Reliable power and water supply, quality infrastructure, efficient transport and ease of doing business were essential to attract investments, Mr. Rao said. 4223785a7993584b.title: Bhatti Vikramarka calls for judicious use of water, electricity amid El Nino concerns
4223785a7993584b.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:02 pm IST - KHAMMAM Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka on Saturday called for collective efforts to conserve water and electricity amid dry weather conditions and rising power demand, urging the Opposition parties to set aside political differences to tackle the emerging El Nino-related challenges. . Addressing the media at Kodumuru in Chintakani mandal of Khammam district, he appealed to the Opposition to rise above political differences, recalling the collective efforts during the COVID-19 pandemic. Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy had reviewed the situation and constituted a Cabinet Sub-Committee to address the challenges, he said. Mr. Vikramarka said peak power demand had risen from 6,648 MW at the time of Telangana’s formation in 2014 to 20,018 MW now. Daily electricity consumption had increased from 245.35 million units in October last year to 335.05 million units this October, a rise of about 37%. He said the expansion of transmission infrastructure and construction of new substations were helping the State manage the growing demand. However, declining reservoir levels were affecting hydropower generation, which normally supplies around 3,500 MW during peak night-time hours. Of the nearly three million agricultural pump sets in the State, around 1.5 million were reportedly facing groundwater shortages. He urged farmers in areas with inadequate groundwater to avoid operating motors to prevent damage to pumps and transformers. The State’s major reservoirs, with a combined capacity of 470.22 TMC, held only 178.60 TMC of water, while nearly 40% of its 44,034 tanks had less than one-fourth of their capacity filled. Mr. Vikramarka said the government would prioritise water conservation while protecting livelihoods of farmers, labourers and rural communities. Published - October 24, 2026 09:10 pm IST As in the previous year, Amirda Varshini, councillor, Ward 126, has initiated a slew of measures to reassure residents that her team would be available to attend to any monsoon-related issue. This time, she has launched a helpline number (8010000126) and a QR code for people in Ward 126 to report any issue. “This service is available all through the day during the monsoon time,” she says, adding that water logging, electricity-related complaints and tree fall are among the top grievances they get. Talking to The Hindu Downtown, she says that barring a few areas where storm water drain work is yet to be commissioned many other localities are ready to face the monsoon. Mandavelipakkam, parts of Mandaveli, Devanathan Street, Jeth Nagar, Trustpakkam, and fishing hamlets such as Pattanipakkam and Rajiv Gandhi Nagar are among areas that fall under Ward 126. “My big focus will be on the coastal regions as many of the houses are old and they really need help,” says Amirda. Published - October 24, 2026 08:56 pm IST - PALAKKAD The Palakkad chapter of the Victims Information, Sensitisation, Welfare and Assistance Society (VISWAS) India will conduct a district-level children’s parliament competition for Class XI and XII students here on November 9. The event will be held in association with the State Bank of India (SBI) as part of the State government’s anti-drug campaign Operation Toofan. The competition will focus on drug use among students. Schools must conduct preliminary rounds and nominate the first prize winner for the district-level final. Students can choose from six topics covering drug prevention, awareness, youth responsibility and the need to protect students from substance abuse. Schools must email the details of their winning students to viswaspkd.programs@gmail.com before November 3, 2026. The final will be held at the Collectorate conference hall at Civil Station here. District Collector Sudheer K. will preside over the function. MLAs and senior police and excise officials will attend. Minister for General Education N. Samsudheen will be the chief guest. 0097d0d8d6ff8464.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:07 pm IST - Riyadh, Saudi Arabia Smoke rises after an attack by Houthi rebels. File | Photo Credit: AP Yemen’s Houthis said on Saturday (October 24, 2026) they attacked the southern city of Aden, the interim seat of the Saudi-backed government, after accusing Riyadh of killing 16 people in strikes on capital Sanaa and a Red Sea port city. Saudi Arabia and the internationally recognised Yemeni government have come under sustained attack from the Iran-backed Houthis, shifting the focus of the wider West Asia war that erupted with U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran in February. The Saudi-led coalition said earlier on Saturday (October 24) it had intercepted two missiles targeting Saudi cities Taif and Yanbu in the kingdom’s west, before explosions were heard in Aden, the home of the government that Riyadh supports in the years-long civil war. The Houthis quickly claimed the attack, saying they targeted a naval base and military camp overseen by Saudi forces. “Our armed forces targeted Saudi enemy concentrations at the so-called Al-Nasr camp and the naval base in Aden,” Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said. The Houthis’ Al-Masirah outlet earlier reported a series of “Saudi enemy airstrikes” targeting Yemen’s capital Sanaa, including one on a house that killed at least four people and wounded several others. A separate strike at a residential building for cement factory workers in the Sanaa governorate killed six women and one child and wounded three others, the broadcaster said. It later reported “five people, the head of the family, two of his children and his two wives, have been martyred” in a strike on their home in the western port city of Hodeida, blaming it on Saudi Arabia. Yemen’s civil war, pitting the Iran-backed Houthis against the Saudi-supported and internationally recognised government, had been dormant since a ceasefire in 2022, but erupted again in July as the wider West Asia war roiled the region. 5880547296026a16.title: Caste harassment case: deceased student’s parents refuse to accept body demanding arrest of teacher, headmaster
5880547296026a16.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:10 pm IST - COIMBATORE The parents and relatives of Akilan, a Class 11 student of a government-aided school in Peelamedu who had ended his life due to alleged harassment over caste and eating habits, staged a sit-in protest demanding the arrest of his teacher, headmaster and other students purportedly involved in abetment. They refused to accept the body of the student. The Peelamedu police had registered a case against the teacher and a few classmates based on a complaint lodged by the deceased student’s mother Kausalyadevi. Two students were arrested after the case was registered. A press release issued by the city police said two students have been arrested in the case, and 30 other students, teachers and other witnesses were questioned. Separate inquiries were also conducted by officials of School Education Department and Child Welfare Committee. The autopsy report will provide more clues. Five special teams have been formed and CCTV camera footage and scientific evidence were being examined. The press release said that a transparent investigation was under way and that spreading of rumours should be avoided. Assistance for overcoming suicidal thoughts is available on the State’s health helpline 104, Tele-MANAS 14416, and Sneha’s Suicide Prevention Helpline 044-24640050 Published - October 24, 2026 09:10 pm IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. Updated - October 24, 2026 09:00 pm IST - AMALAPURAM The Konaseema Centre for Migration (KCM) is gearing up to launch a village-level campaign against fake recruitment agents and agencies in Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Konaseema district to prevent locals from being stranded in the Gulf region. The local agents are allegedly active in recruiting people—mostly women—for employment in the Gulf region, where victims are reportedly subjected to physical harassment, assigned work beyond their physical capacities, and stranded without employment. KCM manager Golla Ramesh stated that 284 people stranded in the Gulf region had been repatriated and 128 grievances pertaining to fake agents and agencies are being redressed. In a review meeting with the officials concerned, District Revenue Officer Veerla Subbarao directed the revenue, police, and other officials to launch a campaign against fake agents and agencies and create awareness on the employment opportunities and recruitment procedures. e2c2fd5cab2c5014.title: France protests: Police say 1,10,000 marched in Paris
e2c2fd5cab2c5014.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:11 pm IST - Paris, France Protesters march along the Avenue Jean Zay during a demonstration "against racism, fascism and imperialism" on October 24, 2026 | Photo Credit: AFP Paris police said that 1,10,000 people marched in the capital Saturday (October 24, 2026) as part of nationwide demonstrations over the cost of living, and the situation was “calm”. That contrasted with other cities, including Lyon, Lille, Toulouse, Montpellier and Nantes, where clashes broke out during demonstrations. Paris police said that more than 3,000 people were stopped and checked by officers and 65 people were arrested during the demonstration in the French capital. 398f6c917d9a94cd.title: Five-day inclusive art festival from October 28
398f6c917d9a94cd.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:03 pm IST The fifth edition of Tattva 2026, an inclusive art platform dedicated to celebrating the creativity, talent, and aspirations of artists with disabilities, will be inaugurated on October 28. Initiated by V-Excel Educational Trust, this year the festival brings together 270 plus artists from across Tamil Nadu and Kolkata for five immersive days of artistic expression, mentorship, and public engagement. This is being organised around five thematic pillars — Drishti, Srishti, Anubhav, Vistara, and Ekattva, serving as a catalyst for social inclusion, offering structured workshops, live demonstrations, collaborative murals, a curated art auction, and dedicated sales platforms designed to foster economic independence and livelihood opportunities for participating artists, said a release. In a release, Vasudha Prakash, Founder-Director of V-Excel Educational Trust, said: “This year, we also celebrate the success stories of past participants, reaffirming our core belief that talent flourishes when properly nurtured. Through exhibitions, live demonstrations, and our new art auction, Tattva 2026 connects extraordinary creators with wider audiences.” As part of this year’s celebrations, V-Excel Educational Trust will host a special art auction on October 25 at 5 p.m. at Hotel Savera. The auction will showcase selected artworks created by artists with disabilities, offering art enthusiasts and collectors an opportunity to engage with their work while supporting the artists and their creative journeys. af99ec9c0f1921d8.title: Over 1,000 get offer letters at job fair held in Srirangam
af99ec9c0f1921d8.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:03 pm IST - TIRUCHI As many as 1,031 candidates, including four persons with disabilities, were issued offer letters at a mega job fair organised by the district administration and the District Employment and Career Guidance Centre at Srimad Andavan Arts and Science College in Srirangam on Saturday. As many as 3,841 aspirants, including 1,651 women and 19 with disabilities, attended the job fair meant to find private placements for unemployed youth. Over 200 companies attended the fair to recruit candidates for various positions, according to an official press release. Minister for Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments S. Ramesh distributed the offer letters to candidates and said that 40,625 candidates, including 684 with disabilities, had been placed through 208 job fairs organised in the State since the TVK government assumed office. Private placement fairs would continue to be held in the districts to find suitable jobs for unemployed youth. Collector Pratik Tayal and other officials participated. a435a348810cc741.title: Forum urges CM to frame rules for Malayalam Language Act
a435a348810cc741.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:02 pm IST - Thiruvananthapuram Eminent names from the cultural, literary, and other spheres in Keralam, under the umbrella of the Aikya Malayala Prasthanam, have urged Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan to implement the Malayalam Language Act to coincide with the 70th anniversary of the State’s formation. In a representation, prominent figures such as Adoor Gopalakrishnan, George Onakkoor, V. Madhusoodhanan Nair, C. Radhakrishnan, K. Satchidanandan, M. Mukundan, and N.S. Madhavan have pointed out that though Keralam was formed in 1956 along linguistic lines with Malayalam as its language, it neither had a language policy nor planning. Malayalam was not seen as the foundation of the State’s development nor was it projected with pride. Governments too were responsible for the neglect of Malayalam. This should change. The Malayalam Language Bill that was passed by the State Assembly in October last year became an Act after the Governor gave his assent in March this year. However, only on implementation could the Act be said to have achieved its objective. Seven months after Malayalam was declared the official language of Kerala, the Act was yet to get Rules. This was a matter of concern. On Kerala Piravi day (November 1) this year, Rules for the Malayalam Language Act should be framed and the State government should declare that Act will be implemented effectively, the representation sought. Some of the other signatories include C.V. Balakrishnan, M.N. Karassery, V.N. Murali, K.N. Ganesh, Subhash Chandran, Ezhacherry Ramachandran, P.K. Rajasekharan, Ambikasuthan Mangad, R.V.G. Menon, Alankode Leelakrishnan, Kaleeswaram Raj and M.R. Thampan. 9243627e57fe77bd.title: CJP seeks impartial probe into Chorabagan stampede that killed 19 in Bengal
9243627e57fe77bd.summary: CJP's West Bengal unit on Saturday demanded an impartial probe into the Chorabagan stampede that claimed 19 lives and called for accountability for any negligence established during the investigation. The party organised a condolence programme and a press conference to pay tribute to the victims and express solidarity with the affected families. Addressing the press conference, a Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) member called for safety audits, trained personnel, emergency evacuation plans and better coordination among emergency services. In a statement, CJP coordinator Prakriti Sahu outlined the party's demands, including timely financial assistance and medical support for the affected families and injured, stronger safety guidelines for major public gatherings and festival pandals across the state, and regular public updates on the investigation and relief measures. The party said it would submit its demands in writing to the relevant authorities and seek details of the action taken.

Alleging institutional capture and demanding measures to restore the integrity of the electoral process, economist Parakala Prabhakar, who joined the protest, called for the scrapping of the SIR and the reconstitution of the Election Commission of India (ECI). Economist Parakala Prabhakar addressing the gathering at Tank Bund in Hyderabad on Saturday. | Photo Credit: SIDDHANT THAKUR Rejecting the idea that dissent was confined to designated protest venues, he said resistance could emerge from any part of the country. “Jantar Mantar is not a physical space in New Delhi. Wherever dissent is expressed and wherever we register our objection to SIR, anywhere in the country, in any village, town, lane or street, that is our Jantar Mantar. Every person who is questioning and dissenting is a walking Jantar Mantar. Every mind that questions is a Jantar Mantar,” he said. 785a4a28291d1789.title: BJP discusses preparations for MLC, GHMC elections
785a4a28291d1789.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:17 pm IST - HYDERABAD State BJP president N. Ramchander Rao, national general secretary Sunil Bansal and other party leaders at a meeting in Hyderabad on Saturday. | Photo Credit: G RAMAKRISHNA The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has discussed preparations for the upcoming Graduates’ MLC elections and Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) elections at a meeting of its State leaders and office-bearers here on Saturday. The meeting, chaired by State BJP president N. Ramachander Rao at the party’s State office, reviewed the prevailing political situation in Telangana and discussed the party’s organisational activities in nine districts falling within the GHMC limits. Party leaders outlined strategies to secure victory in the Graduates’ MLC elections and called upon cadres to mobilise workers at the booth level and intensify public outreach. The meeting also discussed the BJP’s ‘Loktantra Bachao – Bheedtantra Hatao’ (Save Democracy – Remove Mobocracy) campaign against what the party described as actions undermining democratic values. It was decided to intensify grassroots-level protests against the Congress government’s policies in Telangana. BJP State in-charge Sunil Bansal, co-in-charge Abhay Patil, State organisational general secretary N. Madhukar, State joint organisational general secretary Dashrath, MPs, MLAs, MLCs and presidents of the nine district units attended the meeting. Rekha Sharma was also present. dca4cf39d8031b80.title: Prakasam Collector calls for utmost vigilance in handling polling materials
dca4cf39d8031b80.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:12 pm IST - ONGOLE Prakasam District Collector P. Raja Babu and Joint Collector Kalpana Kumari inspect ballot boxes ahead of the Municipal Corporation elections on Saturday. | Photo Credit: KOMMURI SRINIVAS As the State gears up for the local body elections, Prakasam District Collector P. Raja Babu has emphasised the need for utmost vigilance in handling polling materials and in making arrangements for the counting process to ensure that no lapses occur. The Collector, along with Joint Collector Kalpana Kumari, inspected the ballot boxes at RISE Engineering College on the outskirts of Ongole on Saturday. Officials have set up facilities for the distribution and reception of election materials, as well as strong rooms and a counting centre for the local body elections, within the college premises. At the centre, the Collector inspected how the 101 statutory and non-statutory items of equipment required for the elections were being maintained. He instructed the officials to prepare the equipment required for the 224 polling stations in the Municipal Corporation limits. He also inspected the manner in which the barricades were prepared and the necessary arrangements made as per the rules of the Election Commission. 681662735aec5502.title: Sichuan to meet Denso Iris in the final of FIBA-Women’s Basketball League Asia tournament
681662735aec5502.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:13 pm IST - BENGALURU By experience and pedigree, American Chennedy Carter towers above everyone else in the FIBA-Women’s Basketball League Asia. A former WNBA player and the only one in the tournament, the 27-year-old has been one of the top scorers for Sichuan Yuanda Meile (China) in the league at the Sree Kanteerava Indoor Stadium here. Against KB Stars in the semifinals on Saturday, Carter appeared to play every role, switching between guard, shooting guard and even power forward. Carter (31 points), ably supported by Australia’s Sara Blicavs (22) and captain Song Gao (21), powered Sichuan to a 93-74 win over KB Stars, taking the Chinese side into its second final in three WBLA editions—it last won the title in the inaugural edition in 2024. Carter also made her presence felt on the boards, collecting five rebounds and dishing out five assists. Denso Iris (Japan) faced a stiff challenge from Cathay Life Tigers (Chinese Taipei) before emerging triumphant 86-78 in the other semifinal to set up a final against Sichuan on Sunday. Maki Takada, the 37-year-old Olympic medallist and centre, starred for Iris, finishing as its top-scorer with 20 points. Earlier, Indian Railways suffered its third successive defeat to finish sixth and last in the tournament, losing to Akari Sparks (Philippines) 86-56. b6af02c1ad349ac0.title: Iran president says many struggling for food as war bites
b6af02c1ad349ac0.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:29 pm IST - Tehran Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian attends the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) summit in Turkmenbasy, Turkmenistan. File | Photo Credit: AP Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Saturday (October 24, 2026) that many Iranians were struggling to put food on the table, as the economic pressure from the Middle East war with the United States mounts. Washington has in recent weeks dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure, while Iran's leaders have said peace negotiations will only succeed without pressure and threats from Washington as the conflict remains locked in a stalemate. "There are many people in this society who are struggling to put food on the table because of the war we have found ourselves in, because of the wartime conditions we are living under," Mr. Pezeshkian said in a speech shared on his website. The war began on February 28 when the United States and Israel attacked Iran, killing supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and senior military commanders. Iran retaliated with attacks on U.S. assets in the region and on Israel, while restricting passage through the strategic Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global energy supplies. Washington responded by imposing a blockade on Iranian ports, restricting the country's oil exports and trade. A ceasefire deal mediated mainly by Pakistan in mid-June was intended to end the war and pave the way for broader negotiations, but it collapsed soon afterwards, with both sides accusing each other of violating its terms. Since then, the U.S. has carried out sporadic attacks on Iranian targets, while Iran has targeted vessels attempting to cross the strait, accusing them of violating conditions set by Tehran for safe passage. Mr. Pezeshkian called for an end to what he described as a "state of neither war nor peace", saying Tehran "must also get out of this situation", without specifying how. His remarks came as fears of renewed fighting

1ef9ff41f378ac2b.title: Ward 126 councillor launches QR code and helpline number for residents to raise rain-related issues
1ef9ff41f378ac2b.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:46 pm IST As in the previous year, Amirda Varshini, councillor, Ward 126, has initiated a slew of measures to reassure residents that her team would be available to attend to any monsoon-related issue. This time, she has launched a helpline number (8010000126) and a QR code for people in Ward 126 to report any issue. “This service is available all through the day during the monsoon time,” she says, adding that water logging, electricity-related complaints and tree fall are among the top grievances they get. Talking to The Hindu Downtown, she says that barring a few areas where storm water drain work is yet to be commissioned many other localities are ready to face the monsoon. Mandavelipakkam, parts of Mandaveli, Devanathan Street, Jeth Nagar, Trustpakkam, and fishing hamlets such as Pattanipakkam and Rajiv Gandhi Nagar are among areas that fall under Ward 126. “My big focus will be on the coastal regions as many of the houses are old and they really need help,” says Amirda. eec99c39dbf4cedc.title: Coimbatore NXT pitches for major railway infrastructure push in its meeting with Southern Railway GM
eec99c39dbf4cedc.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:33 pm IST - COIMBATORE A delegation of Coimbatore NXT, Railway Task Force, at its high-level meeting here with the General Manager of Southern Railway U. Subba Rao and the Divisional Railway Manager, Salem Division, Panna Lal, on Friday, sought urgent improvements in railway infrastructure, additional train services, enhanced passenger amenities and better suburban connectivity across Coimbatore. Led by Vanitha Mohan, vice-chairman, Kongu Global Forum, the delegates, including Dorairaj, president, Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry; Naushad, chairman, CII, Coimbatore Zone; Balasubramanian, president, Residents’ Awareness Association of Coimbatore (RAAC); and Dileep who represented the Customs Brokers and Shipping Agents Association, strongly emphasised that the development of Coimbatore Junction, a major revenue-generating railway station in Southern Railway, has been long overdue and must receive immediate attention. The major demands constituted operating Coimbatore–Chennai Vande Bharat Express with more coaches to meet growing passenger demand; introduction of Coimbatore–Tiruvananthapuram Vande Bharat Express; restoration of direct train connectivity to the southern districts of Tamil Nadu that were in place during the metre-gauge era; and rerouting of trains currently bypassing Coimbatore Junction. The delegates also called for upgrade of Coimbatore Junction with additional infrastructure, improved passenger amenities and facilities for simultaneous train operations; expediting the development of Coimbatore South - Podanur Junction; establishing additional island platforms at Coimbatore North Junction and according it a status of terminus; and improvements to platforms and passenger amenities at Irugur, Singanallur, Kinathukadavu, Peelamedu and other suburban stations. They mooted strengthening of circular suburban railway connectivity from Coimbatore to Tiruppur , Pollachi and Palakkad to serve Coimbatore’s growing metropoli

01f26b4112395f20.title: Minister inaugurates bus stand in Chekkanurani
01f26b4112395f20.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:45 pm IST - MADURAI Minister for Energy Resources and Law C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar inaugurating the new bus stand at Chekkanurani in Madurai on Saturday. Minister for Energy and Law C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar here on Saturday inaugurated the newly constructed bus terminus built at a cost of ₹8.50 crore under the Integrated Assigned Revenue Scheme in Chekkanurani in Tirumangalam Panchayat Union. Facilities established in the bus terminus included seven bus bays, 27 commercial shops, two restaurants, two waiting rooms for men, two waiting rooms for women and nursing mothers, a transport office, a police office, restroom facilities for both men and women, and 21 vegetable market stalls. Speaking there, he said, as the bus stand work was lagging behind, the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government expedited the works and completed the works earlier. “Chekkanurani bus stand which connects the nearby villages is very important for the farmers and villagers around. It serves as a hub for the nearby regions,” he added. Recognising the importance of the Usilampatti bus stand, the government has directed the officials to fasten the works carried out there. “Further, we have also heard from the public about further upgradations required in the Chekkanurani bus stand and it will be taken to the Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay for approval,” he noted. Regarding the works carried out in Madurai for upcoming rains, he said, all works which were stagnated for over five years in the previous government have all been kicked off. “In Sellur following an inspection we have ordered the pipe laying works to be expedited and it is expected to be completed in the next five days. Along with this, many other works are also being carried out,” he said. d73cebf1fb6380b7.title: Siruthuli requests Railways to rename Coimbatore-Chennai Superfast Express as ‘Noyyal Express’.
d73cebf1fb6380b7.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:40 pm IST - COIMBATORE Siruthuli, the Coimbatore-based environmental organisation working on water conservation and afforestation, has requested the Southern Railway to rename Train No. 12680 Coimbatore-MGR Chennai Superfast Express as ‘Noyyal Express’. In a representation to Southern Railway General Manager U. Subba Rao, on Friday, managing trustee of Siruthuli Vanitha Mohan said the Noyyal river originating in the Velliangiri Hills of the Western Ghats and flowing to a length of 160 km before joining the Cauvery river was integral to the historic development of Kongu region encompassing Coimbatore, Tiruppur, Erode and Karur districts. The Noyyal river, with its network of streams and irrigation channels sustained agriculture, supported livelihoods, and shaped the region’s cultural heritage. The Indian Railways has recognised the cultural and geographical significance of rivers and natural landmarks through the names of several trains: Vaigai Express, Cauvery Express, and Pothigai Express. Renaming Train No. 12680 Coimbatore-MGR Chennai Superfast Express as ‘Noyyal Express’ will be a meaningful tribute to the Noyyal river and the legacy, and would inspire future generations to protect the invaluable natural resource, Ms. Vanitha Mohan said. In another representation, Siruthuli while thanking the Railways for permitting planting of 62,800 trees on railway lands in and around Coimbatore since 2012, sought consent for extending the afforestation activities, under its Green Guard initiative, to raise 1.62 lakh trees in the open spaces to a cumulative extent of 46.4 acres in Singanallur railway station, Nallampalayam, Kavundampalayam, Podanur, Karamadai railway station, and Coimbatore Railway Station. 28630bd49731fc82.title: Sri Lankan Navy seizes two Indian boats in beedi leaves smuggling bid
28630bd49731fc82.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:29 pm IST - THOOTHUKUDI Sri Lankan Navy and the Coast Guard seized two Indian fibre boats and two Sri Lankan local dinghies on Wednesday (October 21) off the coast of Udappuwa, Puttalam while attempting to smuggle a consignment of beedi leaves. According to Sri Lankan Navy’s website, a total of 11 suspects, Indian and Sri Lankan nationals were also apprehended. The interception was made after having spotted two suspicious Indian fibre boats that had entered the Sri Lankan waters, along with two local dinghies. Upon searching the boats, naval and coast guard personnel recovered about 2,400 kg of beedi leaves packed into 60 sacks. Seven Indian nationals aboard the fibre boats and four Sri Lankan suspects on the dinghies were taken into custody in this operation. The suspects, seized boats and beedi leaves were handed over to the customs preventive office for further legal proceedings. 2490f901117886d9.title: SHG members, students participate in nutrition awareness programme at PU
2490f901117886d9.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:23 pm IST - PUDUCHERRY A Nutrition Assessment Camp was held recently at the Pondicherry University as part of the celebrations to mark National Nutrition month and World Food Day 2026. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Members of self-help groups, community representatives and students participated in a Nutrition Assessment Camp held as part of the celebrations to mark National Nutrition month and World Food Day 2026, at the Pondicherry University recently. Vice-Chancellor P. Prakash Babu inaugurated the programme aimed at spreading awareness on nutrition. The camp, organised by the Department of Food Science and Technology of the university, had on display many value-added food products, including micro-greens, millet-based premixes, minor millet cookies, organic vegetables, honey, edible oils and other locally-produced foods, the University said in a release. The camp provided BMI assessment, blood pressure reading, haemoglobin analysis and random blood glucose testing. In addition, dietary and lifestyle counselling, along with personalised nutrition guidance was provided to the participants to help adopt healthier food habits and improved lifestyle practices, the release added. The event was an opportunity for community groups to popularise their value-added products and promote sustainable food practices, the release said. a598a27a9389ba22.title: Guntur doctor presents research at neurosurgeons’ meet in London
a598a27a9389ba22.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:27 pm IST - GUNTUR Dr. Mohana Rao Patibandla, founder and chief neurosurgeon of Dr. Rao’s Hospital, participating in the Society of British Neurological Surgeons centenary meeting in London. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Dr. Mohana Rao Patibandla, founder and chief neurosurgeon of Dr. Rao’s Hospital–International Institute of Neurosciences (IIN), Guntur, presented research on complex craniovertebral junction surgery at the Society of British Neurological Surgeons (SBNS) centenary meeting in London. In a statement on Saturday, Dr. Patibandla said the international scientific meeting was held from October 12 to 16, bringing together neurosurgical experts to discuss advancements in neurological care and surgical techniques. His presentation, titled “Transnasal Endoscopic Odontoidectomy for Failed Posterior Craniovertebral Fusion: Salvage Decompression and Outcomes in 6 Complex Cases,” examined a minimally invasive approach for patients experiencing persistent compression despite previous posterior stabilisation surgery. The craniovertebral junction connects the skull to the upper cervical spine. Compression in this region can threaten brainstem and spinal cord functions. The endoscopic technique enables surgeons to access the odontoid process through the nasal passages to relieve pressure from the front. The research analysed six complex cases, highlighting the importance of individualised surgical planning, careful assessment and evaluation of neurological outcomes. The findings contribute to international discussions on minimally invasive neurosurgery and complex spinal disorders, he added. bbb5f9d88d72b508.title: IRDAI extends distribution reforms feedback timeline to Oct 31
bbb5f9d88d72b508.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:50 pm IST - HYDERABAD The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has extended the last date for submission of comments on its consultation paper on distribution reforms till October 31. The consultation process has received an encouraging response, with over 650 comments received thus far. In view of the significant interest and to facilitate wider participation, the last date for stakeholders and the public to submit feedback and suggestions is being extended, the regulator said on Saturday. Placing its two-part consultation paper on the proposed distribution reforms titled ‘Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution’ in public domain on September 23rd, IRDAI had set October 25 as the deadline. Desirous stakeholders and members of the public are encouraged to utilise the extended timeline and submit their comments and suggestions. The feedback received will help inform the further examination and refinement of the proposed reforms. All other details and terms of the consultation paper remain unchanged, IRDAI said. The insurance regulator is proposing a major overhaul of norms governing insurance distribution, commissions and expenses. It said the objective is to foster a more efficient and inclusive insurance distribution ecosystem. e660a98a5348b5f4.title: Dominant India aims to seal ODI series against Zimbabwe
e660a98a5348b5f4.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:52 pm IST - VADODARA Skipper Smriti Mandhana will be happy with Pratika’s form. The sun will rise in the east. A day has 24 hours. India will beat Zimbabwe. Some certainties are written into the fabric of the universe. This one comes stamped with a scoreboard. None of this is meant as a disrespect. Even the visitor speaks of an upset as a miracle: improbable, yet gloriously welcome should it arrive. But miracles demand fresh legs, and Zimbabwe’s are running on fumes. They come into the second ODI at the BCA Stadium in Kotambi on Sunday carrying the bruises of a nine-wicket loss and the weight of a calendar that has given them little mercy. The Lady Chevrons have been the busiest side in international cricket recently, playing non-stop since September. Niggles have crept up, with Josephine Nkomo and Kelis Ndhlovu missing the 1st ODI. Recovery has been a challenge, with the priority for the camp being the ICC Emerging Nations Trophy, which gets underway in Bangkok in November. India, meanwhile, eyes an unassailable lead but isn’t without its own headaches. The pacers were erratic in the 1st ODI. Nandani Sharma, who made way for debutant Jintimani Kalita, was spotted doing her routines with her left knee in a compression brace. But the bigger issues are the wayward lines India settled into after the PowerPlay and an inability to bowl to set fields, which Zimbabwe smartly capitalised on. Will India be brave and give wicketkeeper Richa Ghosh, whose errors have been piling up, a rest to allow Baroda girl Yastika Bhatia, who graces several billboards around the venue, a spot in the side? Or is there room for both, the way India has managed to embrace Shafali Verma and Pratika Rawal? Coach Amol Muzumdar and captain Smriti Mandhana must weigh rotating players to build depth for the South Africa tour or stick with a winning lineup. b2bf9ac9c1ddb5b7.title: Centre extends Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh's tenure by one year
b2bf9ac9c1ddb5b7.summary: The Centre has extended the tenure of Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh by one year, till October 31, 2027, according to an official order issued on Saturday. The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) approved the extension of Singh, a 1989-batch IAS officer of the Kerala cadre, beyond his scheduled tenure ending on October 31, 2026. "The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet has approved extension in the service of Rajesh Kumar Singh, IAS (KL:89) as Secretary, Department of Defence, Ministry of Defence, for a period of one year beyond 31.10.2026, i.e. up to 31.10.2027 or until further orders whichever is earlier," the order issued by the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) read. The extension was granted in relaxation of the provisions of Fundamental Rule 56(d) and Rule 16(1A) of the All India Services (Death-cum-Retirement Benefits) Rules, 1958, the order said.

They also demanded an access road to reach public facilities such as bus terminus and a railway station in Arakkonam town. Residents said that Ramdass Nagar forms part of Kainoor village panchayat. The residential area is surrounded by Winterpet, Ambedkar Nagar, and Jothinagar. “We have been using a common pathway in the area for many years to reach central parts of the town, and to access public facilities such as banks, hospitals, and a bus terminus. They said that the pathway was also completely closed after a resident on the pathway erected fencing on one portion of the stretch. As a result, residents had to take a detour of three km to reach Ramdass Nagar and surrounding areas. 5790de2cc52c3644.title: Healthcare challenges require collaborative, technology-ledsolutions, says Health Secretary
5790de2cc52c3644.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 01:00 am IST - CHENNAI Health Secretary Darez Ahamed presents the Lifetime Achievement Award to R.V. Ramani, founder and managing trustee, Sankara Eye Foundation. Sathish Devadoss, convener, CII TN Healthcare Panel, and C. Devarajan, chairman, CII, T.N., are also seen. | Photo Credit: S.R. RAGHUNATHAN While the Tamil Nadu public health system is one of the best in the country, demonstrating great achievements in maternal and child health care, challenges such as the growing burden of non-communicable diseases require innovative, technology-led solutions. This is where, perhaps, a partnership with the private sector and industry could help, Tamil Nadu Health Secretary Darez Ahamed said. He was speaking at TN MedClave, 2026, of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) on the theme ‘Intelligent Healthcare: From Innovation to Implementation’, held on Saturday. Noting that hypertension, diabetes, cancer and mental health were some of the big emerging challenges in the healthcare sector, Dr. Ahamed said cardiac issues were one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in the State and it was here — in ensuring that interventions reached people on time — that innovation could play a role, but this had to co-exist with implementation. Tracing patients across the health system and ensuring continuity of care for chronic diseases were other issues that needed tackling. The State had proved it could deliver quality care at scale, he added. He said the government was willing to partner to tackle these challenges jointly with the private sector and implored the conclave to take on these challenges, come up with solutions collaboratively, and importantly, evaluate progress in the future. A Lifetime Achievement Award was presented to R.V. Ramani, founder and managing trustee, Sankara Eye Foundation. Dr. Ramani highlighted the importance of evaluating progress in healthcare, the need for strong human resources, and making healthcare accessible

abacc3a3acc5ce80.title: H.E.L.P. conference held at Coimbatore hospital
abacc3a3acc5ce80.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 11:50 pm IST - Coimbatore Health & Environment Leadership Platform (H.E.L.P.) Tamil Nadu Chapter Conference 2026 was held on Saturday (October 24) at Ganga Medical Centre & Hospitals, Coimbatore. Sustainability has become a buzzword across industries, but it is now the need of the hour—particularly in healthcare, where energy consumption, water use, waste generation and climate-related risks have a direct bearing on responsible and resilient service delivery. Guided by the theme ‘Strategic Leadership for Sustainable Healthcare’, the conference aimed at encouraging healthcare institutions to move beyond awareness and adopt practical, measurable sustainability initiatives. Welcome address was by Rama Rajasekaran, director-Ganga Hospitals, president - H.E.L.P Tamil Nadu Chapter. The session included a ceremonial lamp lighting, followed by the inaugural address delivered by Alexander Thomas, chairman of H.E.L.P., Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI). A. Lingiah, medical director- Yashoda Hospitals, regional lead – H.E.L.P South Zone, delivered the special address, highlighting the significance of leadership and collective action in advancing sustainable healthcare. The speakers included Chandan Khanna, India project manager, Healthcare Without Harm, who spoke on the business case for sustainable healthcare; Vinod, chairperson, Healthcare Engineers Forum and head consultant at VBG Consulting Engineers, Kochi, who spoke on hospital utilities and carbon footprint; Chandran Vinoth Kumar, chairperson, Supply Chain Leaders Forum, CAHO, who spoke on green procurement; Krishna Murthy, director, DAK Healthcare Consultancy, Chennai, who spoke on Green OT challenges and implementation; Vanitha Mohan, chairperson, Pricol Holdings Private Ltd. and managing trustee, Siruthuli, who spoke on water conservation and leadership; Ashwini Dokka, associate counsellor, IGBC- Green Commercial, who spoke on green hospital building standards; and Ramesh Babu, medic

36a2b971107368f8.title: We only tried to make Thirumavalavan the Chief Minister, says Dhinakaran
36a2b971107368f8.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 11:47 pm IST - CHENNAI AMMK general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran. | Photo Credit: R. ASHOK T.T.V. Dhinakaran, general secretary of the Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK), said the AIADMK and the DMK never attempted to form a government together, and instead, efforts were made to make VCK president Thol. Thirumavalavan the Chief Minister. Speaking to reporters in Sivagangai, Mr. Dhinakaran said they initiated this move because the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) did not have the support of enough MLAs. “Speaking as someone who was part of that alliance, no effort was ever made for the AIADMK and the DMK to join hands and form a government. The TVK only had 107 MLAs. [DMK president] M.K. Stalin had made it clear that the DMK would not attempt to come to power. Therefore, we tried to form a government led by the AIADMK. At that time, I addressed [Chief Minister] Vijay and said if you were unable to form the government, please extend support so that we, the common people, could form it. However, the Left parties refused their support, stating that backing [AIADMK general secretary] Edappadi K. Palaniswami would be tantamount to supporting the BJP. Following this, all of us, including EPS [Mr. Palaniswami], made efforts to make Thirumavalavan the Chief Minister,” he said. Mr. Dhinakaran further clarified that this initiative was not to prevent the TVK from forming the government, but rather to stop their MLAs from being poached. He asserted that the DMK and the AIADMK could never align under any circumstances. Responding to another query, he said those grieving Mr. Palaniswami’s inability to bring the AIADMK back to power should convey their views directly to him in person rather than airing them publicly, adding that the AMMK and the AIADMK would continue working together. e6e541e1ce3a90d5.title: SRM Medical College holds national geriatric summit
e6e541e1ce3a90d5.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 01:01 am IST - CHENNAI SRM Medical College Hospital and Research Centre, through its Department of Community Medicine, organised ‘Age Well India’, a National Geriatric Summit. Centered on the theme ‘From Prevention to Policy: Building Healthier Ageing Systems’, the summit aims to bring greater attention to the healthcare needs of older adults and the importance of strengthening systems that support healthy ageing. Binod Kumar Patro, director, National Institute of Health and Family Welfare, New Delhi and V.S. Natarajan, founder and chairman, Dr. V.S. Natarajan Geriatric Foundation, participated. Dr. Patro said that geriatric care must be integrated into primary healthcare, with a focus on prevention, rehabilitation, and dignified care for older persons. Dr. Natarajan raised the need to strengthen geriatric services, rehabilitation centres, and train more geriatricians to ensure that older people live with dignity, independence, and quality of life. R. Jayanthi, dean (Medical), SRM Medical College Hospital and Research was present, a press release said. 7de24362ec31c379.title: Tiruvannamalai Corporation sets up 10 temporary shelters for families in Arunachala Hills
7de24362ec31c379.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 11:59 pm IST - TIRUVANNAMALAI Collector Vandhana Garg held an inspection in Tiruvannamalai town to assess rain-preparedness on Saturday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement With the onset of the Northeast monsoon, Tiruvannamalai Corporation has set up at least 10 temporary shelters, mostly community centres, to accommodate families in Arunachala Hills. Corporation officials said that along with the Forest Department, local police and revenue officials, civic officials have identified at least 1,400 vulnerable families - those residing in the upper portion of the hills. “Adequate shelters have been arranged during emergencies. Most of these accommodations are located at least 500 metres away from the hills to ensure safety of relocated families,” K. Balasubramanian, Commissioner, Tiruvannamalai Corporation, told The Hindu. At present, over 6,000 families are living in small settlements in the hills. Of this, the Revenue Department has identified 1,535 illegal settlements, mostly houses and commercial establishments. Around 140 illegal settlements fall under the Corporation limits. Demolition of these illegal structures will prevent landslides in the hills during monsoon. On December 1, 2024, seven persons, including children died after heavy rain triggered a landslide. A total of 576 acres of land in the hills are encroached upon, with most of them being houses. Along with civic officials, Collector Vandhana Garg inspected Mada Streets around Arunachaleswarar temple, a bus terminus, Girivalam Path, and a market in town to assess rain preparedness. Sudden showers for the past few days have inundated key stretches in the town. Shops on Mada Streets were stagnated with knee-deep water. “With Karthigai Deepam festival, the town should be prepared to handle the monsoon, especially by preventing water stagnation ,” said R.
