de85488919f9cd0a.title: Corporation RDCs inspect drain cleaning across Chennai
de85488919f9cd0a.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 12:58 am IST - Chennai GCC Region Deputy Commissioner (Central) H.R. Kaushik inspecting the precautionary arrangements for the Northeast monsoon in Kodambakkam Zone on Saturday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement While the city braces for more rain, the Regional Deputy Commissioners (RDCs) of the three regions of Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) inspected pumping stations, stormwater drains, canals and subways, reviewed ongoing drain works and checked arrangements for National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) personnel deployed for rescue operations on Saturday (October 24). RDC (North) Swetha Suman inspected basic facilities and food supplies for NDRF personnel stationed at the Chief Minister’s Marriage Hall on Anna Pillai Street in Royapuram for rescue operations during the monsoon. RDC (Central) H.R. Kaushik inspected a motor pump-equipped pumping station on Duraisamy Road and the Parangusapuram subway in Kodambakkam Zone, besides Nandanam Canal and the children’s playground area on Puthuth theru in West Saidapet. He also reviewed precautionary measures at a Tamil Nadu Urban Habitat Development Board residential area on Pachaiyappa Veerasamy Street in Ward 97. He inspected desilting of stormwater drains on Railway Border Road and ongoing drain works on Aziz Nagar Street in West Mambalam. Officials were asked to expedite the works and maintain continuous surveillance of canals and subways. RDC (South) Aftab Rasool inspected integrated stormwater drain works on Old Mahabalipuram Road in Ward 178, Adyar Zone, and reviewed precautionary measures in other parts of the southern region. MLAs, zonal officers and officials were present. 0e8b07ea362666d3.title: Association questions DPH over gag order for govt. doctors
0e8b07ea362666d3.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 01:00 am IST - CHENNAI The Service Doctors and Post Graduates Association (SDPGA) has questioned the Director of Public Health (DPH) and Preventive Medicine for issuing a gag order on government doctors. The DPH had recently issued a circular stating that the employees of the directorate should not criticise the policies, schemes, and actions of the Central or State governments in public, through media, or at public meetings. The association asked in a statement issued whether the DPH had passed the gag order to prevent government doctors from questioning him on social media about Government Order (G.O.) 354, relating to pay and promotions. The G.O., issued in 2009, contains a clause for review in 2012, and thereafter every five years. But it was not reviewed in 2017 and 2022. In January 2023, an order was issued by the Additional Chief Secretary (Health), appointing the DPH as head of the committee to review the G.O., but it was not done, the association said. The SDPGA sought clarification from the DPH on whether the services of government doctors were regularised on the completion of one year. It said there were delays exceeding five years, forcing women doctors to struggle to obtain maternity leave benefits. It also flagged the delays in promotions for doctors due to administrative inefficiencies. The association said that when such delays continue to affect doctors, passing gag orders was unacceptable. It urged the Health Minister and Health Secretary to review G.O. 354 and fill all vacant pay band-4 posts on a war footing. 438c5041672ff967.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 01:05 am IST Security personnel keeping vigil outside Jamia Millia Islamia. Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI) on Saturday shifted all classes online and said the campus gates, libraries and canteens would remain closed until further notice to ensure “student safety” amid an ongoing protest demanding the restoration of student union elections. The decision followed a failed attempt by the administration to “persuade” the protesters to call off their agitation, the university said in a statement. The protesting students and the All India Students’ Association (AISA) alleged that the university staff tried to forcibly remove them from the protest site on Saturday afternoon while police deployment outside the campus increased. The university said the decision to move classes online with immediate effect was a precautionary measure taken in view of the prevailing situation and to ensure the safety and security of students. In a notice issued on Saturday, the office of the Dean of Students’ Welfare directed students to follow their online class schedules and avoid visiting the campus until further notice. Several students have been on a hunger strike since October 12, demanding the restoration of student union elections, which were last held in 2006 before the union was dissolved following campus violence. JMI had constituted a high-level committee on October 18 to engage with the protesting students and look into their demands. Mantasha, an AISA member, alleged that university staff attempted to forcibly remove the protesters while faculty members watched without intervening. “None of the professors intervened when students were being dragged. 92a920725b63b3c6.summary: Updated - October 25, 2026 01:04 am IST - Chennai Persons with disabilities are disappointed that a government order for free travel in buses has still not been formulated. Since its announcement in the State Budget in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly in August, 2026. While women with disabilities are automatically covered under the Vetri Payanam scheme where women and transpersons can travel in State buses for free, men with disabilities have not been included. The announcement made by the Social Welfare and Women Empowerment Minister K. Jegadeshwari expanded it to persons with disabilities and their companions with a UDID card. However, as there has been no G.O. published in this regard, men with disabilities continue to wait to avail themselves of the scheme. Nethrodaya founder C. Govindakrishnan said, “The G.O. for free bus travel for persons with disabilities has not been issued even after 53 days of the announcement. aa9f629f06beb7a9.title: BJP says textbooks meet quality norms; AAP seeks lab testing
aa9f629f06beb7a9.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 01:00 am IST Delhi Education Minister Ashish Sood on Saturday said the government followed the prescribed process in procuring NCERT textbooks for schools at ₹28 per copy against ₹55 under the previous dispensation. Responding to Aam Aadmi Party’s (AAP) allegations of “substandard” quality textbooks supplied to students, the Minister said a review has been ordered. AAP challenged Chief Minister Rekha Gupta to send the books to a laboratory for testing. Addressing a press conference, Mr. Sood said, “AAP is alleging a scam to stay relevant and misleading the public. Despite inflation, the BJP government has capped the price of textbooks for government schools that was almost double during the AAP’s tenure.” Following a review, strict penal action will be initiated against those involved in spreading deliberate falsehoods, he added. On Friday, AAP’s Delhi chief Saurabh Bharadwaj alleged irregularities in the BJP government’s school textbook printing and tendering process. He claimed that the quality of the paper used in the textbooks was substandard. In response, Mr. Sood displayed a copy of the tender document and said the government had followed the prescribed process. Challenging Mr. Sood to make public the file in which his department officials have moved for full payment to the vendors, Mr. Bharadwaj said, “The Minister has not answered why these books have very poor printing quality and use cheap 60 GSM paper, while the tender specified standard 80 GSM paper.” Published - October 25, 2026 01:00 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. d3ef12dcd1709824.title: Chhath ghats must remain clean and well-organised: Delhi CM
d3ef12dcd1709824.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 01:00 am IST Chief Minister Rekha Gupta taking stock of preparations for Chhath Puja at a ghat along the Munak Canal on Saturday. | Photo Credit: PTI Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday inspected the ongoing construction of a Chhath ghat in the Munak Canal area near Prem Bari Bridge. She said the ghat would provide devotees with better facilities to offer prayers and a clean, beautiful and well-organised space ahead of Chhath Puja. Directing officials on site to ensure that the work was completed on time, Ms. Gupta said the government aimed to complete the construction of all such ghats and related development works before Chhath Puja. “Chhath is deeply connected with Delhi’s cultural identity and public faith. A large number of devotees offer prayers to the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya during this sacred festival. The government, therefore, has a responsibility to provide better facilities for devotees and ensure that places of worship remain clean and well-organised.” During the visit, she reviewed the progress of various works and directed officials to ensure proper lighting during the festival, celebrated predominantly by Purvanchalis, people from eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and parts of Jharkhand, living in the national capital. She also issued instructions on waste management . “There must be no accumulation of garbage on roads and footpaths, foul smells or haphazard waste collection under any circumstances. A proper system for waste collection and disposal must be developed,” she added. The government, therefore, has a responsibility to provide better facilities for devotees and ensure that places of worship remain clean and well-organised.” During the visit, she reviewed the progress of various works and directed officials to ensure proper lighting during the festival, celebrated predominantly by Purvanchalis, people from eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and parts of Jharkhand, living in the national capital. She also issued instructions on waste management . “There must be no accumulation of garbage on roads and footpaths, foul smells or haphazard waste collection under any circumstances. A proper system for waste collection and disposal must be developed,” she added. 648584b7d7a73d75.title: Law and order situation in T.N. is in an extremely dire state, says Palaniswami
648584b7d7a73d75.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 12:22 am IST - CHENNAI AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami. | Photo Credit: E. LAKSHMI NARAYANAN AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami has alleged that the law and order situation in Tamil Nadu was in an extremely dire state. He listed several incidents reflecting the prevailing law and order conditions and questioned the inaction of the government. “Reports that a woman was hacked to death by an unidentified intruder inside her house near Sathankulam, a young boy who sought a lift went missing near Uthangarai in Krishnagiri district, and a student died due to caste discrimination at a government-aided school in Coimbatore are deeply shocking. What action has been taken over the death of a student due to caste discrimination under this regime, which merely invokes ‘social justice’ in its rhetoric?” Mr. Palaniswami asked. Pointing out that the young girl who went missing in Gingee has still not been traced, he asked whether the government had not even suspected that the repeated disappearances of children might be following a pattern. Mr. Palaniswami urged the government to conduct an intensive investigation into the disappearances of children from all angles and demanded stringent action regarding the incidents in Coimbatore and Sathankulam. 6dd8e6d9aea6ab24.title: P.B. Siddhartha College signs MoU with Tech In to enhance students’ employability
6dd8e6d9aea6ab24.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 11:54 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA P.B. Siddhartha College of Arts and Science, Vijayawada, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Tech In Process Private Limited to enhance students’ employability, technical skills and industry exposure. The three-year agreement was signed by college principal Meka Ramesh and Managing Director of Tech In Gubbala Srinivasa Rao on Ssaturday. Director Vemuri Baburao and dean P. Rajesh C. Jampala said the collaboration aims to bridge the gap between academic learning and industry requirements by providing students with practical knowledge and industry-oriented training. Under the MoU, Tech In Process Private Limited will extend technical support and guidance for industry-focused training programmes, student internships, academic and industry projects, resume preparation, conferences, workshops, faculty development programmes, and career guidance and counselling. The partnership may also include mock interviews, aptitude training, soft-skills development and job-readiness programmes to prepare students for employment opportunities and meet the evolving demands of the industry. The initiative is expected to strengthen industry-academia collaboration and provide students with greater exposure to professional practices and workplace expectations. MBA faculty member Rahman, the placement officer, and Computer Science faculty member Kavuru Sridhar participated in the programme. 7395cfa99f03e793.title: Six election officials removed in U.P. after SP flags voter list errors
7395cfa99f03e793.summary: Updated - October 25, 2026 01:02 am IST - LUCKNOW The Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) of Uttar Pradesh on Saturday removed five Booth Level Officers (BLOs) and a computer assistant from election duties following an investigation into voter list discrepancies in Azamgarh. Action has also been initiated against three senior electoral registration officials. The orders come after the Samajwadi Party (SP) held a press conference on October 15, alleging that a voter named ‘Vikas Yadav’ was listed 10 times in the voter list for the Azamgarh assembly constituency (347). Following a detailed probe by the District Election Officer of Azamgarh, authorities found that the name “Vikas Yadav” appeared 13 times in Hindi on the rolls. According to the CEO’s office, one of the entries belongs to a voter of the same name and age from the Chauri Chaura constituency in Gorakhpur district. Deletion proceedings have been initiated for two other duplicate entries. The investigation revealed that the remaining 11 entries actually belong to 11 different individuals living in Azamgarh. Officials have now filled out Form-8 to correct the names and personal details of 10 of these individuals, ensuring only the actual Vikas Yadav remains on the roll under that name. In response to the clerical lapses, the CEO directed the immediate removal of the responsible computer assistant and five BLOs from voter registration work. Authorities have also issued notices regarding the termination of their services. Furthermore, the state election body has ordered charge sheets and departmental action against the then Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) and two Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs) for negligence and poor supervision. The three senior officials face potential action under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. 05d719958793295c.title: PSGIM students use management learning for community benefit
05d719958793295c.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 11:49 pm IST - COIMBATORE During the National Management Week 2026, around 250 students of PSG Institute of Management (PSGIM), Coimbatore, will take management learning beyond the classroom and into the community through initiatives focusing on waste management, rabies awareness, and preventing pollution caused by indiscriminate poster pasting, under the overarching theme of ‘Clean and Safe City’. Observed from October 26 to 31 under the aegis of the Association of Indian Management Schools (AIMS-New Delhi), the initiatives reflect a simple yet meaningful belief: building a better city is a shared responsibility. During the week, students will engage with communities at more than 30 identified waste hotspots across Coimbatore. By promoting waste segregation at source and responsible disposal, they will encourage everyday practices that protect the environment and improve neighbourhoods for everyone. The initiative will also highlight the connection between unmanaged waste and street dogs. Discarded food and other waste can attract dogs to public spaces, increase the risk of conflict and create unhealthy conditions for people and animals. Students will also conduct rabies awareness activities across 30 identified locations in the city in association with the Humane Animal Society (HAS), to promote rabies prevention, safe interactions with street dogs and humane animal care. These activities will reinforce the importance of keeping public spaces free of food waste and other refuse that can attract dogs. Students will also work with NGOs, including Olirum Kovai, on poster-related interventions and community engagement in locations such as Vellalore. Through these efforts, they will contribute to making public spaces cleaner and more welcoming. Through these initiatives, PSGIM aims to nurture future managers who recognise that leadership is defined not only by professional achievements, but also by the willingness to understand community need

8aecefea472c8045.title: Andhra Pradesh braces for very severe cyclonic storm; landfall likely between Bapatla and Vizag on October 28
8aecefea472c8045.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 01:20 am IST - VIJAYAWADA Dark clouds over the Kandula Obul Reddy Reservoir in Prakasam district on Saturday. | Photo Credit: KOMMURI SRINIVAS The cyclonic storm brewing over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said. It is likely to be the second highest in terms of intensity. Last year’s Montha was classified as a ‘severe cyclonic storm’. The maximum sustained wind speed associated with a very severe cyclonic storm is likely to be between 118 km per hour and 221 km per hour. During Montha, the wind speed recorded at Machilipatnam was 65 kmph, while the wind speed this time may go up to 130 kmph, weather experts said. According to the IMD bulletin released at 9.30 p.m. on Saturday, the well-marked low-pressure area formed over the east-central and adjoining south-east Bay of Bengal on Saturday morning concentrated into a depression by the evening. The depression lay centred over the same region, which is about 510 km off the coast of Andaman Islands, 820 km off Vishakhapatnam coast, 910 km off Kakinada coast, 1,020 km off Machilipatnam cost and 1,100 km off Bapatla coast. The weather system is likely to intensify into a deep depression and then gradually recurve towards the east-central and adjoining south-east Bay of Bengal on Sunday. It is very likely to intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the east-central and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal by Monday morning, and further intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over west-central Bay of Bengal around October 27. Thereafter, it is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and reach the west-central Bay of Bengal near the Andhra Pradesh coast around October 28. 1dd7c7fba6d94005.title: Man arrested with 66 kg of firecrackers in Rohini
1dd7c7fba6d94005.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 12:58 am IST - New Delhi Police found that the accused brought the firecrackers for sale without a valid licence. | Photo Credit: SUSHIL KUMAR VERMA A 33-year-old man was arrested for allegedly storing and transporting 66 kg of firecrackers illegally in the Vijay Vihar area of Rohini, police said on Saturday. Police personnel on patrol spotted a three-wheeler parked outside a park on the night of October 20. When questioned, the driver failed to give a satisfactory response, police said. "On checking the vehicle, various types of firecrackers were found inside," a senior police officer said. The driver was identified as Vijender Kumar, a resident of Rampura. During questioning, police found that the accused had brought the firecrackers for sale without a valid licence. The firecrackers and the three-wheeler were seized. An FIR was registered on October 21 under Section 9B of the Explosives Act and Section 323 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Further investigation is under way, police said. 3ef745fde0ee5413.title: My father pushes me to become a better player, says Tagenarine
3ef745fde0ee5413.summary: Updated - October 25, 2026 01:28 am IST - Chennai Tagenarine had a stint at the Super Kings Academy recently. | Photo Credit: AFP Every time Tagenarine Chanderpaul makes his way into the middle, he carries the weight of a surname that is etched in cricket fanatics’ hearts. No day on the pitch passes by without the mention of his father Shivnarine Chanderpaul, a legendary figure in the world game. Unfortunately for the West Indies opener, he has not kicked on in his Test career after entering the international arena with promise. Four years into his journey with the Men in Maroon, Tagenarine has come to terms with the constant comparisons with his dad but is striving to create a name for himself. “Wherever I go, people expect me to perform as good as him. But I cannot be him, I can only be myself,” the 30-year-old told The Hindu recently. “He was a great player, but I just try to be myself. As an individual, I do the best I can.” While Tagenarine wades through challenges, Shivnarine, as both a father and mentor, attempts to make the former’s path easier. “He shares his knowledge and experience to make me a better player. He is a very competitive and serious guy. He keeps pushing me to get better,” said the southpaw. Tagenarine, lucky enough to be taught a masterclass on a regular basis, knows where he is lacking: he has just one ton and two half-centuries in 15 long-format matches (758 runs). “I need to be more consistent, convert starts into big scores. Sometimes, you get comfortable in the middle and get out. But Test cricket is tough... there is no time to relax,” the top-order batter added. His stint at the Super Kings Academy — in the company of West Indies red-ball teammates — may be the launchpad for bigger things ahead. “I always believe in putting in the work, so hopefully I can reap the rewards of it”. 97958a5bcc68fac9.title: Students mark 90th anniversary of Temple Entry Proclamation
97958a5bcc68fac9.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 12:02 am IST - Thiruvananthapuram A copy of the Temple Entry Proclamation being distributed by students of Government Boys Higher Secondary School, Karamana, and ward councillor Karamana Ajith to autorickshaw drivers Students of Government Boys Higher Secondary School, Karamana, marked the 90th anniversary of the historic Temple Entry Proclamation of 1936 by distributing copies of the proclamation in houses and public spaces on Saturday. The Temple Entry Proclamation was issued by Chithira Thirunal Balarama Varma, former king of the erstwhile Travancore kingdom, on November 12, 1936, in the wake of the social reformation under way then. It opened the doors of Hindu temples in the State to marginalised communities and drew the attention of the entire nation to Travancore. A copy of the proclamation in possession of the Archives department was received by students and teachers of the school, and then distributed to houses, residents’ associations, shops and commercial establishments, and libraries for display. Through autorickshaw drivers, the proclamation reached passengers too. The proclamation’s 90th anniversary also saw nonagenarians Gopalakrishnan, a retired income tax official, and his wife Sarojam, who live near the school, being felicitated with the proclamation and a ponnada by class V student Shikha and ward councillor Karama Ajith. At a time when marginalisation was re-emerging, the proclamation taught lessons, head teacher Mini. Y said. Principal Bilu V.B. was present. As part of the year-long celebrations, a proclamation rally from East Fort to Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple, cultural meets with historians, trips to memorials for reformation leaders, quiz, and other events will be organised, PTA representatives said. cde6ab97d8e39e41.title: US administrations asked Musk to switch Starlink on or off in multiple countries: Report
cde6ab97d8e39e41.summary: The administrations of former US President Joe Biden and current President Donald Trump have repeatedly asked Elon Musk's SpaceX to activate or restrict its Starlink satellite internet service in different countries, highlighting Washington's growing reliance on private technology companies to implement foreign policy objectives, according to a Reuters report citing six former senior US officials. The requests, made before the recent restrictions on Ukraine's military access to SpaceX satellite communications, included disabling Starlink to prevent Iran-backed militias in Yemen and Lebanon from using the service and activating it to provide internet access in Iran and Ukraine, Reuters reported. During Biden's presidency, US officials sought to restrict the service's availability to certain militant groups while also requesting its activation to support internet access in Iran and military communications in Ukraine, four former officials told Reuters . The Trump administration similarly asked Musk, SpaceX's chief executive, to make Starlink available in Iran following US-Israeli strikes in 2025 and 2026. The objective was to strengthen internet connectivity and communications for anti-government protesters, the report said. The recent restrictions on Ukraine's access to SpaceX satellite services have renewed concerns about the relationship between the US government and Musk, whose company operates satellite communication systems considered important to the US military and its allies. The earlier requests by both administrations illustrate how Washington has increasingly depended on a private company to support diplomatic, political and military objectives abroad. The restrictions affecting Ukraine have also caused concern among European officials, some of whom argue that Europe needs to develop independent military satellite communication capabilities. 3c1cb8664e9eed7e.title: Delhi govt begins identifying ineligible old-age pension beneficiaries
3c1cb8664e9eed7e.summary: Delhi government has started a verification drive to identify and weed out ineligible beneficiaries of its old age pension scheme covering around 4.4 lakh senior citizens, officials said on Saturday. The verification process was to begin earlier, but it was halted as permission for Aadhaar authentication of the beneficiaries via a third party was not allowed. Now, the third party is carrying out door-to-door biometric beneficiary verification after receiving permission, said a senior functionary of the Delhi government. "The verification exercise will conclude in three months and we expect to create 20-25 per cent vacancies out of the total 4.4 lakh beneficiaries after weeding out the deceased and duplicate beneficiaries getting other government assistance besides the old age pension," he said. The government currently provides a monthly pension of Rs 2,000 to senior citizens aged between 60 and 69 years, while those aged 70 years and above are entitled to Rs 2,500 per month. Earl

29d990236d4e2b58.title: Old values, new avenues: On India-Poland ties
29d990236d4e2b58.summary: Updated - October 26, 2026 01:03 am IST Sixteen years after his visit as Poland’s Prime Minister, Donald Tusk’s travel to Delhi and Bengaluru last week was to signal a renewed desire to work closely with India. Mr. Tusk’s visit, two months ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s trip to Brussels to sign the India-European Union (EU) Free Trade Agreement , indicated one part of his agenda. Both sides agreed that it was time to develop trade, currently worth just $6 billion, to double its size by 2030. Mr. Tusk’s last visit to India was in 2017, as President of the European Council for the EU-India summit, and it is fitting that his trip was just as the FTA is finalised and ratified after years of delays. Another area of increased India-Poland collaboration is in technology, AI and defence hardware, critical minerals, renewable and nuclear energy given Poland’s expertise in the last few decades and India’s capacity for scale. As the EU’s sixth largest economy, Poland has officially crossed the $1 trillion GDP (nominal terms) milestone. Its $120-billion-dollar tech economy is also gaining global interest. A large part of Polish machinery and parts is exported to Germany, which in turn has a growing share of Indian imports, and India could consider more trilateral collaborations for manufacturing and mining technology. The two sides agreed to establish a “Defence Industry Dialogue” and explore a dialogue on counter-terrorism cooperation. Finally, the Modi-Tusk talks focused on geopolitics, particularly the ongoing war in Ukraine. The war’s impact, especially on the Global South, has been a concern for India, and the Modi government’s initiative to work on an agreement acceptable to Kyiv and Moscow on grain exports and seafarers’ safety was discussed. The four-pronged plan, announced by External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar during his September visit to Warsaw, won Mr. Tusk’s support. 4e56639fd7539d80.title: Delhi govt. to clear ₹2 Lakh higher education aid for youth leaving care homes
4e56639fd7539d80.summary: Updated - October 26, 2026 12:30 am IST - NEW DELHI The Delhi government is set to introduce Individual Aftercare Plans (IAPs) for teenagers exiting Child Care Institutions (CCIs) at 18, based on their specific circumstances, requirements and rehabilitation needs, under the proposed ‘Aftercare Scheme for Young Persons’, a senior government official said on Sunday. Under the scheme, the eligible beneficiaries will receive up to ₹2 lakh for higher education and ₹60,000 for vocational training. The scheme is likely to be approved by the Delhi Cabinet soon, according to a senior government official. In May, the Women and Child Development Department proposed a budget of ₹3.50 crore for the implementation of the scheme for the current financial year. The government also plans to allocate ₹5 crore from the Chief Minister’s Development Fund to strengthen the juvenile justice system, including the aftercare scheme, the official said. The government is also seeking Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) partnerships to provide mentorship, additional financial resources, and other forms of support. The scheme will be implemented under a two-tier structure where the District Aftercare Committees will assess eligibility, map out individual plans, and track beneficiary progress, and the State Aftercare Committees will oversee the implementation, fund disbursement and policy reforms. “There will also be a provision for financial assistance, subject to the recommendation of the District Aftercare Committee, for eligible young people who have no income or insufficient income,” the official said. “A database of individuals eligible for aftercare will be maintained and these individuals will be recommended to various Delhi government departments for internships, contractual roles, or outsourced employment opportunities, provided they meet the prescribed eligibility criteria,” the official added. Under the scheme, the government will start preparations when a child in a CCI is 15 years

80d949e9a1642cc2.title: Jantar Mantar to ‘Dilli Chalo’, protest challenges power
80d949e9a1642cc2.summary: Updated - October 26, 2026 01:33 am IST ‘The demonstrations that have gathered momentum since early October mark a significant shift in Opposition politics’ | Photo Credit: AFP Over the past few months, three distinct streams of dissent have emerged in India: the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) -led agitation, actions by left-wing student organisations, and campaigns spearheaded by the Congress and the INDIA bloc. Although these streams have largely evolved independently, their paths have increasingly converged around shared concerns about democracy, dissent, citizens’ rights and the fairness of the political and electoral process. Their significance lies in their capacity to bring disparate grievances and constituencies together in a broader challenge to the government. The first phase of the agitation unfolded at Jantar Mantar in June and July, focusing on education reform, the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) paper leaks and demands for the (then) Education Minister’s resignation. The CJP played a pivotal role in galvanising public discontent, drawing large numbers of young people into the streets, where they articulated their grievances through a distinctive blend of humour, creativity and youthful energy. This indicated that dissatisfaction with the ruling establishment extended well beyond the established Opposition parties, with the political disaffection of this constituency having been seriously underestimated. The Minister’s eventual resignation gave the movement fresh impetus, demonstrating that sustained public pressure could secure political concessions. 0d9cfd4faa4dca37.title: Free medical camp held for construction workers in Vellore
0d9cfd4faa4dca37.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:04 pm IST - VELLORE A medical camp being held for construction workers to commemorate the birthday of G.V. Selvam, vice-president, VIT. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Thalaimurai Peravai, Vellore, in association with Sri Narayani Hospital and Research Centre organised a medical camp for construction workers on Sunday to commemorate the birthday of G.V. Selvam, vice-president, Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT), in recognition of his commitment to social welfare, community development, and public service. According to a press release, G. Ramakrishnan, Politburo Member, Communist Party of India (Marxist), inaugurated the camp in the presence of Mr. Selvam, Katpadi MLA M. Sudhakar, and N. Balaji, director, Sri Narayani Group. In his address, Mr. Selvam highlighted the contribution of construction workers to the infrastructural development of the country. “The medical camp has been organised to emphasise the importance of ensuring the physical and mental well-being of construction workers, who play a vital role in nation-building,” he said. More than 600 workers participated in the day-long camp that provided general medical check-ups, cardiac evaluations, dental check-ups, and orthopaedic assessments, along with Siddha and Ayurveda treatments, the release said. 889e3b8e738f2bb3.title: ISKCON unveils 800-kg robotic elephant in Visakhapatnam
889e3b8e738f2bb3.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:56 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Devotees gather around Ranga, a fully mechanised elephant, during its ceremonial unveiling as part of ISKCON Visakhapatnam’s Sharad Purnima celebrations at MGM Park on Beach Road on Sunday. | Photo Credit: V. RAJU A moving robotic elephant named Ranga, weighing 800 kg, was unveiled on Sunday at MGM Park on Beach Road in front of a large gathering of devotees during ISKCON Visakhapatnam’s Sharad Purnima celebrations. The organisers described it as the first-of-its-kind in Andhra Pradesh. ISKCON Governing Body chairman Madhusevita Prabhu inaugurated the elephant. Branch president Samba Das Prabhu and Nitai Sevini Mataji led the programme. According to ISKCON, the elephant was brought from Thrissur in Kerala and donated by PETA India. A ‘Nauka Vihar’ (boat festival), Bhajan Clubbing and the ‘Kartika Deepotsavam’ followed ‘sankirtan’ of the Hare Krishna Maha Mantra. CMR Group managing director Mavuri Venkata Ramana, Andhra University former Vice-Chancellor G.S.N. Raju, Simhachalam Devasthanam chief priest G. Srinivasacharyulu, and Pydah Educational Institutions chairman Pydah Krishna Prasad were also present on the ocassion. b7cb5b650b3eebd0.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:26 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM A total of 15 candidates are contesting for the post of Mayor in the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) general elections–2026, Mayor Election Returning Officer B. Dayanidhi said in a release on Sunday. A total of 29 nominations were received for the GVMC Mayor’s post, of which 8 nominations were rejected, while the remaining 21 nominations were found valid. During the withdrawal of nominations on October 21, six candidates withdrew their nominations, he said. Subsequently, in the notification issued by the Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission on October 22, 2026, it was directed that the final list of candidates contesting for the post of Mayor in the GVMC elections be announced on October 25, 2026. Accordingly, 15 candidates remain in the fray for the Mayor’s post, the Returning Officer stated. Prominent candidates among them include Mukka Sravani from Telugu Desam Party (TDP), Varudu Kalyani from YSRCP (YSRCP), Devara Naga Sunanda Devi from Indian National Congress (INC), K. Keerthana Grace from Bahujan Samaj Party, and Nammi Bhavani from Bharata Chaitanya Yuvajana Party. 175bbc032de8866f.summary: Published - October 26, 2026 01:01 am IST - New Delhi Police personnel outside the government school where a 17-year-old student was found with severe burns. | Photo Credit: ANI The Delhi Commission for Protection of Child Rights (DCPCR) on Sunday sought an inquiry report within two weeks from the Directorate of Education over the death of a 17-year-old Class 12 student who was found with severe burns at a government school in east Delhi’s Krishna Nagar on Saturday. The girl was found behind the school’s guard room after school authorities heard cries from the area. She was taken to Dr. Hedgewar Arogya Sansthan, where she was declared dead on arrival. According to police, a water bottle used to carry petrol was recovered from the spot. Taking cognisance of media reports, the commission raised concerns about student safety, questioning how the girl managed to bring an inflammable substance into the school without being noticed. “The content of the news report, if true, are disturbing and raise serious concern on the safety of children inside the school premises. The incident as a whole has resulted in violation of child rights on account of negligence of public servants,” the commission stated in its notice. ff1a379985d43bb0.title: U.S. immigration restrictions may outlast Trump
ff1a379985d43bb0.summary: Updated - October 26, 2026 01:12 am IST ‘As the bipartisan focus on immigration reform continues, the issue is likely to sustain as a friction point in India-U.S. relations.’ | Photo Credit: AP In its second term, the Donald Trump administration has been active in restricting legal immigration to the United States. The administration’s attempt to impose a $100,000 payment requirement on certain new H-1B petitions, changes to visa renewal procedures, the introduction of a wage-weighted selection system, and the latest suspensions of the Program Electronic Review Management (PERM) process are cases in point, disproportionately impacting Indian immigrants and firms. It is tempting to read these developments as a product of the Trump administration alone, but they reflect deeper political interests that are likely to survive post-Trump. Indian nationals account for 70% of H-1B visa approvals, with one-fifth of the visas going to employees of Indian-origin companies. This means that, as the bipartisan focus on immigration reform continues, the issue is likely to sustain as a friction point in India-U.S. relations. 60625e20732b6626.title: Two feared trapped after building collapse in Delhi's Harsh Vihar
60625e20732b6626.summary: Updated - October 26, 2026 12:51 am IST - New Delhi NDRF personnel at the site after a slab of a house under construction collapsed in Milan Garden in Harsh Vihar area on Sunday. | Photo Credit: - Two men, aged 60 and 36, are suspected to be trapped after roof slabs collapsed during construction in north-east Delhi’s Harsh Vihar on Sunday evening, police said. The collapse occurred in Milan Garden as an additional floor was being built on an old, single-storey house on a 200-square-yard plot, said an officer. A resident said a newly laid slab gave way over an older slab. The Delhi Fire Services received a call at 6.46 p.m. and sent five fire tenders. Teams from the National Disaster Response Force, police, Civil Defence and Delhi Disaster Management Authority joined the rescue efforts. “Two people are suspected to be trapped, but there is no confirmation yet,” Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Sandeep Lamba said. No casualties had been reported till the time the report went to the press. “Their family members suspect that they are trapped as their mobile phones are not reachable,” the officer said. Some relatives alleged that rescue work was slow and tried to remove the debris themselves. Later in the evening, Ministers Ashish Sood and Kapil Mishra also visited the building collapse site. Police said, the cause of the collapse and the status of construction approvals are yet to be established. 6f7f0097fe010712.title: Wicked surprise: On the northeast monsoon
6f7f0097fe010712.summary: Updated - October 26, 2026 12:48 am IST As India recovers from a monsoon-deficit year , there is both hope and trepidation regarding the prospects for that ‘other monsoon’, or the ‘northeast monsoon’ . While contributing only around a quarter of India’s annual rainfall, it is largely focused on the south-east peninsula regions of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, coastal Andhra Pradesh, Rayalaseema, south interior Karnataka and Keralam. The southwest monsoon, influenced by a strengthening El Niño , has already left its desiccating mark. Rainfall from June-September was 759.4 mm against 868.6 mm, a 12.6% deficit, the driest in 11 years. This has impacted kharif sowing and is reflected in food inflation. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that this year, the northeast monsoon rainfall, spanning October to December, would likely be ‘normal’ , meaning in line with a 50-year average and within a 12% error window. Most parts of the country, it said, are expected to receive below-normal rainfall, except some areas of northwest India and southern parts of peninsular India, where rainfall is likely to be normal to above-normal. The wide error window, however, is far less precise than its forecasts for the southwest monsoon with its margin of 5%, and can sometimes make the northeast monsoon the bearer of nasty surprises. a8dfb0f1c174b461.title: Three North Andhra districts step up cyclone preparedness
a8dfb0f1c174b461.summary: Updated - October 25, 2026 11:42 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Fishermen use an earthmover to haul a boat ashore at Pedda Jalaripeta in Visakhapatnam on Sunday, as a cyclonic storm is forecast over the Bay of Bengal. | Photo Credit: V RAJU The administrations of Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli and Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR) districts have stepped up preparedness on Sunday by setting up control rooms and readying relief centres, as a deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a cyclone, according to the India Meteorological Department. Visakhapatnam Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore, reviewing arrangements at a videoconference with Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) Commissioner Ketan Garg said the impact could be as severe as that of Cyclone Montha . He directed officers to remain at their places of work. A control room has been set up at the Collectorate, with others planned to be opened at the GVMC office and at zonal and mandal levels. Officials were instructed to monitor reservoir levels, alert residents living on hill slopes and keep relief centres ready. Mr. Garg said that people had earlier been evacuated from seven areas. The Collector directed officials to arrange for the shifting of those residents again. Tree-cutting machines are to be stationed in advance, while the GVMC and APEPDCL were asked to ensure uninterrupted power supply. Fishing boats on the beach at Pedda Jalaripeta in Visakhapatnam on Sunday, ahead of the forecast cyclonic storm. | Photo Credit: V RAJU Ambulances, medical teams and medicines are to be kept ready. Pregnant women nearing delivery are to be moved to hospitals. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea and, tourists and residents were warned against visiting beaches. Special officers have been appointed for each constituency and mandal. The round-the-clock Collectorate control room can be reached on 0891-2590100 and 0891-2590102, said Special Deputy Collector and District Project Manager

8c1ac680ad45562b.title: Harmanpreet, Deepti on fire as India seals emphatic series win against Zimbabwe
8c1ac680ad45562b.summary: Updated - October 26, 2026 12:21 am IST - VADODARA Harmanpreet and Deepti put the Zimbabwe attack to the sword. | Photo Credit: BCCI Picture this. Harmanpreet Kaur and Deepti Sharma scored centuries to power India to a big win. Now ask yourself: which of the two blazed her way to triple figures? If your gut said Harmanpreet, it failed you. On a sweltering Sunday at the BCA Stadium in Kotambi, the second ODI against Zimbabwe turned the script on its head. A restrained Harmanpreet played the artisan while Deepti played destroyer, with their record-breaking 153-run fifth-wicket stand laying the foundation of India’s 121-run win and unassailable 2-0 lead. India was stuttering at 19 for two in the third over — Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma both undone by Nomvelo Sibanda’s short-ball ploy — when Harmanpreet joined Pratika Rawal. Pratika, fresh from a hundred in the first ODI, and Harmanpreet added 124 off 118 balls. The former looked set for another ton when Nyasha Gwanzura deceived her with a change of pace. Tejal Hasabnis followed soon after. But Harmanpreet remained unfazed, aided by a fearless Deepti who arrived as if stepping in for a net session. As many as 32 of the pair’s first 47 runs came through Deepti’s audacious shots on the leg-side while Harmanpreet whipped out a catalogue of puritanical drives and cuts on the off-side. When the century came, celebrations oddly didn’t. Neither did tears, like the 91 she scored in the third T20I had drawn out of her. Deepti, too, eventually braved a slowdown to reach her second ODI century in the final over — nine years after her first — helping India set an intimidating 329-run target. Modester Mupachikwa’s sprightly start, despite losing Loryn Phiri early, gave Zimbabwe hope. With support from Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano, the Lady Chevrons got to 100 in just 19 overs, helped by India’s worrying inability to take wickets, especially the seamers. Sayali Satghare finally succeeded in breaching Mugeri-Tiripano’s defence. Left-ar

96cfa179ef2c8f3f.title: APSCHE to hold State-level AISHE workshop for university nodal officers in Vijayawada on October 26
96cfa179ef2c8f3f.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:36 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA The Andhra Pradesh State Council of Higher Education (APSCHE) will organise a State-level workshop on the All India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE) for university nodal officers from Andhra Pradesh on Monday (October 26, 2026), in collaboration with the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, Government of India. A statement issued on Sunday (October 25) said the workshop will be held at Hotel Fortune Murali Park in Vijayawada. Principal Secretary, Higher Education Department (FAC), Andhra Pradesh J. Syamala Rao, will be the chief guest, while AISHE resource persons from New Delhi N.M. Biswas, Assistant Director; Shubhda Sharma, Senior Statistical Officer and Shivam Pandey, Programmer, will conduct expert sessions. The workshop aims to facilitate interaction between university nodal officers and AISHE experts, address issues related to the survey and improve coordination in implementing AISHE-related activities across higher education institutions in the State. 45c3a1ff3a7ccf7d.title: A Korean cultural evening in Hyderabad, with a distinctly Telangana touch
45c3a1ff3a7ccf7d.summary: Updated - October 26, 2026 12:32 am IST - HYDERABAD Atti classic vocal crossover performance at the 'K Harmony Festa' at Shilpakala Vedika in Hyderabad on Sunday. | Photo Credit: SIDDHANT THAKUR What happens when the rhythms of Korean culture meet the beats of Telangana’s traditional drums? At Shilpakala Vedika here on Sunday, the answer unfolded through a lively mix of music, dance, martial arts and cultural exchange, as Korea Culture Day 2026 brought the traditions of two countries together on one stage. From afternoon, stalls selling Korean products drew curious visitors, with crowds gathering around them to explore a slice of Korean culture. As the evening approached, the buzz moved towards the auditorium, where hundreds of people began assembling from 5 p.m., eager to witness the performances lined up for the occasion. Inside, the anticipation gave way to a celebration that travelled between two cultures, from the precision and power of Korean martial arts to the vigorous movements of Telangana’s traditional dances. The programme began around 5.30 p.m. with an address by Lee Seong-ho, Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to India, who welcomed the audience to Hyderabad and spoke of the cultural ties that the event hoped to strengthen. Drawing a connection between Diwali, India’s festival of lights, and Chuseok, Korea’s harvest festival, Mr. Lee spoke about the shared values underlying celebrations in both countries: family, togetherness, gratitude and hope for the future. Though the traditions may differ, he said, the emotions they evoke are remarkably similar. Cultural exchanges, he added, help people discover just how much they have in common. 08a71a25e47f3b55.title: Universities urged to embrace continuous learning and innovation in AI era
08a71a25e47f3b55.summary: Published - October 26, 2026 12:02 am IST - VIJAYAWADA Universities must move beyond incremental changes and embrace continuous learning, experimentation and innovation to keep pace with the exponential growth of artificial intelligence (AI), said Soumitra Dutta, advisor to the SRM Group. Delivering the keynote address at a symposium on ‘Advancing Management Knowledge in the AI Era: Research Frontiers and Future’ organised by the Paari School of Business (PSB) at SRM University-A.P., he highlighted the close links between engineering advancements and modern digital ecosystems. He also stressed the need for developing countries such as India to strengthen their technological capabilities and research networks to participate effectively in global innovation, particularly as computing infrastructure remains concentrated in a few wealthy economies. The symposium, themed ‘Reimagining Management through AI’, brought together academics and researchers to examine the impact of artificial intelligence on management practices, economic models, organisational transformation and global business. During a chat on human capital, leadership and organisational transformation, Allan Bird of the Goa Institute of Management and Michael Stevens of Weber State University explored the implications of AI for organisational strategy and decision-making. They discussed globalisation in terms of ease of communication, systemic interdependence and operational complexity. The speakers emphasised the importance of cognitive engagement and independent thinking, cautioning against excessive dependence on automated tools. Ashay Kadam, dean of PSB, said the business school was integrating AI into its curriculum and departmental workflows while conducting faculty development programmes to improve the use of AI in teaching and research. These initiatives were aimed at preparing students for changing industry requirements and advancing the institution’s ambition to become AI-native. Ranjit Thapa, Dean

bd3712139e3eba79.title: A hundred years ago | The Indian civil service
bd3712139e3eba79.summary: Published - October 26, 2026 02:30 am IST Simla, October 25: The following Press Communique is issued: In accordance with the recommendation of the Lee Commission, direct recruits to the Indian Civil Service are now being selected in equal numbers from Europeans and Indians. For the purpose of calculation, London examination of one year and Allahabad examination and nominations of the next year are taken together as forming one year. In the year 1925-26, i.e. London examination of 1926 and Allahabad examination and nominations of 1925, numbers actually recruited were 20 Europeans and 22 Indians. These figures are being adjusted in the year 1926-27 by recruiting 29 Europeans and 27 Indians. The London examination of 1926 has yielded 19 Europeans and 11 Indians. This leaves 16 Indians to be recruited in India in 1927 through examination and nomination. Nine of these vacancies are definitely offered for open competition of the Allahabad examination to be held in January next, while the remaining seven are for the present held in reserve to be filled by nomination. 9f8c115d4f239e60.title: Officials urged to remain alert as severe cyclone approaches
9f8c115d4f239e60.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:46 pm IST - MACHILIPATNAM NTR District Collector G. Lakshmisha reviewing cyclone preparedness in Vijayawada. | Photo Credit: G.N. RAO Krishna District Collector D.K. Balaji has directed officials to remain alert for the cyclone and take steps to prevent human and property loss. Mr. Balaji, who reviewed cyclone preparedness with the district and mandal-level officials, instructed them to be available at the posted places and take measures for supply of drinking water and other essentials. Meanwhile, Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Corporation Limited (APCPDCL) CMD P. Pulla Reddy said leaves of officials and staff were cancelled in wake of the cyclonic storm. He also asked the field staff to caution the public against touching snapped electric cables. Control Rooms have been set up in all districts under CPDCL, Mr. Pulla Reddy said. Eluru District Collector K. Vetri Selvi has directed the officials to be alert and asked the Irrigation department engineers to take measures to prevent damage to canal and tank bunds. Villagers were requested not to venture into rivers and canals and move on the bunds as the impact of the cyclone would be heavy. Control Rooms have been set up at Eluru Collectorate with helpline numbers 18002331077, 08812-224519 and 9491041419, and public are requested to contact and alert the officers in emergency, the Collector said. NTR District Collector G. Lakshmisha reviewed the preparedness for the severe cyclone with the officials of Revenue, Irrigation, A.P. Transco, Medical and Health, Fire and other departments. He directed the Tahsildars to shift people staying in vulnerable areas to safer locations. A control room has been set up the Collectorate with the helpline number 91549 70454 in Vijayawada, Mr. Lakshmisha said. He appealed to the public not to take shelter in dilapidated buildings, under the trees, electric poles and hoardings during the event of the cyclone. Published - October 25, 2026 11:46 p

51fcfc8ac02b49b9.summary: Published - October 26, 2026 12:25 am IST - New Delhi: Uttar Pradesh CEO Navdeep Rinwa directed that errors identified during the investigation of complaints received regarding the electoral rolls through various political parties and social media platforms should not be repeated. (Representational image) | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto Amid controversy over errors found in the electoral rolls published after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) of Uttar Pradesh on Sunday (October 25, 2026) ordered reverification of all entries made by computer operators since the publication of post-SIR final electoral rolls on April 10 and directed that any future digital applications be filed only by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) and not by outsourced computer operators. “Under no circumstances should the feeding of physical application forms be handled by computer assistants. It must also be ensured that all physical forms received are digitised exclusively by the BLO through the BLO App. Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) must review all pending Form-6, Form-7, and Form-8 applications on a daily basis and ensure their prompt disposal strictly as per rules. Proper custody and preservation of all physically received forms must be ensured”, an official statement said. 3f13679c1ef2880d.title: Tamil Nadu Governor Arlekar calls for efforts to cultivate reading habit among children
3f13679c1ef2880d.summary: Updated - October 25, 2026 11:42 pm IST - Coimbatore Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar (centre) launching a book at the fifth edition of the Western Ghats Lit Fest in Coimbatore city on Sunday. | Photo Credit: SIVA SARAVANAN S. Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar on Sunday (October 25, 2026) called for efforts to cultivate reading habit among children, stressing that publishing books alone was not enough without creating a readership. “Books have to be there, books are to be published in abundant number, but at the same time we have to create readership,” he said at the fifth edition of the Western Ghats Lit Fest 2026, organised by The Verandah Club in Coimbatore city. Recounting his interactions with school students in Himachal Pradesh, Mr. Arlekar said some cited Physics and Geography textbooks when asked whether they read books. He also recalled that teachers at a school in Shimla were unaware of a book exhibition in the city, highlighting the need to encourage reading beyond the curriculum. He urged literary festivals to produce tangible outcomes rather than remain platforms for intellectual discussions. Referring to the cultural, linguistic, literary and ecological links between different parts of the country, Mr. Arlekar said these connections formed the basis of a united Bharat, and stressed on the need to preserve and rejuvenate these bonds. Citing the idea of ‘Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat’, he said people should develop a sense of belonging to the region in which they lived, irrespective of where they originally came from. He said literature and cultural exchanges could help strengthen this sense of national unity. He cited the Kashi Tamil Sangamam and historical links between Maharashtra and Thanjavur as examples of the country’s inter-connected heritage. 140c8de5aa4318c7.title: Vellore Corporation desilts waterbodies in 49 areas prone to waterlogging
140c8de5aa4318c7.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:12 pm IST - VELLORE Vellore Corporation Commissioner A. Catherine Saranya inspects desilting of water channels and storm-water drains in the town. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement With the onset of the Northeast monsoon, Vellore Corporation has identified 49 areas, mostly in Old Town, which are prone to waterlogging. Water channels have been desilted in these areas to prevent water stagnation during the monsoon. Corporation officials said that areas such as Kansalpet, Kaspa, Shenbakkam, Ambedkar Nagar, Thedir Nagar, and Konavattam are identified as flood-prone areas in Old Town. “Most of the identified spots in Old Town are low-lying areas. Desilting of storm-water drains and key water channels have been done to ensure free flow of excess rainwater into the river,” A. Catherine Saranya, Commissioner, Vellore Corporation, told The Hindu. Corporation officials said that as part of monsoon-preparedness measures, special teams led by a sanitary inspector have been deployed in identified areas prone to waterlogging in town. Surveillance teams will also patrol waterbodies to prevent dumping of waste that could choke the flow of rainwater in these water channels. Key water channels such as Nicholson, Thorapadi, and Pandian canals have been desilted to a distance of 64 km in the town. Among these water channels, Nicholson canal is the oldest waterbody and runs upto nine km. Built by the British in the 1890s, the canal discharges excess rainwater from nearby hillocks such as Pinchamandai, Kurumalai, Nechimedu, Pallakollai, and Vellakalmalai to the Palar River. Along with Corporation Commissioner Ms. Saranya, Collector P.S. Leena Alex inspected rain-related works in town. Ms. Alex also directed civic officials to take up road repair works and remove garbage, especially in congested spots such as markets and bus termini. Corporation officials said that the civic body has set up at 12 relief centres, to relocate families during emergencies. Ea

09328191bd1a24cb.title: Man jumps from terrace in bid to escape from police, dies
09328191bd1a24cb.summary: Published - October 26, 2026 12:02 am IST - Chennai A 42-year-old man working in the Commercial Taxes Office in Chengalpattu, who sustained injuries while trying to escape the police and was admitted to the Rajiv Gandhi Government Hospital, died on Sunday. The city police said R. Rajapandian, a resident of Kathirvedu, was working as an Office Assistant at the Commercial Taxes Department in Chengalpattu district. In July this year, a woman filed a sexual harassment complaint against Rajapandian, based on which a case was registered against him. The accused failed to appear before the court despite a warrant being issued against him, due to which the Puzhal police initiated proceedings against him. When a team of police officials from the Puzhal station visited his house on Friday, he tried to escape by jumping from the terrace on the third floor of the building. He sustained serious injuries and was admitted to the Rajiv Gandhi Government Hospital for treatment. However, he died on Sunday. e6a0b3edb920cbae.title: Denso Iris reigns supreme
e6a0b3edb920cbae.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:35 pm IST - BENGALURU The best part about Denso Iris (Japan) is that it does not rely solely on its foreign imports, unlike most teams in the FIBA Women’s Basketball League Asia at the Sree Kanteerava Indoor Stadium here. Instead, it thrives on collective effort, with every player contributing and the foreigners complementing the team’s overall game. On Sunday, in the final against favourite Sichuan Yuanda Meile (China), Iris underlined the strength of that approach. Iris’s commanding 81-63 victory over the Chinese side was a powerful vindication of its philosophy. Sichuan, heavily dependent on American Chennedy Carter and Australian Sara Blicavs, struggled to find its attacking rhythm. Carter was disqualified early in the second quarter after picking up two technical fouls, while Blicavs was not at her best. With Iris’s defence denying it the space to operate freely, Sichuan found it increasingly difficult to raise the tempo. Iris’ disciplined approach and sustained intensity were reflected in the way it built its advantage quarter after quarter, moving from 24-20 after the first quarter to 43-36 at half-time before sealing an 81-63 victory. Maki Takada, a three-time Olympian at 37 years was a striking example of experience triumphing over age. Neither exceptionally quick nor overly aggressive, the veteran centre relied on composure, sound positioning to finish as the game’s top scorer with 23 points, including seven two-pointers and a three-pointer. G. Parameshwar, Deputy Chief Minister of Karnataka, gave away the prizes. The results: Final: Denso Iris (Japan) 81 (Maki Takada 23, Haruna Kasagi 15, Mai Kawai 13) bt Sichuan Yuanda Meile (China) 63 (Sara Blicavs 18, Gao Song 12, Chennedy Carter 11). Third place: Cathay Life Tigers (Chinese Taipei) 73 (Shelbynal Cheyanne Cheslek 24, Penina Davidson 20) bt KB Stars (South Korea) 68 (Yunjeong Na 22, Yeeun Heo 18, Yunha Song 15). 83561d0577b6a453.title: Food Safety Department destroys 922 kg of food items in raids: CMO
83561d0577b6a453.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:46 pm IST During a special drive at Mori Gate Khoya Mandi, the department destroyed around 370 kg of k hoya. | Photo Credit: KAMAL NARANG The Food Safety Department destroyed about 922 kg of food items during surprise inspections ahead of the festival season, the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) stated on Sunday. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said no compromise on public health or the purity of food products would be tolerated. “During festivals, when demand for sweets and other food items rises, greater vigilance and responsibility are essential to ensure food safety,” she said. Ms. Gupta said sweets are an integral part of traditions, faith and mutual affection, making their purity a matter of public health as well as a legal obligation. During a special drive at Mori Gate Khoya Mandi, the department destroyed around 370 kg of k hoya and 150 kg of c hhena found to be “spoiled and emitting a foul smell”, according to the CMO. Three samples of k hoya were also collected for laboratory testing. In west Delhi’s Nihal Vihar, officials inspected unlicensed units manufacturing sweets and destroyed around 402 kg of food items, including 265 kg of r asgullas, 45 kg of c hhena, 80 kg of milk cake and 12 kg of grated coconut. “The teams also collected 14 samples for testing, including six of c hhena, two each of milk cake and r asgullas, and one each of m otichoor laddoos, a tta laddoos, r asbhari and paneer,” an official statement said. The department said the inspections were conducted on a holiday, with teams deployed simultaneously in different lanes to prevent establishments from being alerted in advance. 51f9f424086d64f5.title: Two persons arrested in Ranipet for stealing two-wheelers
51f9f424086d64f5.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:08 pm IST - RANIPET Two persons were arrested by Thimiri police on Sunday for stealing two-wheelers in Vellore, Ranipet, and Tiruvannamalai districts. The arrested persons were identified as M. Dhanasekaran, 48, and R. Arumugam, 42. They are residents of Ranipet. The police recovered 12 two-wheelers from them. Initial inquiry revealed that the duo stole parked two-wheelers at temple festivals, hospitals, banks, markets, and government offices. Based on complaints from affected persons, Ranipet Superintendent of Police P. Sibin formed special teams to nab the duo. The police intercepted the duo during a surprise vehicle check. Stolen two-wheelers were kept in a godown before they were sold at cheap rates without documents. Each stolen two-wheeler was sold at a price of ₹5,000 to ₹10,000. A case was registered and later they were lodged at Central Prison in Vellore. A probe is under way. eb9e437d19555c49.title: India's heatwave tag flags global adaptation finance gap ahead of COP31
eb9e437d19555c49.summary: As India officially recognised heatwaves as natural disasters nearly three months ahead of the UN climate change conference (COP31) in Turkiye, officials and experts have pointed out that the move exposes a stark reality of a global climate finance system that pushes vulnerable nations to pay for immediate climate survival entirely on their own. "This task would have been much simpler if we had a good amount of international assistance that allowed us to access funds for various heat adaptation measures," Krishna S Vatsa, National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) member and Head of the Department, told PTI Videos in an interview. Stressing that the resources available for adaptation are "inadequate and unpredictable", Vatsa emphasised the need to improve access to the right kinds of technologies, including those required for efficient cooling. 15136289bbe20b8c.title: Fifty years ago | Chinese herb medicine cures cancer
15136289bbe20b8c.summary: Published - October 26, 2026 02:05 am IST Tokyo, October 25: A Chinese herb medicine preparation claimed to be remarkably effective against cancer has been developed by scientists at Osaka University and Kink University’s Oriental Medicine Research Institute. The preparation, composed of about 30 kinds of herbal medicines, produces comparatively little of the adverse effects generally noted in cancer-arresting drugs. Patients suffering from breast, abdominal, rectal and uterine cancer showed marked improvement when given the herb medicine, the researchers said. The preparation is based on recipes listed in an ancient book of Chinese medicine and said to be effective for breast and skin cancer. The formula was worked out after performing animal tests for a three-year period. Experiments had been conducted since 1974 on advanced cancer cases treated at the hospitals attached to the two universities. Nine out of 13 cases administered the preparation made good progress and one person was able to resume a normal life even though rectal cancer had recurred and spread. bdbfd11e85293053.title: Delhi’s longest cycling track planned along Yamuna: Route details, opening date, cost and purpose
bdbfd11e85293053.summary: The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) is planning to develop a 24-km cycling track along the Yamuna riverbank , which could become the national capital’s longest cycling track. The proposed route will run from the Old Railway Bridge near Wazirabad to National Highway 24 near Sarai Kale Khan, forming part of a wider plan to improve public access to the riverfront. The DDA has floated a tender for the first phase of the project, with the overall estimated construction cost pegged at around ₹ 16 crore, PTI cited an official as saying. The project is part of the DDA’s broader vision under the approved Master Plans of Delhi 2047 to strengthen the connection between the river and residents through green spaces, cycling routes, walking trails and recreational facilities. The proposed cycling track will stretch along the western bank of the Yamuna, connecting areas from the Old Railway Bridge near Wazirabad to National Highway 24 near Sarai Kale Khan. The route forms part of a larger 52-km Yamuna corridor planned to be developed in three phases. The first phase will cover the stretch from the Old Railway Bridge near Wazirabad to National Highway 24. A public greenway measuring between 75 metres and 100 metres in width is planned along the riverbank. It will include cycling and walking trails, along with spaces for passive recreational activities. adce862eae080676.title: Serbia election: Vucic faces tough challenge from student-backed movement
adce862eae080676.summary: Serbians are voting Sunday in a parliamentary election that is seen as a showdown between the Balkan country's populist leader Aleksandar Vucic and a movement of university students who led protests against him for almost two years. Though Serbia's 6.4 million voters get to choose from 18 parties hoping to enter the 250-member Parliament, the election has taken shaped as a referendum between Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party and the youth-backed Students' List. The main contenders are believed to be polling neck-and-neck, making Sunday's election the most uncertain in recent years. Turnout is expected to be high and could push most smaller parties below the 3% threshold needed to make it into the assembly. 5459b7a9cbdc4cc3.summary: Punjab National Bank (PNB) aims to bring its cost-to-income ratio below 50 per cent in the current financial year and further reduce it to around 45 per cent by 2028-29, said Ashok Chandra, MD and CEO of the country's second-biggest lender. The bank's cost-to-income ratio stood at 50.38 per cent in the first half of the current fiscal year, down from 53.3 per cent in September 2025, as it focuses on rationalising expenses and maximising profitability, he told PTI in an interview. "We are aiming to go below 50 per cent this financial year. That is the first target we have set for ourselves. In the next two years, by 2028-29, we should be somewhere around 45 per cent," he said. Chandra said the bank was working on two key areas -- rationalisation of expenses and maximisation of profits-- while sensitising its various units about the importance of improving operational efficiency. Every review meeting of the bank now focuses on the cost of deposits, yield on advances, fee-based income

35f3097a2554a437.title: Bhavani devotees throng Kanaka Durga temple atop Indrakeeladri
35f3097a2554a437.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:49 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam, abode of Goddess Kanaka Durga, atop Indrakeeladri, witnessed a massive influx of Bhavani devotees and general pilgrims from the early hours of Sunday (October 25, 2026), with thousands arriving from far-flung places to conclude their Bhavani Deeksha. The hill shrine was filled with devotees dressed in red, while chants of “Jai Bhavani” reverberated across the temple premises, creating a spiritually charged atmosphere. The rush began early in the morning, with devotees arriving from both the Ghat Road and Kanaka Durga Nagar routes. The queues grew crowded as the number of pilgrims continued to swell. In view of the heavy rush, the temple administration introduced several measures to regulate the crowd and facilitate faster darshan for Bhavani devotees and general pilgrims. As part of these arrangements, Antaralaya Darshan, which allows devotees to enter the inner sanctum, was completely suspended from the morning. Later, following the offering of Maha Nivedana to the presiding deity at noon, the temple authorities cancelled all categories of special-entry darshan tickets as well. Consequently, only free Sarva Darshan was being permitted, allowing devotees waiting in the queues to have the darshan of Sri Kanaka Durga Devi without purchasing special-entry tickets. The move was aimed at improving the flow of pilgrims and providing greater access to ordinary devotees amid the unprecedented rush. Temple officials were closely monitoring arrangements to ensure uninterrupted distribution of drinking water to pilgrims waiting in the queues and to prevent inconvenience during the prolonged waiting periods. Temple Executive Officer V.K. Seena Naik appealed to the devotees to cooperate with the temple staff and security personnel, maintain discipline and follow the prescribed arrangements to ensure a smooth and orderly darshan of the Goddess. Published - October 25, 2026 11:49 p

29a994a4d65033eb.title: Israelis abroad expected to fly home to vote in high-stakes election
29a994a4d65033eb.summary: For two decades since leaving Israel for Canada, Yael Natra said, she didn't consider returning to vote in her home country's elections. 6845d73386159dbd.summary: Published - October 27, 2026 03:45 am IST - Bhopal Days after locals alleged the death of around 13 people in a month due to consuming spurious liquor, the police in Madhya Pradesh’s Dewas district have arrested 10 people for allegedly selling illicit liquor in the region, officers said on Monday (October 26, 2026). According to the police, the crackdown was launched based on information from the district hospital about the deaths of two people on October 15 and 18, whose families alleged that they died after consuming liquor. The 10 accused have been booked under Section 34(2) of the Madhya Pradesh Excise Act, 1915. The crackdown comes days after Ujjain Divisional Commissioner Asheesh Singh formed a five-member special panel to carry out a detailed probe into the alleged deaths in Chandana and Binjana villages. The Dewas district administration, however, had earlier dismissed new reports and Congress claims, denying any deaths related to spurious liquor while saying that the samples of the two deceased who underwent post-mortem examinations have been sent for forensic tests for clarity. It also said that various liquor samples tested following locals’ allegations were not found to contain poisonous contents. The locals of the two villages have claimed that 13 people have died so far since September 26. M.P. Congress president Jitu Patwai, who visited the affected villages, also alleged that about 35-40 people had damaged their vision due to spurious liquor. e80568339f935cea.title: Fifty years ago | Foreign bank accounts: 400 cases detected
e80568339f935cea.summary: Published - October 27, 2026 02:40 am IST Madras, October 26: A huge basket of foreign currencies and securities, equivalent to about Rs 30 lakhs, held by Indians in banks abroad have been detected by the Central authorities. Nuclear scientists, engineers, and economists of Karnataka, doctors of Calcutta and East African repatriates in Bombay, account for a big chunk of the over 400 cases that have come to light. The drive launched early this year, gained momentum in recent months and paid rich dividends in August and September, during which a majority of these cases were discovered. Quite a few of the cases, officials say are from Karnataka and the persons involved belong to various professions, who managed to secure employment in West European countries. In West Asia also, the State has contributed a bulk of semi-skilled craftsmen, like tailors and carpenters. Of late, there has been a big spurt in the number of Indians going abroad on assignments from the United Nations and other international agencies, or seeking lucrative positions in West Asian and West European countries. As part of the crackdown on smuggling activity, the Central authorities started enquiries about the various persons who went for employment abroad and returned to India after the tenure of their duties outside but retained their foreign bank accounts. This type of foreign holdings is lapped by foreign exchange racketeers to finance smuggling into India. 62712cb91e80caa1.title: A ready solution to tackle anaemia
62712cb91e80caa1.summary: Updated - October 27, 2026 01:18 am IST ‘At an estimated cost of ₹14-₹20 per person annually, DFS represents one of the most affordable population-level nutrition interventions available’ | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto Despite significant economic progress and sustained public health efforts, anaemia — driven significantly by iron deficiency — continues to be one of India’s most pressing public health challenges. Affecting over half of Indian women and almost three-fourths of children, anaemia contributes to maternal mortality, an intergenerational cycle of malnutrition, impaired cognitive development, reduced productivity and substantial economic losses. The Government of India’s 7X7X7 Anaemia Mukt Bharat (AMB) strategy, which was launched recently, rightly recognises the multifactorial nature of anaemia through a comprehensive approach spanning prevention, screening, treatment, dietary diversification and behaviour change. Yet, one proven preventive intervention remains significantly underutilised. That intervention is Double Fortified Salt (DFS) — salt fortified with both iodine and iron. Salt offers an unparalleled opportunity to address iron deficiency. Consumed daily by virtually every household across India, in predictable quantities regardless of income or geography, it is uniquely suited to deliver a preventive nutrition intervention at population scale. DFS also addresses one of the fundamental challenges of anaemia control — sustained compliance. Delivering iron through an everyday food complements interventions such as iron supplementation and dietary diversification, whose effectiveness depends on regular adherence. India already has one of the world’s most successful public health platforms in Universal Salt Iodisation, with around 95% of households consuming iodised salt. Building on this existing infrastructure, DFS is already distributed to an estimated 76 million people across four States through government safety-net programmes. Global a
