101d47c14420a9a8.title: A hundred years ago | Japan becoming a second-rate power
101d47c14420a9a8.summary: Published - October 29, 2026 04:10 am IST New York, October 26: The newspapers here published a remarkable story sent from Brussels on the authority of highly placed diplomatic officials, according to which it is apparent that Japan is reverting to the status of a second rate power. Consequently the importance of Britain’s imperial defences is being minimised at the discussions of the Imperial Conference in London. It is emphatically stated in the reports that are published that it will be utterly impossible for Japan to regain her status owing to the serious decline in her trade, the enormous havoc wrought by the severe earthquakes that devastated Japan, the labour agitations that are menacing her powers as a manufacturing country and her financial troubles which are believed to be heavy. beb97b60f834e48b.title: CM to release book co-authored by late B. Madhusoodana Kurup
beb97b60f834e48b.summary: Updated - October 29, 2026 01:22 am IST - KOCHI Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will release a book co-authored by the late B. Madhusoodana Kurup, founder Vice-Chancellor of the Kerala University of Fisheries and Ocean Studies and former Director of the School of Industrial Fisheries, Cusat, at a function in Kochi on Friday (October 29, 2026). The book, Exploring the Legacy of Fishing and Farming Below Sea Level: Vembanad-Kole Wetlands of Southern India , has been co-authored by Dr. Kurup and Dr. Sileesh Mullasseri. The School of Industrial Fisheries, Cusat, will organise the function in memory of Dr. Kurup. Fisheries Minister V.E. Abdul Gafoor will preside over the event, which will be held at BTH Hotel at 3.15 p.m. Former Fisheries Ministers K. Babu and S. Sharma will receive the first copies of the book. 0ac8682804248381.title: Clinging on: On Netanyahu and the Israel elections
0ac8682804248381.summary: Updated - October 29, 2026 01:22 am IST Benjamin Netanyahu was at the centre of Israel’s October 27 elections. For Israel’s longest-serving Prime Minister, who oversaw a genocidal war in Gaza following Hamas’s October 7 attack , the election was the biggest test of his political career. For the Opposition, which promised to hold him accountable for the failures of October 7 and end the country’s “forever wars”, the election offered an opportunity to oust him from power. The results, however, sent a mixed message. With 85.6% of the votes counted, Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition has lost its majority but is still the largest bloc . His Likud party is projected to win 26 seats, while its main rival Yashar, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, is expected to secure 21. Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism, the far-right extremist parties in Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition, demonstrated their continued strength, winning 13 seats between them. The dark horse, however, could be the Arab parties — the Joint List is projected to win 12 seats while the United Arab List (Ra’am) could secure seven seats. With neither bloc commanding a majority, the Arab parties could propel the opposition coalition to power. But the big question is whether the anti-Netanyahu coalition is ready to join hands with the Arab parties, which have historically been kept on the margins of Israel’ s power politics. Mr. Netanyahu’s central promise has been that only he can guarantee Israel’s security. Yet, the October 7 attack took place on his watch and he has refused to take responsibility for the failures that led to it. 32e02ed1cbc8803a.title: Jamia stir: two NSUI members detained; exams moved online
32e02ed1cbc8803a.summary: Published - October 29, 2026 05:00 am IST Security personnel outside Jamia Millia Islamia University in New Delhi on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: SUSHIL KUMAR VERMA Delhi Police on Wednesday detained two members of the National Students’ Union of India from outside the Jamia Millia Islamia campus, where public assembly has been banned under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita. The police action comes amid an ongoing hunger strike by students demanding the restoration of their students’ union, which was dissolved in 2006. NSUI identified the detained students as Faizan, president of its Jamia unit, and Zishan, a former national head of its social media wing. They were taken to Fatehpur Beri before being brought back to the Jamia Nagar police station. NSUI national president Vinod Jakhar posted on X: “Instead of listening to the voices of National Students’ Union of India comrades who have been on a hunger strike for the past 17 days... Delhi Police has taken comrades Faizan and Zishan into custody from Gate No. 4 and both have been taken to an unknown location.” As the agitation entered its 17th day on Wednesday, the university administration alleged vandalism by the students overnight on October 27. “Groups had vandalized university gates and walls, brought down Gate No. 4 C, pelted stones, [and] damaged closed-circuit television control room” overnight on October 27, damaging gates, walls and the CCTV control room,” it said in an official release. It also claimed that “female wardens and faculty members were threatened”. However, protesters denied the allegations, accusing the administration of staging the vandalism to frame them. One of the protestors, Neville, said, “They [the administration] had erected aluminium sheets... and by evening themselves got them broken and are blaming students.” Students also alleged harassment by proctorial teams in hostels, with their ID cards being snatched and the mess ordered to close from November 1 to pressure

69c32cc2e88eff77.title: Morning Digest: Heavy rain hits 17 Odisha districts amid Cyclone Arnab; 64.5 lakh voters potentially missing from Karnataka rolls, most young, and more
69c32cc2e88eff77.summary: Published - October 29, 2026 06:47 am IST A worker uses a hand saw to clear a tree that fell and blocked a road due to strong winds and rain triggered by Cyclone Arnab, in Bhubaneswar. | Photo Credit: ANI Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) said 17 districts of Odisha had been affected by heavy rainfal l triggered by severe cyclonic storm Arnab, which crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast early in the day. The State government is prepared to deal with any eventuality, as the cyclonic system is expected to bring heavy rainfall until the morning of October 29 before weakening. af122f8b40f2637a.summary: Updated - October 29, 2026 06:21 am IST - New Delhi The Air Force Golf Course, which houses a sports complex, swimming pool and other recreational facilities, remained closed on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) as the Centre expedited efforts to reclaim prime land parcels in the surrounding area. bbb79f4520b1f420.title: Furniture thrown, proceedings disrupted as lawyers’ protest against HC judge turns chaotic
bbb79f4520b1f420.summary: Published - October 29, 2026 01:00 am IST The lawyers were protesting over the alleged mistreatment of their colleague by Justice Ajay Bhanot of the Allahabad HC. | Photo Credit: video grab Chaos erupted in one of the courtrooms at the Allahabad High Court on Wednesday as protests against a judge escalated, with advocates allegedly throwing furniture towards the dais. The conduct of the lawyers prompted the court to consider disciplinary and contempt proceedings against those involved. A Bench of Justice Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal was hearing a bail application when slogans and commotion from the adjoining corridor interrupted the proceedings. After being informed that the lawyers were protesting over the alleged mistreatment of their colleague, the judge expressed concern over the disruption caused to litigants and the functioning of the court. The protest reportedly stemmed from allegations that a lawyer had been mistreated by Justice Ajay Bhanot. Terming the conduct of the lawyers as “wholly unjustified” and “contemptuous”, the Bench observed that litigants approach the court seeking judicial relief and should not suffer because of disagreements between lawyers and a particular judge. “Registrar (Protocol) is directed to get the CCTV footage of camera installed outside of Court No.66, identify the advocates involved in the incident and submit a report to this court by next date of listing. After identifying the advocates, the matter may be referred to the Bar Council of U.P. for initiation of disciplinary proceedings as well as initiation of contempt proceedings against them,” Justice Deshwal ordered. bf5fd2ef65548963.title: 20 units of illegally mined sand near Ambur seized
bf5fd2ef65548963.summary: Published - October 29, 2026 01:02 am IST - TIRUPATTUR Mounds of mined sand in Machampattu village on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement More than 20 units of river sand that was illegally mined from the dry Malattaru River was found at Machampattu village on Wednesday. Revenue officials said that based on information from farmer and social activist J. Paranthaman, a team of revenue officials and the police inspected a private open land near the river, where huge quantities of river sand were stored in the open. “Based on preliminary assessment, we have found over 20 units of river sand illegally kept in the private land. We have sealed the premises for further inspection by the Water Resources Department (WRD) team, for public auction of the seized sand,” S. Devi, Tasildar (Pernambut), told The Hindu. A farming village, Machampattu forms part of Pernambut Panchayat Union in Vellore district. Most of the farmers depend on the river for domestic consumption and irrigation purposes. “Over the years, illegal sand mining has turned the perennial river into a seasonal waterbody. Illegal sand mining in the river also depleted groundwater in surrounding farming villages,” Mr. Paranthaman said. Along with the local police, revenue officials led by tahsildar Devi had inspected the site where they found a large quantity of river sand stored in the open. Revenue officials said that as per norms, mining of river sand, including for government purposes like construction of school buildings and Anganwadi centres, is prohibited in the State. For government infrastructure works, sand could be procured at designated government sand quarries in the district. Revenue officials said that the revenue earned in the public auction will go to the State exchequer. Legal action will also be taken on the landowner, identified as Navin, for illegal mining of river sand. A probe is under way. 9790e23ee54fad38.title: Persons with disabilities can now travel for free in government buses with UDID card
9790e23ee54fad38.summary: Published - October 29, 2026 12:58 am IST - Chennai Persons with disabilities and their companion can now travel free of charge in government buses with their Unique Identification Card (UDID). The Welfare of Differently Abled department issued a government order for persons with disability with over 40% disability to travel n the city ordinary, express buses, low-floor buses, deluxe buses excluding air-conditioned buses of the Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporations and in the ordinary fare buses excluding air-conditioned buses of the Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporations in the suburban (Mofussil) and hilly areas. It comes into force from October 28. This had been a long pending demand of various disability associations for free travel in buses. The order further noted that the current bus travel concessions for persons with disability including the 75% travel concession, will continue as usual. “The free bus travel concession card obtained in the financial year 2026-2027 will not be valid when this scheme is implemented. The bus operator should issue a free travel ticket to them when they travel,” the order stated. The announcement of the scheme was made in the State Budget in the Legislative Assembly in August, 2026. The Social Welfare and Women Empowerment Minister K. Jegadeshwari expanded it to persons with disabilities and their companions with a UDID card. Welcoming the move Nethrodaya founder C. Govindakrishnan said, “We can now travel in all these buses without a pass and with just a UDID card. We are thankful to the Chief Minister for the initiative.” The Hindu published an article on the issue on October 25, 2026. 138d27b4a389e14e.summary: Published - October 29, 2026 04:30 am IST The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) and several government universities have joined hands to organise an inter-university sports tournament featuring five disciplines, following an initiative by Lieutenant-Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu to promote team sports among students, according to a release from Lok Niwas on Wednesday. Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Mansukh Mandaviya, Mr. Sandhu and Delhi Education Minister Ashish Sood inaugurated the DDA-University Sports Cup 2026 at Roshanara Club on Tuesday. Organised by Delhi Technological University (DTU) in collaboration with the DDA, the tournament is being held at the DTU Sports Complex from October 28 to November 2, the release stated. According to Lok Niwas, students will compete in men’s and women’s categories in hockey, football, kabaddi, basketball and cricket. The participating universities include DTU, Netaji Subhas University of Technology, Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology Delhi, Indira Gandhi Delhi Technical University for Women, Delhi Skill and Entrepreneurship University, Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University, Ambedkar University Delhi, Delhi Teachers University, and Delhi Sports University. Addressing students and athletes at the inauguration, Mr. Mandaviya described the initiative as “a significant step towards building a culture of sports and fitness among the youth” and urged young sportspersons to pursue excellence with discipline. He also referred to India’s ambition to host the 2036 Olympics and its successful bid to host the Commonwealth Games in 2030. Mr. Sandhu said, “The tournament will bring Delhi’s universities together on a common platform and encourage sportsmanship and team spirit. As the Prime Minister has said, sports teach us not only to become champions, but also to become better competitors. f52a2e5a18a99318.title: Hero MotoCorp Q2FY27 results: Net profit soars 42% to ₹1,861 crore
f52a2e5a18a99318.summary: India's largest two-wheeler maker Hero MotoCorp on Wednesday reported a 42 per cent year-on-year rise in consolidated profit after tax for the second quarter of the current fiscal. The company's consolidated profit for the quarter came in at Rs 1,861 crore, against Rs 1,308 crore in the year-ago period, according to a regulatory filing. Revenue from operations increased to Rs 14,971 crore, up 23 per cent from Rs 12,218 crore a year ago. "Results for the quarter and half-year include a Rs 397 crore gain from the equity consolidation of an associate company, following its capital raise via a Qualified Institutional Placement and Private Placement," the company said. Revenue was largely driven by volumes. Hero MotoCorp dispatched a total of 18.68 lakh motorcycles and scooters, registering a 10 per cent growth year-on-year. The scooter segment recorded a 47 per cent growth to 2.40 lakh units in the September quarter of FY27. VIDA electric scooter volumes rose 76 per cent year-on-year

84ddd5a26ceb3cef.title: T.N. govt. declares holiday on November 9 in view of Deepavali
84ddd5a26ceb3cef.summary: Published - October 29, 2026 01:00 am IST - CHENNAI In view of Deepavali falling on November 8 (Sunday), the Tamil Nadu government has declared a holiday for government offices, State public sector undertakings, schools, colleges, and other educational institutions on November 9 (Monday). According to a government order (G.O.) issued by the Public Department, the holiday has been declared to allow people to travel to their native places to celebrate Deepavali with their families. Further, the government has announced that November 28 (Saturday) will be a working day to compensate for the holiday. As November 9 has not been declared a holiday under the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, the State government has directed district Collectors to make arrangements for the functioning of treasuries and sub-treasuries with a limited number of employees. Countering the criticism and BJP spokesman Sunil Sethi’s description of “National Conference as Muslim Conference” over dropping a Hindu minister, Deputy CM Choudhary asked the BJP to identify one Muslim minister in the BJP Cabinet. “Is there any Muslim who is a minister at the Centre or BJP-ruled States in the country. If it is about ‘Sab Ka Sath, Sab Ka Vikas’, why is there no Muslim minister in the BJP?. The party spokesman has no right point fingers at the NC,” said Mr. Choudhary. 59026cdb53592953.title: District Magistrate declares Anantnag Bar elections ‘null and void’, cites ‘violations of official orders’
59026cdb53592953.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 05:48 am IST - Srinagar The elections to District Bar Association Anantnag in south Kashmir held on October 27 has been declared “null and void” by the District Magistrate over alleged “violations of official orders and non-fulfilment of mandatory requirements”. In an order, the District Magistrate said these elections “have been conducted in blatant violation of the orders, without fulfilment of the prerequisite conditions, without any intimation to this office and without any permission from this office”. “The election has been conducted in violation of the provisions of Societies Registration Act 1860 (As applicable in Jammu and Kashmir) and Indian Trust Act 1882. The elections conducted by the organisation operating under the name and style of District Bar Association Anantnag, held on 27-10-2026, are hereby declared null and void, ab initio and non-est in the eyes of law,” reads the order. It also mentioned that the election process of the District Bar Association, Anantnag, was prohibited under order Dated 02-01-2025 until “submission of Certificate of Registration; Constitution or Memorandum of Association of the organisation; bye-laws governing the functioning of the organisation; list of current executive members and members of previous 10 years, including their full names, designations, permanent residential addresses, and actives mobile contact numbers and detailed account statements along with a summary of financial transactions and any relevant banking details. Around 700 lawyers are enrolled in the Bar in Anantnag. The elections were held for the posts of president and secretary. “These elections were held after proper permission and observation of the authorities. It’s wrong to term these elections illegal,” said a senior lawyer, on condition of anonymity. He said the District Magistrate notification came in at night. “The elections were held with the intention to benefit lawyers and maintain decorum and dignity of courts.

0e6480d9e5de07db.title: Deemed ineligible: On the Supreme Court and SIR
0e6480d9e5de07db.summary: Updated - October 30, 2026 01:10 am IST At Wednesday’s hearing of a petition on the Delhi SIR in the Supreme Court, Justice Joymalya Bagchi asked questions that cut to the heart of the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s SIR of electoral rolls . If an existing voter was “lax, inert or did not respond” to enumeration forms, was that a ground for the ECI to “forfeit his or her right to vote forever”? The Bench headed by the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that the ECI was in “error” to force such voters, struck off for not returning enumeration forms, to reapply on Form 6 as if they were new voters. It asked why voters who had shifted residences could not just disclose details and why deleted voters could not fill enumeration forms belatedly. This is the central design flaw of the SIR as it shifts the burden of enrolment from the state to the elector, including those who have voted before, and treats a mere change of address as ground for deletion. The share of draft deletions recorded as “shifted” or “absent” rose from 55% in Bihar to 72% in States/Union Territories in Phase 3. In Karnataka, about 84 lakh electors were deleted, marked as “shifted” or “absent” during enumeration. But only a net of 8.2 lakh, including new electors, were added during the claims phase, with the final roll being 64.5 lakh short of the projected adult population. Requiring moved voters to re-register as fresh applicants defeats the ECI’s historic mandate of widening the franchise, which was inherent in the 2002-03 intensive revision, where enumerators enrolled shifted voters at their new homes and the Chief Electoral Officer reconciled the old entries. Justice Bagchi also mentioned that the Bihar judgment was not a “binding precedent” and that the legality of “logical discrepancy” checks, allowed only as an “interim arrangement” in West Bengal, had not been finally adjudicated. No statute or rule provides for judging a voter’s eligibility on the basis of family size or the age gap

42c3ff6548496dc5.title: Hike to help farmers, says CM; Ashok accuses govt. of placing burden on people
42c3ff6548496dc5.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 01:05 am IST - Bengaluru While Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar defended milk price hike by ₹8 on Thursday, saying that the decision was taken to support dairy farmers, Leader of Opposition R. Ashok accused the State government of placing an additional financial burden on the people. He also warned the Congress government of a protest. After the Cabinet meeting that approved the hike, the Chief Minister said, “The hike has been made to prevent losses to farmers.” He pointed out that input costs, price of packaging of milk, transportation have all increased in the past one year. “There was a demand to increase the price by ₹12 to ₹15. We made this decision after consulting with everyone,” he said. He also highlighted that all MLAs had demanded a milk price hike across party lines in both the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council, cutting across partylines. Meanwhile, Mr. Ashok questioned whether increasing the cost of essential commodities and imposing additional taxes was the Congress government’s “guarantee to the people of Karnataka”. He said that while people were already struggling with rising prices, the government appeared focused on further burdening their pockets. 5ac73fe48c556253.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 12:52 am IST - Chennai The Tamil Nadu government has also allocated Rs 125 crore in the first phase to help persons with disability acquire modern assistive devices with artificial intelligence (AI) help them perform activities independently. The government has also issued orders to provide people of short stature with specially designed petrol scooters or battery-powered equipment with coupling wheels at a cost of Rs. 4 crores These announcements were made during the Social Welfare Minister’s speech for demand for grants during the Tamil Nadu Assembly session in August, 2026. Issuing a government order, the Welfare of the Differently-Abled department said that advanced new aids based on AI such as sports prosthesis, upper limb prosthesis operated by electrical signals, cochlear implant battery and a bed equipped with a commode facility will be covered by the government at 50% of cost or Rs. 30,000. In the first phase, this scheme will be implemented for 1,000 beneficiaries at a cost of Rs. 3.00 crore. “Preference for the scheme will be given to students with disability and persons with disability under the age of 50. 066662ee7d0b0eb3.title: Manisha Bhanwala becomes third Indian woman to reach World Wrestling Championships Final
066662ee7d0b0eb3.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 06:19 am IST - Sports Bureau Manisha Bhanwala (59kg) was the third Indian woman to enter the final at the World wrestling championships in Astana on Thursday (October 29, 2026). Manisha, who returned from the Asian Games without a medal in 57kg and jumped to the non-Olympic weight category at the Worlds, shocked World championships bronze medallist Laurence Beauregard by pinning the Canadian in the second period. Then she beat Mongolian Olympian Bolortuya Khurelkhuu 6-0 and pinned Kazakhstan’s World under-23 bronze medallist Altyn Shagayeva to reach the title clash. In the final on Friday (October 30, 2026), Manisha will face USA’s Pan-American champion Abigail Elizabeth Nette. Earlier, Neelam Sirohi (50kg) and Kajal Dhochak (76kg) secured silver medals for the country. Ahilya Shinde (55kg) was beaten 9-6 by Turkey’s Tuba Demir in the last-eight stage. In men’s freestyle, Vicky (97kg) was defeated 12-2 by Japan’s Asian champion and Worlds bronze medallist Arash Yoshida in the quarterfinals. The Indian made it to the repechage round to stay in the race for a bronze medal. Asian Games champion Sujeet Kalkal (65kg) had disappointment in store as lost 3-3 on criteria to Abdulmazhid Kudiev in the quarterfinals. Sujeet had rallied from 2-9 down to beat the Tajikistan wrestler in the Asiad final. d3b27918b25b2260.title: A security deal, but not the end of the Arctic contest
d3b27918b25b2260.summary: Updated - October 30, 2026 01:16 am IST ‘The way Denmark, the U.S. and Greenland manage this balance will shape the island’s future’ | Photo Credit: REUTERS The agreement signed between the United States, Denmark and Greenland on September 22, 2026, marks an important moment in the changing geopolitics of the Arctic. Greenland is an autonomous part of the Kingdom of Denmark. Under the 2009 Self-Government Act , it has extensive control over its domestic affairs, while foreign, defence and security policy remain with Denmark. Greenland came into the news this year because of the Trump administration’s repeated interest in gaining control over the island. What began as a territorial controversy gradually became a wider debate about sovereignty, security and the future of the Arctic. The agreement, signed at the United Nations, expands the American military presence in Greenland while reaffirming Danish sovereignty and Greenland’s right to self-determination. It brings, at least for now, an end to the unusual tensions between Washington and Copenhagen over the future of the strategically important island. The agreement’s entry into force is subject to the completion of the necessary parliamentary procedures in Denmark and Greenland. 63e0a48f83bad2a4.title: Ex-Mayor Bhagyalakshmi appeals to voters to give her another opportunity
63e0a48f83bad2a4.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 12:52 am IST - VIJAYAWADA YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) Mayoral candidate Rayana Bhagyalakshmi on Thursday appealed to voters to give her another opportunity to serve as Mayor, adding that the city had witnessed significant development during the party’s previous five-year tenure. Addressing the media in Gandhi Nagar, Ms. Bhagyalakshmi said the party was committed to accelerating urban development and remaining accessible to the public. She urged voters to elect her and the party’s corporator candidates in the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation elections. Alleging that the coalition government had failed to deliver on its promises, she questioned the development works undertaken in Vijayawada over the past three years. She claimed that the previous YSRCP government had improved water tanks, drainage systems, parks, community halls and the Ajit Singh Nagar dumping yard. She also cited the construction of a retaining wall in Krishnalanka as a major achievement. YSRCP NTR district president Devineni Avinash said Ms. Bhagyalakshmi had discharged her responsibilities as Mayor with commitment and helped the city secure awards during her tenure. He appealed to voters to support all 86 YSRCP corporator candidates. Former Minister Vellampalli Srinivasa Rao alleged that the coalition government had failed to take adequate measures to address Vijayawada’s civic problems, including flooding and drainage issues. He claimed that the previous YSRCP government had undertaken significant development works and expressed confidence that his party would win the municipal elections. 7e803788dc597d52.title: Open to investigation: On the challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
7e803788dc597d52.summary: Updated - October 30, 2026 01:02 am IST The Digital News Publishers Association’s (DNPA) challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 , and its Rules , has drawn attention to concerns that a law to safeguard informational privacy risks creating a serious chilling effect on the media. The absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activity could subject reporters investigating official misconduct or corruption to the obligations of a “data fiduciary”, requiring them to notify and seek consent from the very individuals they are investigating. Such onerous requirements could affect investigations undertaken in the public interest. The implications extend to routine newsgathering too, where personal information is integral to reporting. The omission is particularly consequential because the drafts in 2018, 2019 and 2021 carried a journalistic exemption. The Act already provides exemptions for certain forms of data processing, including for research and statistical purposes, making the denial of similar protection to journalists difficult to justify. Non-compliance can attract penalties of up to ₹250 crore, posing an existential threat to smaller and independent newsrooms. The DNPA petition also challenges Section 44(3), which amended the RTI Act, 2005, removing the earlier public-interest qualification concerning disclosure of personal information. The protection of personal information must not be absolute; an overriding public interest must remain a legitimate ground for disclosure, particularly when the information is held by public authorities. Investigations into corruption often rely on asset disclosures and tender documents containing personal data. Restricting access to these records risks reducing journalism to merely reproducing government releases. The Supreme Court, while issuing notice on the petition, rightly emphasised the need to balance press freedom with the right to privacy. Although journalists in India enjoy no specific statutor

85958afbde1720ce.title: India remains growth engine; Super El Nino impact yet to materialise: IMF
85958afbde1720ce.summary: The IMF on Thursday said the impact of weather events such as the Super El Nino was yet to materialise for India, which remains the engine of growth for the world economy. The IMF listed lower crop yields, increased food price inflation and its impact on the purchasing power of households in India due to the Super El Nino. "So these are risks that we see that India faces, but right now those risks have not materialised," IMF Communications Director Julie Kozack told a press conference here. She said the IMF will reassess India's growth projections in the January World Economic Outlook update after the risks posed by the weather event materialise. Earlier this month, the IMF raised India's growth forecast for fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2028 to 7 per cent, from the 6.4 per cent and 6.7 per cent projections respectively made in July. 64348e28d88bca8d.title: Chennai Corporation considers new feasibility study for rope car project
64348e28d88bca8d.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 12:48 am IST - Chennai The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) is planning to prepare a fresh feasibility report for a rope car service connecting the Marina and Besant Nagar beaches, after the project was found unfeasible along the Marina Beach. At the Council meeting on Thursday, Anna Nagar councillor T.V. Shemmozhi enquired about the status of the Marina Beach rope car project, pointing out that a feasibility study, which estimated the project cost at ₹74 crore, had already been completed. Mayor R. Priya responded that the initial feasibility study had not been approved as it had raised safety concerns over potential overcrowding, and the proposal had been referred to another team for reconsideration. Mr. Shemmozhi said he had repeatedly raised the proposal since his maiden speech at the Council. He added that the rope car service could develop Chennai into a major tourist destination. Notably, on May 25, 2025, when Mr. Shemmozhi demanded that the Marina project be taken up with the government for implementation, the Mayor had said the feasibility study was under way. b45c92f6f1809c05.title: SI arrested for alleged theft of seized drug from police station
b45c92f6f1809c05.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 07:00 am IST - KOCHI A sub-inspector (SI) attached to the Ernakulam Central police station was arrested for allegedly stealing suspected MDMA seized in connection with a Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) case and kept at the station. The officer was identified as Anas S. Thaufeeq, a native of Thiruvananthapuram. The Central police registered a case against him shortly after he was suspended based on a Special Branch report. He had earlier been part of the anti-drug awareness campaign conducted under ‘Operation Toofan’. He was booked under Sections 306 (Theft by clerk or servant of property in possession of master) and 238 (causing disappearance of evidence) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Section 21(c) (punishment for offences involving a commercial quantity of manufactured drugs) of the NDPS Act. The first information report was registered on a complaint by an officer in charge of the strong room at the station. Suspected drugs seized in various narcotics cases were stored in the strong room before being moved to the godown at the district headquarters camp for disposal. The accused allegedly entered the strong room without permission where a packet containing 87.37 grams of suspected MDMA seized by the Elamakkara police was being kept. The accused allegedly stole the packet and tampered with the evidence, resulting in a difference in the quantity of the drug. An investigation is under way to ascertain the motive behind the officer’s actions. The authorities are further looking into whether he received assistance from anyone else at the station. 3f04f33e57a2e858.title: A hundred years ago | Depression in cotton industry
3f04f33e57a2e858.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 04:45 am IST Bombay, Oct. 29: Representatives of the Ahmedabad Millowners’ Association were examined by the Tariff Board (Cotton Textile). Replying to the Chairman, they stated that during the last two or three weeks the condition of the textile industry had changed for the worse. Owing to the heavy drop in cotton prices, cloth merchants had lost their confidence. The purchasing power of the agriculturists was also going down and the phenomenal fall in American cotton prices had accentuated depression in the cotton industry, but did not affect textile industries of America and Japan to any extent. On the other hand, they were making profits. The drop in cotton prices during the last two or three years had been gradual, and it was admitted that the bumper cotton crop of America accentuated the depression. c63f246d28a29ff8.title: Who is Anil Menon? NASA astronaut on fourth spacewalk, ranks behind Sunita Williams among Indian-origin space walkers
c63f246d28a29ff8.summary: NASA astronaut Anil Menon is undertaking his fourth career spacewalk alongside Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk on Thursday, October 29, 2026. The mission marks the 100th US spacewalk at the International Space Station (ISS), with the duo working to install a new roll-out solar array on the orbital laboratory. With his fourth spacewalk, Menon ranks second to veteran NASA astronaut Sunita Williams among Indian-origin astronauts by number of spacewalks. Williams has completed nine spacewalks, totalling 62 hours and six minutes. Before the October 29 mission, Menon had completed three spacewalks, accumulating 19 hours and 20 minutes. The latest mission is part of the continuing maintenance and upgrading of the ISS, where spacewalks are used to install equipment, repair systems and improve the orbital laboratory’s capabilities. Menon has a background spanning medicine, engineering, aviation and human spaceflight operations. Before joining NASA’s astronaut corps, he worked as a flight surgeon for both NASA and SpaceX, helping prepare crews for missions and develop medical systems to support astronauts in space. According to his official NASA biography, Menon was selected for the agency’s 2021 Astronaut Candidate Class and reported for duty in January 2022. He subsequently completed initial astronaut training to prepare for space missions. Menon was born and raised in Minneapolis, Minnesota, to Ukrainian and Indian immigrants. He is married to Anna Menon, and the couple have two children. NASA astronaut Anil Menon has a background spanning medicine, engineering, aviation and human spaceflight. 01b741194d692039.title: Trial Index of Services Production shows sustained momentum in August
01b741194d692039.summary: New Delhi: India’s services activity remained broad-based in August, with 17 of 19 sub-sectors recording growth and 13 posting double-digit increases, indicating sustained momentum in formal-sector services despite mixed signals from manufacturing and external trade, showed the Centre’s fifth trial Index of Services Production (ISP) on Thursday. The 19-sector index covering about 60% of the services sector provides a new monthly gauge of activity in a sector that accounts for more than half of India's economy. The overall ISP will be brought out later after studying the stability and resilience of sub-sectoral ISPs and improving the overall coverage of services, the ministry of statistics and programme implementation said in a statement. Top sub-sectors that reported continued strong growth in are accommodation and food (11.9%), retail trade (19.9%), repair services (17.6%), administrative and support services (13.1%), banking (14.9%), professional, scientific and technical services including research and development (14.2%), IT and computer -related services (13.8%) and real estate (17.6%). While rising energy prices due to the West Asia war have continued to keep air transport services growth in the negative zone at -9.6%, growth of arts, entertainment and recreational services also remained in the negative zone at -4.7%. Growth in other transport services—railways, roadways, and waterways—also remained in the single digits at 3.7%, 9.4%, and 9.5%, respectively. Postal and courier services and information and broadcasting services, which were in the negative zone in earlier months, showed sustained growth of 13.2% and 7.2%, respectively. Repair services, where growth contracted in July, also made a smart recovery, registering double-digit growth in August. While retail trade saw high double-digit growth in August, the wholesale trade growth remained relatively lower at 102%. Telecommunication, warehousing and support activities for transportation expanded by 11.8%

e0c2d90163cf612c.title: Blast in explosives godown in Vellore; three vehicles damaged
e0c2d90163cf612c.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 01:00 am IST - VELLORE The building collapsed to the ground, and three vans parked near the building were damaged. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Three vans were burnt and a calf was killed after an explosion in an explosives godown at Arjunapuram village near Gudiyatham town in Vellore on Thursday. The police said that S. Padmanaban, 42, runs a stone quarry operator in K.V. Kuppam area. He has a vast open land in Arjunapuram village where he stored raw materials to make explosives in a licensed godown in the land. The explosives are used for blasting in stone quarry units. Police said that a special police team attached with Katpadi police seized raw materials used to manufacture fire crackers from a house in Katpadi recently. The seized raw materials were stored at the private explosives godown in Arjunapuram village near Gudiyatham to prevent any untowards incidents. Around 50 kg of raw materials to manufacture explosives were stored in the godown. Police said around 2 a.m, residents heard an explosion from the godown. The building collapsed to the ground, and three vans parked near the building were damaged. Based on an alert from residents, K.V. Kuppam police and experts from the explosives unit at District Police inspected the spot. A case was registered. A probe is underway. 4eaefb546687e028.title: Students take part in stroke awareness programme
4eaefb546687e028.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 12:44 am IST - CHENNAI Students of Bhavan’s Rajaji Vidyashram in Chennai, formed the letters ‘FAST’, an acronym for face drooping, arm weakness, speech difficulty, and time to act immediately. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement Apollo Hospitals, Chennai, and Apollo Shine Foundation organised a stroke awareness programme to highlight the importance of recognising its symptoms and seeking immediate medical attention. As a part of this, students of Bhavan’s Rajaji Vidyashram in Chennai formed the letters ‘FAST’, which stand for face drooping, arm weakness, speech difficulty, and time to act immediately. Minister for School Education Rajmohan and P.G. Subramanian, principal, Bhavan’s Rajaji Vidyashram, Kilpauk, participated. Ilankumaran Kaliamoorthy, Chief Executive Officer, Apollo Hospitals, Chennai Region, said schools provide an opportunity to introduce important health messages to young people, who can also share them with their families. Srinivasan Paramasivam, Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon, Apollo Hospitals, Greams Road, raised the need for regular health checks and appropriate management of conditions such as high blood pressure, a major risk factor for stroke. The company had reported a net loss of Rs 52.13 crore in FY25. Revenue from operations rose 24.58 per cent to Rs 247 crore in FY26 from Rs 198 crore in the preceding fiscal year, while total income stood at Rs 265 crore, FarEye Technologies said in a statement. In the January-March quarter of FY26, the company achieved profitability, FarEye Technologies said on Thursday. FarEye's cash reserves stood at Rs 270.66 crore at the end of FY26. International markets, including North America, Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA), and Asia Pacific, contributed 91.88 per cent of revenue from operations in FY26, it said. FarEye Co-founder and CEO Kushal Nahata said the FY26 performance was driven by enterprise customer growth, improved operational efficiency and disciplined cost management. 90d34315d695cdbc.title: ACB, Food Safety and Drug Control teams inspect NIMS amid corruption allegations
90d34315d695cdbc.summary: Published - October 30, 2026 12:37 am IST Officials of the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB), Food Safety and Drug Control departments conducted simultaneous inspections at Nizam’s Institute of Medical Sciences (NIMS), Punjagutta, on Thursday following allegations of corruption and irregularities. A team of around 10 ACB officials, led by Central Investigation DSP Lakshmi Kanth Reddy, inspected records at the hospital’s administrative section as part of the probe. Meanwhile, four food safety inspectors inspected the NIMS canteen, while another team of four drug inspectors checked the surgical stores. The drug inspectors examined medicines, medical equipment and records pertaining to their storage. The food safety officials focused on the canteen, while the ACB team scrutinised administrative records in connection with the allegations of irregularities. A detailed statement from the ACB on the inspections is expected to be released on Friday. 6705c3e1d83169bc.title: SC pulls up RBI over cyberfrauds, seeks strict liability for losses
6705c3e1d83169bc.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday pulled up the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) over cyberfrauds, saying banks must compensate victims for losses when their employees are found to be involved. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant noted that digital arrest scams persisted despite public awareness campaigns, media coverage and earlier judicial directions. The court was hearing a suo motu case on the issue. The court questioned why the banks should not be held accountable for the losses suffered by their customers, when the financial institution can waive loans worth crores as a one-time settlement. “Banks can waive thousands of crores in loans by entering into so-called one-time settlements for ₹ 5 crore or ₹ 10 crore. Why should they not be accountable to these victims?” Attorney general R. Venkataramani opposed implementing such a rule, stating that the liability of banks needs to be addressed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). The court’s observations came after senior advocate N.S. Nappinai, assisting the bench as amicus curiae, flagged the continued prevalence of digital arrest scams. She referred to a recent incident in which a woman allegedly lost ₹ 2.5 crore. In such scams, fraudsters impersonate police officers, government officials or judicial authorities and threaten victims with arrest to force them to transfer money. The bench also told the banks that the customers have given them access to their account details and transaction history, and they must act as a “protective umbrella” for them. They also raised the question of why banks do not take the necessary steps as soon as suspicions arise or a money-related message appears. “What we are shocked about is why people are not realizing? What is wrong with the victims? Are they not normal people? This is everywhere in the media,” the bench observed. The bench also raised issues of bank employees being involved in such frauds. 485238bc61fc8568.title: Corporate demand for workers with green skills rises: LinkedIn report
485238bc61fc8568.summary: Demand for workers with green skills is growing as businesses increasingly seek talent that can help save energy, reduce waste and operate more efficiently, according to new research from LinkedIn. LinkedIn's Global Green Skills Report 2026 noted that demand for workers with green skills is growing almost as fast as supply in India, with the share of green hiring up 31 per cent in India compared with 29 per cent growth in the share of green talent in the workforce. Moreover, a significant percentage of green hires in India are now going into jobs without traditionally green titles, as businesses look for workers who can help cut costs, improve efficiency and reduce their environmental impact. "In India, a green career no longer starts with a green job title. Employers want people who can make their operations safer, leaner and more efficient, and they are hiring for that ability well beyond sustainability teams," Susan Mathew, India HR Lead, LinkedIn said. dc4f520993d2d64f.title: Govt, Volkswagen clash in court over record $1.2 billion tax dispute
dc4f520993d2d64f.summary: Volkswagen is challenging India's $1.2 billion tax demand over alleged undervaluation of imported car parts.(Photo: Reuters) By Aditi Shah India defended its record $1.2 billion tax demand against Volkswagen in a Mumbai court on Thursday, saying the German ​company never provided required information in time, while the ​carmaker argued the demand came years too late. India has since 2024 alleged ‌Volkswagen undervalued auto imports for years and paid below the full tariff rates. The case is a major overhang for the carmaker which is currently in talks with India's JSW to sell a stake in its India operations. Volkswagen, which has a roughly 2% market share in the world's third biggest car market, denies the allegations, and has previously said the case is a matter of "life and death" for its India business, and is "impossibly enormous". The dispute over India's biggest ever import tax demand restarted last week ‌after the High Court in Mumbai said in August it would hear Volkswagen challenge afresh as judges failed to pass a ruling in time. On Thursday, Volkswagen's counsel Arvind Datar told the judges India tax authorities could not have gone back 12 years in scrutinising its imports as Indian law allows officials to only go back up to the past five years. Additional Solicitor General N. ​Venkataraman, one of the government's top lawyers, said Volkswagen didn't provide the information sought in ‌time, adding that no other automaker in the country which imports parts had indulged in such misconduct. "No other company has challenged this," he said. Volkswagen ​is ‌accused of declaring its imports as individual auto parts and paid 5% to 15% ‌tariff, though it was bringing in "almost the entire car" in unassembled condition for which it should have paid a 30-35% tax rate, India has alleged. b4d11997adf86a36.title: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams
b4d11997adf86a36.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 01:06 am IST Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s exasperation , during the Supreme Court’s hearing on October 29 on the “digital arrest” scams , that people still fall for such scams despite abundant warnings and orders from the Court is understandable. About ₹800 crore has been lost to these scams this year even after recoveries, a hefty sum from the savings of individual victims. But this is not merely about gullibility. Scammers posing as CBI or police officers succeed because their victims, older citizens in particular, defer to or fear law enforcement. When Indian police are widely seen as high-handed towards ordinary citizens and as serving only the powerful, the threat of an “arrest” over a video call cannot be that implausible for many. That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. The Court’s insistence that banks compensate victims addresses an issue with the RBI’s zero-liability provisions. Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse. Yet, full compensation for the victims whenever banks are found wanting in due diligence must be implemented with care as this might force banks to flag far more than the actual mule accounts. f96ca61442a25a78.title: Japan’s Omron Healthcare opens first India manufacturing facility near Chennai
f96ca61442a25a78.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 01:09 am IST - CHENNAI Japan’s Omron Healthcare on Friday formally inaugurated its first India production facility in Gummidipoondi near Chennai. The new unit, spread over an area of 258,333 square feet at Origins by Mahindra industrial estate in Puduvoyal, has been built within three years of the Japanese firm signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Tamil Nadu government in 2023. Designed to produce about 300,000 blood pressure monitors annually, the company plans to increase its production capacity tenfold to make 30 lakh units annually in the next two years. Omron will manufacture three models of blood pressure monitors at the new facility. The firm is also looking at exporting blood pressure monitors manufactured at the new factory to the European market by next year. “We plan to make Chennai a base not just for the Indian market but also develop it as a base for exports,” Ayumu Okada, president and CEO, Omron Healthcare Company Limited, said. Muneo Takahashi, Consul General of Japan in Chennai said: “Tamil Nadu has become an important destination for Japanese investment, supported by its strong industrial base, skilled human resources and excellent infrastructure.” Deepak Jacob, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Guidance said: “In 1972, Omron‘s founder joined hands with Dr. Yutaka Nakamura — a doctor known as the father of Japan’s Paralympic movement — to open Omron Taiyo in Beppu. It was Japan’s first welfare factory run and staffed by people with disabilities. People called it “the factory with wheelchairs.” And a second such factory followed in Kyoto in 1985.” Omron‘s commitment to employing persons with disabilities in this plant (Chennai) reflects exactly that value. It will inspire industries across our State to see ability first, he added. c6695201f3e69211.title: NVS-03 launched successfully; satellite placed in intended orbit | Highlights
c6695201f3e69211.summary: Updated - October 31, 2026 06:11 am IST GSLV-F18 NVS-03 mission accomplished. Photo credit: X/@isro The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV-F18) on Friday (October 30, 2026) successfully launched the NVS-03 satellite from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, according to the ISRO. Also read | Countdown progressing for ISRO’s crucial GSLV-F18 launch carrying navigation satellite NVS-03 The GSLV-F18 with the NVS-03 satellite lifted off from the second launch pad of the spaceport and, 18 minutes later placed the satellite into the intended geosynchronous transfer orbit. “The GSLV-F18 vehicle has successfully and precisely injected the NVS-03 satellite weighing 2250 kg in the intended elliptical orbit. Let me congratulate each and every team member of ISRO, industrial partners, academia for this outstanding accomplishment,” ISRO Chairman Dr. V. Narayanan said. NVS-03 has reached its intended orbit, says ISRO The GSLV rocket carrying the next-gen navigation satellite NVS-03 lifts off from Sriharikota Spaceport. 18.46 minutes later, the GSLV-F18 is expected to place the NVS-03 satellite into the intended geosynchronous transfer orbit. Cryo-stage performance of GSLV rocket normal ISRO’s live coverage of the GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission will begin at 11:20 pm IST on October 30, ahead of the scheduled 11:51 pm launch from Sriharikota. ISRO’s NVS satellite launch programme has seen considerable gaps between missions. NVS-01 was launched in May 2023, followed by NVS-02 in January 2025, a gap of 19 months. The next satellite, NVS-03, is scheduled for launch in October 2026, nearly 20 months after its predecessor. The pace of launches has also been affected by setbacks in ISRO’s broader mission programme. The space agency recorded three failures in six missions launched from Indian soil between January 2025 and January 2026, adding to the challenges of maintaining a steady launch schedule. Nagaprasanna says that the court will pass orders on head of the SIT by considering the names of four senior officers suggested by the State government in terms of the order passed by the apex court on an appeal filed by the government. The State government on Friday issued a notification declaring the Special Investigation Team (SIT), which has been constituted by the High Court of Karnataka to probe cases related to alleged irregularity and corruption in recruitment process in the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC), to be a police station under Section 2(1)(u) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). The investigation officers appointed to the SIT are authorised under Section 193 of the BNSS to file police reports before the competent courts after investigation into the two cases related to the KPSC irregularities, it has been stated in the notification, a copy of which has been submitted to the High Court on Friday. c1472de631cd1612.title: Heavy polling in second phase panchayat elections for Sarpanch, Ward Panch in Rajasthan
c1472de631cd1612.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 04:25 am IST - JAIPUR Women voters walk towards a polling station to cast their votes during the second phase of the Panchayat elections (Sarpanch) in Ajmer. | Photo Credit: ANI A heavy polling took place in the second phase of village panchayat elections for Sarpanch and Ward Panch in 22 districts of Rajasthan on Friday (October 30, 2026). While 45 Sarpanches were earlier elected unopposed, as many as 3,626 village panchayats went to polls and 1.06 crore voters exercised their franchise. The highest voter turnout was recorded at 84.37% in Jaipur district’s Rampura Dabri. Voters arrived at polling booths in large numbers, enthusiastically, with elderly people and women seen standing in queues to exercise their right to vote. People turned up to vote despite light rain and drizzle at places such as Kotputli-Behror, situated on the Jaipur-Delhi national highway, and the Malakhera area in Alwar district. Counting of votes started immediately after the polling ended, while the results were expected to be declared by late night. Residents of Karanpur village in Dausa district’s Mahwa area boycotted polling in protest against the delimitation exercise, while the villagers at Dausa’s Pyara Ka Nagla and Jalore’s Bawatra and Dayalpur did not turn up for voting in protest against the change of their panchayats. Rajasthan gram panchayat polls: second phase held amid reports of minor clashes, protests Rival groups of villagers in Kotputli-Behror’s Majra Aheer and Jodhpur’s Sangariya Phata clashed over allegations of bogus voting. Police intervened at both places and brought the situation under control. 0c619ef70855dd06.title: Delhi BLOs to record reasons for removing names of eligible voters
0c619ef70855dd06.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 04:30 am IST - NEW DELHI Details of an elector being recorded at a special camp in New Delhi. | Photo Credit: SUSHIL KUMAR VERMA Booth Level Officers (BLOs) in Delhi have been asked to record why eligible electors were earlier marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate (ASDD), and why those traced during re-verification are unwilling to submit Form 6 to get their names back on the rolls as new voters, The Hindu has learnt. The instructions come amid the ongoing re-verification of 47.56 lakh names dropped from the draft roll published on August 31 after being placed in the ASDD categories. On Thursday, the Election Commission of India (ECI) pushed the deadline for publishing Delhi’s final electoral roll to December 22, marking the fourth such revision. As per the revised schedule, the deadline for filing claims and objections has been extended by 26 days, from October 30 to November 25, giving eligible electors more time to seek inclusion in the final roll during the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) drive. The disposal of claims and objections will have to be completed by December 15. A new ‘Remarks’ column has been added to the BLO mobile application to record details of the re-verification exercise. This field will be used to record why an elector was placed in the ASDD categories during the enumeration phase, whether the person was found residing at the registered address and, if eligible, why the person was reluctant to submit Form 6. The column will also be used to record cases in which an elector is found at the registered address but has already enrolled in another constituency. BLOs have been provided with the ASDD lists, along with the corresponding addresses, and instructed to conduct door-to-door visits to verify the voters’ details. 60f4661931bde0bf.title: Keralam Chief Minister calls for protecting Vembanad lake system
60f4661931bde0bf.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 07:00 am IST - KOCHI Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan releases B. Madhusoodana Kurup’s book, ‘Exploring the Legacy of Fishing and Farming below Sea Level: Vembanad-Kole Wetlands of South India’, by handing over copies to former Fisheries ministers K. Babu and S. Sarma at a function held in Kochi on Friday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan has called for steps to protect the ecology of the Vembanad lake system, which has come under severe stress due to a host of factors including climate change. Mr. Satheesan was speaking at a commemorative function organised here to pay tributes to noted fisheries expert B. Madhusoodana Kurup who passed away recently. Kurup, who co-authored the book, ‘Exploring the Legacy of Fishing and Farming below Sea Level: Vembanad-Kole Wetlands of South India,’ with Sileesh Mullasseri, had brought out issues facing the lake ecosystem, which has shrunk to 10,000 sq. km. from its original extent of 40,000 sq. km. Anthropogenic activities and impacts of climate change have adversely affected the lake system, which is spread over three districts of the State and sustains the lives of millions. He had also put forth a series of projects for the revival and protection of the lake, Mr. Satheesan said. The Chief Minister suggested setting up a chair at the Kerala University for Fisheries and Ocean Studies (Kufos) in Kurup’s name to take forward the academic and research activities initiated by him. Kurup was the founding Vice-Chancellor of the university. Mr. Satheesan released the book by handing over copies to K. Babu and S. Sarma, former Fisheries ministers. Fisheries Minister V.E. Abdul Gafoor presided. Mayor V.K. Minimol, T.J. Vinod and Mohammed Shiyas, MLAs; K.V.P. Krishnakumar, councillor, Kochi Corporation; A. Bijukumar, Vice-Chancellor, Kufos; M. Junaid Bushiri, Vice-Chancellor, Cochin University of Science and Technology (Cusat); and P.C. Hari Govind, Registrar, Cusat, spoke. Publish

05beb36896da58a1.title: Fiscal deficit rises to ₹7.14 trillion or 42.1% of FY27 target in first six months
05beb36896da58a1.summary: New Delhi: India's fiscal deficit widened in the first six months of FY27, as capital spending and subsidy outlays continued to rise. Fiscal deficit, or the gap between government expenditure and receipts, stood at ₹ 7.14 trillion at the end of September, latest data from the Controller General of Accounts (CGA) showed. This amounts to 42.1% of the full-year budget estimate, higher than 36.5% in the corresponding period of the previous year. At the end of August, the fiscal deficit had stood at 41.9% of the annual target. The higher proportion of the budgeted fiscal deficit already incurred in the first half of FY27 indicates mounting pressure on the government's fiscal balance, with expenditure growing faster than the pace of deficit accumulation seen in the year-ago period. The Centre has budgeted a fiscal deficit of ₹ 16.96 trillion, or 4.3% of GDP, for FY27. It is relying on robust tax collections and higher non-tax revenues in the coming months to meet this target. The fiscal deficit is typically financed through borrowings. The widening gap assumes significance as the government has cut its FY27 market borrowing by nearly ₹ 1.2 trillion and now plans to raise ₹ 7.86 trillion through dated government securities in the second half of the fiscal year, as Mint reported on 25 September. The Centre now expects to borrow ₹ 15.995 trillion through dated securities during FY27, compared with ₹ 17.2 trillion estimated in the Union budget, according to the finance ministry 's borrowing plan released in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on 25 September. “The impact of higher subsidy outgo as well as front-loading of capex has led to a much higher H1 fiscal deficit compared to previous fiscal year, with the increase being 4.6 percentage points. f0b2416c0355ccd3.title: Glacial Lake Outburst Flood damages roads, washes away bridge in Bhutan
f0b2416c0355ccd3.summary: Updated - October 31, 2026 03:06 am IST - GELEPHU (BHUTAN) A road blocked with mud and debris in the aftermath of a flood, in Punakha, Bhutan. | Photo Credit: Reuters GELEPHU (BHUTAN) A glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) in Shintapu Tsho in the Laya area of northwestern Bhutan’s Gasa district on Thursday night (October 29, 2026) triggered flooding along the Mochhu, damaging roads, bridges and public infrastructure in two districts. Officials on Friday (October 30, 2026) said no human casualties have been reported, but there are growing concerns over a large artificial lake formed near Taktsemakhang, about 2,000 feet downstream of Laya. The accumulation of water at the confluence of the flood-affected channels of Mochhu (river) has raised fears of another sudden outburst, which could be disastrous for downstream areas. Officials said they could not immediately assess the GLOF impact on Thursday night (October 29, 2026). Royal Bhutan Army personnel stationed at Taktsemakhang and people near Gasa Tshachu, a hot spring, were instructed to evacuate to a safer location. “Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay is in Laya to assess the artificial lake at Taktesakhang, while Industry, Commerce and Employment Minister Namgyel Dorji is monitoring the situation in Punakha,” a Department of Local Governance and Disaster Management official said. Punakha and Thimphu districts are south of Gasa, which borders the Tibetan Autonomous Region. These and other neighbouring districts were put on high alert for potential danger from the GLOF-induced artificial lake. According to disaster management officials, Gasa Tsachu, one of Bhutan’s popular hot spring destinations, suffered extensive damage due to Thursday’s (October 29, 2026) GLOF. Floodwaters washed away almost all public facilities in the area. 2bb490adffdd451a.title: High Court directs BU to collect charges from autonomous colleges only within parameters of UGC regulations
2bb490adffdd451a.summary: Updated - October 31, 2026 07:01 am IST - COIMBATORE Image used for representational purposes only | Photo Credit: The Hindu Bharathiar University was directed by the Madras High Court on Thursday, through an interim order, to collect charges from autonomous colleges only within the parameters of UGC regulations. Justice K. Surendar passed the interim order and listed the matter for hearing on November 25, 2026. The writ petition filed by Association of Self Financing Arts, Science and Management Colleges of Tamil Nadu (ASFASM TN) had sought a directive to the respondents: the State of Tamil Nadu represented by then Principal Secretary to the Government, Higher Education Department, the Registrar of Bharathiar University, and University Grants Commission, to desist from demanding and collecting affiliation fee, continuation of provisional affiliation fee and permanent affiliation fee from the Autonomous Colleges contrary to Clause 3.5 of the University Grants Commission (Conferment of Autonomous Status upon Colleges and Measures for Maintenance of Standards in Autonomous Colleges) Regulations, 2023. The association was also against the university’s insistence on prior approval for starting certificate/diploma courses and U.G./P.G. programmes, pointing out that it was a violation of Clause 10 of UGC Regulations, 2023. 8fe951e2cb488efa.title: Man sets house ablaze; firefighter injured in cylinder blast
8fe951e2cb488efa.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 04:45 am IST A 30-year-old man, described as an alcoholic, allegedly set his house on fire in northwest Delhi’s Jahangirpuri on Friday, triggering a massive blaze in which an LPG cylinder exploded and a firefighter sustained 25% burn injuries, police said. The police received a PCR call at 11.26 a.m. about a fire on the ground floor of a house in Jahangirpuri. Bharat (30), who lived with his mother, Raj Rani, allegedly set the house on fire. His mother was also present at the house when the incident occurred, the police said. While the fire brigade team was engaged in extinguishing the blaze, an LPG cylinder exploded, injuring Ankit (32), an Assistant Fire Officer with the Delhi Fire Service. He sustained burns to his face, hair and both hands, the police said. Ankit was initially taken to Babu Jagjivan Ram Memorial Hospital, where his injuries were assessed at around 25% burns. He was subsequently referred to the burn ward of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences for further treatment. Fire department officers said the blaze involved household articles and an LPG cylinder on the ground floor of the three-storey building. The police have registered an FIR against Bharat under Section 36(g) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for mischief by fire. Further investigation is under way. The 120 wards have 18,37,901 voters and 1,990 polling stations, of which 1,581 are in government buildings and 409 in private ones. Palem, Mr. Kishore directed officials to finish preparations well in advance and plan an orderly issue of material. Material for each station is to be sorted beforehand with identification labels, and the checklist is to be verified at the time of issue. With campaigning having ended at 5 p.m., he reminded parties, candidates, and agents that the silent period is in force. Public meetings, rallies, processions, and campaigning through loudspeakers or on social media in violation of the rules are prohibited. Voters will be given a pink ballot paper for the mayoral candidate and a white one for the corporator, and both are to be dropped in a single box. 74f97baf653e9aa4.title: Environmentalists express ‘serious concerns’ over Yamuna riverfront project
74f97baf653e9aa4.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 04:30 am IST A former Union Ministry Secretary and other environmentalists on Friday wrote to Union Jal Shakti Minister C. R. Patil and others, raising “serious concerns” over the proposed riverfront development project along the Yamuna in Delhi. They urged the authorities to ensure that no project compromises the integrity of the river, its floodplain and the national capital’s long-term flood security. The letter said several media reports over the past week had quoted Water Minister Pravesh Sahib Singh as announcing the initiation of the process for an MoU with the Sabarmati Riverfront Development Corporation Limited (SRFDCL) for a Sabarmati-style riverfront development project along the Yamuna in Delhi. “We wish to underline that replication of a Sabarmati-like riverfront development plan cannot resolve the crisis of Yamuna pollution, floodplain mismanagement and flood threats; it will only worsen the situation. The Government first needs a scientifically sound plan to restore the river’s environmental flows, reduce pollution load, protect its floodplain and understand the causes of its changing flood behaviour,” the letter said. The letter was signed by Shashi Shekhar, former Secretary at the Ministry of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation; Bhim Singh Rawat of the South Asia Network on Dams, Rivers and People (SANDRP); environmental activist Bhavreen Kandhari; and others. The signatories urged the Central government Ministries concerned and the Delhi government to ensure that no project compromises the Yamuna’s integrity, its floodplain and the national capital’s long-term flood security. “Public resources should be directed towards addressing the causes of the river’s degradation and flood risks, rather than undertaking large-scale riverfront development plan,” the letter said. 17f0ee319a7537c7.title: TNUHDB identifies 20 sites for reconstruction across State; appeals to residents of dilapidated tenements to vacate
17f0ee319a7537c7.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 01:17 am IST - CHENNAI The Tamil Nadu Urban Habitat Development Board (TNUHDB) has identified 20 locations across the State for reconstruction of ageing tenements during 2026-27 and plans to build greenfield resettlement sites in Perambur and Madurantakam. TNUHDB Chairperson Ku. Pa. Krishnan, in an interaction with journalists on Friday, said that the reconstruction projects involve demolishing existing ageing tenements and constructing new housing units at the same locations. Residents can return after the work is completed. The Board has identified a total of 70 sites for reconstruction across the State, which will be taken up in phases, he said. The TNUHDB also appealed to residents of 23 dilapidated sites to temporarily vacate their houses in view of the ongoing northeast monsoon. Of the 23 tenements identified in its safety advisory, 14 fell within the locations proposed for reconstruction this year, for which a Government Order is to be issued in the coming week. The remaining nine have been additionally prioritised for safety during the monsoon in view of their dilapidated condition. The 23 tenements include Srinivasapuram, V.O.C. f77cd49b7d46836b.title: Probe into synagogue arson in Keralam’s Kochi intensified: Chennithala
f77cd49b7d46836b.summary: Published - October 31, 2026 07:00 am IST Central agencies are currently gathering information related to the case. The probe into the alleged synagogue arson case has been intensified by constituting a special investigation team (SIT) under the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Ernakulam Central, in accordance with the directions of the Deputy Commissioner of Police (Kochi City), Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has said. He was replying to a submission on the matter raised in the Assembly by T.J. Vinod, MLA. Mr. Chennithala said the Ernakulam Central Police had registered a case under Section 326(g) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita against Ebin B. Paul, a native of Ikkaranad. The Minister further said that Sections 15 and 16 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) had also been added to the case after investigators obtained information suggesting possible extremist links of the accused. Central agencies are currently gathering information related to the case. c2e2ddbb5421332d.summary: This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. The Delhi High Court has sought details of assets held by Future Group promoters Kishore Biyani and his brother Rakesh Biyani as lenders move to recover nearly ₹ 800 crore in dues linked to personal guarantees given for loans to group companies. A bench of Justice Vinod Kumar on Friday issued notices to the brothers and directed them to file affidavits disclosing their assets, including bank accounts and shareholdings, within a week. The court will hear the matter next on 19 November. The petitions have been filed by Catalyst Trusteeship Ltd and Phoenix ARC Ltd under Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. The lenders have sought directions requiring the promoters to disclose their assets and financial interests, furnish security for the outstanding amounts and refrain from selling or transferring assets that could affect recovery. They have also sought details of the brothers' personal and beneficial assets, including bank accounts, investments, securities and interests in companies and limited liability partnerships (LLPs). The lenders have expressed concerns that assets could be transferred or disposed of before their claims are resolved. The dispute involving Kishore Biyani dates back to December 2017, when L&T Finance extended loans totalling ₹ 375 crore to Future Entertainment Pvt Ltd, backed by his personal guarantee. After the Covid-19 pandemic hit the company's business, the loans were restructured in June 2021 to around ₹ 262.2 crore, with Biyani providing a fresh personal guarantee. The lenders allege that a promised investment of ₹ 250 crore by Future Brands Ltd in Future Entertainment was never made. They also claim that insolvency proceedings against another Future Group company triggered a default under the loan agreement. 5ad7bef16bff48b4.title: Ayur AI Integrative Diabetes Centre launched in Chennai
5ad7bef16bff48b4.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:55 am IST - CHENNAI The Centre aims at combining traditional Ayurveda with modern diagnostic tools and medicines and AI-driven health assessment to develop individualised approaches to diabetes management. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement An Ayur AI Integrative Diabetes Centre, which adopts an interdisciplinary approach to diabetes management, blending traditional Ayurvedic knowledge, modern medicine, and artificial intelligence, was inaugurated at Dr. RK Diabetic Foot and Podiatry Institute here on Saturday. The Centre aims at combining traditional Ayurveda with modern diagnostic tools and medicines and AI-driven health assessment to develop individualised approaches to diabetes management, said the Institute’s founder and director, Rajesh Kesavan. A clinical study involving about 100 patients has reported promising outcomes, with a 50% improvement in diabetes management and reduction in blood sugar spikes. At the centre, dietary interventions will be customised based on individual body composition and metabolic profiles for diabetes management. An AI kiosk will facilitate AI-based health assessments. Ayur AI founder Bala Pesala said the holistic intervention aims at achieving diabetes remission. Samir Kumar Brahmachari, former Director General, Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, and Bandi Venkateshwarlu, assistant director, Regional Ayurveda Research Institute, Ministry of Ayush, also spoke. c26e86f97531b3ec.title: VIS–The Hindu U-15 inter-school football tournament draws to a close
c26e86f97531b3ec.summary: Published - November 01, 2026 12:31 am IST - Chennai: Students of Velammal Matriculation Higher Secondary School, Mogappair, receiving the trophy and cash prize. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT The third edition of the Vellore International School (VIS) U-15 inter-school football tournament, in association with The Hindu, concluded at the VIS campus near Kelambakkam on Saturday. The tournament witnessed participation from 64 teams representing schools across Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram, Chengalpattu, Vellore, and Tiruvannamalai. It also featured around 14 government and government-aided schools. Young footballers demonstrated their technical abilities, tactical understanding, as well as sporting discipline through a series of competitive encounters. Velammal Matriculation Higher Secondary School, Mogappair, emerged as the champions for the second consecutive year. Don Bosco Matriculation Higher Secondary School, Egmore, secured the second place, while Dr. Guruswamy Mudaliar Thondaimadala Thuluvala Vellala Higher Secondary School, Sowcarpet, finished third. The winning teams received cash prizes – ₹1,00,000 for the champions, ₹75,000 for the runners-up, and ₹50,000 for the second runners-up. Individual honours were also awarded to outstanding performers. VIS Chennai Chairman and VIT vice-president G.V. Selvam said, “We began the tournament with just schools from Chennai. This year, we have extended it to six northern districts of Tamil Nadu. Next year, we hope to extend it to other States as well.” Chief Guest Sayed Sabir Pasha, Technical Director of the All India Football Federation, said that while hosting a tournament with 64 schools is a great achievement, the tournament should grow further and feature more schools.
