911b88855c3e65da.title: Rain begins in north Andhra ahead of Cyclone Murasu
911b88855c3e65da.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 02:06 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Rough waves lash the Palepalem coast near Kothapatnam in Prakasam district on Monday, ahead of Cyclone Murasu’s expected landfall near Ongole. | Photo Credit: Kommuri Srinivas The first rain from Cyclone Murasu has fallen in north coastal Andhra Pradesh, far from where the storm is headed. The central and south coastal districts, which are on red alert, were yet to see any major rainfall on Monday (November 2, 2026). Kakinada (Rural) mandal recorded the most rain between 8.30 a.m. and noon, 51.75 mm at the MRO office gauge, according to real-time data from the Andhra Pradesh Directorate of Economics and Statistics (APDES). Most of the rain fell in Kakinada, Vizianagaram and Srikakulam districts. Visakhapatnam’s highest reading was 12.5 mm at Gambheeram in Anandapuram mandal. Ongole in Prakasam district, where the landfall is likely to happen, had not recorded any rain as of 10 a.m. The Rayalaseema districts stayed dry. In the 24 hours to 8.30 a.m. on Monday, Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram district recorded the most rain in the State, 102.49 mm at the KVBR School gauge. Meanwhile, the severe cyclonic storm over the west-central and southwest Bay of Bengal is moving west-northwestwards at 22 kmph towards the A.P. coast. More of SRN Mehta State School in Kalaburagi with representatives of the school’s management and teachers after securing fifth place in the State-level under-14 chess championship and qualifying for the national-level competition. | Photo Credit: ARUN KULKARNI Anish P. More, a student of SRN Mehta School in Kalaburagi, has been selected to participate in the national-level chess championship to be held in Madhya Pradesh after securing fifth place in the State-level under-14 chess competition. 1eff5fc8eac5c5a4.title: Coast Guard evacuates fisherman in distress 100 km off Mangaluru coast
1eff5fc8eac5c5a4.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 01:24 pm IST - MANGALURU Indian Coast Guard Ship C-448 reaches Indian fishing boat Shiv Sagar, about 100 km off the Mangaluru coast, to rescue a fisherman in urgent need of medical attention on the night of November 1, 2026. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Indian Coast Guard (ICG), District Headquarter 3, Mangaluru, safely evacuated a fisherman in urgent need of medical attention from a fishing vessel sailing about 100 km off Mangaluru coast on November 1 night. The headquarters received a distress call over VHF from Indian Fishing Boat (IFB) Shiv Sagar, operating approximately 54 NM (100 km) off Mangaluru on November 1. They were told that a fisherman had fallen overboard while hauling fishing nets. He was rescued, but required urgent medical attention, and shifting to a hospital. The ICG deployed Indian Coast Guard Ship C-448, which located the fishing boat amid the darkness of the night. The disoriented fisherman, identified as Komara Ramu, was safely evacuated, provided immediate first aid, and transferred to New Mangalore Port Authority jetty. He was subsequently shifted to the nearest hospital for further medical management. IFB Shiv Sagar had sailed out of Old Mangaluru Port three days ago, ICG informed. a00438c594b93c32.title: KBN Hospital hosts workshop on hysterectomy and advanced laparoscopy in Kalaburagi
a00438c594b93c32.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 12:18 pm IST - KALABURAGI Dignitaries inaugurate the advanced live laparoscopy workshop organised by Khaja Banda Nawaz University and the Karnataka State Obstetrics and Gynaecology Association at KBNTGH in Kalaburagi on October 30, 2026. | Photo Credit: ARUN KULKARNI A workshop on ‘Hysterectomy: Different Approaches and Advanced Laparoscopy’ was conducted at Khaja Banda Nawaz Teaching and General Hospital (KBNTGH) in Kalaburagi on October 30 as part of the conference of the Karnataka State Obstetrics and Gynaecology Association (KSOGA), in collaboration with Khaja Banda Nawaz University. The workshop provided a platform for gynaecologists and medical professionals to interact with experts and gain insights into the latest technologies, techniques and developments in the field. Around 150 delegates from different parts of Karnataka had registered for the programme. Ten surgical procedures performed in the operation theatre were telecast live to the seminar hall, enabling participants to observe the procedures, and interact with experts during the sessions. Highlighting the importance of the workshop, Professor Syed Ashfaq Ahmed said it could bring positive changes to the lives of many women by promoting awareness and knowledge of modern treatment options. He said participants had benefited from direct interaction with specialists and gained valuable information about recent advances in medical technology. He reiterated the hospital’s commitment to providing quality healthcare to all sections of society, particularly the poor and needy. He said the hospital was upgrading its departments with advanced technology to emerge as a leading, well-equipped medical centre in the region. It was also organising free medical screening and treatment camps regularly to protect public health, he added. Khaja Banda Nawaz University Registrar Mir Wilayat Ali praised the university’s continued service to society. He said the workshop was an important initiat

dabaf9ca34ba5c18.title: Chaubey's proposal to liquidate AIFF FD faces opposition from members
dabaf9ca34ba5c18.summary: A proposal by AIFF President Kalyan Chaubey to liquidate the fixed deposit of the federation to pay the deficit arising out of hosting high-profile international friendly matches recently was stalled by members during its Special General Body Meeting (SGBM) on Sunday, officials who attended the event said. Chaubey's attempt to withdraw the AIFF's fixed deposit to make up for the deficit after hosting matches against Brazil, Uruguay and Panama could be a U-turn from his earlier reported claims that the federation would not have to bear any financial burden of the three home friendlies, the officials who attended the meeting, said. "Yes, he (Chaubey) said he wants to liquidate the AIFF's fixed deposit to pay the deficit (arising out of the international friendlies)," a top official of a leading state association told PTI on conditions of anonymity. The state official attended the online meeting on Sunday. "Later, he (Chaubey) also said that he would arrange funds from outside sources

35d271bddf5e0566.title: Cyclone Murasu: List of flights cancelled to and from Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada
35d271bddf5e0566.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 04:16 pm IST Representational Image | Photo Credit: Velankanni Raj Cyclone Murasu, which has intensified into a ‘Severe Cyclonic Storm’ over the West Central and Southwest Bay of Bengal, has led to flight cancellations on November 2, 2026, owing to adverse weather conditions. Flight services to and from Chennai, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam have been impacted. Chennai International Airport, in a post on social media platform X, said eleven flights have been cancelled to and from Chennai owing to the Cyclone. IndiGo has also confirmed in a post on X that “flight operations to and from Rajahmundry, Vijayawada and Tirupati are impacted.” Cancelled departures from Chennai #FlightUpdate | In view of the adverse weather conditions due to #CycloneMurasu, the following flights have been cancelled. Passengers are requested to contact the concerned airline for further information and assistance. #ChennaiAirport #Cyclone #Murasu #MurasuCyclone #CycloneUpdate #CycloneMurasuUpdate #FlightCancellations #Chennai #Airport #AAIAirports @MoCA_GoI | @AAI_Official | @IndiGo6E | @Pib_MoCA | @PIBChennai Also Read: Cyclone Murasu: 12 flight services cancelled at Vijayawada; Visakhapatnam flights hit IndiGo, in its X post, has said that “We are notifying affected customers on the mobile number provided at the time of booking. Customers are advised to check their flight status before proceeding to the airport.We remain in close coordination with the relevant authorities and continue to closely monitor the situation. The safety and well-being of our customers and crew remain our highest priority.” Chennai Airport has requested passengers to contact the airline for more information and assistance. Travel Advisory Due to adverse weather conditions associated with Tropical Cyclone Murasu, flight operations to and from Rajahmundry, Vijayawada and Tirupati are impacted. We are notifying affected customers on the mobile number provided at the time of booking. Customers

0056552907126bc0.title: Bajaj Auto's total sales during October rise 14% to 591,876 units
0056552907126bc0.summary: Bajaj Auto on Monday posted a 14 per cent year-on-year growth in its total sales during October, with double-digit growth across two-wheelers and commercial vehicles. The automaker's total wholesales stood at 5,91,876 units, against 5,18,170 units in the year-ago period, according to an exchange filing. Domestic sales rose 12 per cent to 3,51,148 units, while exports grew 18 per cent to 2,40,728 units. Total two-wheeler sales increased by 13 per cent to 5,01,194 units from 4,42,316 in the year-ago period. Total commercial vehicle sales were higher by 20 per cent to 90,682 units, compared to 75,854 units. Bajaj Auto's total sales during the April-October period rose 22 per cent to 35,79,011 units. Two-wheeler sales rose 22 per cent to 30,07,707 units, while commercial vehicle sales were higher by 23 per cent at 5,71,304 units.

13f1db64f5be6e0c.title: Ashok Leyland reports 23% growth in October sales to 21,888 units
13f1db64f5be6e0c.summary: Commercial vehicle major Ashok Leyland on Monday reported a 23 per cent year-on-year growth in its total sales during October. The Chennai-based automaker's total sales, including exports, stood at 21,888 units, up from 17,820 units a year ago, according to an exchange filing. Sales in the Medium and Heavy Commercial Vehicle (M&HCV) segment grew 28 per cent to 13,927 units from 10,865 units, while the Light Commercial Vehicle (LCV) segment registered a 14 per cent rise to 7,961 units. Total domestic sales rose 24 per cent to 20,224 units from 16,314 units a year ago, with 32 per cent growth in the M&HCV segment to 12,646 units. Domestic LCV sales increased 13 per cent to 7,578 units.

4576f06676c06a16.title: Suspended Punjab AAP leader Kunwar Vijay Pratap quits as MLA ahead of polls
4576f06676c06a16.summary: Amritsar North MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh announced his resignation, citing a push for clean politics and transparent administration | File Image: X@Kvijaypratap In a major political development ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, Amritsar North MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh announced his resignation from the Punjab Legislative Assembly on Monday. Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh was suspended from the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on June 29, 2025. In a X post addressed to the people of Amritsar, Singh said he would remain indebted to them "until my last breath" for their love and respect. He called for a collective effort to rise above "the politics of lanes and ribbon-cutting" and to bring Punjab, which he described as "trapped by drugs, extortion, gangsterism and corruption", back to being a progressive state. ਬਹੁਤ ਹੀ ਸਤਿਕਾਰਯੋਗ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਸਰ ਦੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਭੈਣ-ਭਰਾਵੋਂ, ਪੰਜਾਬ ਵਿਧਾਨ ਸਭਾ ਦੀ ਮੈਂਬਰਸ਼ਿਪ ਤੋਂ ਮੈਂ ਇਸਤੀਫ਼ਾ ਦੇ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਹੈ। ਮੈਂ ਤੁਹਾਡੇ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਮਿਲੇ ਪਿਆਰ ਅਤੇ ਸਤਿਕਾਰ ਵਾਸਤੇ ਆਖ਼ਿਰੀ ਸਾਹ ਤੱਕ ਰਿਣੀ ਰਹਾਂਗਾ। >ਤੁਹਾਡੇ ਸਹਿਯੋਗ ਅਤੇ ਪਰਮਾਤਮਾ ਦੇ ਆਸ਼ੀਰਵਾਦ ਨਾਲ ਗਲੀ-ਨਾਲੀ ਅਤੇ ਰਿਬਨ-ਕਟਿੰਗ ਦੀ ਰਾਜਨੀਤੀ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਪਰ ਉੱਠ ਕੇ ਨਸ਼ਾ, ਫਿਰੌਤੀ, ਗੈਂਗਸਟਰਵਾਦ ਅਤੇ ਭ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟਾਚਾਰ ਤੋਂ ਜਕੜੇ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਨੂੰ ਮੁੜ ਉੱਨਤਸ਼ੀਲ ਅਤੇ ਮੋਹਰੀ ਸੂਬਾ ਬਣਾਉਣ ਲਈ ਅਸੀਂ ਸਾਰਿਆਂ ਨੇ ਮਿਲ਼ ਕੇ ਇਕਜੁਟ ਪ੍ਰਯਾਸ ਕਰਨਾ ਹੈ। >ਵੈਸੇ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਸਾਰੇ ਜਾਣਦੇ ਹੋ ਕਿ ਮੈਂ ਬਤੌਰ ਵਿਧਾਇਕ ਆਪਣਾ 90 ਪਰਸੈਂਟ ਟਾਰਗੇਟ ਪੂਰਾ ਕਰ ਲਿਆ ਹੈ; ਜੋ ਕੰਮ ਇੱਕ ਵਿਧਾਇਕ ਨੇ ਕਰਨਾ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਕੌਂਸਲਰ, ਮੇਅਰ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਂਸਦ ਦੇ ਕੰਮ ਇਸਤੋਂ ਇਲਾਵਾ ਹਨ। >ਮੈਂ ਇਲਾਕਾ ਵਾਰ ਆਪਣੇ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਕਰਾਏ ਕੰਮਾਂ ਦਾ ਵੇਰਵਾ ਵੀ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਅਖ਼ਬਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਫੇਸਬੁੱਕ ਪੇਜ ਤੇ ਮੌਜੂਦ ਹੈ। >ਮੇਰੀ ਸੱਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡੀ ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਮੈਂ ਰਾਜਨੀਤੀ ਤੋਂ ਮਾਈ-ਬਾਪ ਕਲਚਰ ਨੂੰ ਖਤਮ ਕੀਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਇੱਕ ਜਨਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣਾ ਪ੍ਰੇਰਣਾ-ਸਰੋਤ ਸਮਝ ਕੇ ਕੰਮ ਕੀਤਾ। >ਪੰਜਾਬ ਵਿਧਾਨ ਸਭਾ ਦੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੈਂ ਹਮੇਸ਼ਾ ਅੰਬਰਸਰੀਆਂ ਦੀ ਆਵਾਜ ਬੁਲੰਦ ਕੀਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਪਾਣੀ ਸੀਵਰੇਜ ਤੋਂ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਸਰਕਟ ਹਾਊਸ, ਕੰਪਨੀ ਬਾਗ, ਗੰਦਾ ਨਾਲਾ, ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਵ ਯੂਨੀਵਰਸਿਟੀ, ਸਰਕਾਰੀ ਮੈਡੀਕਲ ਕਾਲਜ, ਸਰੂਪ ਰਾਣੀ ਕਾਲਜ ਅਤੇ ਬਰਗਾੜੀ ਬੇਅਦਬੀ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਦੇ ਬੇਬਾਕੀ ਨਾਲ ਰੱਖੇ। ਇਹ ਪਹਿਲੀ ਵਾਰ ਹੋਇਆ ਕਿ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ ਵਿਧਾਨ ਸਭਾ ਦੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਗਲੀ ਅਤੇ ਮੁਹੱਲਾ ਦਾ ਨਾਂ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਇਲਾਕੇ ਵਾਰ ਮੁੱਦੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਵਲੋਂ ਉਠਾਏ ਗਏ। >ਤੁਹਾਡੇ ਨਾਲ ਮਿਲਕੇ ਅੱਗੇ ਦੀ ਸਟ੍

Despite the defeat, India bagged the five-match series 3-2. 836fbbd76fe0e28f.title: Andhra goes ahead with Kotia local body polls despite Odisha’s plea in Supreme Court
836fbbd76fe0e28f.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 03:39 pm IST - PARVATIPURAM A resident of Madkar village in the Kotia gram panchayat shows voter cards issued by both the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha governments. Andhra Pradesh is going ahead with local body polls in the disputed villages on November 5. File | Photo Credit: Biswaranjan Rout The Andhra Pradesh government and the State Election Commission are making all arrangements to conduct local body elections in the Kotia group of villages on the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha border, despite strong objections from Odisha. The neighbouring State has approached the Supreme Court to stop the election process in the disputed region. Both the States have been at odds over the jurisdiction of the Kotia group of villages for about seven decades. Both have also been holding local body elections there for many decades. Odisha has objected before: it filed contempt petitions when Andhra Pradesh held polls in the villages in 2021. This time, it filed a fresh contempt petition last month, alleging that the poll notification violates the Supreme Court’s 2006 order directing both States to maintain the status quo. The villages are located 35 km from Salur town of Parvathipuram Manyam district. Since the court has not passed any order on Odisha’s petition, the Parvathipuram Manyam district administration is making all arrangements to hold elections in places like Ganjai Bhadra, Pagalu Chennuru, Pattu Chennuru, Kurukutti, Sarika, Kotia and other villages on November 5, 2026. The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), which won the Salur Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency and all four Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies in 2021, is keen to win them again with its spirited campaign in all Kotia villages. 7ac472482663b212.title: Cyclone Murasu: Red alert in two Telangana districts, orange in three more on November 3
7ac472482663b212.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 04:21 pm IST - HYDERABAD Nagarkurnool and Nalgonda districts in Telangana were placed under red alert on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT With Cyclone Murasu likely to make landfall at Andhra Pradesh coast between evening of Monday (November 2, 2026) and early morning of Tuesday (November 3, 2026), the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for two Telangana districts and an orange alert in three districts for Tuesday (November 3, 2026). According to the IMDs latest bulletin, a red alert — meaning, heavy to very heavy rain with isolated extremely heavy rainfall — was issued for Nalgonda and Nagarkurnool districts. An orange alert — meaning heavy to very heavy rainfall — was issued for Suryapet, Mahabubnagar and Wanaparthy districts. Additionally, a yellow alert — indicating heavy rainfall with thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds — was issued for Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Mahabubabad, Warangal, Hanumakonda, Jangaon, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri, Rangareddy, Vikarabad, Narayanpet and Jogulamba Gadwal districts. Hyderabad city for the next 24 hours will see a generally cloudy sky. “Moderate to heavy rain or thundershowers by lightning accompanied with gusty winds are very likely to occur in parts of the city towards evening or night. The maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to be 33 C and 23 C respectively’,” as per the bulletin. The latest observed and forecast track of cyclonic storm Murasu, as per India Meteorological Department’s hourly bulletin issued in the afternoon on Monday (November 2, 2026) | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT Published - November 02, 2026 03:02 pm IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. 06beca9cee78fcfc.title: ‘Cyclone Murasu’: Palnadu District Collector declares November 2 holiday for schools, colleges
06beca9cee78fcfc.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 03:00 pm IST - NARASARAOPET (PALNADU DISTRICT) Palnadu District Collector Kritika Shukla. Photo: Special Arranagement Palnadu District Collector Kritika Shukla has announced holiday for all government and private schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres on Tuesday (November 2) in view of Cyclone Murasu. The Collector, in a press release here on Sunday, informed that the district administration has made all necessary arrangements to effectively deal with Cyclone Murasu. Cyclone Murasu LIVE updates: November 02, 2026 A special control room has been set up at the Collectorate to ensure that people do not face any inconvenience due to the cyclone and to facilitate immediate relief measures. The control room will function round-the-clock. Staff have been deployed to provide necessary information to the public and coordinate relief operations. People can contact the control room for emergency assistance or information on the number 08647 252999 In view of the cyclone warnings, the District Collector urged people to remain alert and avoid going outdoors unless absolutely necessary. f0f2e9e125ddf598.title: Shock and regret: scientists react to AI roiling life’s work
f0f2e9e125ddf598.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 03:42 pm IST For decades, three computer scientists built their careers around an idea about the limits of what computers can do. Artificial intelligence may now have shown it to be wrong: OpenAI and Anthropic each said last week that one of their AI models had disproved the exponential time hypothesis (ETH). The hypothesis holds that some problems are so hard that computers can solve them only by trying nearly every possible answer. Hundreds of studies in computer science and biology rely on it. The claim is the latest in a string of AI results that have shaken academia, setting off soul-searching, most notably among mathematicians, over the value of human expertise and the future of their profession. Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi of the University of California San Diego first proposed the hypothesis around 25 years ago. Ryan Williams of MIT, a leading researcher in the field, had long publicly doubted it. The three are now helping organise an independent review of the claims from the AI companies. Q: How did you feel when you learned that a machine may have overturned this hypothesis? Ryan Williams: I did not fully believe the hypothesis, and I’m on the record as a prominent sceptic. So I felt vindicated. Russell Impagliazzo: I’m afraid I am less cheerful about this than the others. I would have much preferred it to be discovered by a human who could explain their thought process. And I’d like to have shaken the (actual) hand of the person who disproved ETH. Q: What is left for human researchers facing the machine? What would you tell a student? Paturi: These breakthroughs extend the frontier of research, but I believe shaping that frontier and moving it forward remain within human capacity and creativity. I would encourage young students to join. They should learn to use these tools while developing their own judgment. c987aed75b01f9ef.title: 37% of pre-SIR Form-6 applications rejected due to absence of declaration form
c987aed75b01f9ef.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 04:35 pm IST - HYDERABAD A large number of applications for fresh voter registration, submitted through Form-6 before the start of Special Intensive Revision, got rejected because they were not accompanied by a declaration form mandated as a prerequisite for enrolment. The image is used for representative purposes only. Shifting goal posts by the Election Commission of India (ECI) with regard to the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the Electoral Rolls have resulted in rejection of tens of thousands of application forms for new voter enrolments in Telangana. A large number of applications for fresh voter registration, submitted through Form-6 before the start of the SIR process, got rejected because they were not accompanied by a declaration form mandated as a prerequisite for enrolment. The declaration form, which was an attachment to the Form-6 exclusively for the SIR process, sought details of the voter or the voter’s parents/relatives from 2002 SIR. In the absence of such details, the applicants were required to submit any of the listed 12 documents as proof of their citizenship. The ECI recently announced that the declaration was not required for submission of Form-6 in States where SIR is not on . It was too late for Telangana, where a large number of voters who had submitted Form-6 before the start of SIR were rejected for lack of the declaration form. As per data obtained from the office of the Telangana Chief Electoral Officer, a total of 5,20,331 applications were received for new enrolments during the pre-SIR period between January 1, 2026 and June 14, 2026. They were not accompanied by the declaration form which was made mandatory only during the SIR process. As per the Registration of Electors Rules, 196, such claims should be exhibited at the office of the Electoral Registration Officer, and disposed of in a week’s time. fa68ea5f3342fcdf.title: Cyclone Murasu: Seven fishermen caught in rough seas rescued in Nellore
fa68ea5f3342fcdf.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 04:10 pm IST - Nellore Fisheries Department officials rescue seven fishermen whose boat was caught in rough seas near Juvvaladinne village in SPSR Nellore district on Monday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement SPSR Nellore district officials have rescued seven fishermen who ventured into the sea near Juvvaladinne village in Kavali constituency on Monday (November 2, 2026) morning. They were brought safely to shore after their boat’s engine broke down at sea. Fishermen had been advised not to venture into the sea in view of Cyclone Murasu. Speaking to the media, District Collector Himanshu Shukla said, “Seven fishermen who had set out for a fishing trip from Juvvaladinne Fishing Harbour noticed changes in the sea conditions while off the coast of Nellore and attempted to return to the harbour. However, their boat’s engine broke down en route, leaving them stranded at sea. Surveillance personnel on duty at the harbour spotted this and immediately alerted the relevant authorities.” Officials and local fishermen pull a boat ashore at Patakadapalem in SPSR Nellore district on Monday after its engine failed in seas made rough by Cyclone Murasu. All seven fishermen on board were rescued. Special Arrangement https://t.co/FbNW0z6qGQ The boat’s anchor snapped, and because of the strong waves, the vessel drifted towards Patakadapalem village in Bogole mandal of the district. The officials of the Fisheries Department and the Marine Police responded immediately. With the assistance of local fishermen, they initiated rescue efforts. Initially, reaching the boat proved difficult because of the high waves. Ultimately, they managed to bring the boat to the shore at Patakadapalem and ensured that all fishermen were safe. 494bf2da99576b8e.title: Cyclone Murasu: CM directs officials to brace for flood into Bapatla district
494bf2da99576b8e.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 04:47 pm IST - BAPATLA Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu reviews preparations for Cyclone Murasu with district officials through a video conference on Monday. Bapatla district is likely to bear the brunt of the storm. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to take all precautionary measures to prevent loss of life and property in Bapatla district in view of Cyclone Murasu , which has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm. He reviewed the preparedness of district administrations through a video conference on Monday (November 2, 2026), attended by Bapatla Collector Vinod Kumar V. The Chief Minister warned that Bapatla was likely to bear the brunt of the cyclone, since heavy inflows of floodwater were expected through irrigation canals from upstream districts, including Guntur, Palnadu, Prakasam and Markapuram. He asked officials to inspect canal bunds, remain alert for four days of heavy inflows, evacuate people from low-lying areas and establish rehabilitation centres. He also said a special officer would be appointed for Bapatla district. In a review meeting on cyclone preparedness, Mr. Naidu said the District Collectors should be alert to meet any contingency keeping in view the likelihood of heavy rains and gales. 5daf79f1d4fa17b2.title: EVMs vs paper ballots: What makes MLC polls different? | Explained
5daf79f1d4fa17b2.summary: Why are paper ballots still used in MLC elections when India uses Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) for Lok Sabha and Assembly polls? The BJP-led NDA’s victory in the recent Legislative Council elections has renewed the political debate over EVMs and paper ballots. But MLC polls follow a different voting system, where voters rank candidates in order of preference. We explain how the single transferable vote system works, why existing EVMs cannot be used for these elections, and which other elections in India still rely on paper ballots.

114481a9559f90ba.title: US consortium pushes for $4.4 billion LNG project in Pakistan: Report
114481a9559f90ba.summary: A consortium of American companies, backed by US President Donald Trump's administration, is seeking up to USD 4.4 billion in investment for an integrated liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Pakistan, according to a media report on Monday. The proposed project will cover imports, storage, regasification, gas transmission and sales to large consumers on a merchant basis, the Dawn newspaper reported. LNG is natural gas that has been cooled to around minus 162 degrees Celsius, turning it into a liquid and reducing its volume by about 600 times. This makes it easier to store and transport by specialised ships. At its destination, the LNG is converted back into gas through a process called regasification and supplied to consumers. It is used to generate electricity, fuel industrial processes, produce fertilisers and provide energy for heating and cooking. It is also used as a fuel in some vehicles and ships. 78d84b6820602584.title: Cyclone Murasu strengthens, heavy rain alerts issued across southern States
78d84b6820602584.summary: Cyclone Murasu has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal and is expected to make landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast near Ongole on November 3. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), wind speeds could reach 100–110 kmph, gusting up to 120 kmph. Schools and colleges have been closed in Chennai and Tiruvallur, while heavy rain alerts have been issued in parts of Telangana. The storm comes just days after Cyclone Arnab battered parts of the eastern coast, leaving six dead in Odisha.

bd9e4166ce611995.title: Palaniswami expresses concern over lower growth rate in Tamil Nadu’s GST collections
bd9e4166ce611995.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:55 pm IST - Chennai AIADMK General Secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami. | Photo Credit: R SENTHILKUMAR The AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Monday expressed concern over the previous month’s reported three per cent growth in the Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections in Tamil Nadu, which was much below the national average. In a post on his social media handle, Mr. Palaniswami referred to the State’s level of inflation which was higher than that of the all-India figure and “diversion” of industrial projects to other States, similar to what was shown in a feature film of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. “How would the GST collections go up unless industry achieved progress, which would, in turn, generate jobs; enable higher growth in Gross Domestic Production and rise in per capita income?” Mr. Palaniswami wondered. Recalling that the Guidance Tamil Nadu, the nodal agency for investment promotion and single-window facilitation, was established when Jayalalithaa was Chief Minister, the AIADMK leader accused the present TVK-led government of having “ruined” it. e21b19eda890a1b1.title: Telangana plans AI-enabled transactions in agri. market yards
e21b19eda890a1b1.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:51 pm IST - HYDERABAD Minister for Agriculture Tummala Nageswara Rao holding a meeting with marketing officials in Hyderabad on Monday. | Photo Credit: By Arrangement The Telangana government is planning to make the agricultural markets in the State AI (artificial intelligence)-enabled for the first time in the country and also make them model markets, Minister for Agriculture Tummala Nageswara Rao said. At a meeting with the agricultural marketing and agriculture departments here on Monday, he said the AI technology would check for irregularities in transactions in market yards. Tenders for introduction of AI technology in the market yards’ transactions would be called within a week. He suggested them to bring into a single digital system all transactions related to farmers — from the farmer entering the market with his/her produce, its sale, payments and others till he/she leaves the market yard. Listing of farmers’ details, allocation of identity number to every lot/crop, assessing crop quality, fixing price, digital bidding/tender details, online auction, farmer’s consent, weighing, sale bills, market charges, payments to farmers, recording of gate exit, e-receipts and e-permits issuance should be done on a single platform. The management information system should also have details of commission agents, traders, price patterns, auction details and others so that they can be cross-checked in future too. The Minister told the officials to study the digital marketing systems being implemented elsewhere in the country. Even the attendance of marketing department officials, including biometric attendance registering, be also made part of the new digital system. The market yards should also have closed-circuit camera systems to monitor maintenance of godowns and daily activities. In a representation, party district secretary M. Jaggunaidu alleged that Mr. Ramesh Babu voted for the mayoral and corporator candidates at Booth No. 115/8 in Ward 115, where, he claimed, the MLA had no vote. The party leaders demanded a thorough enquiry and action against the legislator and concerned officials. According to the leaders, complaints were submitted to the State Election Commissioner and the Returning Officers of the GVMC Pendurthi zone. 88523712e648304f.title: Joint survey to resolve Revenue-Forest land disputes: Ponguleti
88523712e648304f.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:43 pm IST - HYDERABAD Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy at a review meeting with Revenue, Forest and Survey and Settlement officials at the Secretariat on Monday. The Telangana government has decided to undertake joint surveys by the Revenue and Forest departments to find a permanent solution to long-pending disputes over land boundaries, particularly those involving forest, revenue and patta lands. Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy directed officials of both departments to work in close coordination and ensure that ordinary people and farmers do not suffer because of inter-departmental boundary disputes. At a review meeting with Revenue, Forest and Survey and Settlement officials at the Secretariat, the Minister said the government, under the leadership of Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy, was committed to resolving land-related issues that had remained unsettled for decades. Pointing out that the erstwhile Khammam, Warangal and Adilabad districts had substantial forest areas, Mr. Ponguleti said boundary disputes between the Revenue and Forest departments had persisted for several decades. He called for scientific and technology-based joint surveys to establish clear boundaries and prevent such disputes from recurring. Officials should examine the actual ground position and comprehensively reconcile land records, maps and survey details before arriving at conclusions. Issues that could be settled at the field level should be resolved locally, while matters requiring higher-level intervention should be referred to the State government without delay, he said. Observing that prolonged disputes had caused considerable hardship to farmers and landowners, he said he would personally monitor the joint survey exercise and periodically review its progress. ecee93d69cbdb6d7.title: One held in Keralam for securing job in panchayat with fake mark list
ecee93d69cbdb6d7.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:39 pm IST - PALAKKAD Representational image. | Photo Credit: Getty Images A former Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) unit secretary was arrested for allegedly securing a contractual job at Puthukkode grama panchayat here by submitting a fake BCom mark list. The arrested person, K.V. Ganapathy, a native of Puthukkode Kizhakke Gramam, worked as an accountant-cum-IT assistant in the panchayat’s employment guarantee scheme section. The Vadakkenchery police arrested him in connection with the case on Monday. Mr. Ganapathy joined the panchayat on a contractual basis in July 2021, when the Left Democratic Front (LDF) was in power. He continued in the post until July 2026. He had submitted a BCom mark list purportedly issued by the University of Calicut as proof of his educational qualification. After the United Democratic Front (UDF) came to power in the last local body elections, the panchayat committee refused to extend his contract. Mr. Ganapathy then approached the High Court and obtained an order allowing him to continue in the post until September 2026. The alleged fraud came to light during the verification process for his reinstatement. The new panchayat administration became suspicious because Mr. Ganapathy had submitted only a mark list, rather than an original or provisional degree certificate, to prove his qualification. Growing suspicious, the panchayat authorities sent the mark list to the University of Calicut for verification. The university informed them that the document was fake and that Mr. Ganapathy had not passed the BCom degree. 53c883e3af2a990d.title: A.P. set for counting of votes in 92 ULBs on November 3
53c883e3af2a990d.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:39 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA The State Election Commission (SEC) has made arrangements for the counting of votes in 92 urban local bodies (13 Municipal Corporations and 79 Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats) from 8 a.m. on November 3 (Tuesday). SEC Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha, in a press release, said that counting was being conducted for a total of 3,186 wards, including 804 in Municipal Corporations (MCs) and 2,382 in Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats (M&NPs). The total number of counting centres is 138 — 22 in Municipal Corporations and the remaining in Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats. The counting process will be undertaken by 47,817 supervisors, assistants and staff (28,182 in MCs and 19,635 in M&NPs). A total of 1,372 CCTVs have been installed at strong rooms and counting centres (98 in MCs and 126 in M&NPs). Meanwhile, the SEC reported that the final voting percentage in the 92 urban local bodies that went to polls on November 1 stood at 62.16, with 60,22,411 of the 96,89,061 voters exercising their franchise. 1e06532f2305d2f6.title: TG-Redco for speeding up implementation of renewable energy schemes
1e06532f2305d2f6.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:33 pm IST - HYDERABAD Vice-chairman and MD of TG-Redco Jithesh V. Patil holding a virtual meeting with district managers from Hyderabad on Monday. | Photo Credit: Arrangement Vice-chairman and managing director of the Telangana State Renewable Energy Development Corporation (TG-Redco) Jithesh V. Patil has asked officials to accelerate the implementation of renewable energy schemes across the State and achieve planned targets within stipulated timelines. In a virtual meeting held on Monday with the district managers of the Redco, he stressed the need to identify field-level challenges and resolve them promptly through coordination with the departments concerned. He reviewed the Model Solar Village Programme, installation of rooftop solar power plants, solarisation of agricultural pump sets, PM-KUSUM scheme, energy conservation activities and development of electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure. He sought details from the officials on the work completed so far, current status and pending issues. Mr. Patil told the district managers to create awareness among eligible consumers about the benefits of rooftop solar under the Gruha Jyothi scheme. He called for district-level action plans to achieve the targets under agricultural pump set solarisation and the PM-KUSUM scheme. On pending approvals and inspections, he instructed officials to speed up the process of obtaining necessary approvals from various departments and complete pending inspections without delay. 6514719c07d112bf.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:37 pm IST - MADURAI A 21-year-old medical student from Madurai, who was trapped in a Russian detention facility for 10 days amid flight cancellations caused by ongoing war tensions, has returned safely to her hometown following the intervention of Madurai Member of Parliament Su. Venkatesan. Daisy Asha Moraes, a fourth-year student at the South Ural State Medical University in Russia, had planned to return to India on leave for medical reasons. With her visa set to expire on October 20, she booked a flight via Moscow and arrived at the airport on October 18. However, ongoing drone attacks linked to the Russia-Ukraine conflict forced the cancellation of domestic flights, grounding her scheduled journey. When alternative flights failed to materialise immediately, Russian authorities detained her under the classification of overstaying her expired visa, initiating detention proceedings on October 20. Although a local court granted a 10-day grace period, her family faced mounting anxiety that she could be held in detention for up to 90 days. After exhausting other avenues, the student’s father, Arul Moraes, sought the assistance of Mr. Venkatesan. Operating through parliamentary offices in Madurai and New Delhi, Mr. Venkatesan’s team coordinated directly with the External Affairs Minister, senior ministry officials, and the Indian Embassy in Russia. Compiling documentation regarding her medical condition and the war-related flight disruptions, officials presented the case to Russian authorities on October 27, establishing that the student bore no fault in the travel disruption. Originally informed that the student could not leave until November 15, the intervention successfully expedited her departure. Medical assistance and travel arrangements were secured, and Moraes boarded a flight to India on November 1, arriving safely in Madurai. 3ce124ce86c16ef5.title: Chittoor, Annamayya districts brace for Cyclone Murasu
3ce124ce86c16ef5.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:34 pm IST - CHITTOOR/MADANAPALLE The officials are prepared for any emergency following a high alert for Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu across South Andhra Pradesh, projected to impact Chittoor and Annamayya districts over the next 48 hours. While the core system is projected to make landfall between Nellore and Narsapur, the sprawling outer bands of the cyclone are expected to reach the interior Rayalaseema region. Officials have issued an orange alert for Chittoor district, warning of heavy to very heavy rainfall through Monday and Tuesday. Neighbouring Annamayya district, which began the week under a yellow warning, is bracing for an escalation to an orange alert on Tuesday, with expectations of downpours in isolated areas. Officials said that the sudden rain could trigger severe waterlogging in low-lying tracts, spill over swollen streams, and trigger localised flooding in vulnerable rural pockets. Farmers across the Nagari, Chittoor, and Palamaner revenue divisions in Chittoor district and the eastern parts of Annamayya district initiated measures to protect standing paddy, horticultural orchards, and vegetable plots from gusty winds and floodwaters. Officials of the APSPDCL and civic officials were instructed to be prepared in the event of potential snapping of power lines and major roadblocks caused by uprooted trees. Annamayya district Collector Nishant Kumar said that with the crucial 48-hour window under way, the district machinery has swung into action at all vulnerable areas. “Revenue, police, municipal, and disaster response teams remain stationed on high alert in flood-prone zones,” he said. a14467189d646d17.title: Telangana Civil Supplies officials uncover rice sale violations, hoarding in Hyderabad
a14467189d646d17.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:35 pm IST - HYDERABAD Diversion of rice meant for Public Distribution System (PDS) was one of the violation detected by Telangana Civil Supplies teams during checks between October 29 and 31. The image is used for representative purposes only. | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT Telangana Civil Supplies Department officials uncovered violations in sale of rice at a few outlets in Hyderabad and Rangareddy districts. The violations include weight manipulations by traders by affixing 26-kilogram labels onto bags having only 25 kilograms of rice , and exorbitant prices pasted over the rates printed by manufacturers. The department’s teams lodged complaints at Saroornagar, Jeedimetla, and Alwal police stations, based on which action was initiated, as per official information. This follows surprise checks by the Enforcement Task Force (ETF) along with the Legal Metrology Department across Hyderabad and Ranga Reddy districts between October 29 to 31. The other violations detected include diversion and hoarding of Public Distribution System (PDS) rice, traders operating without mandatory trade, GST, Labour, or FSSAI licenses. The teams have documented the offences on-site by taking videos and photos. The department stated that the vigilance will continue. The State government on Saturday (October 31, 2026) announced a ceiling on maximum retail price (MRP) on three varieties of fine rice in the urban limits , which are most consumed by people. As per the orders, price of a kg of BPT/KNM variety was fixed at ₹66; RNR/Telangana Sona at ₹74 and HMT/JSR variety at ₹79, in Hyderabad and Medchal. d4535bfeee0e14e6.title: Pawan Kalyan directs high alert as Cyclone Murasu nears Nellore coast
d4535bfeee0e14e6.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 07:38 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan | Photo Credit: File photo Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan has directed officials to remain on high alert as cyclone Murasu approaches the coast, even as the State is yet to recover from the damage caused by cyclone Arnab. At a review meeting with senior officials of the Panchayat Raj and Rural Development and Rural Water Supply Departments on Monday, Mr. Kalyan said the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had warned of extremely heavy rain in Nellore, Prakasam, Markapuram, Bapatla and Krishna districts. In view of the forecast of intense rainfall, he stressed the need to evacuate people living in low-lying areas to safer locations, ensure proper coordination among departments, minimise hardship and prevent loss of life. Officials informed the Deputy Chief Minister that the cyclone was initially forecast to cross the coast between Bapatla and Machilipatnam. However, it had changed course and was now expected to make landfall near Nellore. Heavy rain was already lashing Nellore, Prakasam, Bapatla, Tirupati and Markapuram districts under the influence of the cyclone. Six National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and seven State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams had been kept on standby, officials said. They added that other necessary precautionary measures were being taken. 8d7756523fa00748.title: Residents seek closure of Tasmac outlet, illegal recreation club in Keela Arasadi panchayat
8d7756523fa00748.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:43 pm IST - THOOTHUKUDI: Residents of Thuppaspatti and Ayyanarpuram at the Collectorate in Thoothukudi on Monday. | Photo Credit: N. RAJESH Residents of Thuppaspatti and Ayyanarpuram in the district on Monday submitted a petition to the Collector, seeking closure of a newly opened Tasmac outlet and an ‘llegal’ recreation club nearby. The petition was submitted at the weekly grievance redressal meeting chaired by Collector Vishu Mahajan. In their petition, the villagers said the Tasmac outlet and the club in Thuppaspatti-Ayyanarpuram area under Keela Arasadi panchayat were causing several problems. Also, while staging continuous protests demanding the closure of both outlets, anti-social elements were issuing death threats to the protesters. The petitioners said that drunken people made it a regular practice to engage in quarrels in nearby thickets, break and throw liquor bottles and lie around in an intoxicated state. This raised serious safety concerns among women, who left for work at the salt pans early in the morning, and school students passing through the area. The residents urged the authorities to permanently shut down the Tasmac outlet and the recreation club, which were causing inconvenience to the public, and take stringent action against those threatening and intimidating the villagers. In a separate petition, Sudalai of Meelavittan and other villagers said that 70 goats died after allegedly consuming wastewater discharged from a fertilizer godown owned by a private company at Veeranayakkanthattu near Thoothukudi. The animals had been grazing in the area. They sought criminal action against the godown management and adequate compensation for the loss of goats. 668d07ff7e0eaaea.title: Ranji Trophy: Urvil and Vishal boost Gujarat
668d07ff7e0eaaea.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:37 pm IST - Ahmedabad Opener Aarya hit six fours and three maximums in his 95. | Photo Credit: VIJAY SONEJI A frustratingly familiar script unfolded again for Kerala at the Narendra Modi stadium here on Monday. For the third time this season, Kerala allowed the opposition’s lower-order to fight back and wrest away the hard-earned advantage. An unbeaten, counterattacking 111-run partnership for the sixth wicket between Urvil Patel (63 batting, 67b, 7x4, 1x6) and Vishal Jayswal (50 batting, 83b, 3x4, 2x6) was the latest to hurt Kerala as Gujarat ended the opening day of the Ranji Trophy Elite Group C match at 300 for five. Soon after tea, Kerala had Gujarat in a spot of bother at 189 for five when Jaymeet Patel (one) was stumped by Mohammed Azharuddeen off Aditya Sarvate. But the visiting side let Gujarat off the hook when it failed to grab the chances and wilted under the calculated assault by Urvil and Vishal. Rohan Kunnummal showed poor judgement while running back and failed to reach a skier from Vishal off Vaisakh Chandran when the batter was on 33. Azharuddeen fumbled when Urvil, on 32, stepped out to attack Sarvate. Urvil and Vishal capitalised on these errors to take their side to a position of strength in the final session. Earlier, Kerala had crawled back into the contest in the post-lunch session, picking up four wickets to reduce the host to 182 for four. The strikes included that of top-scorer Aarya Desai (95, 132b, 6x4, 3x6), who in a hurry to reach his hundred top-edged a wild slog and was caught by Vishnu Vinod off Vaisakh. In the morning, openers Aarya and Abhishek Desai played fluently against the Kerala bowlers who found little help from the track. However, a better disciplined show with the ball in the second session choked the flow runs which forced the Gujarat batters to take the risks, which ultimately led to their downfall. The scores: Gujarat — 1st innings: Abhishek Desai c Rohan b Nidheesh 42, Aarya Desai c Vi

The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has proposed a 70-km inter-corridor highway connecting NH 81 in Tiruppur district to NH 544 near Sankari in Salem district. The project cost is estimated at ₹ 2,000 crore and the four-way lane is expected to pass through about 19 km in Namakkal district. Farmers have raised opposition, stating that the project would severely affect farmlands, schools, spinning mills, and houses. P. Perumal, general secretary of the Tamil Nadu Vivasayigal Sangam, said the project starts at Padaiveedu town panchayat in Namakkal district and passes through Sowdapuram, Patharai, Pallipalayam Agraharam, Elanthakuttai, Kadachanallur, and Pappampalayam panchayats before entering Erode district. The project envisions laying 150-ft road for 19 km in Namakkal district. This would affect around 200 acres of farmland, schools at Padaiveedu, Uppupalayam, spinning mills, and over 100 houses. Likewise, 18 village roads will have to be destroyed for the project. Two weeks ago, farmers from seven villages submitted a petition against the project at the divisional-level farmers’ grievances meet at the Pallipalayam panchayat union office. 783e08fb334bc57d.title: PWD employees stage black badge protest over delayed October salary
783e08fb334bc57d.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 07:52 pm IST - MADURAI Employees of the Tamil Nadu Government Public Works Department Accounts and Administrative Staff Association staged a State-wide protest on Monday, wearing black badges to condemn the non-disbursement of October salary to over a thousand employees across the Public Works Department (PWD) and the Water Resources Department. The salary delay, affecting personnel from chief engineers down to office assistants, has severely impacted livelihoods as the Deepavali festival approaches, said Abdul Najimudeen, general secretary of the association. Association representatives revealed that the delay stemmed from files pending in the Finance Department and the salary item being disabled in the IFHRMS portal, leaving employees unable to receive timely pay even with government intervention. They noted that pay authorisation bottlenecks—with delays recurring every three to six months—and unapproved temporary posts have created major administrative hurdles, echoing a similar crisis last July when salaries were delayed past the 15th of the month. The association has put forward an eight-point charter of demands, urging the State government to disburse salaries immediately on a war footing and find a permanent solution to departmental issues rather than handling staff livelihoods casually. Key demands include issuing requested transfers pending for the last five months, promoting over 450 junior assistants and typists, regularising temporary workers who have served for over a decade, revoking Government Order No. 69, converting divisional accountant posts into a State service, and filling all vacant positions. Warning that this year’s festival risks becoming a ‘black Deepavali’ for PWD staff, the union announced escalated protests if their grievances are ignored. A zonal-level dharna is scheduled for November 17, followed by a massive hunger strike at the Chennai PWD campus on December 8. Published - November 02, 2026 07:23 pm IST Te

e32d6b6853bbb527.title: Facial recognition attendance system introduced as pilot project in SCCL’s Kothagudem Area
e32d6b6853bbb527.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:39 pm IST - BHADRADRI KOTHAGUDEM A facial recognition-based attendance system was introduced on a trial basis in the Kothagudem Area of the Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) on Monday. The initiative is part of the SCCL’s efforts to adopt technology in its employee attendance system to enhance transparency. Biometric attendance systems are already in use at some General Managers’ offices in SCCL. However, this is the first time the system is being implemented across the coal mines and departments of an entire area. The initiative is aimed at promoting discipline and punctuality among employees and is expected to improve transparency and productivity, according to an SCCL press release. SCCL has around 40,000 employees, of whom approximately 1,600 work in the Kothagudem Area. The trial run began in the Kothagudem Area as a pilot project on Monday. The system is expected to be extended to mines and departments in other areas in a phased manner. 8568b14a98d223eb.title: Karnataka deploys 500 linemen, equipment to restore power supply in cyclone-hit Andhra Pradesh
8568b14a98d223eb.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:49 pm IST - Bengaluru The State government is providing contingency funds to meet travel, accommodation and other emergency expenses of the deployed personnel. | Photo Credit: File Photo Karnataka has deployed 500 trained power utility workers and specialised equipment to Andhra Pradesh to help restore electricity infrastructure damaged by Cyclone Arnab. The deployment follows a request from the Andhra Pradesh government for manpower and equipment to carry out restoration work in cyclone-affected areas. The Karnataka government has mobilised the teams under the supervision of Energy Minister K.J. George as part of inter-State cooperation. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar spoke to his Andhra Pradesh counterpart N. Chandrababu Naidu over the phone and assured him of Karnataka’s support. “Electricity is an essential service, and restoring it immediately is necessary for the well-being of people affected by the disaster. Karnataka stands firmly with the people of Andhra Pradesh during this difficult time,” the Chief Minister said. Mr. George said Karnataka’s teams would work closely with Andhra Pradesh officials to restore power supply at the earliest through field-level coordination and the deployment of specialised equipment. The State has sent 500 trained linemen, 15 Palfinger trucks equipped with cranes and earth augers, and 25 tractor-mounted drilling machines. The teams were mobilised on an emergency basis and left for Andhra Pradesh on Monday afternoon, reaching the State by midnight. For effective deployment and coordination, each electricity supply company (ESCOM) has appointed a single-point contact officer to liaise with the concerned Andhra Pradesh officials. The linemen have been divided into teams of 10, each led by a junior or assistant engineer. 87ebc376380a8fdf.title: Tight security arrangements for ULB vote counting in Chittoor, Annamayya, Sri Sathya Sai districts
87ebc376380a8fdf.summary: Updated - November 02, 2026 07:36 pm IST - CHITTOOR Elaborate arrangements are in place for counting votes in the urban local body elections across Chittoor, Annamayya, and Sri Sathya Sai districts on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), with officials intensifying security to ensure a tension-free and transparent declaration of results. Annamayya district Collector Nishant Kumar inspected the strong rooms and counting centres in Madanapalle, while Chittoor Collector Sumit Kumar reviewed the arrangements in Chittoor on Monday (November 2). In Sri Sathya Sai district, SP S. Satish Kumar inspected the strong rooms in Dharmavaram and reviewed security arrangements. “Heavy police bandobast has been deployed at counting centres, with special focus on preventing unauthorised entry, maintaining law and order and avoiding clashes between political groups. Strong rooms housing ballot boxes are under round-the-clock security,” said Sumit Kumar. “CCTV surveillance and strict entry regulations will be enforced at counting venues. Candidates and their authorised counting agents only will be allowed inside after verification,” Sri Sathya Sai district Collector A. Shyam Prasad said. a02bb588eee39523.title: Six fishermen safe as fishing boat runs aground at Rushikonda beach in Visakhapatnam
a02bb588eee39523.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:37 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Rescued crew members of the fishing vessel that drifted ashore at Rushikonda beach in Visakhapatnam on Monday. | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT A major maritime mishap was averted when a mechanised fishing boat drifted ashore near Rushikonda Beach on Monday, after its engine failed and ran out of fuel in rough seas. All six fishermen aboard the vessel were unharmed as the boat grounded near the shoreline. According to the fisheries officials and coastal police, the fishing boat, bearing registration number IND.AP.V5.MM.255 and owned by Korangi Narsinga Rao, had set out on a routine fishing expedition off the Visakhapatnam coast a few days ago. Trouble began at mid-sea when the vessel’s engine developed a technical snag and subsequently ran out of fuel. The crew dropped anchor in an attempt to stabilise the drifting vessel. However, strong tidal surges and turbulent waves caused by the adverse weather conditions along the coast caused the anchor line to snap. Unable to manoeuver the vessel in the swelling waters, the boat along with the crew was carried westward by high-energy waves before the boat ran aground near Rushikonda beach. Recounting the incident one of the crew members said: “We lost power after running out of fuel, and before we could secure the boat, the anchor broke under heavy wave pressure. Fortunately, the ocean tides pushed us towards the shore rather than towards the deep sea.” Beach lifeguards, local fishermen, and Coastal Security Police quickly rushed to the spot on seeing the grounded vessel. Officials confirmed that all six crew members managed to disembark safely without sustaining injuries. Marine police authorities and fisheries department staff arrived at Rushikonda to inspect the vessel for structural damage and made arrangements to tow it once sea conditions improve. 00d12a7aa8bf2173.title: Tasmac workers shut shops in Namakkal, Salem
00d12a7aa8bf2173.summary: Published - November 02, 2026 07:49 pm IST - Salem A total of 155 Tasmac outlets in Namakkal and many outlets in Salem downed shutters on Monday, in protest against the implementation of new Environmental and Social Welfare Cess. Meanwhile, on Sunday evening, three customers went to an outlet at Pillur near Paramathi Velur, returned the empty liquor bottles and demanded money. Due to server issues, the bottles could not be scanned and it resulted in a quarrel between the customers and the salesman, Purusothaman (46). During the quarrel, the three men hit Purusothaman with a bottle and he sustained injuries. He was admitted to Paramathi Velur Government Hospital. Similarly, customers attacked another salesman, Marimuthu, at Nallar outlet and damaged his two-wheeler. In Salem district, acting on complaints that Tasmac workers were collecting excess money for bottles, the officials checked an outlet at Venkatappa Chetty Street at Pal Market on Sunday evening. They found the allegations to be true. Following this, the outlet salesmen Senthil, Pachaperumal, and supervisor Govindan were placed under suspension. The Collector assured that action will be taken. More than a hundred villagers and members of the women’s self-help group from Velanoor (South) village in Keelakarai taluk, Ramanathapuram district, besieged the Collectorate, demanding the establishment of a mobile ration shop in their village. They then stated that they intended to submit their family cards along with a petition to Collector M. Sivaguru Prabhakaran at the public grievance redressal meeting. After the Collector assured them that appropriate action would be taken, the villagers returned with their family cards. The villagers stated, “There are 210 family cards in our village. We all purchase essential goods from the ration shop operating in Velanoor North Street, which is located one km away. As Scheduled Caste community people, we face various hardships when we go there to buy goods from a ration shop located in an area where people of another community reside. So, we have submitted petitions multiple times to the District Supply Officer to set up a mobile ration shop in our village once a month. On July 7th, we staged a siege protest at the Keelakarai Tahsildar’s office. During the talks held under the chairmanship of the Tahsildar that day, an assurance was given to set up a mobile ration shop. However, no ration shop has been set up to date. Hence, we came to surrender our family cards to the District Collector. The Collector has assured us that action will be taken.” Published - November 02, 2026 07:35 pm IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. 5f086c92e806d54a.summary: Former India batter Cheteshwar Pujara believes the ODI series between India and New Zealand starting on Wednesday will end 2-2 as he expects the visitors to be at a slight disadvantage owing to some pre-decided mid-series changes in the squad. Pujara also reckoned that at least one game of the five-match series will be washed out. India would be without regular skipper Shubman Gill, and his deputy KL Rahul in the last two games as they will begin preparing for the two-match Test series starting November 19. The ODI series will wind up on November 15. "Two-all. In the first three matches, one team is playing, and then, in the last two matches, another Indian team is going to play. So, I think New Zealand have a slight advantage because you aren't playing the same team in all five matches," Pujara told 'JioStar'. "I'm still backing the Indian team in the first three matches, as I feel they will do well. The last two matches could be a bit of a challenge, but it will be a hard-fought .

In a post on Facebook, Singh -- the MLA from Amritsar North seat -- said he has sent his resignation to Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan. Singh, along with Punjab MLAs Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, joined the BJP in the presence of senior leaders at its headquarters here. His resignation from the Punjab Assembly came on the heels of two other AAP legislators -- Chetan Singh Jouramajra from Samana and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra from Sanour in Patiala district -- resigning from the party on Sunday.

bf5ea52deba87aaa.title: IPO fundraising rises 30% to record ₹84,400 crore in H1FY27: Report
bf5ea52deba87aaa.summary: India's mainboard IPO market witnessed a record fund mobilisation at Rs 84,400 crore in the first half of FY27, registering a 30 per cent rise over the year-ago period, with nearly 94 per cent of the funds raised during the July-September period, according to a report by Grant Thornton Bharat. As many as 71 companies made their stock market debut during April-September 2026, compared with 55 in the corresponding period a year ago. According to the report, the funds raised increased from Rs 64,900 crore in H1 FY26 to Rs 84,400 crore in H1 FY27. The average listing-day gains improved to 18 per cent from 10 per cent a year ago, while average retail oversubscription increased to 28 times from 25 times, the report titled 'India IPO Market: H1 FY27 and Q2 FY27 Review' said. Notably, September was the busiest month, with 32 IPOs collectively raising Rs 40,400 crore. In terms of sectoral contribution, financial services accounted for 43 per cent of the total capital mobilised during H1 FY

As of 3 a.m., the inner spiral band in the northern sector has touched land, and the wall cloud region is also entering land, according to the official bulletin from the India Meteorological Department. The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, on Monday (November 2, 2026) challenged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to an open debate , alleging that it was with “foreign help” that Mr. Modi became Prime Minister and continues to occupy the position. The Congress leader’s challenge came after the Prime Minister had accused the Opposition of taking foreign help to destabilise the country. Foreign social and home care workers, who arrived in the U.K. before May 2025, will be able to normally settle (become permanent residents) in five years , rather than in 15 years, as was first proposed in the British government’s ‘earned settlement’ scheme announced in November 2025. Those earning more than £50,271 per annum, doctors, nurses and teachers will be able to settle in five years, while those earning more than £1,25,140 per annum could settle in three years, as was proposed in the November 2025 draft rules. The Union government plans to establish Foreigners Regional Registration Offices (FRROs) in all State capitals by 2027, the Ministry of Home Affairs said on Monday (November 2, 2026). Since 2025, five new FRROs have been established, including two this year. The move is part of a wider effort to strengthen the institutional framework for managing foreign nationals visiting India. 92e91ead481f85e3.title: Amit Shah backs SIR, alleges 3 crore ‘illegal infiltrators’ identified in 13 crore deleted voters
92e91ead481f85e3.summary: Updated - November 03, 2026 01:48 am IST - HYDERABAD Union Home Minister Amit Shah addresses a public meeting during the ‘Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy’ campaign in Hyderabad on Monday (November 2). | Photo Credit: RAMAKRISHNA G Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Monday alleged that the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise had identified around three crore ‘unaccounted voters’, whom he described as ‘illegal infiltrators from Bangladesh’, among the 13 crore names removed from electoral rolls. He asserted that all such infiltrators would be expelled from the country. Addressing a public meeting at MJ Market in Hyderabad’s Old City after a ‘Save democracy-Remove anarchy’ foot march , Mr. Shah claimed that of the nearly 13 crore names deleted from voter lists during the SIR process, 4.25 crore voters were registered in two different locations, three crore were deceased, and another one crore were duplicate entries. He questioned if such names should continue to remain on the electoral rolls. “Do we need to remove infiltrators from the country’s voter lists or not?” he asked. The Home Minister accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of defending the alleged three crore ‘unaccounted’ voters. “No matter how hard Rahul Gandhi or Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy may try, the BJP is committed to driving every infiltrator out of the country,” he said. Mr. Shah alleged that the Congress and other Opposition parties were opposing the SIR exercise to protect ‘infiltrators from Bangladesh’, whom he described as their ‘vote bank’ and maintained that only genuine Indian citizens should be included in electoral rolls. Ridiculing Sunday’s joint rally of Opposition parties in New Delhi, Mr. Shah described it as a ‘Save Infiltrators’ rally and urged BJP workers to counter what he termed ‘fear-mongering’ by the former on the SIR exercise through a door-to-door campaign. The Congress was determined to halt SIR while the BJP would continue to support it

b850f1e5733062c8.title: Petronet LNG reports 52.3% growth in net profits, in talks for availing undelivered cargoes
b850f1e5733062c8.summary: Published - November 03, 2026 05:43 am IST Petronet LNG declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share. | Photo Credit: The Hindu State-owned Petronet LNG reported 53.2% growth in net profits in the September-end quarter, driven by improved operational efficiency, although cargoes from its most prominent supplier, Qatar, continued to be affected because of the reignited conflict in West Asia. The company also declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share. The country’s largest LNG importer’s net profit stood at ₹1,235 crore in the reported quarter against ₹806 crore in the same period last year. Revenue from operations although declined about 35% during the period to ₹7,200.35 crore. The company processed 231 trillion British Thermal Units (TBTU) during the period, higher than 228 TBTU it processed in the same period last year. Overall capacity utilisation in the reported quarter narrowed to 64% against 78% in the same period last year. Capacity utilisation at their Dahej terminal stood at 73% against 92% in the comparable period last year. Speaking to the press, Akshay Kumar Singh, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) informed that the company was also in talks with QatarEnergy to secure delivery of the cargoes that could not be delivered because of the force majeure. “On the sidelines, we also discuss if they would be able to give more cargoes before the contractual date. If there is a requirement in the country, we will take that as well,” he said. The supplier has declared forced majeure until December-end. Mr. Singh told reporters that the contractual terms have provisions to recoup the lost cargoes for one year after the expiry of the current contract period, that is, May 2028. He stated that Petronet LNG lost an average 9-10 cargoes each month in the last eight months, thus, about 75-80 cargoes whilst it has received 6 cargoes from the supplier. It was willing to help in energy producing projects, deepening fishing port construction and irrigation projects, he said. Trade expansion and economic co-operation with foreign countries were in line with Russia’s latest five-year plan to produce more goods for export. 478c19867d6818b6.title: Cyclonic storm Murasu to make landfall close to Ongole
478c19867d6818b6.summary: Updated - November 03, 2026 02:42 am IST - VIJAYAWADA A satellite image of Cyclone Murasu over the Bay of Bengal on Sunday. IMD | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement As the cyclonic storm, Cyclone Murasu , moves towards the A.P. coast, the State has deployed six National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams and seven State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams in districts likely to be affected by the cyclone. According to information from the A.P. State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA), the landfall point is likely to be Ongole and in this connection, two teams each have been stationed in the districts of Krishna, Bapatla, Guntur, Nellore and Prakasam, while one team each has been deployed in Markapuram, Palnadu and Tirupati districts. Additional teams are also available for deployment if required. Murasu is the second cyclonic storm to hit A.P. in less than a week. According to the 9 p.m. bulletin from the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the cyclonic storm centred over Southwest and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal at 5.30 p.m. It was located about 420 km east-southeast of Chennai, 490 km east-southeast of Nellore, 500 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 510 east-southeast of Kavali, 530 km southeast of Ongole and 560 km south-southeast of Vishakhapatnam. The IMD said the system may intensify further into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over Westcentral Bay of Bengal in the early hours of November 2. The landfall will be close to the Ongole coast, with a wind speed of 100 to 120 kmph, in the early hours of November 3. Isolated extremely heavy rainfall is expected at one or two locations in the districts of Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam, Markapuram and Nellore on Monday. NTR and Guntur districts have announced holidays for all government and private schools, junior colleges and degree colleges on Monday (November 2, 2026). 9c21bc940db95f10.summary: A federal judge on Monday dismissed a lawsuit against Harvard University over its alleged failure to provide admissions records that the Justice Department had demanded to ensure the Ivy League school stopped using affirmative action in admissions. The Justice Department said Harvard had "thwarted" efforts to investigate potential discrimination. It accused Harvard of refusing to comply with a federal investigation and asked a judge to order the university to turn over the records. But US District Judge Myong Joun concluded that the Justice Department didn't take the necessary procedural steps to obtain the data before filing the lawsuit. "Before taking enforcement action under the statutory framework, the agency must advise the recipient of its failure to comply and determine that compliance cannot be secured by voluntary means," Joun wrote. 69f62dc9701a46b5.title: Craft Council of A.P. receives praise for providing platform for weavers, artisans
69f62dc9701a46b5.summary: Updated - November 03, 2026 12:36 am IST - VIJAYAWADA Heritage Foods executive director Nara Brahmani examines a saree at a stall after inaugurating ‘Vasantam’ crafts and textiles exhibition in Vijayawada on Monday. | Photo Credit: K.V.S. Giri The Craft Council of Andhra Pradesh (CCAP) inaugurated ‘Vasantham’, an exhibition showcasing the rich heritage of handlooms, handicrafts and traditional crafts of India, in Vijayawada on Monday. Heritage Foods executive director Nara Brahmani visited the exhibition and interacted with the weavers and artisans, and appreciated the efforts of the Craft Council of A.P. in organising the exhibition. She also commended the initiative for providing a valuable platform to weavers and artisans to showcase their products, reach customers and promote their traditional crafts. She said that such exhibitions were extremely beneficial in supporting the weaving community and encouraging the preservation of our rich craft heritage. The two-day exhibition will conclude on November 3 (Tuesday). It remains open from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. at Sesha Sai Kalyana Mandapam, Vedika in the city. e9958b1c4de528c6.title: Police foil bid to snatch smuggled gold from woman at Karipur
e9958b1c4de528c6.summary: Updated - November 03, 2026 08:23 am IST File photo for representational purpose only. The police foiled an attempt to abduct a woman carrying 817 gm gold worth over ₹1.10 crore at Calicut International Airport, Karipur, on Monday. They also arrested two members of the alleged robbery gang. According to the police, the incident took place around 3 a.m. A police team noticed a group behaving suspiciously in the arrival area and kept them under watch. The group followed Abhirami, 27, a native of Vandanmedu in Idukki, after she arrived from abroad. When Abhirami reached the parking area with a man who had come to receive her, the gang blocked their way and grabbed her trolley bag. The police team intervened when the gang tried to overpower the man accompanying her. During the struggle, the accused attacked the police and bit home guard Murali Krishna. They also tried to run over a member of the police team with a car while escaping. The officer narrowly escaped from being hit. The police arrested Sayanth, 28, and Babilesh, 40, both from Kallachi, Nadapuram. Abhirami and Harshal, 40, a native of Kochi who had arrived to collect the gold, were also taken into custody. The police said the gold had been sent with Abhirami by Swalih, a native of Thamarassery. Around 10 people had reached the airport in two cars to seize the gold and abduct her. A search of Abhirami’s baggage led to the recovery of 14 gold plates concealed inside an emergency lamp. The gold weighed 817 gm after cleaning and is estimated to be worth more than ₹1.10 crore. The gold, along with ₹67,000 allegedly kept to pay Abhirami for carrying it, a car and the two people detained in connection with the gold, were handed over to the Customs Department for further action. The police said the arrested men had been involved in several similar cases. One of them had lost a hand in a blast. The high court refused to intervene in a case involving 20,000 people the Republican administration flagged as likely noncitizens on the largely Democratic state's voter rolls. It was the latest in a flurry of election-related litigation the day before the midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress for the last two years of Trump's second term. In California, the Trump administration had asked the high court to set aside the challenged ballots until the voters' citizenship status could be verified. But officials there said that the list appeared to be filled with errors and that setting the ballots aside could effectively disenfranchise legal voters. The high court did not detail its reasoning, as is common in emergency decisions.

ec05d0c73acf6bca.title: Netanyahu presses Trump for fresh Iran strikes after US midterm elections
ec05d0c73acf6bca.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for another wave of strikes on Iran after Tuesday's midterm elections in the United States, according to two regional officials and a third person familiar with the matter. A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week's elections. US President Donald Trump has alternated between threatening major strikes while pushing for a deal with Iran. The two officials said diplomatic efforts have made progress, with Qatari mediators holding two rounds of talks last week with Iranian officials. The two officials said the mediators are trying to advance a framework for Iran to cease its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in return for the US lifting its blockade on Iran's ports. They said more talks are planned for this week. The two officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were discussing classified briefing

f5c1503860f7f7db.title: Cascading effect: On dams and land rights
f5c1503860f7f7db.summary: Published - November 03, 2026 12:56 am IST The bureaucratic impetus for the 11.2-GW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh purportedly comes from China’s aggressive development of a 60-GW mega-dam in Tibet , stoking anxieties among Indian authorities over ‘weaponised’ transboundary waters. Beijing may be able to divert flows in the Yarlung Tsangpo river, which becomes the Brahmaputra in India, to cause drought downstream or release water en masse to trigger catastrophic floods in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. New Delhi thus imagines SUMP as a strategic buffer, but in so doing faces a dilemma it should not attempt to resolve with force. Its extant top-down approach, exemplified by deploying security forces to guard survey teams and imposing the State Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against activists, only validates fears among locals that the state will grab their land. The region also hosts sustained protests against the Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project , expanding the indictment to Arunachal Pradesh’s model of hydroelectric power development. The eastern Himalayas are among the most tectonically active and erosion-prone landscapes in the world. The mega-dam in Tibet will comprise five cascading power stations over the river’s roughly 2,000-metre fall over 50 km. Beijing has maintained the dam will not harm countries downstream but has declined to share crucial engineering details. This is why diplomacy will be an essential part of operating SUMP, in addition to Beijing’s disputed claims on Arunachal Pradesh. The Brahmaputra basin in Assam and Bangladesh receives most of its water from monsoon rains and tributaries downstream of the Tibetan Plateau, so China cannot straightforwardly control the river’s total flow through India. Yet since Chinese interventions would have greater consequences closer to the border, SUMP will need information about both the mega-dam’s operations and downstream inflows to plan its own operations, and Beijin
