d93d19dc3bb70bb4.title: APPCB steps up State-wide measures to curb air, noise pollution
d93d19dc3bb70bb4.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 12:19 am IST - VISAKHAPATNAM The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board (APPCB) has stepped up measures to curb air and noise pollution across the State, directing district administrations and police, transport and municipal authorities to enforce environmental regulations and monitor pollution levels, particularly during Deepavali. In a recent communication to Collectors, Magistrates, Superintendents of Police, Municipal Commissioners and Police Commissioners of Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam, the Board called for joint inspection teams to prevent the sale, transportation and use of banned firecrackers. It also directed officials to monitor air quality and noise levels in all district headquarters and towns, following orders issued on October 16. The APPCB on Wednesday said its monitoring during Deepavali 2025 had recorded PM10 levels of up to 238 micrograms per cubic metre and PM2.5 levels of 138 micrograms per cubic metre in Visakhapatnam. Only green crackers approved by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI) will be permitted in cities and towns where air quality is moderate or better, subject to court directions. Conventional crackers containing banned chemicals, including barium salts, are prohibited. Permitted packs must carry unique QR codes linked to their registration, licence and test certificates, the Board said. The prescribed noise limits (in dB(A)) are 75 during the day and 70 at night in industrial areas; 65 and 55 in commercial areas; 55 and 45 in residential areas; and 50 and 40 in silence zones. Daytime is from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. and night-time from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Areas within 100 metres of hospitals, educational institutions and courts are designated silence zones, where honking is prohibited. 481be06aae8907b4.title: World Trade Center township on the anvil for Chengalpattu
481be06aae8907b4.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 12:31 am IST - CHENNAI GTB Developers (GT Bharathi Urban Developers Pvt Ltd) announced that it has been granted a licence by the World Trade Centers Association (WTCA) to develop World Trade Center Chengalpattu. This particular project is planned as an IT integrated township of 100 to 150 acre, rather than an industrial estate. The project has an estimated value of ₹7,000 crore and will be developed in phases over approximately ten years. The proposed masterplan includes commercial and IT office space, hospitality, residences and an education zone. GTB is at an advanced stage of identifying and securing land for the project. GTB is also pursuing a second World Trade Center development in Kanchipuram district, proposed across approximately 500 acres. Unlike Chengalpattu, it is envisaged as an industrial World Trade Center, with manufacturing and data centre zones alongside infrastructure, education and hospitality. GTB intends to explore the project under a public-private partnership (PPP) model, one of the structures under which World Trade Centers are developed globally. Nilakantan Unni, Mahopadhyaya brings to the notice of the public through the columns of the “Malayala Manorama” that there is an interesting image of Buddha in Pallikkal in the Mavelikkara Taluk in central Travancore. It is a stone image exactly similar in appearance to that of the well-known Karumandi Kuttan with which people who have travelled along the backwater route between Alleppey and Quilon, are very familiar. The image is worshipped by the villagers who believe that it is a deity presiding over their destinies. 0a95a192b6b5d108.summary: Israel’s Herzog accepts vote results, opens talks on forming a government Al Jazeera Joint List says it will back Eisenkot to form Israel’s next government Al Jazeera Palestinian voters upset Netanyahu's political calculations Frontline Magazine From 'Bibi or Tibi' to kingmakers: Arab parties could decide Netanyahu's fate The Times of India As Eisenkot wins 67 nods to be PM, Herzog says he’ll announce mandate decision on Sunday The Times of Israel
0a95a192b6b5d108.headline_en: Israel’s Herzog accepts vote results, opens talks on forming a government
0a95a192b6b5d108.raw_facts: Israel’s Herzog accepts vote results, opens talks on forming a government Al Jazeera Joint List says it will back Eisenkot to form Israel’s next government Al Jazeera Palestinian voters upset Netanyahu's political calculations Frontline Magazine From 'Bibi or Tibi' to kingmakers: Arab parties could decide Netanyahu's fate The Times of India As Eisenkot wins 67 nods to be PM, Herzog says he’ll announce mandate decision on Sunday The Times of Israel
flags: Contradictory claims: Summary states Herzog opens talks, but another line says he will announce decision on Sunday (implying talks haven't started or mandate not yet given).

Factually incorrect: In the 2019 Israeli election (which this appears to reference), Benny Gantz (Blue and White) won the mandate to form a government, not Benny Eisenkot (Yesh Atid). Eisenkot did not win 67 nods to be PM; Gantz's coalition had the majority.

Timeline inconsistency: Herzog typically gives the mandate to the leader of the largest party or a coalition with a majority. Eisenkot's party was not the largest, and no coalition led by him had 61 seats at the time of the initial mandate decision.
Source reliability: The source is a Google News RSS feed, which aggregates headlines from various outlets, leading to a jumbled and potentially contradictory summary.

3722fa8859ea88c9.summary: Bakery food company Britannia Industries Ltd on Thursday reported an increase of 10.82 per cent rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 725.99 crore for the September quarter of FY27, on a year-on-year basis, led by volume growth. The company had posted a net profit of Rs 655.06 crore in the July-September quarter a year ago, according to a regulatory filing from Britannia Industries. Britannia Industries' revenue from the sale of products was up 16.6 per cent to Rs 5,541.57 crore in the September quarter. The sales growth was "led by volume growth of 13 per cent", said Britannia Industries in its earnings statement. Its revenue from operations was up 15.64 per cent to Rs 5,597.79 crore in the second quarter of FY27. It was at Rs 4,840.63 crore in the corresponding quarter. Britannia's total expenses were at Rs 4,690.47 crore, up 17 per cent in Q2, FY27. Its total income, which includes other income, was up 15.9 per cent to Rs 5,671.30 crore in the September quarter. b9f1a3137bab4876.title: Chawri Bazar building collapse: CM orders inquiry, FIR against contractor
b9f1a3137bab4876.summary: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Thursday ordered an inquiry into the collapse of a three-storey building under construction in Old Delhi's Chawri Bazar, which claimed two lives and left four others injured, and directed the registration of an FIR against the contractor. The chief minister also ordered the immediate suspension of the concerned junior engineer (JE) and assistant engineer (AE) in connection with the incident. She directed officials to ensure the best possible medical treatment for the injured and provide immediate ex-gratia assistance to the affected families. "Stringent action will be taken against those found responsible, in accordance with the law," the chief minister said. The building collapsed around 9.50 am in Gali Sitara, near the Chawri Bazar Metro station, police said. Two bodies were pulled out from the debris by a Delhi Fire Services (DFS) rescue team, while four injured people were taken to a hospital by locals before the fire department teams arrive

0bd4985135c1371a.title: India-US trade deal: What midterm elections mean for trade policy, tariff and export sectors? Experts explain
0bd4985135c1371a.summary: As India and the US work to finalise a long-awaited trade deal, the ruling Republicans' major electoral loss in the recently concluded US midterm polls has raised crucial questions: How may this flip in the US Congress affect the India-US negotiations? Will the setback to US President Donald Trump's party give India room to negotiate? Experts believe that the Republican Party's stinging loss in the midterm elections, which shifted the balance of power in the US Congress , may push Trump to accelerate negotiations that had been reportedly stalled over tariff concerns. This, however, may not make the "US trade policy less restrictive", they said. Another expert explained why India may get some room to negotiate on “substance rather than under deadline pressure”. Professor Rituparna Kaushik, Assistant Professor at FLAME University, told Mint that the midterm election results will not rewrite US trade policy overnight. This is because "the Section 301 and Section 232 duties [under which tariffs were imposed] rest on executive authority and any rollback faces a presidential veto," he said. He believed that a Democratic Congress with oversight powers "makes abrupt tariff escalation politically harder, which gives India room to negotiate on substance rather than under deadline pressure". "Labour-intensive exporters in textiles, apparel, and gems and jewellery stand to gain most from that stability," he noted. On India’s strategy, Kaushik said New Delhi must "secure a predictable, rules-based tariff schedule rather than chase short-term concessions, and to broaden engagement beyond the White House to Congress and US states." "At the same time, India must keep diversifying through the EU agreement and other partners, so the US remains a key market but not a single point of vulnerability. On agriculture and dairy, India should hold firm, as US farm-lobby pressure cuts across party lines," he added. Ajay Srivastava, Founder of the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), said

bbc6be00bd36b3cc.title: Investing in US stocks from India: Check how these 5 platforms stack up
bbc6be00bd36b3cc.summary: More Indian investors are buying US and other overseas stocks through apps and brokers. Indian investors who want US and other overseas stocks have more routes than ever. Mutual funds have hit the industry-wide $7 billion SEBI cap on overseas investments, so more investors are going direct under the RBI’s Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), which allows up to $250,000 per person a financial year. Demand is moving the market quickly. Platforms are adding features, changing how they are set up and launching products at pace, so it helps to know what each one does best and whether it fits your needs. This story looks at five: INDmoney, Interactive Brokers (IBKR), Vested Finance, Paasa and ZFunds. Business Standard heard from executives at four of the five and spoke to two investors who have used most of them. Four things separate these platforms. Notes: Vested charges $5 per USD withdrawal, which mainly applies to NRI accounts. “Size” figures are as reported by each company and are not like-for-like. Launched in 2019, INDmoney targets salaried retail investors and runs as an IFSCA-licensed Global Access Provider in GIFT City. It also files income tax returns for users, with Schedule FA filled in. The company reports $3.5 billion in global investing assets and plans to add European and Southeast Asian exchanges by December 2026. “We are not building a platform exclusively for wealthy individuals making large international remittances,” founder and CEO Ashish Kashyap told Business Standard . Founded in 1978, IBKR is a direct broker with no Indian intermediary and reported about 5.7 million client accounts in October 2026. It offers UCITS ETFs and several overseas markets, but has a complex interface, manual tax work and bank wire fees of ₹500–1,000 plus GST per transfer. Pranay Kapoor, a tech professional and YouTuber who has tried most of these apps, told Business Standard that with IBKR “there is no middleman.” Kapoor sends money in large tranches so the flat wire fee

6bb06909f49a0814.title: Book launched to honour work of child rights activist Thomas Jayaraj
6bb06909f49a0814.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:32 am IST - Chennai: The Centre for Child Rights and Development (CCRD) launched a book titled Voices of Transformation – Walking the path of Thomas Jayaraj towards a Culture of Child Rights to honour the contributions of Thomas Jayaraj, who passed away in 2021. He was at the forefront of many child rights initiatives at both the State and national levels. The book was released at the Madras School of Social Work (MSSW) on Friday by Sudha Ramalingam, senior advocate of Madras High Court. D. Geetha, Managing Trustee, CCRD, received the first copy. Stegana Jency L.T., Director of CCRD, said the team was committed to carrying forward the principles of Mr. Jayaraj. “We are launching this book because everything Mr. Jayaraj did should t become a guide for future leaders,” she said. Mr. Jayaraj’s daughter, Liby Rajam, said her father not only spoke for child rights, but also built a community that would continue to advocate for child rights in the future. Meanwhile, Ms. Ramalingam said there was considerable work to be done in this field. “When it comes to child rights and development, we must get the youngsters involved,” she said. Journalist and activist Aishwarya, and Antony Stephen, assistant professor and head of partnerships, MSSW, spoke about child rights advocacy. Stegana Jency L.T., Director of CCRD, said the team was committed to carrying forward the principles of Mr. Jayaraj. “We are launching this book because everything Mr. Jayaraj did should t become a guide for future leaders,” she said. Mr. Jayaraj’s daughter, Liby Rajam, said her father not only spoke for child rights, but also built a community that would continue to advocate for child rights in the future. Meanwhile, Ms. Ramalingam said there was considerable work to be done in this field. “When it comes to child rights and development, we must get the youngsters involved,” she said. Journalist and activist Aishwarya, and Antony Stephen, assistant professor and head of partnerships, MSSW, spoke about child rights advocacy. In the previous week, the forex kitty had reduced by USD 1.269 billion to USD 719.748 billion. The reserves had touched an all-time high of USD 785.706 billion during the week ended September 4, driven by a heavy flow of currency as part of a special concessional swap for deposits from the diaspora through which banks raised a record USD 133 billion, but have been on a decline ever since. Experts attribute this decline to the deployment of the FCNR(B) resources and also to currency defence put up by RBI through dollar sales. During the week ended October 30, foreign currency assets, a major component of reserves, decreased by USD 2.088 billion to USD 591.118 billion, according to the data released by Reserve Bank of India (RBI). d47a5aca9eff8a29.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 03:20 am IST - New Delhi Every unit holding stocks will have to update details on the Food Stock Portal every Friday, the Food Ministry said in a statement. | Photo Credit: M. Units that are not registered on the portal or that violate stock limits will face action under Sections 6 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955. In a separate letter, also dated November 6, the Centre has given its consent to Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana to impose stock limits on paddy and rice through control orders. 0aa42e8c21ff097a.title: T.N. govt. allocates monthly maintenance fund of ₹1,000 to 12,646 VAO offices
0aa42e8c21ff097a.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:50 am IST - CHENNAI The Tamil Nadu government has issued an order allocating ₹1,000 each as a monthly maintenance fund to 12,646 Village Administrative Officer (VAO) offices functioning across the State, involving an annual expenditure of ₹15.18 crore. A Government Order to this effect was issued by the Revenue and Disaster Management Department on Friday. It follows an announcement made by Minister for Revenue and Disaster Management K.A. Sengottaiyan in the Assembly on August 17 during the Budget session. The maintenance fund will be used to arrange drinking water facilities, seating, ramps for persons with disabilities and other amenities for members of the public visiting VAO offices to obtain birth certificates, death certificates, patta, chitta, certificates for small and marginal farmers, legal heir certificates, income certificates, nativity certificates, community certificates and first-generation graduate certificates, among others. The monthly maintenance fund will be credited to the VAOs’ salaries under the head of maintenance allowance. The government has also allocated ₹8.85 crore towards this fund for the period from September 2026 to March 2027 in the current financial year. Veeramani under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012. In an order issued on Friday, the State Government said considering the sensitive and complex nature of the cases, K.R. Sankaran, M. Sandhiya and Swami Subramanian were appointed as Special Public Prosecutors under Section 31(1) of the Act to conduct prosecution of the case investigated by the Special Investigation Team (SIT). Mr Veeramani and his associates are facing seven cases under the POCSO Act and one case of abetment to suicide of a minor in 2004. Police sources said that the investigation in at least two cases was in the final stages of completion and chargesheets were likely to be filed next week. 23850def92ab4fc4.title: Agasthyamalai conservation case: SC directs temporary and non-resident silk cotton cultivators not eligible for protection under FRA Act
23850def92ab4fc4.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 01:47 am IST - NEW DELHI The Supreme Court directed on Friday that individuals with temporary residence in the Agasthyamalai biosphere or those living entirely outside the forest boundaries cannot be classified as traditional forest dwellers merely for cultivating silk cotton within the forest. “Persons falling in Category II and Category III, as classified in the additional affidavit of September 6 filed by Department of Revenue, State of Tamil Nadu, shall be excluded from consideration as forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers for the purposes of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 or FRA Act,” a Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta directed. According to Tamil Nadu’s own affidavit, 232 persons are cultivating the forest area with temporary residence while 2,767 persons who occupy 2,867.70 hectares land are residing outside the forest boundary and are managing silk cotton cultivation. The order was passed in furtherance of a May 2026 judgment, which had issued various directions for a structured and time-bound process of eviction, rehabilitation and ecological restoration in the forest areas. The court had ordered the preparation of a division-wise eviction plan, removal of encroachments, and action against identified government servants. It had imposed a prohibition on approval or commencement of new non-forestry activities or diversion proposals within the Agasthyamalai landscape, and directed continued monitoring of the area by the Central Empowered Committee (CEC). Justice Mehta, who authored the order, held the State government “primarily responsible” for delaying the receipt of claims under the 2006 Act. 3254ea801e375485.title: Demonetisation and the health costs of cash shortages
3254ea801e375485.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:15 am IST Liquidity is an economic determinant of health’ | Photo Credit: THE HINDU/MANJUNATH H.S. On November 8, 2016, 86% of India’s currency by value — in the form of ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes — ceased to be legal tender at just four hours’ notice. The stated objectives included curbing counterfeit currency and black money and accelerating the adoption of digital payments. It was among the largest transitory liquidity shocks engineered in a cash-reliant economy. Nearly all demonetised currency returned – some 99.3% as per Reserve Bank of India data – and broader financial indicators such as interest rates and deposits remained stable. As Chodorow-Reich et al. in their influential 2020 Quarterly Journal of Economics study have documented, the direct effect was a temporary reduction in the stock of money in the economy. 8da91880dd5ffb6b.title: Minister inaugurates dialysis centre
8da91880dd5ffb6b.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:35 am IST - CHENNAI Health Minister K.G. Arunraj inaugurated the “Rotary Kamdar Dialysis Centre” at the Government Peripheral Hospital in Anna Nagar on Friday. The centre, which was established by Rotary District 3234 in association with the Rotary Club of Chennai Kilpauk through a collaborative public-private partnership, aims at strengthening public healthcare infrastructure and improving access to essential dialysis services for patients requiring regular renal care. The initiative has been supported by the Pushpavati Babulal Kamdar Charitable Trust, Rotary Clubs of Chennai, and Wockhardt Foundation, in collaboration with Government Peripheral Hospital, Anna Nagar. The Rotary Clubs and Kamdar Charitable Trust have jointly provided medical equipment worth approximately ₹1.6 crore, including 10 dialysis machines, a Reverse Osmosis plant, and an effluent treatment plant. The centre is designed to serve up to 30 patients per day. The day-to-day dialysis expenses will be funded through the Chief Minister’s Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme, a press release said. Speaking at the inauguration, Dr. Arunraj said, “Healthcare is a shared responsibility, and it is important for all of us to contribute towards the well-being of society. The role played by Rotary in the eradication of polio is a wonderful example of what collective efforts and partnerships can achieve. We must build on this spirit of collaboration and work together towards our mission of eradicating cervical cancer.” The District Rotaract Council, Rotary International District 3234, in association with the Rotary Club of Chennai Kilpauk, also organised a Blood Donation Drive. D. Suresh Jain, District Governor 2026–27, Rotary International District 3234 and J.B. Kamdar, Managing Trustee, Pushpavati Babulal Kamdar Charitable Trust, were present. c56a4b320b6d550d.title: Mohammed Shami retires from Test cricket, to continue playing white-ball formats
c56a4b320b6d550d.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:28 am IST - Kolkata Mohammed Shami of India poses for a portrait prior to the ICC World Test Championship Final 2023 at The Oval | Photo Credit: ICC via Getty Images Out-of-favour India pacer Mohammed Shami on Friday announced his retirement from Test cricket, bringing an end to a 12-year career in which he claimed 229 wickets from 64 matches. The 36-year-old, who has been out of the Indian team since the 2025 Champions Trophy, announced his decision through an Instagram post, adding that he would continue to play white-ball cricket. "I am leaving the white jersey, but never the memories connected to it. When I first wore India's Test jersey, I had only a dream — to do something for my country. After that every wicket, every struggle, every injury and every comeback taught me something," Shami wrote. Mohammed Shami exults after taking David Warner’s wicket during the Test match between India and Australia at Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi on February 17, 2023 | Photo Credit: V.V. Krishnan "Test cricket is not just a format for me, it is a very special part of my life. Today I am deciding to retire from Test cricket with a heavy heart and unlimited beautiful memories," he added. Shami made his Test debut against the West Indies at the Eden Gardens on November 6, 2013. He finished with 229 wickets at an average of 27.71, including six five-wicket hauls. His ability to generate seam and swing with both the new and old ball made him a key component of India's pace attack across conditions. He claimed 131 wickets in 35 Tests in South Africa, the West Indies and India, averaging under 25. Some of his most memorable performances came in South Africa. He returned figures of 5/28 in the second innings of the Johannesburg Test during India's 2018 tour to help the visitors secure a consolation victory. ecdfcae84b13fb27.title: Unhappy Milind Deora shoots a letter to BMC chief over event exclusion
ecdfcae84b13fb27.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 04:22 am IST - MUMBAI Shiv Sena MP Milind Deora. | Photo Credit: Emmanual Yogini Member of Parliament Milind Deora wrote a letter to Ashwini Bhide, Commissioner of the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), on Friday regarding an omission. Mr. Deora stated that the BMC did not invite him to an inauguration in Colaba. Mr. Deora is a Rajya Sabha MP from the Shiv Sena, which is part of the ruling alliance in Maharashtra. Colaba falls in the area he represents. The event was for a housing project under the Ashray Yojana on November 6, 2026, with Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde attending. Speaker Rahul Narwekar, Mayor Ritu Tawde, and Deputy Mayor Sanjay Ghadi also attended. The BMC distributed keys to workers under the scheme. Mr. Deora wrote in the letter that representatives require notice of events in the areas they represent, noting that the event took place without informing him. He wrote that coordination and courtesy towards representatives must accompany initiatives, stating that representatives need to receive information about developments for the people they serve. The MP requested Mr. Bhide to look into the matter and asked the Commissioner to ensure that protocol is followed to prevent an omission. He requested that officials receive advice to ensure coordination with representatives for functions. 04b27ca4a8352a99.title: Supreme Court decision on BBMB arrears a victory for Himachal, says CM Sukhu
04b27ca4a8352a99.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 01:30 am IST - New Delhi Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu. | Photo Credit: ANI Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Friday (November 6, 2026) termed the Supreme Court’s decision directing Punjab and Haryana to supply 11,973 million units of electricity to the State over 20 years towards its outstanding dues from the Bhakra-Nangal and Beas hydroelectric projects a historic victory for its people. The order settles a decades-old dispute over Himachal Pradesh’s 7.19% share in the power generated from the projects. The State will receive nearly 60 crore units annually during the lean season, generating an estimated revenue of ₹10,000 crore to ₹20,000 crore over the 20-year period, depending on electricity prices, Mr. Sukhu said in a statement. He said the decision could fetch the State additional revenue of up to ₹1,000 crore annually. Even at ₹6 per unit, Himachal Pradesh would earn at least ₹500 crore a year, while a rate of ₹13-14 per unit would significantly increase the returns. Mr. Sukhu attributed the outcome to the State government’s sustained legal battle and determination to secure its financial rights. He described it as the fourth major success in protecting Himachal Pradesh’s interests, citing earlier victories in matters relating to Wildflower Hall, the Kishau Dam among others. The Chief Minister said the government was also pursuing its claims over the Shanan Power Project and the water cess. The additional revenue, he said, would be used to strengthen education and healthcare, improve road infrastructure, generate employment and ensure timely payment of financial benefits to government employees. Congratulating the State’s nearly 75 lakh residents, Mr. Sukhu said protecting its resources and making Himachal Pradesh self-reliant remained a top priority for his government. cee9fdc5046b6afa.title: Rural women narrate stories on how Gruha Lakshmi scheme helped build their lives
cee9fdc5046b6afa.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:07 am IST - Bengaluru Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar admiring a handmade beaded toy cradle gifted by one of the beneficiaries of the Gruha Lakshmi scheme at his home office in Bengaluru on Friday. | Photo Credit: ANI Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar’s interaction with Gruha Lakshmi scheme beneficiaries in Bengaluru on Friday turned out to be a forum for hearing stories about how the monthly cash deposit by the scheme helped poor women not just build their lives, but also make significant achievements like helping their wards pursue higher education. At the interaction, which was held at the Chief Minister’s home office to get feedback from beneficiaries on the occasion of the scheme completing three years of implementation, a woman from Chikkamagaluru district said: “My son is studying MBBS in Koppal. I paid the fee of around ₹59,000 using the Gruha Lakshmi money. Thanks to the Shakti (free bus travel for women) scheme, it has been convenient for me to visit my son frequently.” Another woman from Channarayapatna said she was able to send her daughter to Malaysia for a dance performance with the help of Gruha Lakshmi money along with the family’s savings. An aged woman from Laxmeshwar taluk in Gadag district emotionally observed, “The Gruha Lakshmi money has helped senior women buy their medicines and lead a life of dignity.” A woman from Kudligi taluk explained how their self-help group pooled the scheme money to take up sheep rearing. Everyone was surprised when she said that the group that started with five sheep now had 300 sheep and employed five men to look after them. All the beneficiaries made a fervent appeal to the Chief Minister not to stop the scheme. Responding positively to the scheme, the Chief Minister declared that there was no question of discontinuing the scheme. 7873579ddeec35fd.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:55 am IST - Bengaluru Sudha Yadav, Governor of Karnataka and Chancellor of universities in the State, directed all public universities in the State to conduct a comprehensive review of their current operations and identify areas requiring improvement. The Governor instructed all Vice-Chancellors to prepare and submit a detailed report on the same. “This report should cover the current status of their respective universities, key achievements, challenges, shortcomings, and specific measures proposed for improvement,” she stated. Addressing the Vice-Chancellors of various universities and officials from the Karnataka State Higher Education Council at Lok Bhavan, the Governor emphasised the need to strengthen the quality, transparency, accountability and overall performance of universities across the State. “Emphasis must be placed on the effective implementation of the National Education Policy and the State Education Policy, strong coordination between industries and universities, as well as skill development, research, innovation and employability,” she said. The Governor called upon all Vice-Chancellors and the Karnataka State Higher Education Council to work in coordination and collaboration to strengthen the higher education system in Karnataka. 5160f15808b589f8.title: Krishi mela will be held for three days instead of one day: Agriculture Minister
5160f15808b589f8.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:15 am IST - Bengaluru Agriculture Minister P.M. Narendraswamy | Photo Credit: File Photo Krishi mela will be held for three days instead of one day, as was was announced earlier. Agriculture Minister P. M. Narendraswamy on Friday said that krishi mela at the Gandhi Krishi Vignana Kendra (GKVK) in Bengaluru will be held for three days this year as well. “Given the drought conditions prevailing in the State, there had been discussions about limiting the Mela to a single day. However, the event will continue for three days, just as in previous years,” he said. The three days event will proceed to introduce farmers to agricultural innovations and drought-management strategies, despite the current drought situation. He further noted that a three-day krishi mela will be also held in Mandya. “Three-day krishi mela have already been organised at the Universities of Agriculture Sciences in Shivamogga and Dharwad. These events have provided thousands of farmers with information on new crop varieties and technologies, as well as methods for managing drought,” he said. f6f0dde8fcb3adfd.title: Delhi court rejects plea seeking FIR against CM for comparing govt officials to Lord Hanuman
f6f0dde8fcb3adfd.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 04:30 am IST New Delhi, Nov 04 (ANI): Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta speaks during a fireside chat on 'Rooftop Solar as a Catalyst for Global Energy Transition' at the Solar Plenary Session of the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, in New Delhi on Wednesday. (ANI Photo/Sumit) | Photo Credit: ANI A Delhi court on Friday dismissed a complaint seeking legal action against Chief Minister Rekha Gupta over her alleged remarks comparing government officials to Lord Hanuman during an official event. Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwani Panwar of the Rouse Avenue Courts dismissed the complaint filed by Ram Niwas Sharma. In his complaint, Mr. Sharma alleged that Ms. Gupta, while addressing an event on September 23, 2025, compared Delhi government officials to Hanuman, saying they recognised their authority only when confronted with a situation similar to having their “tails set on fire”. He further alleged that Ms. Gupta referred to Hanuman in the context of the programme being organised near the shrine of Marghat Wale Baba in Kashmere Gate. The remarks were reportedly made during the launch of an interstate Delhi Transport Corporation bus service connecting Delhi with Baraut in Uttar Pradesh. Claiming that the remarks had hurt his religious sentiments, Mr. Sharma sought directions from the court for registration of an FIR and appropriate legal action against the Chief Minister. Last month, the court had sought a response from the Delhi Police on the complaint. In its Action Taken Report (ATR), the police stated that the alleged remarks did not disclose the commission of any cognizable offence. It maintained that Ms. Gupta’s speech, when viewed in its entirety, reflected appreciation for government employees and expressed reverence towards the Hindu deity. 7a7674b95a48cf58.title: Ahead of Deepavali, 3 major blazes erupt in Capital; DFS on alert
7a7674b95a48cf58.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:54 am IST A major fire broke out at a four-storey commercial building in Delhi's Gaffar Market in the early hours of Friday (November 6, 2026), just days before Deepavali and on the occasion of Dhanteras, triggering a massive emergency response. Around 20-25 fire engines were rushed to the spot to bring the blaze under control. No casualties or injuries have been reported. | Photo Credit: Sushil Kumar Verma The Delhi Fire Services (DFS) received 78 calls about fire incidents between midnight and 7.30 p.m. on Friday, including three major fires at commercial establishments across the Capital that required large-scale firefighting operations involving more than 20 fire tenders each. At least 15 people were rescued and seven injuries were reported, officials said. The DFS has issued a high alert and cancelled the leave of its officers and staff amid the increased fire risk ahead of Deepavali on Sunday. In Gali No. 6 of Gandhi Nagar’s Shanti Mohalla, the blaze gutted a ground-plus-four-storey garment warehouse. Assistant Divisional Officer Santosh Kumar said, “Four hose lines were laid from different directions to reach the building while the fire tender remained stationed on the main road.” A local resident said a suspected short circuit caused the fire. In Karol Bagh’s Gaffar Market, fire engulfed a commercial complex housing around 50 mobile accessories shops across its basement, ground floor, three upper floors, and a tin shed on the terrace. “The absence of ventilation led to smoke accumulating inside the building, making it difficult for firefighters to access the premises. There were no firefighting arrangements inside the shops and godowns,” Deputy Chief Fire Officer M.K. Chattopadhyay, who oversaw the operation, said. At a car showroom near the Saket metro station, at least 12-15 people were rescued from the top of the building and another four from its rear. Seven persons sustained injuries and were taken to hospital, police said

df43ab4012430c6d.title: University of Madras, Sutherland Global Services to collaborate for setting up an AI lab
df43ab4012430c6d.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:49 am IST - Chennai The Syndicate of University of Madras (UoM) on Friday approved a proposal to sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Sutherland Global Services, a digital-driven business transformation company, to set up an AI laboratory at the Department of Women Studies. The company has offered to upgrade its older allocation of ₹50 lakh for a Gender Lab that was set up at the Department following an older MoU signed in April 2019. 278fb4dc962bb62f.title: Avadi, Tambaram police destroy over 1.7 tonnes of ganja
278fb4dc962bb62f.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:33 am IST The Avadi and Tambaram City Police on Friday destroyed over 1.7 tonnes of ganja, besides narcotic tablets, heroin, methamphetamine, ganja chocolates, and gutkha products seized in various cases. The Avadi City Police destroyed 906.654 kg of ganja, 3,820 narcotic tablets, 10 ganja chocolates, and 2,685 kg of gutkha and other tobacco products, seized in 190 cases registered across the Commissionerate limits. A committee comprising Joint Commissioner R. Sivakumar, Deputy Commissioner V. Vinodh Santharam, and Assistant Director of Forensic Sciences Vijayalakshmi oversaw the process. The contraband was incinerated at an authorised facility at Thenmelpakkam in Chengalpattu district, following court orders. Meanwhile, the Tambaram City Police destroyed 810 kg of ganja, 0.148 g of heroin, 0.961 g of methamphetamine and 6,610 narcotic tablets seized in various cases. Joint Commissioner R. Jayanthi and Deputy Commissioner K. Karthikeyan supervised the process. With Friday’s destruction, the Tambaram police have destroyed 4,774 kg of ganja since 2025. The disposal was carried out in accordance with the procedures prescribed under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, the police said. 25f8461565d6fe44.title: WTA Chennai Open: Montgomery snaps Maaya’s memorable run, Indian challenge ends
25f8461565d6fe44.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:15 am IST - CHENNAI Robin Montgomery overcame a slow start to beat Maaya | Photo Credit: R. RAGU Robin Montgomery overcame an early setback to defeat wild card Maaya Rajeshwaran 6-3, 6-3 in the quarterfinals, ending the Indian challenge in singles at the WTA 250 Chennai Open on Friday. The 17-year-old Maaya - the first Indian woman to feature in the last-eight stage of a Tour-level event since Sania Mirza in Pattaya City in 2012 - was particularly impressive in the early stages. She tried to handle the 5’10” tall American’s lefty serve, which averaged above the 180km/h mark, by constantly adjusting her position near the baseline. The Indian got the early break in the fifth game of the opener courtesy a netted backhand from World No. 151 Montgomery, much to the delight of the 500-odd spectators under the floodlights on Centre Court at the SDAT Stadium in Nungambakkam here. But when it came to consolidating the break, the girl from Coimbatore, who had been landing plenty of first serves in the high 170s range, couldn’t find one till she was 15-30 down. Montgomery converted her first opportunity to restore parity. Maaya also let the eighth game - in which she committed two double faults - slip after being 40-30 up and was broken again. The 22-year-old Montgomery, former World No. 95, served the first set out. In the second essay, the American was in control as she earned the double break advantage at 4-1. After Maaya retrieved one of them back, Montgomery held quickly for a 5-3 lead and finished the job with a crosscourt backhand winner to break the Indian for the third time in the set. 81e8cbc939bfd5a6.title: NU observes BRICS Sustainable Lifestyle Week with anti-plastic programme
81e8cbc939bfd5a6.summary: Lumami, November 6 (MExN): Nagaland University (NU) organised a special programme on “Say No to Single-Use Plastics” on November 5 as part of the BRICS Sustainable Lifestyle Week (BSLW), being observed from November 1 to 7. The programme was held at the Conference Hall of the Department of Environmental Science (EVS) and commenced with a welcome address by Dr Latonglila Jamir, Head of the Department of EVS and member of the Committee for MISSION LiFE.This was followed by a brief introduction to the programme by Peter Ki, Public Relations Officer, who highlighted the alignment between India's 2026 BRICS Chairship, with its focus on sustainability, and the objectives of Mission LiFE.Delivering a lecture, Dr Jamir discussed the origins and environmental impact of single-use plastics, attributing the growing crisis to the demand for convenience and the widespread use of disposable packaging and products that require no cleaning, storage or maintenance. She pointed out that plastics designed for use over a few minutes can persist in the environment for centuries, creating serious ecological imbalances. Their toxic impacts extend across their entire life cycle, from petrochemical extraction and manufacturing to consumption and eventual waste disposal. Tracing the historical development of plastic use, she said its consumption increased sharply in the early 1950s and expanded further through the 1990s. Although environmental awareness emerged during the 1960s and 1970s, followed by extensive research into the 2010s, effective bans gained momentum only after 2018. She also outlined the seven main categories of plastics: polyethylene terephthalate (PET), high-density polyethylene (HDPE), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), low-density polyethylene (LDPE), polypropylene (PP), polystyrene (PS) and others. Highlighting the scale of the problem, Dr Jamir said approximately 400 million metric tonnes of plastic waste are generated globally every year, with half comprising single-use items.

9a1e90c5c82cee07.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:31 am IST The Greater Chennai Police (GCP), in coordination with the Health Department, on Thursday conducted surprise inspections at 14 hookah bars operating in the city, to curb the use of banned tobacco products and narcotic substances. The joint inspection teams carried out raids at hookah bars in Teynampet, Vepery, Nungambakkam, Egmore, Anna Salai, Mylapore, and Royapettah. During the inspections, officers checked whether the establishments operated with valid licences, complied with government regulations, and allowed the use of banned narcotic substances. Based on suspicions of violations, the police registered cases against those operating 13 of the 14 hookah bars inspected. Materials used for smoking hookah were seized from the establishments. The seized items will be sent to the forensic science laboratory for examination, the police said. GCP Commissioner A. Amalraj has advised the public, particularly youngsters, to refrain from using banned tobacco products and narcotic substances that can adversely affect their health. The police have warned that surprise inspections will continue in coordination with the Health Department, and that appropriate legal action will be initiated against hookah bars found operating illegally or permitting the use of banned substances. 88705d48441c9095.title: Isolated rain likely in Andhra Pradesh till November 12
88705d48441c9095.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:11 am IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Isolated rain was recorded over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam, and Rayalaseema in the 24 hours ending 8.30 a.m. on Friday (November 6, 2026), the Meteorological Centre, Amaravati, said. The northeast monsoon remained normal, with no heat wave or heavy rainfall. Komarada in Parvathipuram Manyam received 50 mm, followed by Nellore 44 mm, and Madanapalle 33.4 mm. An upper-air cyclonic circulation persists over east Telangana and adjoining Coastal Andhra Pradesh. Thunderstorms with lightning and winds of 30-40 kmph, gusting to 50 kmph, are likely at one or two places along the coast till November 9. Isolated light to moderate rain is forecast State-wide till November 12. Kurnool recorded the day’s highest maximum temperature 36°C, which was 4°C above normal. Visakhapatnam recorded 32.3°C, 1.5°C above normal, and Amaravati 33.7°C. Tirupati received 5 mm and Bapatla 4 mm of rain later on Friday. Since October 1, the State has received 191.1 mm against a normal of 194 mm, with Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam 20% above normal and Rayalaseema 33% below. P.L.N. Murthy, Head, Cyclone Warning Centre, Visakhapatnam, said the Extended Range Outlook indicated an upper-air circulation over the southeast Bay of Bengal around November 11. Under its influence, a low-pressure area was likely to form in the same region around November 13 or 14, with no probability of further intensification as of now. ab0926045c5e10a8.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:10 am IST - Coimbatore The Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore has not withdrawn any of the books supplied by Agal Vilakku Pathipagam, whose publications have come under scrutiny following allegations of irregularities in the procurement of books. V. Santhanakrishnan, in-charge librarian of Periyar Arivulagam, told The Hindu on Friday that publications from Agal Vilakku Pathipagam were being kept in a separate rack in the library. “We have not withdrawn any of those books so far. We have also not received any communication from our department regarding the issue,” he said. This comes after Tamil writer Perumal Murugan flagged alleged inaccuracies and questionable authorship in several of the books displayed at the library. He had pointed out that Agal Vilakku Pathipagam had supplied around 1,800 titles to the library. 3026f9d08605b6d4.title: Stakeholders oppose Karnataka govt.’s move to make private schools adopt govt. schools
3026f9d08605b6d4.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:07 am IST - Bengaluru The Save Public Education Committee and the All India Democratic Students’ Organisation (AIDSO) termed the initiative an attempt by the State government to shut down government schools. Educationalists, student organisations, academicians, teachers and other stakeholders have criticised the State government’s plan to link government schools with private schools through adoption. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar recently held a meeting with private schools and companies, where he proposed the adoption of government schools by private schools and other firms under Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds. The Save Public Education Committee and the All India Democratic Students’ Organisation (AIDSO) termed the initiative an attempt by the State government to shut down government schools. “We strongly condemn this anti-people move. The government has allowed private schools to even tag their names to adopted government schools. By doing this, the government is trying to escape its responsibility to address the deficiencies in the public education system,” the committee said. The committee also condemned remarks allegedly made by representatives of private schools at the meeting against government school teachers, including by Aishwarya DKS Hegde, daughter of Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Trustee Secretary of the National Education Foundation. “During the interaction, they said the quality of teachers in government schools is low. They shifted the entire blame onto teachers while ignoring the role of the government’s own policies in creating the situation,” the committee said. Meanwhile, teachers have expressed displeasure over the remarks. “Teachers are burdened with non-academic work. For example, this year we were deputed for Special Intensive Revision (SIR) work. bab4009692b2411d.title: Deepavali: light up inner self
bab4009692b2411d.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 05:04 am IST Scriptures say when one surrenders to Perumal in all humility, He negates all the negative actions of one until that time. Festivals celebrating the fall of asuras and their subsequent liberation illustrate this aspect admirably. Many asuras undertook severe penance and prayed to the Almighty seeking boons, which finally were the catalyst to their downfall. Dharma will always prevail, as will total surrender to God without seeking anything in return, an aspect underscored in the Bhagavad Gita. Deepavali, the festival of lights celebrating the fall of the Narakasura underscores this perfectly, said Damal S. Ramakrishnan. Deepavali is a festival of lights, not merely of the exterior landscape, but more importantly of one’s inner self. The legend of Narakasura is a well-known one. Born as the son of Bhoo Devi, Narakasura undertook severe penance and was granted the boon that he sought, which was that none barring his mother could kill him. Like most asuras, after gaining the boon, he unleashed a series of atrocities that affected all living things. Lord Krishna took on the asura in a fierce bout, but the power of the boon held and Krishna fell faint in the chariot. His Consort Satyabhama took charge of the situation and wounded him mortally. She was none other than Bhoo Devi, who had manifested as Satyabhama when Perumal descended to earth as Krishna. In the time between his fall and death, the asura realised his folly and becoming truly repentant for his sins, sought another boon: His death should be celebrated in a grand manner by mankind as a reminder that only virtue will prevail and will be truly rewarded. On this day the goddesses too help one light up one’s inner self. Ganga, the purifier of one’s sins, flows into all the waterways. It is customary to have oil bath early in the morning of Deepavali and greet one another with the query, “Is Ganga snan over?” as a way of indicating that one should get rid of one’s sins. G

283d7fb296225f60.title: Amid the sparkle of Deepavali, ophthalmologists sound a note of caution
283d7fb296225f60.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:39 am IST - CHENNAI The sound of firecrackers is not far away, with Deepavali drawing closer. But the excitement of bursting crackers comes with a word of caution from ophthalmologists, as they warn that a moment of carelessness could cause eye injuries ranging from minor abrasions to severe ocular trauma. M. Elangovan, Director, Regional Institute of Ophthalmology and Government Ophthalmic Hospital, said there are different types of crackers. “Bursting types (explosive crackers) will produce irregular, small, and forcible particles in all directions, and are the most dangerous. These particles travel at such a velocity that they could hit or penetrate any soft surface. Then, there is the direct heat injury caused by crackers such as sparklers that result in scars in the cornea or conjunctiva due to the heat generated. Sudden and close exposure to bright light-emitting crackers can also cause bleaching or temporary blackout due to the impact on the rod and cone cells in the retina,” he said. G. 8317c1d66e3d9652.title: Tamil Nadu Fire and Rescue Services gears up for Deepavali
8317c1d66e3d9652.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:40 am IST Areas such as T. Nagar, Purasawalkam, Parry’s Corner, George Town, Washermenpet, Royapuram, Triplicane, Mylapore, Anna Nagar, Koyambedu, Ambattur and Tambaram will receive particular attention. The Tamil Nadu Fire and Rescue Services (TNFRS) has strengthened its fire prevention, emergency response and rescue preparedness across the Chennai Northern Region in view of the forthcoming Deepavali festival, when the extensive use of fireworks, increased commercial activity and large public gatherings pose heightened fire safety challenges. G. Sathiyanarayan, Additional Director of TNFRS said the additional deployment would supplement the Northern Region’s existing strength of 813 personnel and 136 vehicles, taking the total available manpower to 1,129 and the fleet to 158 vehicles. The arrangements cover four fire service districts — Chennai South, Chennai North, Chennai Central and Chennai Suburban — with special focus on densely populated residential neighbourhoods, commercial establishments, fireworks outlets, crowded market streets and other vulnerable locations. The existing fleet includes water tenders, quick response vehicles, water bowsers, foam tenders, emergency rescue vehicles and Bronto Skylifts. The additional vehicles will be strategically positioned based on local risk assessments to ensure quicker response to emergencies, particularly in congested localities where access for large firefighting vehicles could be difficult. Areas such as T. Nagar, Purasawalkam, Parry’s Corner, George Town, Washermenpet, Royapuram, Triplicane, Mylapore, Anna Nagar, Koyambedu, Ambattur and Tambaram will receive particular attention. The department will coordinate with the police, local authorities, medical services and emergency control rooms to handle fire incidents and other emergencies during the festival. The Fire and Rescue Services has also appealed to the public to buy fireworks only from authorised outlets and burst them in open

5c17017b0409d18f.title: Bombay HC, Mahalaxmi Racecourse and Amitabh Bachchan's residence receive bomb threat email
5c17017b0409d18f.summary: A bomb threat email sent to the Bombay High Court also threatened the Bombay Stock Exchange, Mahalaxmi Racecourse and actor Amitabh Bachchan's residence, Jalsa, triggering a security alert in Mumbai, NDTV reported. Police and security agencies are investigating the email to identify the sender. Amitabh Bachchan had received a similar threat email earlier on October 23. The message, which was also sent to Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde and Deputy Mayor Sanjay Ghadi, warned of a grenade attack at a school on October 31 and threatened to target the actor’s Juhu residence between October 31 and November 27. The email had claimed that a blast would take place in the mayor's office at the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) headquarters. The premises were searched, but nothing suspicious was found. The email, which made a references to ‘Khalistan’, also threatened an attack during singer Diljit Dosanjh’s November 27 concert in the Mahalaxmi Racecourse area. Following the threat, the 84-year-old actor changed his customary Sunday interaction with fans outside his residence. Bachchan greeted the gathering from behind a transparent bulletproof enclosure installed on an elevated platform. His son, actor Abhishek Bachchan, and several security personnel were also present as he waved to fans from behind the protective glass. The district and sessions courts in Maharashtra's Pune, Thane, Hingoli, Beed, and Nanded received emails threatening bomb blasts on the premises on November 2, triggering a security scare and a police search. Police said nothing suspicious was found during searches. According to police, the court building in Thane city was evacuated in the afternoon as the office received a message that a bomb would explode at 3.30 pm. "Personnel from Thane Nagar police station evacuated the entire court complex. Judges, advocates and other staffers were safely led out of the premises. A dog squad and BDDS personnel then carried out a thorough search," an official was quoted

73f51ce4601d74a1.title: South Africa mourns Indian-origin TV pioneer Ramprakash Gopidayal
73f51ce4601d74a1.summary: Tributes poured in for South African Indian-origin media personality Ramprakash Gopidayal, who pioneered television programmes and radio recordings for the local Indian community, as he was cremated on Friday after succumbing to illness a day before. Popularly known as Ramu, Gopidayal, despite being an introverted, camera-shy man, started the first television programme for the Indian community, 'Impressions', on national state broadcaster South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC), in the apartheid era. He first joined the SABC as its first Indian-origin technician in 1980. With apartheid waning, the SABC started 'Impressions', a weekly magazine programme on TV for the Indian community, in 1986. It fell upon Gopidayal to take on the task of starting an unprecedented programme from scratch. Satheesan said here on Saturday (November 7) that the country’s best disaster management and resilience programme would be implemented in Keralam. He was speaking after inaugurating the valedictory session of the two-day State-level Coastal Sovereignty and Climate Resilience Conference held at the Cochin University of Science and Technology. M. Junaid Bushiri, Vice-Chancellor, presided, according to a release. Mr. Satheesan said the issues faced by fishing communities needed greater attention and effective solutions. He added that ‘Mission Samudra’ would focus on education, skill development, and employment opportunities in the maritime and fisheries sectors. Measures to address climate change, accurate disaster forecasting, early warning systems, disaster mitigation plans, and operational guidelines for disaster management will be strengthened, he said. 75a73a65a2d95bc2.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 03:38 am IST - KOLKATA The Presidency University has expelled two students for allegedly defacing Swami Vivekananda posters inside the campus, official sources said. The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad had alleged that Left student factions had vandalised the poster and had filed a police complaint on October 14. The two female students have been barred from taking admission in any course at the university in the future. The university had formed a committee to investigate the matter and has checked CCTV footage of the campus and heard from various stakeholders to come to a decision. One of them is a current student and the other was an ex-student who had finished her post-graduate course a few months back. “Two students have been expelled from the studentship/post-studentship academic activities. It has also been decided that they won’t be allowed admission to any future degree program in this university,” official sources said. “Presidency University always stood for dignified academic discourse and debate on different scientific/socio-political issues. The university is not in a position to tolerate any abuse to any thinkers/ideas/organizations,” Presidency University registrar Debajyoti Konar said. The Students’ Federation of India (SFI) condemned the expulsion on Saturday (November 7, 2026). “By imposing an expulsion that threatens to destroy the academic lives of these two students, the administration has established a deeply dangerous precedent,” their statement from the SFI Presidency unit added. 7a6420786d89b00e.title: Chennai Mayor condemns workers using bare hands to clear Deepavali waste, silt
7a6420786d89b00e.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:39 am IST - Chennai Workers clear a silt catch pit with bare hands and without protective gloves or boots in Jamalia, Perambur, amid the Northeast monsoon rains, highlighting the lack of adequate safety gear for Greater Chennai Corporation workers on November 2, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement With crackers and other Deepavali waste being cleared from streets across Chennai, conservancy workers of the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) continue to handle silt, garbage and stagnant water without adequate protective equipment, raising concerns over their safety during the Northeast monsoon. A recent report in The Hindu highlighted how workers who were engaged to clear silt from stormwater drain (SWD) catch pits and stagnant water in several parts of the city were working with bare hands, without any protective gear -- gloves and footwear. The practice was also noticed during the recent rains, where workers were seen clearing silt from a catch pit without gloves. Mayor R. Priya said the practice should not continue and pointed out that the waste generated during Deepavali, including discarded crackers, posed additional challenges for workers. “This should not be happening,” she said, adding that cracker waste could contain chemicals and required separate cleaning arrangements rather than being mixed with regular garbage. A GCC official acknowledged that the provisions made for safety equipment in the estimates were inadequate. “Invariably, sewage gets mixed with stormwater drains, whatever we may say. The provisions made in the estimates are very limited and are largely based on the number of man-days. From next time onwards, we will make more liberal provisions for safety gear and incur some additional expenditure, as it is necessary for the workers’ safety,” the official said. 0e60a5a4afc6d607.summary: Noel N Tata, Chairman of Tata Trusts, has been appointed as Chairman Emeritus of Voltas, a day after he retired as Chairman and Director of the leading cooling products maker. Noel Tata will retire as Chairman and Director of Voltas Ltd on November 11, 2026, upon attaining the age of superannuation under Tata Group governance guidelines. Following his retirement, "the Board has appointed him as Chairman Emeritus of the Company with effect from November 12, 2026," said Voltas, a Tata Group firm, in its regulatory filing. The Companies Act 2013 mandates that any managing director or whole-time director cannot be appointed or continue employment if they are 70 years of age or older. Noel Tata, who was born on November 12, 1956, will turn 70 on November 12, 2026. He has been associated with Voltas since 2003. eabbfaffceff3701.title: Students urged to dream big, prepare for a self-reliant India
eabbfaffceff3701.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 11:17 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Students should dare to dream big, think independently and pursue ambitious goals to drive innovation and contribute to the vision of a self-reliant India, said Prof. Ramesh Srikonda, Director of the School of Planning and Architecture, Vijayawada. Addressing the Freshers’ Day celebrations at Dr. RVR NRI Institute of Technology (Deemed to be University), he emphasised that bold aspirations lead to new ideas and innovative outcomes. He urged students to focus on holistic development rather than limiting their ambitions to obtaining academic degrees. The celebrations, organised to welcome newly admitted first-year students, witnessed the participation of over 2,000 students, who showcased their talents through colourful singing and dancing performances. Prof. M.L.N. Rao, Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor of Rajiv Gandhi University of Knowledge Technologies (RGUKT-AP), said emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Quantum Technologies would drive major transformations over the next five to 10 years. He encouraged students to prepare themselves to contribute to the visions of Swarna Andhra Pradesh 2047 and Viksit Bharat 2047. NRI University Chairman and Chancellor Dr. Ravi Venkata Rao said the institution’s four-year academic programme aimed at shaping students into responsible, capable individuals equipped to overcome challenges and contribute meaningfully to society. Vice-Chancellor Dr. K.R.S. Sambasiva Rao urged students to make effective use of the university’s teaching and learning facilities and continuously upgrade their skills to become industry-ready professionals. Organising convener and Dean D. Suneetha, CEO, Pro-Vice-Chancellors, Registrar, Deans, Heads of Departments, faculty members and other dignitaries attended the celebrations. Published - November 07, 2026 11:17 pm IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentence

f086a0b616aada4a.title: D2C brands see 27% more orders ahead of Diwali; sales value up 45%: Report
f086a0b616aada4a.summary: Direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands in India shipped 27 per cent more orders a day in the run-up to Diwali this year than in the same period last year, while the value of goods sold jumped about 45 per cent, according to a report. ClickPost, an AI logistics automation and post-purchase platform for D2C and retail, analysed more than 8 crore orders placed on the websites of nearly 400 D2C brands. It compared the festive shopping windows of September 20 to November 5 this year and September 1 to October 17 last year. According to ClickPost's report, gross merchandise value (GMV), the total value of goods sold, grew about 1.7 times faster than the number of orders. The report said this was because shoppers bought higher-priced products despite rising retail prices, rather than looking for cheaper alternatives. Spending was concentrated in high-value categories such as luxury fashion, skincare, wellness and jewellery, it said. Despite the higher volumes, deliveries became more reliable. .

e85d14ba92076f05.title: Nallur toll plaza on Kolkata National Highway to be moved to Durainallur
e85d14ba92076f05.summary: Updated - November 08, 2026 01:39 am IST - CHENNAI The National Highways Authority of India has planned to shift the toll plaza at Nallur on the Chennai - Kolkata National Highway. It will be moved to Durainallur, which is about 13 km from the present location. The plaza is notorious for long waits during rush hours. Motorists fed up with waiting at the Nallur Plaza will get some relief from this move. “Residents of areas such as Karanodai, Janapanchathiram, Nallur and Periyapalayam will find it very convenient when the plaza is removed. There are several colleges in the area and the buses transporting students too wait in queue to cross the plaza on many occasions. Shifting of the plaza has been a long-time demand,” said K. Suresh Kumar, a resident. Ramesh, another resident, suggested that the width of the road be narrowed at that location. “It is now wider than the road width, making it difficult to cross. It would be helpful if the road stretch is normalised and shops regularised,” he said. Sources in the NHAI said that the existing location was no longer viable as a number of new roads have been laid in the surroundings making it possible for road users to avoid the plaza. This will lead to loss of revenue. “The plaza is also located inside municipal limits, making it pertinent to shift it outside. The contract of the current agency managing the plaza will get over by May next year. We hope to get the design ready for the new plaza by then,” explained a source. Around 50,000 passenger car units use that road on a daily basis. The plaza is also likely to be a multi-lane free flow tolling system without toll booths and operators. bf7eb2a5cf5df45f.title: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings files draft papers with Sebi for IPO
bf7eb2a5cf5df45f.summary: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings Ltd (HCCH), backed by The Coca-Cola Company and Jubilant Beverages, has filed its draft papers with the market regulator Sebi to raise funds through an initial public offering (IPO). The proposed IPO will be entirely an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 99,74,61,456 equity shares by promoter Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings Pte Ltd, according to the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) dated November 6. Since the issue is entirely an OFS, the company will not receive any proceeds from the IPO, with the entire proceeds going to the selling shareholder.

Shami announced his retirement from Test cricket on Friday night. e413be16791dc88d.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 03:56 am IST - KOLKATA The agitation at the Satyajit Ray Film & Television Institute (SRFTI) continued for 42 days as class suspension was extended till December 11, affecting academic life. Students of the film institute on Saturday (November 7, 2026) said that “This Diwali we choose to resist”, while authorities said they were “keen" to resume classes. “Diwali has always been a special occasion at SRFTI... But this year, the familiar celebrations are overshadowed by fear, uncertainty and an ongoing struggle for justice,” an official post by the SRFTI student union said on Saturday (November 7, 2026), a day before Deepavali. They also said that the day they are served justice will be Deepavali for them. “While the faculty and administration are ready to resume classes, a section of students continues to remain disengaged from academics and disrupt the functioning of the Institute through repeated violations of its rules and orders,” Registrar Deepak Kumar told The Hindu on Saturday (November 7, 2026). He further added that they are asking students to come forward for constructive dialogue. As of November 7, at least 25 students have received show cause notices, with 11 of them receiving them last Thursday (November 5, 2026). Six students have faced rustication, and one FIR has been registered against student union Vice-President Shubham. Shubham is one of the six students who got the rustication notice for allegedly vandalising the Vice-Chancellor Santosh Ajmeera’s office and manhandling him. However, all of these allegations have been denied by the students. According to the students, two contractual faculty members, and five resource persons of SRFTI have also been terminated from their jobs for showing solidarity with the students. As the classes remained suspended, the hostels and mess were also closed for students. Addressing the valedictory session of a three-day international conference on “Computation Science and Intelligent Engineering”, organised by the Department of Mathematics in Siddhartha Academy of Higher Education (Deemed-to-be-University), she emphasised that strong mathematical foundations would remain essential for the future advancement of digital intelligence. d607e15879d0bb8d.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 11:42 pm IST - Bengaluru Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) conducted a trial run of a train on the test track at the Byappanahalli depot on Saturday as part of preparations for the much-awaited Blue Line. The trial involved checking electrical systems, assessing the readiness of rolling stock and identifying possible infringements along the track. BMRCL is expected to move testing to the main line shortly. An official said that the testing would resume next week, subject to the availability of workers following Deepavali. Bharat Earth Movers Limited (BEML) has manufactured the driverless trainset for the Blue Line. The Blue Line, comprising Metro Phases 2A and 2B, is a major infrastructure project connecting the city with Kempegowda International Airport. The K.R. Puram–airport stretch is 38.44-km long, while the K.R. Puram–Central Silk Board section covers 19.75 km. 7a6a76cada888f6f.title: DMK flays govt.’s decision to remit money in lieu of distributing rice to ration cardholders in U.T.
7a6a76cada888f6f.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 03:04 am IST - PUDUCHERRY Convenor of DMK’s Puducherry unit R. Siva has flayed the AINRC-BJP government for adopting the cash transfer mode instead of distributing free rice under the scheme in the Union Territory. In a statement, the DMK leader said the government had not distributed free rice through ration shops for the last nine months. Now, the government has remitted money into the accounts of ration cardholders in lieu of free rice meant for six months. The amount remitted by the government was based on a calculation of ₹43 per kg for the rice, he said. However, the cash remitted was not sufficient for buying rice due to cost escalation. The price of rice has gone up substantially in the open market and the money given by the government would be inadequate for the residents to buy the required quantity, he said. “The government’s decision to adopt Direct Benefit Transfer mode was a betrayal of the mandate given by the people. The Chief Minister had promised the voters to provide rice through ration shops. If the implementation of the scheme to distribute rice through ration shops would take more time, the government should remit more money considering the market rate of rice,” Mr. Siva said. 78b4dd6ccab6540f.title: Renovated bus terminus in Ranipet town opened for public use
78b4dd6ccab6540f.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:57 am IST - RANIPET Collector N. Priya Ravichandran inspect the restored bus terminus in the town in the presence of transport and municipal officials. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement After more than four years of renovation work, the restored ₹13.55-crore integrated bus terminus on the Ranipet-Walajah Main Road was opened for public use, ahead of Deepavali. Officials of Ranipet municipality, which executed the multi-crore work, said that the old terminus was built more than five decades ago with very few facilities for commuters. “The restored terminus helps people board long-distance buses. The facility has better seating arrangements and safety features for commuters,” said S. Kumar, a commuter. Funded under Kalaignar Nagarpura Membattu Thittam 2022-23 that aims to fulfil the infrastructural gaps in the urban local bodies, work to restore the terminus was started in 2022. “The restored bus terminus will help commuters, especially women and senior citizens to board buses safely as round-the-clock surveillance is in place. A help desk is also available to guide commuters,” said D. Senthil Kumar, Commissioner, Ranipet municipality. Collector N. Priya Ravichandran inspected the restored bus terminus in the town in the presence of transport and municipal officials. The restored bus terminus will operate buses to Bengaluru, Vellore, Vandavasi, Cheyyar, Chengam, Arcot, Ranipet, Coimbatore, Salem, Kancheepuram, Hosur, and Dharmapuri. Among civic amenities, the terminus has a purified drinking water facility, solar-powered LED streetlights, digital timing boards, feeding room, a police booth, and CCTV cameras. A police outpost will also be set up in the coming days. Every day, on an average, more than 200 buses operated by Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation ply from the terminus. Commuters said that additional buses to towns such as Tiruvannamalai, Sholinghur, Arcot, Gingee, and Kancheepuram should be operated at the terminus. Publ

Scheduled to be held on November 8 in Palace Grounds, the event marks the eighth edition of Salaam Souk and its first Greek-themed edition. It is an initiative of The Tribe & Co that has previously presented cultural themes inspired by Morocco, Turkey, Uzbekistan, India and Dubai. The festival has been designed to recreate the feel of a Greek street market, combining Mediterranean-inspired food, fashion, art, music, home décor, beauty and wellness experiences. The event will feature 35 food stalls, 150 retail stalls, live bands, fire shows and aerial performances, offering visitors a distinctive Greek-inspired cultural experience in Bengaluru. 8464144f1a0e52ff.title: 108 ambulance network geared up to handle emergencies
8464144f1a0e52ff.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:55 am IST - CHENNAI In view of Deepavali, the 108 ambulance network is prepared to handle all types of emergencies. All ambulances across the State have been strategically positioned at identified hotspots to ensure that emergency care reaches the needy at the earliest. According to a press release, this proactive deployment will help in minimising the response time and thereby increasing the life-saved percentage. The network, especially in metro cities, has clocked an average response time of less than seven minutes, and is focused on sustaining and further improving the same. The “EMRI GHS 108 Ambulance Services”, based on the previous year experiences, have taken precautionary measures with regard to deployment of ambulances in identified Deepavali hotspot areas, where more number of fire/ burns and assault cases are expected in the respective locations. Last year, the network received 26,000 calls requiring emergency services across Tamil Nadu during Deepavali. The Emergency Response Centre for helplines 108, 104 and 102 are working with full strength under three shifts. All support staff are working in coordination with respective district authorities, the release said. A medical protocol is being developed to transfer the patient based on their criticality from a lower facility to a higher facility, while inter-hospital transfer of critical patients is earmarked through Advanced Life Support ambulances based on separate despatch criteria. A dedicated Inter Facility Transfer help desk is also functioning, the release said. Through these cells, the university will conduct placement drives, besides holding offline and online skill training essential for employment. While the university already has a placement cell that conducts annual placement drives, and has even appointed placement officers in select affiliated colleges, these officers are currently not active. Allegations have surfaced that, as a result, students are not receiving adequate information regarding placements. “When enrolling in colleges, students and parents place high priority on placements. However, in the current scenario, job availability is limited. Also, students lack accurate information about the jobs that are available. 59f706d6e2da936e.title: Rahul questions E20 petrol ethanol levels, cites Karnataka test results
59f706d6e2da936e.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday attacked the Modi government over the rollout of E20 petrol, citing test results of samples collected by the Karnataka government, and asked the Centre to come clean on the actual ethanol content in fuel being sold across the country. In a post in Hindi on X, Gandhi said, "E20 turned into 420 stealing petrol from the public's cars!" The reference was to Section 420 of the erstwhile Indian Penal Code, which dealt with cheating. Gandhi said the government claims that petrol contains 20 per cent ethanol but tests conducted on samples collected from seven districts in Karnataka had revealed higher levels. "The Karnataka government collected petrol samples from 7 districts and had them tested at an accredited lab. Look at the results 11 out of 14 samples contained more than 20 per cent ethanol; 31.2 per cent at IOCL, 30.5 per cent at HPCL; IOCL, HPCL, BPCL, Nayara, Shell whether government-owned or private all exceeded the limit," he claimed.

74f5ce093329eb6c.title: Two youths arrested for possessing narcotics in Vellore
74f5ce093329eb6c.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:54 am IST - VELLORE Two youths were arrested by Vellore South police for possession of 1300 narcotic tablets (Tapentadol) near the fort complex in Vellore town on Saturday. The police identified them as R. Vinoth, 23, and his friend B. Manimaran, 23. They were residents of Vellore town. Initial inquiry revealed that based on a tip-off to Vellore SP N.U. Sivaraman, special teams were formed to conduct surprise checks in public places in the district. During a surprise check near the fort complex, the team apprehended the suspects. They checked the duo and their bags, where they found a huge quantity of pharmaceutical drugs in them. Investigation found that the gang had placed an order for tablets with pharmacies online. The tablets were sent by couriers to them. The police said the duo were on their way to the railway station to go to Chennai, where they planned to sell the drugs. A case was registered and arrested persons were lodged in Central Prison in Vellore. A probe is under way.
