37bb49dfea8ff924.title: Gang held near Vaniyambadi for burglary
37bb49dfea8ff924.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:54 am IST - TIRUPATTUR A gang of five persons were arrested by Vaniyambadi Taluk police in Tirupattur on Saturday for stealing 52 sovereigns of gold jewellery, one kilogram of silver objects and around ₹20,000 lakh cash from the house of a painter recently. The arrested persons were identified as K. Naveen, 26, T. Parthiban, 30, S. Gopinath, 39, G. Manikandan, 40, and C. Sarathkumar, 25. They are previous offenders and have theft cases against them in Salem, Dharmapuri, Tirupattur, Thanjavur, and Pudukottai. Initial inquiry revealed that the victim, R. Prabhakaran, 39, was living with his family including wife Geetha (34) and mother Ambika (65) in the house near Vaniyambadi town a few days ago when the gang barged into the house. The police said the gang allegedly tied R. Prabhakaran, 39, and his family and stole the valuables from the house before fleeing the spot. Mr. Prabhakaran managed to untie himself and alerted Vaniyambadi Taluk police. Special teams were formed to nab the suspects. The police also analysed CCTV camera footage to identify suspects. The suspects were traced to a hideout in Thanjavur and were arrested. A car used by the gang was also seized. 27b94618dc63453b.title: Divi's Labs Q2 result: Net profit rises 64% to ₹1,127 cr on higher revenue
27b94618dc63453b.summary: Divi's Laboratories Ltd on Saturday posted a sharp 63.57 per cent rise in net profit to Rs 1,127 crore in the September quarter due to higher revenues. The company posted a net profit of Rs 689 crore in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year, a regulatory filing said. Revenue from operations rose 35.39 per cent to Rs 3,676 crore during the second quarter of FY27 from Rs 2,715 crore a year earlier, it said. Its total expenses rose to Rs 2,265 crore in the period under review from Rs 1,948 crore a year ago, it added. The company's net profit for the first half of the current fiscal year, however, declined 35.39 per cent to Rs 2,029 crore from Rs 2,568 crore in the year-ago period, the filing added.

34907735bc26c903.title: RPF steps up Deepavali vigil, apprehends five with firecrackers at Chennai Central, Egmore
34907735bc26c903.summary: Updated - November 08, 2026 01:50 am IST - CHENNAI With a view to ensuring passenger safety during the Deepavali festival, the Railway Protection Force (RPF), Chennai Division, Southern Railway, has intensified surveillance and preventive checks at major railway stations to curb illegal transportation of firecrackers and other inflammable materials. During special checks conducted on Friday, RPF personnel apprehended five persons carrying firecrackers at Chennai Central and Chennai Egmore railway stations in two separate operations. At Chennai Central, four persons were intercepted while attempting to board passenger trains with firecrackers. Three were stopped before boarding the Chennai Central–Jolarpettai Yelagiri Express, while another was intercepted before boarding the Chennai Central–Thiruvananthapuram Express. Four separate cases were registered against them under Section 164 of the Railways Act, 1989. At Chennai Egmore, RPF personnel apprehended a 25-year-old man carrying a box of firecrackers and registered a case under the same provision. Meanwhile, as part of its efforts to sensitise passengers ahead of Deepavali, the RPF conducted a Jan Jagaran awareness programme at Chennai Beach Railway Station on Friday. Passengers were cautioned against carrying firecrackers and other explosive materials on trains, as they could cause fires and explosions, endangering lives and railway property. They were informed about the provisions of Section 164 of the Railways Act, which prescribes imprisonment for up to three years for unauthorised possession or transportation of explosives on railway premises or trains. During the awareness drive, nine persons were apprehended for unauthorised trespassing and fined ₹500 each under Section 147 of the Railways Act, taking the total collection to ₹4,500. 62e36a797e1e03cf.title: Delivery firm employee arrested for stealing mobile phones
62e36a797e1e03cf.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:57 am IST - CHENNAI The Guindy police have arrested a 21-year-old employee of a private online delivery company for allegedly stealing two mobile phones from the firm’s returned goods inventory. Police said the complainant, Bhagavathi Murugan, 40, a resident of Guindy, works as a manager in the security and loss prevention department of a private online delivery company in the Guindy Industrial Estate. According to the complaint, Prathumna Krishna, an employee of the company, was responsible for inspecting goods returned by customers when deliveries could not be completed and processing them for return as per the prescribed procedures. When Bhagavathi Murugan recently checked the returned consignments, he found that two mobile phones received back on October 21 and 28, were missing. An internal check revealed that Krishna had allegedly stolen the phones. The police registered a case and examined CCTV footage and conducted inquiries at the company before arresting Prathumna Krishna, 21, a resident of Subramania Swamy Koil West Street, West Saidapet. Police recovered one mobile phone from him and ₹10,000, which he had allegedly obtained by selling the other stolen phone. a6332848a8dbf79a.summary: The toll in the three-storey building collapse in Old Delhi's Hauz Qazi area rose to three on Saturday after the body of another labourer was recovered from the debris during the ongoing rescue operations, officials said. The deceased has been identified as Pankaj Sharma (40), a resident of Hanuman Nagar village in Bihar's Khagaria district, they said. After nearly 48 hours of operation at the site, five people have been pulled out of the debris -- three dead and two injured persons. Both injured persons have received medical treatment and are stable. The building under construction collapsed in Gali Sitara near Chawri Bazar Metro station around 9.45 am on Thursday. The operation to find more people and clear the rubble continued at the site. Around 10 to 15 labourers were present at the construction site when the three-storey structure came crashing down, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central) Rohit Rajbir Singh had said. 9256e15f091d794d.title: Centre allows transfer of prisoners between Chandigarh, other states
9256e15f091d794d.summary: The Centre has extended the Punjab Police and Correctional Services Act, 2006, to the Union Territory of Chandigarh, introducing provisions for the transfer of prisoners between states and Union territories and changes to the functioning of the prison administration. The notification, issued under Section 87 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966, extends the Punjab legislation to the Union Territory of Chandigarh with certain modifications, according to a notification issued by the Union Home Ministry on Friday. The amended provisions deal with the transfer of prisoners between Chandigarh and other states or Union territories. Under the provisions, prisoners serving sentences in Chandigarh, including life imprisonment, may be transferred to prisons in another state or Union territory with the consent of the government concerned and an order issued by the Chandigarh administrator. The amendments also provide for the transfer of undertrial prisoners in the interest of Chandigarh's .

09b406db0ac57bf2.title: Five killed, over a dozen injured as gunman opens fire in Poland's Krakow
09b406db0ac57bf2.summary: Five people were killed and more than a dozen injured after a gunman opened fire Saturday afternoon in a market square in Krakow, Poland, police said. The gunman aimed at random people as he drove by the city's Main Square, Krakow police said. Police officers are among the wounded. The perpetrator was shot and wounded during a confrontation with police. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, in a post on X, said police are investigating the attack. Other details were not immediately available. Krakow is the second-largest city in Poland and roughly 250 kilometres from the capital, Warsaw.

Industrialist Gautam Adani and NCP leader Praful Patel had also visited the hospital. Pawar was initially admitted to Pune's Ruby Hall Clinic on November 2 and discharged on November 4. The same day, he was admitted to the Mumbai hospital.

8f2075cd50333015.title: UP govt hikes DA by 5%, employees to get arrears retrospectively from Jul 1
8f2075cd50333015.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has hiked the Dearness Allowance (DA) by 5 per cent for state government employees, staff in aided educational and technical institutions, regular and full-time employees of urban local bodies, work-charged employees, and those serving on UGC pay scales. Employees will now receive a Dearness Allowance of 63 per cent, up from 58 per cent. The increased rate will be effective from July 1, 2026, the state government said in a statement on Saturday. A government order was also issued in this regard on Saturday. The enhanced dearness allowance will be paid along with the regular salary for November 2026. This government decision will benefit lakhs of employees across the state. The move by the Yogi Adityanath government will provide relief not only to the state's regular employees but also to staff in aided educational institutions, urban local bodies, and other eligible categories of employees, the statement said.

A government order was also issued in this regard on Saturday. The enhanced dearness allowance will be paid along with the regular salary for November 2026. This government decision will benefit lakhs of employees across the state. The move by the Yogi Adityanath government will provide relief not only to the state's regular employees but also to staff in aided educational institutions, urban local bodies, and other eligible categories of employees, the statement said.

ca4cec0548bff88f.summary: Published - November 09, 2026 04:52 am IST - WASHINGTON U.S. President Donald Trump. | Photo Credit: AP U.S. President Donald Trump said that his mass deportation of undocumented immigrants was "too tough," according to an excerpt of an interview with CBS aired on Sunday (November 8, 2026). Asked about his deportation policy, Mr. Trump told CBS ' "60 Minutes": "I think it was too tough...I think it might be too tough." The excerpt was published by CBS on X ahead of a broadcast of the interview on network TV later on Sunday (November 8, 2026). It was recorded after the Republican Party's heavy loss in midterm elections on Tuesday. While Mr. Trump has won some domestic support for securing the U.S. southern border, his administration's aggressive push to deport millions of undocumented migrants has drawn widespread criticism. However, Mr. Trump on Friday (November 6, 2026) appointed the architect of that hardline policy, Stephen Miller, as his chief of staff, signalling a bare-knuckle fightback after the Republican election loss. Mr. Miller has been synonymous with scenes of masked immigration agents committing violence after he backed federal agents who shot and killed two Americans early this year. 2c2cc6acf539af85.title: Assam OIL facility fire: death toll rises to four as another injured dies; four suspended
2c2cc6acf539af85.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 07:21 pm IST - Dibrugarh (Assam) Workers move away as a massive fire rages following an explosion at Oil India Limited's (OIL) Intermediate Tank Farm (ITF), in Dibrugarh district, on November 6, 2026. | Photo Credit: PTI The toll in the fire incident at an Oil India Ltd (OIL) facility in Assam's Dibrugarh district increased to four with another injured worker succumbing on Sunday (November 8, 2026), while the PSU has suspended all four of its personnel who were in charge of the site, officials said. Three people who were also injured in the blaze on Friday (November 6, 2026) are undergoing treatment in a critical condition. All the victims were employees of Spectron Engineering Private Limited, a Mumbai-based company engaged by OIL. One person was killed in the fire on the day of the incident, while two died the next day. A mechanical helper, Sailen Gogoi, who was undergoing treatment at a private hospital here, died during the day, taking the toll to four, the official said. A fire had broken out on November 6 after an explosion during maintenance work at OIL's intermediate tank farm (ITF) in Tengakhat, the public sector undertaking said in a statement. An ITF is a facility where petroleum products are temporarily stored in tanks before being transferred for further processing or transportation. Meanwhile, OIL has instituted a high-level inquiry to probe into the incident, another official said. The committee has put all four OIL employees who were in-charge of the ITF, including three officers, on suspension, he said. "They were placed under suspension until the investigation is over," the official added. The PSU has announced an ex-gratia of ₹10 lakh to the next of kin of each deceased, and Rs 5 lakh to each injured person. Union minister Sarbananda Sonowal and Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma were closely monitoring the situation, the PSU said on Saturday (November 7, 2026). 4f440a6990bb54de.title: NGT issues notice to Tirunelveli Collector over threats to Tamirabharani fish species
4f440a6990bb54de.summary: Updated - November 08, 2026 07:06 pm IST - CHENNAI Some of the fishes found in the Tamirabharani River in Tirunelveli district. File | Photo Credit: Special arrangement The Principal Bench of the National Green Tribunal (NGT), New Delhi, has issued notice to the Tirunelveli Collector and five others over threats faced by fish species in Tamirabharani River due to pollution and habitat loss. Taking suo motu cognisance of a report, titled ‘Tamirabharani’s Endemic Fish Face Threats From Pollution, Habitat Loss’, published in The Hindu on September 28, the Bench, comprising Justice Arun Kumar Tyagi and expert members A. Senthil Vel and Afroz Ahamed, directed that the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board, the Central Pollution Control Board’s Regional Office in Chennai, Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment (ATREE), and Agasthyamalai Community Conservation Centre (ACCC) be impleaded as respondents, besides the Collector. The order said: “The above news item attracts the provisions of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, and the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, and prima facie raises substantial questions relating to the environment arising out of the implementation of the enactments specified in Schedule I to the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.” The Bench directed the Registry to list the matter before the Southern Bench of the Tribunal, Chennai, on January 22, 2027, as the cause of action had arisen within its territorial jurisdiction. It also directed the respondents to file their responses before the Bench at least one day ahead of the date of hearing. The Hindu had reported that 125 fish species had been identified in upstream, midstream and lower estuarine stretches of the river. Seven of them are endemic to the Tamirabharani. 98c3ceec5687386f.summary: A strong earthquake shook central Japan early Sunday, shattering store windows, causing people to flee buildings and leaving at least 22 people injured, according to local media. Japan's Meteorological Agency put the quake's magnitude at 5.7, while the US Geological Survey reported it at magnitude 5.5. Smaller aftershocks were reported. A wide area near Aichi Prefecture was affected, including the city of Hamamatsu, the ancient capitals of Kyoto and Nara and nearby prefectures of Yamanashi, where Mount Fuji is located, as well as Gifu. Japanese TV footage showed shattered store windows and scattered shards of glass on the streets. A bookstore was left with mounds of books that had flown off the shelves. The injuries included people who fell from stairs while they were trying to flee. The quake, which struck at 1:04 am local time, was located about 40 km below the earth's surface in Shizuoka Prefecture. Aichi and Shizuoka are neighboring regions. f1fb36e5c6e7e558.title: Congress donations fall nearly 75%, sharpest decline in a decade
f1fb36e5c6e7e558.summary: The Congress party's receipts from donations above Rs 20,000 plunged nearly 75 per cent to Rs 130.69 crore in 2025-26, the steepest annual fall in such contributions in a decade, an analysis of the party's filings with the Election Commission shows. The party had received Rs 517.39 crore in such contributions in 2024-25, according to its 2024-25 contribution report submitted to the commission. A comparison with the preceding 12 financial years shows that the last steeper fall was in 2015-16, when Congress' disclosed donations dropped roughly 86 per cent from Rs 141.46 crore the previous year. The latest decline follows two years of higher collections. Congress received Rs 281.48 crore in disclosed donations in 2023-24, rising to Rs 517.39 crore in 2024-25, the year Lok Sabha elections were held. 4eaa140d0d65a62f.summary: Russia has recorded the deaths of about 400,000 of its people fighting in Ukraine since the full-scale invasion almost five years ago, according to confidential data held by the country’s statistics agency, Rosstat.

4eaa140d0d65a62f.raw_facts: Russia has recorded the deaths of about 400,000 of its people fighting in Ukraine since the full-scale invasion almost five years ago, according to confidential data held by the country’s statistics agency, Rosstat.
flags: Timeline inconsistency: The full-scale invasion began in February 2022. As of mid-2024, it has been approximately two years, not 'almost five years'.

Source reliability: The claim attributes the data to 'confidential data held by Rosstat' revealed via 'hacked records'. While independent estimates (e.g., from BBC, Mediazona, or Western intelligence) have suggested Russian casualties in the hundreds of thousands, there is no verified public evidence that Rosstat's internal records were hacked and released with this specific figure.

Official vs. Independent Data: Rosstat has not officially released a figure of 400,000 deaths. Official Russian figures have historically been much lower or non-specific. Independent estimates vary widely but often fall in the range of 100,000 to 200,000+ confirmed deaths, with total casualties (including wounded) being higher. John Harrison, author of "The End of Everything" holds the trophy for winning the Booker Prize during the Booker Prize 2026 ceremony at Old Billingsgate in London, November 10, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP U.K. author M. John Harrison won the Booker Prize on Monday (November 9, 2026) for his enigmatic novel "The End of Everything", which echoes concerns about artificial intelligence in a darkly satirical depiction of post-apocalyptic Britain. Mr. Harrison, 81, became the oldest winner of the award, which comes with a £50,000 ($67,000) prize and a boost in sales and profile for the winner. Review | ‘The End of Everything’ by M. John Harrison: the aliens are here A veteran of the British science fiction literary scene, it was Mr. Harrison’s first time being shortlisted for the coveted prize, which critics have said was long overdue. He beat shortlisted authors Marlon James, Douglas Stuart, Elizabeth Strout, Luke Kennard and Rebecca Perry, whose entries ranged from a queer epic unfolding in 1980s Kingston to a campus satire set in modern-day London. "The End of Everything" came out "ahead in terms of both its extraordinary expert writing, but also huge ambition," chair of the judges Mary Beard told a press conference. Mr. Harrison's 13th novel follows the beachcomber Phillip Tennent and his dementia-stricken, free-spirited aunt Marnie, set in the near-future on the windswept English coast invaded by mysterious objects known as the iGhetti. An unnamed catastrophe plunges the characters into a murky post-apocalyptic world where the European continent seems to have disappeared and the arrival of the iGhetti, which can imitate humans, evoke interactions with artificial intelligence. "One main point of the book is that if, or when, such an apocalypse comes it will be incomprehensible," Ms. Beard said, adding the book spoke to the present "moment". 7f3ebff4cc6a832e.title: Five persons, including four girls, drown in irrigation tank in Tiruvannamalai
7f3ebff4cc6a832e.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 12:20 am IST - TIRUVANNAMALAI Collector Vandhana Garg and Superintendent of Police R. Uthayakumar during their inspection of the irrigation tank on Monday. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement A staff nurse and four girls of a government-recognised children’s home for girls drowned in an irrigation tank at Samuthiram village here on Monday (November 9, 2026). The deceased were identified as staff nurse Thenmozhi, 24, Vijayalakshmi, 14, Alli, 14, Poomika, 13, and Valliammal, 16. Except Valliammal, who belongs to Kilpennathur village, the other three girls are siblings from Karapattu village near Chengam. The deceased did not know swimming, the police said. Initial inquiry revealed the home had been functioning for over a decade in the area. On Monday afternoon, Thenmozhi, along with around 13 girls, went to the irrigation tank on Perumbakkam Main Road to bathe. Poomika and her siblings and Valliammal stepped into the water and slipped and fell into a deeper portion of the irrigation tank. The police said Thenmozhi tried to save the children but also drowned. Hearing the other girls’ shouts, the area’s residents rushed to the spot and alerted the Tiruvannamalai West police and firefighters. Firefighters retrieved the bodies and sent them to the Government Medical College and Hospital in Tiruvannamalai town for a post-mortem. A case has been registered. Collector Vandhana Garg and Superintendent of Police R. Uthayakumar met the families of the deceased at the hospital in the presence of hospital dean Edvina Vasantah and inspected the irrigation tank. A probe is under way. 12f72c3e816cf159.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 12:11 am IST - CHENNAI The postponement of the WTA 250 Chennai Open singles final due to rain and fireworks-induced smog on Sunday evening sparked controversy over the organisers’ handling of the situation. The final, set for a 6:30 p.m. start, was delayed thrice due to rain. Once the rain relented for good, the organisers dried the centre court at the SDAT stadium and rescheduled the final at 9 p.m. However, the smog caused by the Deepavali firecrackers had made the air quality hazardous and the match had to be shifted to 11 a.m. on Monday in which Poland’s Magda Linette defeated Indonesia’s Janice Tjen, the reigning champion, in three sets. Christopher Bint, Tjen’s coach, in an Instagram story late on Sunday night, claimed that the organisers wanted to conduct the final despite the extremely poor air quality. “And they still wanted the match to go ahead,” he wrote, attaching a screenshot showing an AQI of 1556 in Chennai. Later, after Monday’s summit clash, Bint said, “Maybe, it could have just been postponed a little bit earlier.” Linette felt the doubles final, which started at 4 p.m. on Sunday, could have been moved forward. “We should have put the doubles final way earlier which would have given us a lot of time,” said the 34-year-old Pole. Hiten Joshi, the tournament director, said, “In these emergencies, the tournament supervisor (Sheetal Iyer) has to get permission from the WTA. So, they were going back and forth, and she also wanted to wait to see if any play was possible.” Published - November 10, 2026 12:11 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. 40a90eb64af97d91.title: APSDRF rescues eight, evacuates 341 during Cyclone Arnab relief efforts
40a90eb64af97d91.summary: Updated - November 10, 2026 12:20 am IST - VIJAYAWADA DGP Harish Kumar Gupta presenting rewards to the APSDRF personnel at the AP Police Headquarters in Mangalagiri on Monday. | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Response Force (APSDRF) shifted 341 people to safe places, rescued eight, and retrieved a body during Cyclone Arnab. Inspector General of Police (IGP-Operations) Ch. Srikanth, along with senior officers of Andhra Pradesh Special Police (APSP) met Director General of Police (DGP) Harish Kumar Gupta at the Police Headquarters at Mangalagiri on Monday (November 9, 2026), and explained the operations taken up by APSDRF during the calamity. The SDRF officials explained that eleven special teams comprising 328 officers and personnel rendered services in the State from October 27 to November 1. Rescue and relief operations were carried out in Bapatla, Konaseema, Kakinada, Srikakulam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, West Godavari, East Godavari, Polavaram, and Anakapalli districts. A total of 728 fallen trees were cleared, road clearance operations were taken up at 58 locations, and 31 electricity poles that fell on roads were removed, facilitating the movement of emergency vehicles, Mr. Srikanth said. The ‘Dial 112’ State Control Room played a crucial role in providing assistance to the people trapped in cyclone. In three days, the control room staff received 369 cyclone-related emergency calls from 17 districts. The SDRF, with the coordination of Dial-112 rescued 40 passengers travelling in a bus stranded in floodwaters in Srikakulam. In another incident, the personnel assisted in rescuing eight fishermen caught in danger due to the cyclone, the officers said. The DGP appreciated the courage, dedication, and commitment of the APSDRF in saving the lives of people during disasters, stating that their services are a matter of pride for the Police Department. He presented rewards to officers and personnel who exhibited outstanding bravery in rescue

fc50fb31451033a0.title: Diwali 2026: Global leaders – Anthony Albanese, Emmanuel Macron, Mark Carney – call for unity, peace, prosperity
fc50fb31451033a0.summary: Wishing peace, prosperity, and hope, world leaders—including Emmanuel Macron, Anthony Albanese, and Mark Carney—shared their Diwali greetings on Sunday with all those celebrating the festival of lights. Albanese said Diwali was “the great celebration of the victory of light,” bringing communities together across religious and cultural boundaries. “We can all take pride and joy in just how intrinsically Diwali has become part of the face of modern Australia,” he said in a video message, noting that the signs and symbols of Diwali carry a message that speaks beyond religion or culture. Anthony Albanese, Emmanuel Macron and Mark Carney were among the leaders who sent greetings. Messages also came from leaders in Sri Lanka, the UAE, Pakistan, Israel, Malaysia and the Seychelles. Albanese described Diwali as a celebration of light that brings communities together across religious and cultural boundaries. He said its message calls for compassion, understanding, love and unity. Macron wished people unity, peace and hope, while Carney highlighted Diwali’s symbolism: light over darkness, good over evil and knowledge over ignorance. In Bangkok, Thailand’s prime minister inaugurated the Amazing Thailand Grand Diwali Festival, a 27-day event. In the United States, Donald Trump marked the occasion by lighting a diya at the White House. Gautam Gambhir, Jay Shah, the BCCI, former cricketers and IPL teams shared festive messages. Their wishes emphasized peace, prosperity, family, togetherness and hope. “It is a call to compassion and understanding, and of love and unity,” he said. “Wishing all my Indian friends in India, France, and around the world, a very happy Diwali! May its light inspire us to ever uphold unity, peace, and hope!” Macron wrote on social media, alongside a similar message in Hindi. Carney said communities across Canada were joining millions around the world to celebrate Diwali, the Festival of Lights — marking the triumph of light over darkness, good over evil,

6824daa35caf6638.title: Fifty years ago | Power struggle in China had begun 2 years ago
6824daa35caf6638.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 02:26 am IST Tokyo, November 9: Though the ouster from power of the four Shanghai radicals, led by Mao Tse-tung’s widow, Chiang Ching, became known to the outside world only last month, an acute power struggle within the Chinese Communist Party had been going on for nearly two years with Chairman Mao himself ranged against the gang of four, as they have now come to be known. Some light on this hitherto hidden aspect has been thrown by an editorial carried by the Liberation Army Daily, official organ of the People’s Liberation Army. According to the editorial, the gang of four had been engaging over a period of time in an attempt to usurp top party and State leadership. Mao, however, saw through the plot and made it impossible for their schemes to be achieved. 766d5dd61af4ec7c.title: Optional Travel Insurance Scheme urged for railway staff
766d5dd61af4ec7c.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 12:24 am IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Senior National Railway Trade Union leader and Divisional Railway Users’ Consultative Committee (DRUCC) member Chalasani Gandhi on Tuesday urged the Railway Board to extend the Optional Travel Insurance Scheme (OTIS) to serving railway employees, pensioners, and their eligible family members travelling on Privilege Passes and Privilege Ticket Orders (PTOs). Mr. Gandhi stated in a release that following directions from the Supreme Court the Railway Board had extended the optional travel insurance facility – previously restricted to online ticket bookings – to passengers purchasing reserved tickets through Railway Passenger Reservation System (PRS) counters with effect from October 27. Under the scheme, passengers receive an accident insurance coverage of up to ₹10 lakh against a nominal premium of 45 paise. The scheme covers compensation for death, permanent disability, hospitalisation expenses, and transportation of mortal remains. c65d287d2023421b.title: Govt to identify rainfed areas to boost pulses production, check prices
c65d287d2023421b.summary: This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. New Delhi: After India's gram (chana) imports fell in FY26 from a record high a year earlier, the government is stepping up efforts to strengthen domestic production of the pulse and further reduce import dependence and keep prices under control. The Department of Consumer Affairs is identifying rainfed areas that can be brought under chana cultivation, two people aware of the matter said. It has identified 80 districts across states, including Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Haryana, Punjab, Jharkhand and Bihar, where rainfed land could be utilised to grow the crop, the people said. India imported gram worth $3.63 billion in FY26, down from a record $5.54 billion in FY25. The proposed move aims to build on this reduction by expanding domestic chana supplies. “The government has a tentative estimate of around 2.38 million hectares of rainfed land across watershed areas in the identified states, and the exact extent of land suitable for chana cultivation will be mapped by the two departments,” said the first among the two officials cited above. "As part of the plan, the department will approach the agriculture ministry and the Department of Land Resources to identify suitable acreage and assess its additional production potential,” the official added. The department plans to support farmers with quality seeds and technical assistance, along with procurement assurance, the second official said. Chana is a relatively less water-intensive crop that can be grown using residual soil moisture after the kharif harvest. The government expects the proposed expansion to strengthen domestic supplies and eventually create scope for chana dal exports, subject to domestic demand and surplus availability. 2c176b9bf28da1a6.title: State govt. employees who donate organs likely to get leave for recuperation
2c176b9bf28da1a6.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 01:15 am IST - CHENNAI Health Minister K.G. Arunraj speaking at an event organised by Gleneagles Hospital in Chennai on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: J. Johan Sathyadas Health Minister K.G. Arunraj on Tuesday said that the State government was likely to provide 42 days of leave to employees who donate organs. Similarly, if organ donors themselves need organs, their needs will be prioritised. Speaking at an event to honour over 250 living donor liver transplantation journeys, supported by the Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme at Gleneagles Hospital, he said that government hospitals too will soon take up live liver organ transplants in a transparent manner. Dr. Arunraj urged the public to take care of their liver health. He said that those who are used to consuming alcohol every day should gradually reduce the quantum and take to responsible drinking. A. Aravind, Director of Medical Education, said that the cost of one live liver transplant was around ₹22 lakh and it was great that the State government was making it possible through insurance. Joy Varghese, director of Hepatology, Gleneagles, said that over 100 beneficiaries of live liver transplant were children between the ages of 5 and 14. Many of them had been referred from the government-run hospitals, he said, adding that the hospital was indebted to doctors in government hospitals for the trust they placed in them. Sholinganallur MLA P. Saravanan, S. Niranjani, chief operating officer, and J. Sophia Ansetta, medical director were present. 4459a04203b498ad.title: Savita makes way for Bansari in Indian women’s hockey squad for ACT
4459a04203b498ad.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 01:34 am IST - NEW DELHI Indian women’s hockey goalkeeper Savita Punia. File | Photo Credit: PTI Veteran goalkeeper Savita Punia has been rested from the Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal, replaced by Bansari Solanki in the Indian women's hockey squad unveiled on Tuesday, with head coach Sjoerd Marijne also announcing changes to the roles of some players during the event. The tournament is scheduled to be held from November 19 to 28 at the newly-built International Sports Complex, Nathu Barkheda, Bhopal and India will enter as the defending champions. India will begin their campaign against Malaysia on the opening day of the competition. Mid-fielder Salima Tete will continue to lead the team, which is playing its first international tournament after the historic gold medal at the Asian Games in Japan last month. The hosts have secured the ACT title in 2016, 2023 and 2024. The six-team competition will feature India, China, Japan, Malaysia, Thailand and South Korea. Like India, South Korea too have won the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy three times. The 25-year-old Bansari has been part of the squad that won the Asia Cup last year. Bichu Devi Kharibam retained her place as the other custodian in the squad. "This is the moment I want to give other players the chance to showcase their talent on the international stage. Some players will be playing in different positions than they normally do, so that I can see how they perform in a different role," said Marijne. f48a08324b837576.title: A hundred years ago | A case under the Companies Act
f48a08324b837576.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 02:26 am IST Bombay, November 10: Mr. P.D. Shamdasani, a shareholder of the Tata Iron and Steel Company and a most persistent critic of the Tata House, has for once succeeded in putting seven of the Steel Company’s Directors in the wrong though he has in almost every shareholders’ meeting of the company threatened them with prosecution on many allegations of mismanagement. The present case against Sri Dorab Tata, Sir Cowasji Jehangir, Narottam Morarji, Sir Phiroze Sethna, Mr. N.B. Saklatwala, Mr. F.E. Dinshaw and Sir Ibrahim Rabintulla Tata Sons Ltd and others is that they failed to comply with the provisions of the Indian Companies Act in not having convened the Company’s annual general meeting within fifteen months of the preceding meeting. The accused, in pleading guilty, urged that this was a fit case for warning and discharge. The Magistrate expressed inability to do so as this was a case under the Indian Companies Act and not one under the Penal Code. He convicted and fined them to a pay a fine of Rs. 5 each. 774c708eded497ec.title: UPI volume jumps 32% on Diwali driven by last-minute festival buying
774c708eded497ec.summary: Transactions through the popular Unified Payments Interface (UPI) witnessed a 32 per cent surge in volume terms on Diwali driven by last-minute festival buying. UPI volume increased to 916.9 million on November 8 from 695.7 million transactions on the same day last year, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). In value terms, UPI transactions rose to Rs 90,029.43 crore on November 8 against Rs 88,350.79 crore last year. A day prior to Diwali, the transaction volume was 975.8 million resulting in transfer of Rs 1,36,118 crore. UPI is an instant payment system developed by the NPCI. NPCI, an initiative of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Indian Banks' Association (IBA), is an umbrella organisation for operating retail payments and settlement systems in India. 04b9e8c6ff989ba3.title: Karnataka-registered doctors may be allowed to practise in Kasaragod: Keralam Health Minister
04b9e8c6ff989ba3.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 02:04 am IST - KASARAGOD Keralam Health Minister K. Muraleedharan The Keralam government has recommended to the State Medical Council that doctors registered with the Karnataka Medical Council be allowed to practise in Kasaragod, considering the district’s special circumstances, Health Minister K. Muraleedharan has said. The medical council is expected to take a favourable decision on the recommendation soon, the Minister said while inaugurating ‘Kayakalpam’, a public outreach programme of the Health Minister. Government hospitals should have adequate number of doctors, nurses, pharmacists, and laboratory technicians, the Minister said, adding that additional posts had been sought. Their early sanction would considerably ease staff shortage in the district. The extension of the tenure of National Health Mission employees in Kasaragod till March 31 was also an indication of the government’s commitment to the district, he said. The Minister said that he would direct the authorities to convene a meeting of the Endosulfan cell soon. Periye in Kasaragod was among the four locations proposed by the government to the Centre for setting up an All India Institute of Medical Sciences, he said. Instructions had been issued to make hostel facilities available at the Kasaragod Medical College within two months. The construction of a hostel for nursing students would begin within three months, he added. The government would ensure the services of a forensic surgeon at the Kanhangad district hospital. A new building for the District Medical Office would be constructed at a cost of ₹4.8 crore. f34cf13b4eab2f63.summary: Updated - November 10, 2026 11:36 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Govardhan puja and Gau puja were held at the Sri Sri Radha Madan Mohan temple at Hare Krishna Vaikuntham, Gambheeram, Visakhapatnam, on Tuesday. The celebrations began with a palanquin procession of the deities from the temple to the goshala , where the cows were worshipped. Niskinchana Bhakta Dasa, president of the Hare Krishna Movement, Visakhapatnam, spoke about the significance of Lord Krishna’s G ovardhan Leela a nd G au puja. Devotees prepared a traditional Annakuta , a mountain-like offering comprising 108 varieties of vegetarian food for Lord Krishna. They also performed govardhan parikrama (walking around) the offering. The programme included damodara aarti and the offering of ghee lamps to the deity. The celebrations concluded with the distribution of prasadam . 73c1d076fc4d4ad0.title: Fear, stigma, financial concerns keep cancer patients from seeking timely care, says expert
73c1d076fc4d4ad0.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 11:52 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Dr Rupali Basu, senior vice president, regional business head - East and Andhra Pradesh, HCG Cancer Centre, during an interaction with The Hindu in Visakhapatnam on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: V RAJU Early diagnosis of cancer, coupled with timely intervention and access to appropriate treatment, is crucial to improving survival rates and in helping patients lead a better quality of life, said Rupali Basu, senior vice president, regional business head - East and Andhra Pradesh, HCG Cancer Centre. Emphasising the need to strengthen cancer awareness and screening, Ms. Basu said that many patients continued to approach hospitals only at an advanced stage of the disease owing to fear, social stigma, lack of awareness of early symptoms, financial concerns and geographical barriers to accessing specialised healthcare. Stronger community-level awareness programmes and accessible screening facilities could play a significant role in changing this trend, she said. Speaking to The Hindu , she said that cancer was increasingly emerging as a concern across age groups and communities, with several factors, including an ageing population, tobacco consumption, cigarette smoking, changing lifestyles and environmental exposure, contributing to the growing burden. While breast cancer remained a major concern among women, lung and colorectal cancers were among the commonly diagnosed cancers in men. Brain tumours and other forms of cancer also required greater awareness and timely medical attention. Ms. Basu stressed that cancer treatment required more than just identifying the disease. A multidisciplinary approach, involving tumour boards, was essential to determine the most appropriate course of treatment for each patient. Accurate diagnosis, the latest medical technology and coordinated care could make a significant difference to treatment outcomes and the patient’s overall experience. 32e378b7558b4e37.title: The War Putin Wanted to Keep Away Is Coming Home to Russia
32e378b7558b4e37.summary: Olga was jolted awake by an explosion so powerful that her apartment building shuddered and the windows and furniture shook. Looking outside, she saw a plume of thick black smoke rising from a military equipment factory that had just been hit by a missile. Residents panicked, said Olga, a 49-year-old choreographer. “We didn’t know whether we should run to a shelter,” she said. The strike on the plant left six people dead and another 26 injured, according to the local governor. Olga doesn’t live in Kyiv, Kherson or any other Ukrainian city that’s been pounded for years by President Vladimir Putin’s forces. This is Kirov, a Russian city about 800 kilometers northeast of Moscow known for its 16th century onion-domed monastery rather than being in a war zone. The missile strike was one of the many that have inflicted rising civilian casualties inside Russia in recent months. They are bringing Putin’s war home to his own people after he promised a swift and glorious victory. Since Ukrainian strikes intensified in mid-summer, people inside Russia are killed almost every week, according to a Bloomberg analysis of statements from regional authorities on their Telegram channels. Meanwhile, as Russia prepared to resume trilateral negotiations with the US and Ukraine on a potential peace deal in Abu Dhabi this week, confidential data hacked from Russia’s statistics service showed about 400,000 of its people have been killed fighting in Ukraine. It’s a scale of military deaths the country hasn’t seen since World War II. The Kremlin tightly controls the narrative around the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, now nine months into its fifth year. While the death toll touches a huge number of families in Russia, it won’t necessarily have political consequences for Putin, who taps into historical memory to justify the sacrifice in what he claims is an existential fight with the West in Ukraine. ee4a7dd1e82b3913.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 05:30 am IST - New Delhi Delhi’s air quality improved to the ‘poor’ category on Tuesday, with the 24-hour average AQI recorded at 299, just below the ‘very poor’ threshold of 300. | Photo Credit: ANI The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) on Tuesday indicated that it was considering steps to capture peak levels of particulate matter (PM), a major pollutant, that exceed the existing monitoring range, after air quality data from several government monitoring stations in Delhi went missing for hours during the pollution spike following Deepavali on Sunday. The Hindu reported on Monday that the data gaps had led to an artificially lower official air quality index (AQI), making air quality appear better than it actually was, according to experts. In a statement on Tuesday, the CPCB said PM levels were measured only up to 1,000 micrograms per cubic metre (µg/m³) for AQI calculations, which explained the missing data on Deepavali night, when actual concentrations exceeded this limit. “The PM analysers deployed at the time of introduction of the NAQI (National Air Quality Index) [in 2015] were calibrated for a measurement range of 0-1,000 µg/m³. Accordingly, consistent with this, the designed system of automated data validation treats hourly readings beyond the calibrated range as outside range, and such readings are not used in the computation,” the CPCB statement read. “During extreme episodes, which are occasional, like Diwali firecracker bursting, this may appear as a data gap at the particular station concerned, and those hours do not contribute to the 24-hour average of the relevant pollutant for the concerned station,” the statement added. The CPCB said internal deliberations and consultations on processing data “beyond system design range” were under way. 259f3a995c68bcd1.title: Tasmac introduces three year transfer norm for shop employees
259f3a995c68bcd1.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 12:15 am IST - Chennai Tasmac headquarters will classify every shop as an A, B and C shop on the basis of its average daily sales and accordingly deploy workforce. (File) | Photo Credit: B. VELANKANNI RAJ The Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (Tasmac) is set to reshuffle employees across its retail network in Tamil Nadu, deploying staff at outlets based on manpower requirements. Under a new Transfer and Posting Policy for Tasmac liquor Retail Vending Shop Personnel, 2026, the state run liquor retailer has proposed transferring employees across shops once every three years. This is aimed at streamlining staff deployment and addressing manpower shortages. This one time rationalisation will be completed by November 30, 2026. The policy will apply to Supervisor (Shop-In-Charge), Salesman and Assistant Salesman. Exceptions will be given to shop personnel who are differently-abled or any genuine administrative circumstances. Tasmac headquarters will classify every shop as an A, B and C shop on the basis of its average daily sales and accordingly deploy workforce. Outlets with average monthly sales of ₹10 lakh and above will be classified as Category A and will have a minimum workforce of nine employees. Those with sales of more than ₹5 lakh but less than ₹10 lakh will fall under Category B, with a workforce of eight employees. Outlets recording sales of less than ₹5 lakh will be classified as Category C and will have five employees. The minimum number of manpower will vary based on operational requirements. Also, the classification of shops will be done every year based on the sales performance of each outlet, according to official sources. Employees who have complete three years at a shop as on November 1 will be considered for the transfer. 259f3a995c68bcd1.raw_facts: Published - November 11, 2026 12:15 am IST - Chennai Tasmac headquarters will classify every shop as an A, B and C shop on the basis of its average daily sales and accordingly deploy workforce. (File) | Photo Credit: B. VELANKANNI RAJ The Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (Tasmac) is set to reshuffle employees across its retail network in Tamil Nadu, deploying staff at outlets based on manpower requirements. Under a new Transfer and Posting Policy for Tasmac liquor Retail Vending Shop Personnel, 2026, the state run liquor retailer has proposed transferring employees across shops once every three years. This is aimed at streamlining staff deployment and addressing manpower shortages. This one time rationalisation will be completed by November 30, 2026. The policy will apply to Supervisor (Shop-In-Charge), Salesman and Assistant Salesman. Exceptions will be given to shop personnel who are differently-abled or any genuine administrative circumstances. Tasmac headquarters will classify every shop as an A, B and C shop on the basis of its average daily sales and accordingly deploy workforce. Outlets with average monthly sales of ₹10 lakh and above will be classified as Category A and will have a minimum workforce of nine employees. Those with sales of more than ₹5 lakh but less than ₹10 lakh will fall under Category B, with a workforce of eight employees. Outlets recording sales of less than ₹5 lakh will be classified as Category C and will have five employees. The minimum number of manpower will vary based on operational requirements. Also, the classification of shops will be done every year based on the sales performance of each outlet, according to official sources. Employees who have complete three years at a shop as on November 1 will be considered for the transfer. 75e338a3dfe88607.title: India A-New Zealand A series ends in draw after rain washes out fourth day of third unofficial Test
75e338a3dfe88607.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 01:14 am IST - LINCOLN, NEW ZEALAND The third and final unofficial Test between India A and New Zealand A ended in a draw, with the series ending in a draw. All three four-day matches failed to produce a result. At the end of day 4, NZ A was 36/2, with Dean Foxcroft (10*) and Zak Gibson (1*) unbeaten. They trailed by 428 runs. Earlier, New Zealand A won the toss and elected to field first. A 175-run opening stand between Yashasvi Jaiswal (102 in 138 balls, with 16 fours and two sixes) and Sai Sudharsan (88 in 215 balls, with 11 fours) started off things for India. Half-centuries came from the bat of Tilak Varma (81 in 164 balls, with five fours and two sixes), skipper Dhruv Jurel (71 in 95 balls, with nine fours and two sixes) and Washington Sundar (50* in 107 balls, with two fours) as India posted 464/5. Zak Gibson (2/73) was the leading wicket-taker for NZ. India’s batting was a big plus ahead of the Test series starting on November 19, with Devdutt Padikkal (326 runs in three matches and five innings at an average of 65.20, with a century and a fifty) being the top run-scorer. After a few poor scores, Yashasvi Jaiswal (279 runs in three matches and five innings at an average of 69.75, with two centuries) also scored back-to-back tons. Sai Sudharsan (231 runs in three matches and five innings at an average of 46.20, with two fifties) and skipper Jurel (179 runs in three matches and four innings at an average of 44.75, with a century and a fifty) also played some fine knocks for India. Uncapped batter Yash Rathod (223 runs in two matches at an average of 111.50, with a century and a fifty) also was a big positive for India. Auqib Nabi (six wickets in a match) and Mohammed Siraj (four wickets in a match) were the leading wicket-takers for India. India Test squad for two NZ Tests: Shubman Gill [C], Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul [VC], Devdutt Padikkal, Rishabh Pant [WK]*, Dhruv Jurel [WK], Ravindra Jadeja, Anshul Kamboj, Jasprit Bumrah, Pras

db5df5e4f7a3cce5.title: Around 150 persons treated for cracker-related burns in Vellore, nearby districts
db5df5e4f7a3cce5.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 11:55 pm IST - VELLORE Sanitary workers remove cracker wastes in Vellore Corporation. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Around 150 persons received treatment for cracker-related burns at various healthcare centres, government hospitals in Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur, and Tiruvannamalai districts. Health officials said that the Government Medical College and Hospital in Vellore and Tiruvannamalai treated 22 and 35 persons respectively for cracker-related burns. “Most of the victims were treated as out-patients. They were below the age of 15. A team of health officials was deployed for the purpose,” said Edvina Vasantha, dean, Government Medical College Hospital in Tiruvannamalai. In Tirupattur district, on an average, 10-12 cases of burns were reported at the Government Taluk Hospital at Tirupattur, Vaniyambadi, Ambur, and Natrampalli towns each, during the festival. The government health centres in Jawadhu Hills also reported at least 15 burn cases over three days (November 7-9). “No major burns were reported within Vellore town during the festival. Adequate medical teams were in place to attend to emergencies,” P. Pratap Kumar, City Health Officer (CHO), Vellore Corporation, told The Hindu . In Ranipet district, more than 40 cases of burns were reported in government hospitals at Arakkonam, Walajah, Arcot, Ranipet, and Sholinghur towns during the festival. Health officials said that private hospitals and clinics also reported cases of cracker-related burns. Most of the persons are treated as out-patients in these districts. A large volume of cracker waste was generated in these districts. Around 550 tonnes of cracker wastes were generated in Vellore and Tiruvannamalai Corporation on November 8-9. More than 500 sanitary workers were roped in for the purpose. Most of the wastes include paper, cardboard, half-burnt, and unused crackers that are mostly dumped on roads and streets. These were sent to micro compost centres for recycling.

Essentially, as of now, I don’t want to switch federations at all,” Abhimanyu told The Hindu on the sidelines of the Total Chess World Championship Tour pilot here. He said his response to that hypothetical question was that he might consider a switch. “But the thing is, this does not mean that I’m searching to change federation at all currently,” he said. Abhimanyu also spoke about playing simultaneous exhibitions to help cover expenses. The sessions, which involved taking on several opponents and could last hours, provided some income but were tiring. “And I was getting some money out of that, which was helping a bit,” he said. In Budapest, Abhimanyu has been drawn in Group C alongside Magnus Carlsen, Anish Giri, Ian Nepomniachtchi, Haik M. Martirosyan and Shakhriyar Mamedyarov. He will face each opponent twice in the Fast Classic group stage. The 24-player event combines blitz, rapid and Fast Classic, with players tested at all three speeds in the knockouts. The chance to play Carlsen twice was particularly appealing, with Abhimanyu describing it as a source of joy and a learning experience. TThe strength of the field had convinced him to accept the invitation. “I mean, saying no to a tournament like this is a bit ridiculous, honestly,” he said. fe2151dac5c26ccb.raw_facts: Published - November 10, 2026 11:55 pm IST - Budapest Abhimanya Mishra. | Photo Credit: File photo: SUDHAKARA JAIN American Grandmaster Abhimanyu Mishra said he has no current plans to switch federations, explaining that his earlier comments referred to a hypothetical situation. “Actually, this was a huge miscommunication. Essentially, as of now, I don’t want to switch federations at all,” Abhimanyu told The Hindu on the sidelines of the Total Chess World Championship Tour pilot here. He said his response to that hypothetical question was that he might consider a switch. “But the thing is, this does not mean that I’m searching to change federation at all currently,” he said. Abhimanyu also spoke about playing simultaneous exhibitions to help cover expenses. The sessions, which involved taking on several opponents and could last hours, provided some income but were tiring. “And I was getting some money out of that, which was helping a bit,” he said. In Budapest, Abhimanyu has been drawn in Group C alongside Magnus Carlsen, Anish Giri, Ian Nepomniachtchi, Haik M. Martirosyan and Shakhriyar Mamedyarov. He will face each opponent twice in the Fast Classic group stage. The 24-player event combines blitz, rapid and Fast Classic, with players tested at all three speeds in the knockouts. The chance to play Carlsen twice was particularly appealing, with Abhimanyu describing it as a source of joy and a learning experience. TThe strength of the field had convinced him to accept the invitation. “I mean, saying no to a tournament like this is a bit ridiculous, honestly,” he said. bcef827141be2997.title: Two persons killed in separate road incidents
bcef827141be2997.summary: Updated - November 10, 2026 11:48 pm IST - TIRUVANNAMALAI Two persons were killed in separate road incidents near Kilpennathur and Arcot towns in Tiruvannamalai and Ranipet districts respectively on Tuesday. The police identified the victims as V. Nandakumar, 45, and T. Venkatesan, 35. Initial inquiry revealed that Nandakumar, a private school staff, was on his way to school on the Chennai – Bengaluru Highway (NH 48) when a private bus hit the two-wheeler he was riding at Melvisharam in Ranipet. Passersby rushed a badly injured Nandakumar to Government Taluk Hospital in Arcot town, where doctors said that he was brought dead. A case was registered and a probe is under way. In a separate incident, the victim, Venkatesan was riding his autorickshaw from a petrol pump towards the Chittoor – Cuddalore Highway at Kilpennathur, when a car rammed the autorickshaw. The police said in the impact, Venkatesan died on the spot. On being informed, Kilpennathur police inspected the spot and a case was registered. Special teams were formed to nab the car driver, and a probe is under way. 65337055769d5a1d.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 02:44 am IST Washington, November 10: Either with or without the knowledge of the U.S. Government, a number of foreign intelligence organisations appear to have established a regular presence in the United States, and have been engaged in activities which are for the most part illegal. The most publicised case to-date is that of the South Korean Intelligence Agency (KCIA), which has been accused of not only spying on South Korean and American nationals in the U.S., but also of giving huge bribes to U.S. Congressmen and others in a bid to influence U.S. defence and foreign policies — former Defence Secretary Melvin Laird has now disclosed that in 1970 the South Korean “lobby” tried to undermine the Nixon Administration’s decision to withdraw 20,000 American troops from South Korea. March 21, 2022: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy calls for direct talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, an idea rebuffed by Lavrov. March 28-30, 2022: Delegations meet in Istanbul to work on a draft peace agreement. dd83f32e27bf4940.title: US set to become first country to fully shun UN Human Rights Council review
dd83f32e27bf4940.summary: The United States is set to become the first country to fully shun a regular review of its human rights record at the UN's top rights body since it was created two decades ago. The Trump administration last year pulled the US out of the Human Rights Council, accusing it of an anti-US and anti-Israel bias, and alleging that it didn't uphold the very values it promotes. Supporters back the council's mandate to keep tabs on human rights in all UN member states including the US, which has drawn criticism for its policies including strong-arm deportations and targeted killings of alleged drug-runners in the Caribbean and Pacific - which the administration has said are designed to protect US workers and help keep the country safe. The Geneva-based council regularly examines the rights records of all 193 UN member states - generally about every four to five years - as part of a process known as the universal periodic review. The United States, under Trump, already skipped its appointment

4f4a1af698b44ae6.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
4f4a1af698b44ae6.summary: Updated - November 11, 2026 01:13 am IST If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues. In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. d83b333384396245.title: IND vs NZ 3rd ODI abandoned due to rain, India retains 2-0 series lead
d83b333384396245.summary: Rain played spoilsport as the third ODI between New Zealand and India at Seddon Park here on Tuesday was called off. India lead the five-match series 2-0 as the two teams head to Tauranga for the final two games, scheduled for November 13 and 15. India skipper Shubman Gill won the toss for the third time in a row and opted to bowl, fielding an unchanged side from the previous two games. However, just as the covers were coming off for a 40-overs-a-side contest, the heavens opened up once again. With at least 70 minutes remaining before the local cut-off time of 7:50 pm for a 20-overs-a-side game, the two umpires decided to call off the match. The weather forecast for this game had always been gloomy, with a 90 per cent chance of rain predicted throughout the day. This was supposed to be the last game of the series for skipper Shubman Gill and senior wicketkeeper KL Rahul before they link up with the Test squad in Wellington. They will be accompanied by Kuldeep Yadav, Anshul Kamboj

7831602d78cda82e.title: Petroleum contamination makes wells unusable at Palloor in Mahe
7831602d78cda82e.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 07:00 am IST - KANNUR Residents affected by the contamination of well water allegedly due to the operation of petrol pumps near the Thalassery-Mahe bypass staging a protest in front of the office of the Mahe Regional Administrator. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Residents of Palloor in Mahe adjoining the Thalassery-Mahe bypass are up in arms against petrol pumps operating in densely populated residential areas and six proposed outlets, alleging that petroleum contamination has affected drinking water sources, made wells unusable, and rendered life miserable because of the persistent smell of fuel. A joint action council has been formed, and hundreds of residents have joined the agitation against the outlets and the Mahe administration, demanding the immediate intervention of the authorities in the matter. The Kerala Shastra Sahitya Parishad (KSSP) has also demanded the closure of pumps violating safety and environmental norms in Ward 11 of Mahe municipality. The affected stretch from Kunhipuramukku in Naluthara to Spinning Mill Road covers around 0.1 square kilometre and has 11 operational pumps. P.T. Premraj, a Palloor resident and joint action council convener, said the problem became noticeable after an HP petrol pump was shifted to a hilltop around two and a half years ago. A BPCL outlet began operating beside the highway in September, less than 100 metres away. “The water in a nearby well first developed a chlorine-like smell in January. Later, there was a smell resembling soap and now petrol or diesel,” he said. According to Mr. Premraj, samples collected from six wells near three petrol pumps tested positive for petroleum hydrocarbon. The Health department subsequently issued notices warning residents against using the water for drinking, bathing, or other domestic purposes.
